- mr president, following on from the words of our colleague pernille frahm, i would like to express my great disappointment that this iranian regime, which in 2002 stood out as one of the regimes that most repressed its people and most violated human rights, has not been condemned by the united nations because the european union decided not to propose such a condemnation. this does not make any sense to me and leads me to believe that this is an opportunism in the european union's human rights policy, which i cannot accept and cannot understand.
- mr president, a member of this house very rightly condemned cloning a short while ago, calling for a universal rejection of cloning. except you didn't make the proper distinction between reproductive cloning and therapeutic cloning. as regards reproductive cloning, we can all agree that it is an inhuman or dehumanizing technique which must be rejected. but the same cannot be said of therapeutic cloning. we must leave an open door for science, scientists and the scientific community to experiment with areas of great potential for medicine and great innovation. and it is the dogmatists who oppose any form of cloning who are the best allies of those who refer it to clandestinity, to quackery and to trafficking. let us agree on this essential point: if you want to block science and research in the field of cloning, there will always be adventurers and unscrupulous men who want to exploit this sector of knowledge.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the importance of our debate today is based on article 6 of the treaty on european union itself, which states that the union is founded on the principles of liberty, democracy, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms and the rule of law, principles which are common to the member states, that is to say, the european construction has been built on the basis of full respect for, guarantee and promotion of fundamental and human rights, in which the well-being and dignity of its citizens must inspire and be the aim of every act carried out by any state and by the community institutions. hence the importance of the european parliament's annual report on human rights, which has served as the ideal opportunity to analyse the european union's human rights policy, both within and outside the union, and the role which the european parliament has played and of which we can be proud. that is why i am disappointed with the report before us, because it is not balanced and rigorous. the report presented to us last year by mr cornillet was rich in ideas and analysis and was a milestone and a very positive step towards defining a methodology for monitoring and evaluation which should be the basis of any human rights policy, based of course on the european charter of human rights. but the report we are presented with this year - although it has aspects which deserve our sympathy, such as the question of terrorism, trafficking in human beings and human rights and the very current problem of the necessary balance between security and human rights - gives way to demagogy on some other points and departs, as a whole, from the principles of rigor which, in our opinion, should be embodied in the resolution adopted by the european parliament. that is why, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am getting closer to the text of the alternative resolution tabled by mr ribeiro e castro, which will deserve my vote in favour.
- mr president, the weaknesses of this report are not in the denunciations of human rights violations where they exist, but in the way in which this report has been drawn up and in the methodology used to present them. by choosing to describe in the explanatory statement, in a long and detailed way, possible violations of fundamental rights by some member states, this report results in statements and accusations for those member states which are neither rebuttable nor even subject to a democratic vote because they are not in the text of the motion for a resolution. and so these are brass claims, which cannot be challenged, although they are obviously not valid before the house because they are not included in the motion for a resolution. i would also like to point out that, as regards the sources used, and without in any way wanting to call into question the credibility of many ngos, a report drawn up by the european parliament should distance itself from, and even take its own decisions on, the conclusions of each of these organisations, and avoid taking on board, sometimes incorrectly, some of the elements of these studies. for example, in the portuguese case, it is said that there is discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation based on the conclusions and observations of an ngo (i will not quote it, it is in the text), and the rapporteur claims that there is a discriminatory provision in the portuguese penal code on this matter, which i repudiate on the basis of what is a simple reading of the law. in fact, there is no differentiation in the portuguese penal code on sexual orientation as regards the age of consent. mr president, i believe that the european parliament must assume its responsibilities in safeguarding human rights responsibly and cannot in any way limit itself to transcribing the judgments of others. it is clear that this will always be the case until we have a legally relevant charter of fundamental rights; only then will things not go on like this. it is that we all want to ban violations, but there are no violations of political rights, there are legal violations, there are violations of concrete rights, and these either exist or do not exist. no political flexibility, no interpretative criteria allow us to discover violations of rights where they are not legally relevant. nor, on the contrary, can any violation of the law be justified by political criteria of any kind. that is why i will not be in favour of this report: the fundamental balance which is necessary when making a judgment of opinion on such sensitive matters is not present in this text and therefore cannot merit my agreement.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the rapporteur invokes last year's decision by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) to make the charter of fundamental rights the main thrust of its annual report on the situation of human rights in the eu'1, adding that'the charter of fundamental rights of the european union ... has given [this work] ... a greater focus and orientation'. if that is the case, then we must be guided by that same principle: not going too far, going beyond the rights enshrined in the charter; not being distracted by an endless inspection drift, diverting the report from its purpose and its limits and trying to turn the resolution we voted for into an abusive - indeed delusional - instrument of endless political judgment on the member states. the european parliament has no powers to do so, except in specific situations: those situations which are so serious that they are considered potentially relevant for the sanctioning effects of article 7 of the eu treaty. we all know that the charter itself sets out the scope of the charter: the provisions of this charter are addressed to the institutions and bodies of the union, in compliance with the principle of subsidiarity, and to the member states only when they are implementing union law (article 51). both the report and the resolution should therefore be addressed directly to the institutions and bodies of the union; and, except for the specific remark for the purposes of articles 6 and 7 of the eu treaty, only indirectly to the member states, in so far as they apply union law and only in so far as they do so. we were all astonished when the rapporteur finally told us the exact opposite: that on the one hand the report expressly concerns only the situation of human rights in the current eu member states, which is exactly what it should not do, and on the other hand that the report does not include any review or assessment of the acts of the council, the commission and parliament, which is what it should do. if we add to this flagrant methodological deviation the regrettable frivolity of many assessments made about member states, without sufficient and appropriate objective basis (as the rapporteur herself also acknowledges), we have here the set of essential reasons why, in its own terms, the swiebel proposal cannot but be rejected. and instead the alternative resolution i have tabled should be adopted, putting things right and getting this parliament to follow the guidelines we have set ourselves.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating mr hubert pirker on the excellent report he has presented to us and also on the initiative of the commission, the quality of which has already been underlined and which will certainly also deserve the support of my friend mr christian von boetticher. the signing of the schengen agreement in 1990 and the abolition of checks at national borders have increased the importance of external border controls to prevent threats to the security of our citizens from entering the community. the growing threats of terrorism, organised crime, trafficking in human beings and drugs and illegal immigration have been high on our political agenda and at the heart of citizens' concerns. however, it is regrettable that the external borders remain one of the weakest links in the system, which undermines not only the effective protection of internal security but also the full application of the principle of free movement. this is all the more significant in the context of enlargement, where the new countries will have to take over the management of the external borders progressively, assuming a considerable share of responsibility. it is therefore essential that the union adopts coherent measures in the field of border security, without prejudice to the member states' own competences but contributing to increasing the effectiveness of such protection. i agree with the rapporteur, mr hubert pirker, that it is essential to develop a common policy for the control of the present and future external borders, which implies the application of common standards in the field of external border management, a common central guide and training programme for the responsible agents, a europe college for senior officials, priority for the financing of projects aimed at implementing common standards, a european border guard corps, including community funding, which should be, if necessary and at the request of the member states, temporarily made available to the national authorities in risk areas or crisis situations at the external borders. those common measures should also contribute to solving the problems currently encountered and identified in the transposition of the schengen acquis at the current external borders as regards the type and practices of border control, which vary at land and sea borders, as regards the responsibility for border management, which varies from one member state to another, in some cases even creating overlapping competences, and finally as regards the use of different technologies, which are sometimes not compatible and make it difficult to achieve a uniformly high level of security. i would like to end with the words of commissioner vitorino: this concern for a better management of our external borders must contribute to strengthening internal security in the union and in the member states.
- mr president, we naturally support all measures to strengthen the role of rail transport by reversing the current situation of favouring the highway. that is why we particularly support the reports by colleagues sylviane ainardi and gilles savary. if we want to have a competitive european railway system, we will have to harmonize technical standards and eliminate bottlenecks in the international network, while at the same time setting high safety standards. however, the intended interoperability will not be achieved through the liberalisation of the sector. where this has occurred, private operators have not responded, in particular to the high investment needs. the commission does not tell us where the necessary funding will be obtained to achieve this objective, and it will not help to increase the flow of traffic by competition between several operators if all trains have to run on the same line, because this will only lead to more disorganization and congestion. however, we are against full liberalisation of the passenger and freight sectors by 2008. we are against this maximalist position, just as we are against the commission's proposal to open the international freight transport market early, and we also do not accept that states are prevented from setting higher safety standards than those of the union just so as not to create difficulties in opening this market. we have responsibilities to the europeans. let us have the courage to defend a high-quality and safe public rail transport service which will actually encourage its use.
in writing. - the economic capacity and productivity of the european economy increasingly depend on efficient, interoperable transport systems that allow goods and people to move quickly within the european area and to international traffic. however, no significant progress has been made in rail transport. the decisions have been predominantly intergovernmental in nature, with each country seeking to protect its own interests and thus putting the creation of a european railway market into question. this situation is unsustainable because we are reaching a situation of congestion on the roads, which is very burdensome in economic and environmental terms, and which must be tackled with political will and adequate financial means. the problems of rail transport in peripheral countries, such as portugal, also need to be integrated into european solutions if the european union is to function as a whole and be economically efficient. the council, like the european parliament, must therefore show the political will and find the financial means to create a european rail transport market.
in writing. - (pt) i voted for this report on the european commission's communication on the annual report on humanitarian aid in 2000-2001 because i agree with the diagnosis made by the rapporteur and i also agree with many of the suggestions that have been made. as the rapporteur for the afet opinion says: 'the essential objective of the union's humanitarian action is to respond in a timely and effective manner to the needs of the victims of humanitarian crises in order to alleviate their suffering in a spirit of human solidarity. it goes without saying that no political considerations have any place in this conception". the committee also welcomed the fact that the commission had already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the food supply. in order to counteract this trend, and as has already been suggested, i believe it is important to strengthen echo's action, to develop awareness-raising actions among the citizens of the european union, in a more pro-active way, and, of course, to reverse the negative budgetary trend. better coordination of humanitarian aid and its actors should be one of our priorities, so as to avoid situations such as the one recently observed in angola, where aid was 'guaranteed' but where it was very late on the ground. the mechanisms of the response procedures need to be much more flexible.
in writing. - (pt) we are aware that this second railway package proposed by the commission and specifically the proposal for a directive on the development of community railways, to which the jarzembowski report refers, affects long-standing and consolidated interests in various member states, including my own, portugal. although the previous package is still recent (the agreement with the council dates from 2001), the present commission proposal seeks to go a step further by means of measures to liberalise the sector, particularly in the field of freight transport, together with the strengthening of safety standards applicable to this means of transport. we feel that we should support this liberalization effort proposed by the commission, while rejecting the amendments which already contained a timetable for the total opening up of the rail passenger and freight transport market. that is why we cannot support amendment no 13, which is endorsed by our colleague mr miranda, because it reflects a rigid position on the need to promote an environmentally friendly means of transport, which helps to reduce the traffic congestion in europe in the field of goods transport, but which requires heavy financial investments made viable only by opening up markets.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report because i share the view that in order to increase the safety of the community rail system and to improve the level of international rail services, it is necessary to promote the gradual transition to a system of common safety standards within the member states. i am pleased with the good safety indicators of european rail transport - which further confirms the urgent need to promote this transport solution and to reduce the use of less safe road transport, especially for heavy tonnage. it should be noted, however, that the liberalisation of rail services - which is planned for 2008 and is part of the package of which this report is a part - must draw the important lesson from the british experience of recent years, in which the public authorities have retained control and supervision of compliance with railway safety rules, particularly as regards infrastructure maintenance. i also looked at some of the suggestions made by the committee responsible, concerning the introduction of a safety certificate for railway undertakings and infrastructure managers. it also proposed appropriate training supplemented by certification of railway staff, as well as full access to safety information for all new railway companies and the adoption of a common vehicular language for international transport, as is the case for aviation.
in writing. - (pt) for the safety, quality and efficiency of inland transport, both of people and goods, priority should be given once and for all to rail transport and solutions (in addition to short sea shipping or cabotage). it therefore considers that the creation of a european railway agency is very important, as it will contribute, together with the european commission, to better consultation and coordination between the various actors involved in the policy and the operability of the railway system, and to continuously enrich the debate through recommendations and opinions. its consultation, proposal and observation missions will, if properly carried out, lead to an ever-increasing awareness of the member states and european citizens of the enormous advantages of this transport solution, especially in relation to the increasing difficulties (and dangers) of road transport. in this context, i would like to mention the commission's white paper 'european transport policy for 2010: steps for the future', which repeatedly stresses the need to reverse the decline in rail transport compared to road transport. i therefore hope that it will be a further step towards the creation of a genuine internal railway market, which will above all make it possible to reduce effectively the intensity of traffic on our roads, especially the enormous volume of goods transported by heavy-duty lorries.
in writing. - (pt) mr markov's report deserves to be voted on. while attempts are being made at european and national level to adopt measures to reduce the number of road fatalities (an area in which portugal is unfortunately a champion), one cannot but agree with a report whose content aims to improve the social and working conditions of road drivers. the report which has just been approved envisages positive measures: withdrawal of the proposal for a flexible working week; definition of driving time and limitation of working time; fixing of the minimum age of drivers for the transport of goods; limitation of possible derogations; strengthening of the involvement of the social partners; promotion of the extension of the regulation to all drivers operating within the territory of the european union. these measures deserve our approval, because they make a serious contribution to improving road safety. however, we can only regret that the majority of members of this parliament did not support the rapporteur in his proposal to reduce the weekly driving time to 45 hours. we hope, however, that the commission and the council will show the necessary openness to the amendments adopted.
in writing. - (pt) we support the regionalisation and the strengthening of the role of regional and local authorities on the basis of the constitutional framework and with respect for the sovereignty of the member states in decision-making, and therefore we support the aspects highlighted in the report in this area. we also think it is important to have a space at eu level - and there is already one, the committee of the regions - where these regions can exchange their experiences of their activities and give their views at eu level on matters of interest to them. however, the napolitano report, even after the adoption of certain positive amendments, is imbued with itself and also has a more or less explicit objective of trying to create direct links between the institutions of the european union and regional and local authorities, thus going beyond the principle of sovereign decision-making by the states, something with which we do not agree, because their internal organisation concerns only the latter, in particular the way in which decisions are taken. we therefore agree with the strengthening of the role of the regions, but we do not agree with the federalist logic, which seeks to override the sovereignty of the member states of the european union.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate our colleague mr napolitano on his timely and excellent report, which i support, on the role of regional and local authorities in the construction of europe. i particularly support the need for the union to formulate new methods of involving regional and local authorities in community life, without however neglecting the important role of the committee of the regions. i also strongly support the need to ensure that regional and local authorities are involved in the design and preparation of community policies and legislation - they are the ones who are responsible for their implementation most of the time. however, i think that this cooperation should be at the level of each member state. i strongly support mr napolitano's request for the consolidation of article 299 (2) of the ec treaty on the outermost regions. the first step is to make full use of the means of action provided for by the present status of the outermost regions, by making it possible to put into practice a genuine community policy for the outermost regions, a policy genuinely committed to combating the limitations imposed by their situation.
in writing. - (pt) for the committee on constitutional affairs, the hierarchical and pyramidal conception of the institutional system of the union must be abandoned and a system of greater participation of regional and local authorities in the european decision-making process must be introduced. one of the key issues in this report concerns precisely the role of the committee of the regions, by reaffirming its legitimacy and essential role as the institutional interlocutor of regional and local authorities in the context of the union. in this context, genuine amendments to the treaties are being considered as the work of the convention is progressing, such as the right of appeal to the court of justice for breaches of the principle of subsidiarity, which can be extended to regional and local authorities who have legislative powers when the defence of their rights is at stake, often against their own member states. these and other proposals (for example, the proposal to add article 6 (3) teu) would lead to the states, which are the only members of the union, playing a secondary role in its construction, and constitutional problems would certainly arise in some member states. i can only vote against this report, despite some positive proposals such as the defence of linguistic diversity and the promotion of the outermost regions.
in writing. - (pt) i largely agree with the diagnosis made in this report of the evident diversity of the phenomenon of regionalisation and of the very concept of region, and with the interpretation that regionalisation is 'to a large extent the result of institutional and political dynamics peculiar to each of the countries concerned'. although i agree with the principle that each member state has different administrative approaches, arising from its history, traditions and specificities, i no longer agree with the report's attempt to subordinate the political role of the member states by encouraging interference in the decision-making processes of the member states, by promoting their legal and institutional 'blockage' with powers being assumed by the european institutions and the regions, and by arguing that in the treaties the political legitimacy of the regions is artificially placed on the same footing as that of the member states. the attempt to dilute the functions and importance of the member states, which the report conveys, using the proximity of the peoples to the institutions of the union as a pretext, constitutes, in my view, a resurgence, perhaps unacknowledged, of federalist opportunism, which tries to make people forget the interstate character which presided over the creation of the union, by neglecting the pivotal and irreplaceable role of the states as the privileged architects and interpreters of the process of european construction. that is why i voted against this report. i would nevertheless like to make an important positive note of the recommendation for consolidating article 299 of the ec treaty, which relates to the outermost regions.
- mr commissioner, i thank you for your answer to my question - a reply in the style of a report - i welcome the action of the commission and the european union in angola, and i note that the commission is increasing its intervention in development aid and humanitarian aid to angola in many areas. i fully agree that the best solution for angola is to take advantage of the immeasurable potential that the country has. angola has been generously endowed by nature but, unfortunately, has been a victim of man's madness for decades and decades. today, these immense natural resources can be harnessed for the benefit of its people, who, by the way, in a colossal territorial expanse, amount to only 13 or 14 million inhabitants. we are therefore faced with a vivid paradox: a rich territory and a population living on the edge of poverty, hunger and death. i am very grateful to you, commissioner, and i think the commission should continue along the lines it has just communicated to us.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, health care in general and care for the elderly in particular must be given the greatest possible attention by the various institutions of the european union and the member states, because health is a fundamental human and social right recognised in international and national legislation. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (emahp) is based on the principle of equal treatment for all medicinal products. it is also emphasized that there is a close link between socioeconomic measures and health, particularly in the areas of employment, housing, education, transport, income distribution, social welfare. thus, the insistence on monetary policies and the priority of nominal convergence, on the maintenance of blind criteria of the stability pact, which lead to and serve as justification for restrictive social policies, have a negative influence on public health policies and health care for the elderly, as has been clear in portugal. the commission's communication on this subject, which the report welcomes, although with some criticism, is a proof of the contradictions of social policies. despite its claims to defend the quality and accessibility of health care, it overvalues the objective of financial viability in order to pave the way for the internal market in health services and products, which may lead to liberalisations and privatisations of an essential public service such as health care, ultimately calling into question equal access to all quality services in the field of health. it is an unacceptable position and one which is decisive for our rejection if the report under discussion is not - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating mr mario mantovani on his excellent report, which stresses the need to guarantee the right to quality protection against the risk of illness and dependence and the importance of adapting this right to the challenges of our time, in particular the ageing of the population. this phenomenon results from low birth rates and increased life expectancy and is more evident in women. in less than a decade, between 1990 and 1999, the population of women over 65 increased by nearly 3%. the effects of aging are felt on many levels. in portugal, for example, the higher female longevity in the working age population group has meant that since 1995 the number of elderly women has exceeded that of young people of the same sex. at the same time, the increase in the number of older people has increased the needs for health care and social services. the question we are asked is very simple and intuitive: there is no real progress for society when longer life expectancy does not correspond to a quality of life. the great challenge is therefore to achieve the satisfaction of a high standard of living for older people while controlling the costs involved. the public financing approach is therefore unavoidable, and in all member states it represents a major part of health expenditure. in the country where it is lowest, greece, it is still around 56% and in the united kingdom it is 84%. the increase in the number of elderly people will have a considerable budgetary impact, which in turn will lead to an increase in public expenditure. health care systems in the european union should therefore aim to be affordable, of quality and financially viable. each member state is responsible for organising and financing its own social protection system. however, this competence is increasingly exercised within a general framework which affects several community policies. as has already been pointed out, the barcelona european council therefore stressed the need to establish and develop closer cooperation between member states in the field of social protection, based on the exchange of good practice and information, research, the establishment of common indicators and standards, and the development of health and social services for the elderly. finally, i would like to stress that, within the framework of the european strategy and action programme on health, the greek presidency should consider this issue so that the next spring european council adopts the application of the open method of coordination and a precise and concrete timetable for cooperation between member states.

in writing. - (pt) the report makes both criticisms and praise of the human rights situation in portugal, criticisms and praise which we believe are both deserved and balanced. it would be unacceptable if these were not fully taken into account by the portuguese institutions on the pretext that the state's reason takes precedence over the rights of the citizen and that is why i voted in favour of the report. the explanatory statement of the report contains less rigorous information which, either because its content did not seem to me to be decisive or because it was not voted on or published, did not influence my vote. like local, regional or national institutions, the european institutions must be able to take a stand, criticize or praise the practices of institutions at a level other than their own. however, a report on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union which does not assess the legislation and practices of the european institutions is not a report on the european union but rather a report on the member states. that is why this report on the member states must be followed by another report, of a larger scale, which will assess the practices of the european institutions with regard to human rights.

in writing. - nothing like a good political conflict! from a democratic point of view, i congratulate mrs swiebel on her final success. but the tiny difference in votes which led to the rejection of my own alternative motion for a resolution in the plenary (by only 23 votes) and the majority - even smaller - by which this final motion was adopted (by only 5 votes) clearly show that we have been on the wrong track. it does not bode well for the construction of europe that we should be so deeply divided on a european subject so traditional, historical and consensual, and so close to radical clashes. in fact, anyone reading the resolution that was approved might well imagine that he was facing terrible persecution under one of the darkest dictatorships of the 20th century! the methodological drift of the rapporteur (and of the very small majority) has given rise, in terms of assessment, to exaggerations which completely ignore the fact that the european union is, in the whole world, one of the few privileged regions in the field of human rights and respect for and guarantee of these rights. in the end, we ignore the reality that everyone knows and we turn into ridiculous, giving in to a leftist and sectarian political agenda. this is not a good tribute, either for europe or for human rights. in conclusion, i welcome the initiative taken to present a proposal for a global alternative. since it is clear that the uen group has only 22 members, the 246 votes in plenary for my proposal give an idea of the relative success it has had as an instrument of political clarification and of affirming our difference.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate mr hubert pirker on the excellent report he has drawn up on the commission communication to the council and the european parliament entitled 'towards an integrated management of the external borders of the member states of the european union', which deserves my support, particularly as regards the relevance of the creation of a european border guard corps, which, without replacing the national authorities responsible for the management of their respective external borders, would allow for collaboration in order to guarantee the internal security of the union and the application of the principle of free movement. i would also like to stress my conviction that the effectiveness of border management will undoubtedly be enhanced by the adoption of common measures on external border management.
in writing. - (pt) illegal immigration networks, trafficking in human beings, organised crime and the fight against terrorism are undoubtedly topics which deserve general and priority attention and which, as defined in laeken, require cooperation mechanisms between the services currently responsible for external border control. however, in the context of the schengen acquis, we find that there are already structures with competence and powers to define 'common rules' and police cooperation procedures. however, the proposal under consideration goes further, it aims at nothing more than the creation of a european border guard corps with functions which are exclusively the responsibility of the national authorities, and we therefore disapprove of it. the effective action of this body would consist, among other things, in checking identity papers, questioning foreigners, and notifying the authorization or refusal of entry into the territory. clearly, the effectiveness of such a european police force raises questions. however, as stated in the commission's own communication, the creation of this body would above all raise sensitive constitutional issues in various member states. it is therefore essential to strengthen the effectiveness of national police forces with such powers and to ensure appropriate cooperation between them in order to respond satisfactorily to such situations.
in writing. - (pt) this report examines the commission communication on better management of external borders, which combines action by the member states with measures of a european character, which are essential in view of the threats posed by organised crime, terrorism and illegal immigration, and the imminent entry of new countries into the eu. in the light of the experience gained in the application of the schengen acquis, we believe it is appropriate to develop a common policy on the management of current and future external borders, integrating into this policy the best practices established by the member states. however, european border management remains a national competence and must be exercised at national level. i fully agree with the rapporteur on this point. in these circumstances, training and continuing training programmes for officials and managers, updating the design and installation of equipment and the development of an integrated risk analysis are absolutely essential. despite the rapporteur's controversial suggestion to create a european border guard corps composed of special units, which would be temporarily made available to national authorities on dangerous sections of the external borders, if necessary and at the request of the member states, i have a positive opinion of this report and have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report for the following reasons: firstly, because of the importance of the commission's communication, which, in its approach to better management of the external borders, combines the action of the member states with measures of a european character, which are really indispensable in view of the threats posed by organised crime, terrorism and illegal immigration, not to mention the imminent entry of new countries into the eu; secondly, because of the positive approach taken by the rapporteur, who stresses that the management of our borders remains a national competence and must be exercised at national level. this should not, however, prevent the development of a coordinated policy on the management of the current and future external borders in the light of the experience gained in the application of the schengen acquis, while integrating into this policy the best practices established by the member states. i therefore also support the proposal to adopt training programmes (including continuing training) for officials and managers at community level, or to develop an integrated risk analysis. i am also in favour of the creation of a european border guard corps composed of special units, which would be temporarily placed at the disposal of the national authorities on dangerous sections of the external borders, if necessary and at the request of the member states. i would also like to ask for special attention to be paid to the fact that portugal is one of the most important and sensitive external borders of the eu - in this case, a maritime border - which requires everyone's attention.
in writing. - (pt) this report is part of the action plan for financial services provided for in the lisbon strategy, which aims at the integration of financial markets and services by 2005 and greater liberalisation of capital movements, which we oppose. based on a recent commission communication on the regulation of clearing and settlement of securities transactions, i.e. the functioning of integrated securities markets, especially for crossborder transactions, and with the objective of liberalising capital movements and creating a single market for financial services, this report proposes to harmonise the rules, legislation and clearing and settlement mechanisms of the various member states, taking into account the profound national disparities in this field. hence the idea of creating a common european infrastructure and the proposals to follow the american example, inviting the commission to consider a similar architecture for the european union and also asking that, in the next revision of directive 93/22/eec on investment services, member states grant investment firms from other member states a right of access to national clearing and settlement systems, which we oppose.

in writing. - (pt) thanks to the policies of the member states, the eu has health systems that are quite exceptional in the world. but it is still essential to protect those who are particularly vulnerable or who face financial difficulties in the face of high treatment costs. it is in this perspective that the commission's proposals are strategic if accessibility, quality and financial sustainability of health care for older people is to be guaranteed. the fact that the organisation, financing and planning of health care systems are the responsibility of the member states does not prevent community coordination of policies on ageing, in particular as regards health. on the contrary, the sharing of experiences and solutions can contribute to the desirable social cohesion. i fully supported this report, which also incorporated some relevant contributions by the rapporteur for the opinion, mr mussa (uen group), particularly with regard to: the recognition of the fundamental role of health workers, the proposal for community funding of certain training projects and the issue of mistreatment of the elderly. finally, it is important to stress the need for a 'new attitude' towards the elderly, regarding them as an important new resource to be valued and not as a burden on society. the average life expectancy has almost doubled in the last fifty years. a new world was born. with better levels of protection, europe and its citizens will benefit from the vast wealth of knowledge, experience and knowledge that is the valuable capital of older people.

spain, france, italy, among others, including portugal, which, although atlantic, has important economic and neighbourly links with the mediterranean countries of the maghreb - and the multilateral dimension assumed by the european community, which can and should reinforce each other. we have no doubt, mr president, that the stability of the mediterranean region, and in particular of the middle east, depends to a large extent on appropriate partnerships for economic, political, social and cultural development, for which the union is especially suited. however, there are still other problems, which are absolutely unavoidable today, mainly those linked to security and the fight against terrorism, but also those linked to the fight against corruption and money laundering, and to the promotion of democracy and human rights, which, in the particular case of lebanon, are of particular concern to us. that is why we find the questions put by mr brok, chairman of the committee on external affairs, of the greatest relevance and for which we need concrete and consistent answers from both the council and the commission. we cannot ignore the fact that the political orientation of the lebanese authorities is still strongly dominated by syria and that damascus is a decisive factor in the lebanese government's position on the israeli-palestinian peace process, despite the withdrawal of the israeli army from southern lebanon in may 2000. the truth is that syria - unlike lebanon, whose regime is fortunately progressing towards democracy and the separation of powers, despite the obvious institutional fragility and intricate political-religious imbalances - is a dictatorship, particularly one with a monarchical bent, which has technically been at war with israel since the six-day war, with all the dangers this situation of tension poses to the middle east peace process, and, worse, it is a country which maintains a large military force in lebanon, of some 30,000 personnel, in addition to more than 300,000 immigrants who work mainly in agriculture and construction. if we add to this presence - or should we call it 'occupation' - so many other palestinian refugees, who are generally poor and poorly integrated into lebanese society, and who number no more than three and a half million, and the presence of the extremist movement, to put it another way, hezbollah, in the lebanese parliament, we can well understand the delicate lebanese situation in which the union must be vigilant and play a moderating role in peace, security and development. this euro-mediterranean commitment is all the more important at a time when the union is enlarging towards central and eastern europe and will concentrate the bulk of its financial resources there. we must not forget that europe is or should be polycentric: it is nordic, it is mediterranean, it is atlantic, it is also ultraperipheral and it is certainly also continental, but it is in the balance of its components and in respect for its diversity that europe becomes more democratic, more secure, more developed and, certainly, more respected internationally.

- mr president, this report expresses a positive position on aquaculture, which we support, considering it as complementary and not as a substitute for the fisheries sector, and placing it in the context of sustainable development and the precautionary principle, which implies, in particular, full attention to environmental issues and the refusal of the production of genetically modified fish. we support the rapporteur in her defence of the maintenance of fifg support and the participation of the main stakeholders, as well as the need to strengthen research and create an economic instrument to support possible crisis situations in the sector, such as a natural disaster. however, we would like to draw your attention to some particular aspects and special care that must be taken in this activity. aquaculture should not be compared with any other industry but with agriculture and livestock farming, since its implications are directly linked to the development of species and the natural environment, in particular coastal areas and alternative uses of space. on the other hand, the potential for intensification and verticalisation of production can create important risks to human and animal health, which must be controlled to prevent any 'mad cow' situation in fish. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. finally, i would like to say that our group supports both this report on european aquaculture by our colleague mr hugues martin, whom i commend, and the report by mrs rosa miguélez ramos on fisheries in international waters, which i also commend and which will be debated here today.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the wealthy romans of the early days of our era, between the first century bc and the first century ad, were already breeding certain species of fish and molluscs. but it was more of a costly fad then than an economic activity. sea fish farms were then highly prized for their beauty and for the prestige they represented. traces of at least 50 fish farms dating back to roman times have been identified along the mediterranean shore. then, especially in the 19th century, some countries developed oyster farming, which is considered a fine-tasting food - and rightly so. but it is only in the last decades of the 20th century that, faced with the risk of depletion of fisheries resources, which are subject to overexploitation, there has been an accelerated expansion of aquaculture. in fact, in 40 years the world's fish production has quadrupled to about 100 million tonnes today, and world demand is inexorably increasing with population growth. while it is true that aquaculture cannot replace fishing in the wild, it is nevertheless intended to supplement and reinforce certain highly prized and sought-after species which are now part of our daily fish menu and which fishing cannot provide in sufficient quantities. in the future, aquaculture will only be able to develop. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the fisheries sector is not left to the mercy of the market, and that the fisheries sector is not left to the mercy of the market, and that the fisheries sector is not left to the mercy of the market, and that the fisheries sector is not left to the mercy of the market. all this is dealt with in a comprehensive, rigorous and intelligent way in the report by mr hugues martin, which should become the reference book on aquaculture in the european union.

in writing. - (pt) the current importance of aquaculture in europe is evident in the 1.8 million tonnes of fish, shellfish and molluscs produced and the 57 000 jobs it provides. as the rapporteur proposes, to ensure the future of this sector, consideration should be given to aspects such as: the development and management of integrated environmental management programmes, both in maritime areas and in inland waters; the strengthening of food security, in order to ensure the health of stocks and guarantee the confidence of citizens; the strengthening of research, in order to find new solutions, both in technological, environmental and health terms; the appropriate financing of the sector, both for the modernisation of existing units and for new units. therefore, in the face of the obvious difficult situation in which many wild fish species find themselves, aquaculture is a complementary alternative to fishing and has a certain future. the crisis of confidence in aquaculture products must therefore be overcome by strengthening food safety measures and modernising production technologies. it is in this context that i support the martin report.

- madam president, commissioner, the purpose of this report is to monitor the implementation by the commission of the recommendations of the european parliament. this is a healthy exercise which gives our work more efficiency and credibility and for which i congratulate the commission and also our rapporteur. i would therefore like to review the main issues relating to the common agricultural policy which i have included in the discharge for the 2000 budget, recalling, as required by rule 9 (1) of our rules of procedure, my status as an olive grower. the high risk and even the practical impossibility of effectively controlling the operation of the export refund system was then our main concern. we note with satisfaction that in his first annual activity report the director-general for agriculture has confirmed our view by expressing his two main reservations to the budget on this mechanism: that the commission has reduced and simplified the system of refunds in the beef sector and that it has committed itself to a progressive reduction in the use of these mechanisms in the framework of the world trade organisation negotiations. we cannot, however, fail to deplore the maintenance of export refunds for sugar to european countries from which we import sugar freely, in an obvious invitation to repeat the same carousel fraud already detected in the butter sector. we note the commission's intention to invest in research and development of means of detecting olive oil counterfeiting, but we regret that we continue to spend absurdly high resources and impose enormous cost schemes on national and regional administrations, and also on olive growers, in controlling the number of olive trees, without any interest in preventing fraud, in complete contrast to the absence of means to prevent and combat the great fraud against the community budget, consumers and farmers, which is olive oil counterfeiting. the same or worse is true of wine, dairy products and livestock products in general. i still find it unacceptable that farmers who exceed their milk quota are pursued with very heavy fines and that nothing is done to punish dishonest industrialists and criminal networks who make dairy products without milk. finally, i must say that the commission's refusal to disclose the names of the companies to which it grants export refunds and other subsidies on the grounds that this would be contrary to the provisions on the protection of natural persons is totally unacceptable. it is a conception of citizens' rights that only works for multinationals and big interests and that does not exist for the defence of the consumer or even the farmer, who is often the victim of a hellish and crushing bureaucratic machine.
- madam president, i would first like to congratulate our colleague, mr jan mulder, on his excellent report and on the work he has done in the area of the clearance of accounts. i should also like to congratulate my colleague mr mccartin. we have indeed tried to work, although with different political views, in a direction which i believe is necessary to support a thoroughgoing reform of the common agricultural policy. in any case, it would be a serious mistake to regard the clearance of accounts as an activity whose success can be measured by the profits it generates. the need for member states to recover funds is more of a failure than a success indicator, and shows that agricultural subsidy systems are not working properly. this is often due to the extreme complexity and disproportionate bureaucratic burden that these systems place on both the administrations and the farmers themselves. secondly, we must take account of the fact that the clearance of accounts in situations where the member state takes the place of agri-food or agricultural undertakings constitutes an abusive form of state aid which distorts the rules of competition in a particularly unfair way, benefiting those who defraud public coffers and harming those who act honestly. thirdly, the forms, procedures and criteria for the clearance of accounts do not always seem to us to be the most balanced. in this last connection, we note, for example, that the commission, with regard to the mega-scandal of the butter counterfeited by the neapolitan camorra and marketed by several european satisfied. we consider this situation to be totally unacceptable and we hope that the commission will correct it as soon as possible.
- madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i give my general support to mr jan mulder's own-initiative report on the reform of the clearance of accounts which was approved by the committee on budgetary control. i also believe that it is too early to say whether the new system is valid, because the complexity it introduces and the limited capacity of the community's administrative institutions to respond prevent a definitive judgment from being made at this stage. it is remarkable, however, that the european parliament, which is a political body par excellence, is concerned on its own initiative and according to specific rules of assessment with the form and outcome of the allocation of common resources to the whole of europe. it is essential that the reform under consideration be developed, thus enabling the control bodies to be provided in good time with information enabling comparisons over many years. this is a responsibility of the commission to which the rapporteur, mr jan mulder, is calling - - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, one of the complaints most frequently raised by citizens is that of the reduced role of the european parliament in representative democracy. it is precisely in the area of the environment that people's dissatisfaction is most acute. we all know of cases where, in the face of a particular project or installation, citizens are forced to demonstrate their right to indignation in the streets or in the courts. the indignation is growing exponentially when many of these projects with unacceptable environmental impacts are financed under the common agricultural policy and the structural funds. it was therefore very important that, following the aarhus convention, the commission should legislate on public participation and public access to information. and i congratulate the commissioner for the environment on that. greater public participation not only gives more legitimacy to the decisions taken by our institutions, but also increases the quality of those decisions. this proposal for a directive on public participation in the drawing up of environmental plans and programmes is a good example of how citizens' participation in policy can be democratized. i congratulate our rapporteur on the work she has done in parliament and also in the conciliation committee. and i would like to highlight three main outcomes of this conciliation. firstly, the fact that ngos are fully involved in the debate on access to information in this process; secondly, the fact that all community legislation now has to provide explicitly for the conditions for public participation; and thirdly, the obligation for public participation in cases considered significant. finally, i welcome the announcement by the commissioner that legislation on access to justice for citizens will be in place as early as 2003.
- mr president, the world food situation is indeed dramatic and is tending to worsen. millions of humans live in extreme poverty, and many more die of hunger every hour. it is therefore imperative that rapid and far-reaching measures be taken to put an end to this situation, which cannot but weigh heavily on the conscience of mankind. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem. and it is equally necessary to accompany these background measures with urgent measures capable of saving lives now. the emergency humanitarian aid that has been developed so far is proving to be insufficient, both in terms of food and in terms of the supply of medicines. for example, there is a need for a more meaningful response to campaigns for at-risk areas such as the 'famine in africa' alert launched by the world food programme. it is also necessary to support timely initiatives such as those launched very recently by the new president of brazil, lula da silva, both the one aimed at eliminating hunger in his country, with the 'zero hunger' programme, and the other presented in davos and of a universalist nature, which calls for the creation of an international fund to combat poverty and hunger in the third world countries. but it is also essential, as i said earlier, to take measures of substance, first of all breaking with a model which has proved inadequate and unfair, which subordinates and mistreats the least developed countries - in writing. - (pt) i welcome the outcome of the conciliation procedure, which i consider very satisfactory. this proposal is of great importance not only for the average citizen but also for the community's environmental policy, by providing for public participation in the development of certain plans and programmes relating to the environment. at the same time, it aims at harmonising community legislation and thus represents a significant step towards the ratification of the aarhus convention by the european community. the authorities are therefore encouraged to inform the public of their decisions, the reasons and motives for them and the procedures for public participation and to support environmental education. this encourages the active participation of citizens in solving environmental problems. thus, free access, transparency and dissemination of information on the environment become a fundamental right of every citizen who is interested in the quality of his or her place of living and working. in addition, some recent disasters have made it clear that citizens are increasingly entitled to manage their risks, to demonstrate, to demand and to demand commitments to protect their interests in matters such as the environment and health.
in writing. - (pt) i welcome the results obtained in the conciliation procedure which concluded the preparation of the second of the three directives on environmental citizenship. i would like to reiterate the crucial importance of public control in environmental matters; i even think, as i said on 18 december last, during the discussion of another report by our colleague, that access to information and the right to participate in environmental matters must now be regarded as a normal prerogative of citizenship. i am in favour of genuine citizen control of our environmental heritage. it should be recalled that the purpose of this directive is to incorporate into the community system principles already contained in the convention adopted in aarhus on 25 june 1998 (during the ministerial conference 'environment for europe'). however, this directive focused on access to environmental information and called for greater public participation in decisions affecting the environment, with the rights defined by the stockholm declaration (1972) and by article 1 of the rio declaration (1992) thus having greater effects. finally, my vote in favour also aims to underline the guarantee, among other things, of public participation in the authorisation of plans and programmes relating to waste management, air pollution and the protection of water against nitrates, as well as projects which have a significant impact on the environment, such as new airport terminals or certain military projects.
in the case of the united kingdom, the commission has already taken the necessary steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. this directive is fundamental in the fight against air pollution because, by acting on the level of standardisation of engines and fuel quality, it strengthens the reduction of emissions and consumption of vehicles. it seems to me particularly important to establish, through the work of the european parliament, a link between this directive and the drafting of a new national and community taxation policy on fuels. it is crucial to internalize environmental costs into the economy. tax policy is one of the most effective instruments for achieving this objective.
in writing. - (pt) i very much share the rapporteur's concern for the environment and his commitment to the joint project. i therefore voted in favour of his report. i would, however, like to stress the need to ensure, not only in national but also in community terms, a geographical coverage which makes it possible to market fuels with a sulphur content of not more than 10 mg/kg (ppm). otherwise, the multiple disruptions and disadvantages will inevitably increase in the case of the most peripheral economies. finally, i would stress the importance of tax incentives as a means of promoting fuels containing less sulphur, which will certainly be an effective way of promoting their introduction.

in writing. - (pt) the three epidemics mentioned in the report affect the poorest populations most: for example, of the 40 million people infected with the aids virus, 90% live in a developing country and 70% of them in sub-saharan africa. the resurgence of new forms of tb - one billion people are at risk of contracting the virus by 2020 - and the return of malaria to areas where it had been eradicated (1 million deaths per year, 40% of the planet at risk) are destabilising entire societies and dealing a severe blow to the social and economic development of these countries. a specific initiative is therefore warranted in this area, one which defines the community's framework for action in order to maximise the impact of interventions and to provide it with an overall budget of eur 300 million over 4 years (2006). we agree with the general philosophy of the initiative, which is based on the medical and social need to combine prevention and care, and which must also consider increasing the tragically low r&d budget and strengthening health infrastructures and systems, and associating the field of reproductive health with the permanent concern of maximum complementarity. for all these reasons, i could only vote for the report.
in writing. - (pt) i supported the general lines of the report and the proposed amendments, given the urgency of a challenge that everyone agrees on: the fight against poverty-related diseases (hiv/aids, malaria and tuberculosis) in developing countries. but that does not mean that we cannot make some pointed remarks. on the one hand, as regards the coordination of these interventions with actions in the field of 'sexual and reproductive health', it is essential that any partnerships be established on the basis of a serious health approach and with bodies that do not aim to promote an ideological agenda. at the same time, in the face of the growing severity of the aids epidemic, it is important to keep an open mind, without ideological prejudice, and to look at the attention paid to the evolution of this epidemic, so as not to repeat the mistakes made and to identify, support and disseminate the most effective methodologies, even when they deviate from the mainstream - as seems to be the case in uganda. finally, european cooperation with un agencies, funds and programmes, or with ngos active within them, does not exempt - on the contrary, requires - close monitoring of the application of community funds and the rigor, seriousness and wisdom of the actions financed. this is necessary because of the frequent allegations of maladministration, which are particularly shocking in a field where human health and lives are at stake.

commitment that at least 50% of the agricultural and agri-food imports of the rich countries should come from the poorest countries. it is, moreover, a proposal consistent with what is already the current practice of the european union, which, as the commission states in a recent document, imports more agri-food products from these countries than the united states, japan, australia, canada and new zealand combined. that is why we have the moral authority to say that this wto round should be the development round. that is why we have proposed a food safety fund which will enable the poorest countries to implement measures to protect their markets from subsidized exports from the rich countries, thereby enabling them to develop their local production and combat hunger and poverty. but we should also be aware of one important aspect, because an excessive reduction in customs duties could jeopardise the preferential access to the european union market which some of the countries with which we have trade agreements already enjoy. the acp countries, for example, in the framework of the cotonou agreements, and the countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean. and we must be careful about that, because if we create an excessive tariff reduction and do not ensure that their preferences are consolidated in our market, those same poor countries may lose market to other richer but more competitive countries. but it is also because of our attitude of openness and support for the poorest countries that the european union also has the moral authority to say that we also have the right to defend our farmers and to preserve our model of society. our european negotiators will therefore only be able to accept a final agreement at the wto which first of all preserves the european agricultural model based on the contribution of agriculture to rural planning, the balance of the territory and the vitality of the rural areas which represent almost 80% of that same territory. this means, among other things, that the european union can continue to support its farmers and ensure a reasonable, only reasonable, level of community preference in agricultural production. secondly, there is a need to strike the right balance between greater trade liberalisation and greater demands on non-strictly commercial but strictly agri-food trade goods. as is the case, for example, with food quality and safety, with respect for basic environmental rules, or with respect for the trademarks and designations of origin and geographical indications of our products, which, as we know, are now being completely pirated by the most diverse countries in the world, without the rules of the wto being able to prevent this. if we do not, we are doing something that our society does not understand and we are attacking our own interests and, worse than that, we are not supporting the interests of the poorer countries. i think the european union has set an example of good proposals, reasonable proposals, for these countries which have been the most marginal players, the most marginal beneficiaries of the wto - the poor countries. we have had good and positive initiatives in the framework of everything but arms, our negotiating proposal consolidates these proposals and therefore i think we have to demand that other rich countries in the world, even more developed than us, follow the example of the european union.
- madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as i pointed out in my report on european citizenship, which we adopted in this house last september, the recognition of european citizenship has been a long process which still faces too many obstacles, and the necessary initiatives must be taken to implement the concept of european citizenship in its political, administrative, judicial, social and economic dimensions. i also recommend that, in order to deal with the obstacles which still hinder the exercise of freedom of movement and residence by community citizens, the proposal for a directive which we are discussing here today should be adopted as soon as possible. this proposal, by recasting existing texts, was intended to introduce the necessary simplifications by merging the treatment of the right of free movement and residence in the european area into a single legal instrument, and in particular to enshrine the right of permanent residence after four years of uninterrupted residence. it is a welcome proposal. the work of our rapporteur, mr santini, which was very well done, has helped to introduce into this proposal a number of contributions which i think are very positive. there are, however, two issues which have already been raised in this debate and which present difficulties. they have to do with the definition of family, a definition which is too broad and which seems to impose on national relations the recognition of the definition of the partner as a member of the family. i believe that common sense will require that national law and the rules of each member state be respected. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the right of residence is guaranteed to the family members of the deceased. i think, however, that the extension proposed by mr santini is acceptable on humanitarian grounds or serious health grounds.
