in writing. - (pt) although the issue of visas at the border must be exceptional, it is appropriate to provide for common procedures in the member states for the transit of seamen (an occupational category subject to very high mobility for work reasons). the aim of this initiative is to update, clarify and simplify the rules for issuing visas at the border to seamen in transit. the major legislative innovation is the possibility (subject to compliance with certain conditions) of issuing collective transit visas for seamen working on the same ship, travelling in groups of 5 to 50 persons, provided that their transit period is limited. these seamen do not necessarily have to be of the same nationality, because in practice, if that were the case, the effects of this proposal would be basically nil. it is also important to hold the shipping agent and the shipping company accountable for visa applications; the need for exchanges of information (concerning convictions, criminal records, suspicions of illegal immigration or trafficking) should be emphasised. this initiative, together with the amendments which have been introduced by the european parliament, can help to make the complex schengen acquis a little more comprehensible. it provides possible solutions in the absence of desirable solutions - namely the introduction of deeper reforms of the schengen acquis.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report for two main reasons. on the one hand, i recognise that the collection of scattered legislation in this area must be promoted, which is a prerequisite for making the schengen acquis intelligible and accessible. however, i see no problem whatsoever in the existence of differences between national laws on migration and i even think it is counterproductive to want to artificially standardise, beyond what is provided for in article 63 (3) (a) of the ec treaty. on the other hand, i also share the rapporteur's conviction that external border control is important in the fight against illegal immigration and crime. finally, i welcome the inclusion of the practices applicable to seafarers in transit in the common manual and i stress the importance of the collective visa, which would lose its enforceability if it were granted only to nationals of the same state, as the rapporteur has rightly pointed out. i regret, however, the 'politically correct' drift of the rapporteur who insists on adding terms relating to 'gender', when it would be sufficient to use elementary rules of interpretation and it is clear that there has never been any question of discrimination in the commission's text.
in writing. - (pt) it is positive to improve the situation of european union citizens who wish to settle in another eu country, in particular by reducing the bureaucracy that is still very much alive. the european commission's proposal for a directive makes it possible for a citizen of the european union to stay in another member state without any formalities for a period of six months, rather than three months as was the case until now. for stays of more than six months, if the union citizen is an active person, he simply has to declare this. if you are not an active person, you must declare that you have sufficient resources, without the amount of these resources being fixed, and that you have health insurance covering the first four years of your stay. the right of permanent residence after four years is the major innovation introduced by the directive. it consists in the fact that this right is recognized to the european citizen and to his family members. the report makes some positive improvements by broadening the concept of the family, by eliminating or simplifying certain bureaucracies, by guaranteeing more rights than originally envisaged. that is why we voted for this report.
in writing. - (pt) we were aware that the examination of this report was a difficult exercise from the outset, mainly because of the question of the categories of persons to be included in the definition of 'family member' - or the beneficiary, beyond the eu citizen, of the right to move and in particular to reside in the european union - but also because of the difficulties in defining the conditions that the eu citizen must meet in order to be able to benefit from this right. the truth is that the solutions adopted in these nuclear definitions, both by the committee on civil liberties and in plenary, all bear the stamp of the majority of the parliamentary left. indeed, as regards the definition of the term 'family', most of the solutions adopted do not correspond to the values i defend (in particular with regard to amendment 53): 'spouse', irrespective of sex, 'partner' and/or 'cohabitant', irrespective of sex, 'in a de facto union', 'with whom the applicant has a lasting relationship' and 'registered', in accordance with the relevant national legislation, 'partner' and/or 'cohabitant' from third countries or without a residence permit and, finally, direct descendants and ascendants of the spouse or registered partner or cohabitant. my position is not based on any kind of ideological or religious fundamentalism. i do not, and i do not have to, judge anyone's rights based on their sexual orientation or anything else. i see no reason for the eu to legally encourage family definitions which deviate not only from national legislation (and make it difficult to transpose it), but also from traditional values commonly accepted for a long time, which in addition encourage all kinds of abuses by those who want to settle and move illegally in the eu. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. - (pt) although the creation of a genuine european area of free movement and the effective definition of the right of residence of union citizens justify the promotion of a coherent and articulated policy, i voted against the report. i regret that the maximalism of the proposals voted for by the majority of the left in the committee distorts the report, moving it away from the much more balanced line of the rapporteur. the final text contains shortcomings: it does not juxtapose the rights and freedoms enshrined with the duties attached to them, by disregarding their actual value and their real existence; to pretend to impose a european identity while ignoring the real national identities; to establish an artificial equivalence of the family with other human relations, taking advantage of one theme in an opportunistic way to impose another; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. in addition to breaking down the internal doors of the union, this text would not allow the member states to know, internally, the phenomena of migration, a factor which will affect their internal social balance and their respective budgetary executions, particularly as regards social charges. the european parliament has therefore taken a line which is frankly excessive, far more than is necessary - which can only create more difficulties and new unnecessary obstacles to its adoption. as i have already said, the best is the enemy of the good.
in writing. - (pt) the ep was confronted today with the fact that five member states have spoken in favour of adding ecuador to the list of third countries whose nationals are subject to the visa requirement, basically because of illegal immigration, trafficking in human beings, regional coherence and public policy issues. according to reports, many ecuadorians enter europe legally under the pretext of tourism and stay there beyond the legal three months. the expulsion of ecuadorian nationals is becoming more frequent, mainly due to the lack of proof that they have sufficient means of subsistence and also due to their inability to present valid supporting documents concerning the purpose of their trip. there is also a geographical factor to be added. as the visa is currently required for nationals of other andean countries, the ecuadorian passport becomes more "interesting", which encourages forgery and counterfeiting. since the commission's proposal was drawn up in response to the priority given by the seville european council to combat illegal immigration, we voted in favour of it.
in writing. - (pt) by voting for this report, i want to record first of all a new manifestation of the recognition of east timor as a state governed by the rule of law. i understand the need to review the list of third countries subject to the visa requirement, in view of the urgent need to combat crime and illegal immigration, and i welcome the opportunity to reassess the impact of visa requirements, in particular with regard to current business, leisure and study travel. the commission has also received information from the member states on the implementation of the measures taken by ecuador in the framework of the eu-ecuador association agreement. the ecuadorian government's concern about the proposed legislative change is understandable, but the deterrent aspect, which experience has shown needs to be strengthened, cannot be overlooked. the human tragedy of uprooting, illegality and lack of livelihood is more likely to be avoided upstream with the application of this amendment, thus ending the particular attractiveness of the ecuadorian passport for forgers and falsifiers.

in writing. - (pt) the philosophy of the community's immigration policy is evident in the proposal for a directive under consideration: immigrants from third countries should continue to be admitted only to the extent and when they serve the economic interests of the european union. the conditions for entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purpose of gainful employment are so restrictive and demanding that there will be very few immigration applicants able to meet them. this is all the more unacceptable as it is accompanied by a community budget which reduces the amounts allocated to the developing countries. at monterrey, the eu did not go beyond a ridiculous compromise to spend only 0.39% of its gdp on development aid until 2006 - instead of the 0.7% that was set at international level a long time ago. it is unacceptable because the policies developed within the wto do not serve the poorest countries, so the gap between rich and poor countries has widened over the last ten years, producing 100 million additional poor people. it is a fact that the european union cannot accommodate all the poor of the world. but neither can it be its response to the problems of poverty in the world and to the racist and xenophobic rhetoric which has recently emerged in some member states, in total opposition to the humanist values which should guide it.
in writing. - (pt) i fully agree with the interpretation of article 63 (3) (a) of the ec treaty given by the committee on legal affairs and the internal market in the opinion accompanying this report. i consider that by proposing to harmonise all regulatory matters concerning immigration for employment, the commission goes far beyond the possible grammatical, logical, systematic and teleological interpretation of this standard, in clear disregard of the principle of subsidiarity. in the same way, both the commission proposal and this report seek to support the need for legislative harmonisation - justifying this interpretation which goes beyond the treaties, if not against them - on the basis of certain factors which have been mentioned but not proven. in fact, i do not think it is possible to verify the needs of the labour market in the european union; i think that the differences between national laws are quite acceptable and not prejudicial; i consider that any attempt at artificial standardisation in this area is counterproductive; i think it is dangerous to want to open up, lightly, both to external borders and to intra-community traffic, forgetting that insecurity is one of the issues that most concern the citizens of the union today. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. - (pt) the commission's proposals for agricultural negotiations in the wto, unanimously approved by the council, represent a further step towards significant liberalisation of agricultural trade, maintaining the current model based on export promotion and insisting on the idea that it is by liberalising trade that developing countries are helped, forgetting that this liberalisation increases food dependency and specialisation based on the export monoculture dominated by agro-food multinationals from developed countries. instead of new liberalisations, these proposals should take account of the injustices of the international trading system and defend the recognition of the right to food sovereignty and security, that is to say the right of all peoples to define their own agricultural and food policies, and the right of all countries to ban the trade in gmos. the proposal goes beyond the framework of agenda 2000, which already made excessive concessions to the detriment of small and medium-sized family farms. we therefore oppose any negotiations on agriculture within the framework of the wto which would give a new impetus to the concentration, intensification and verticalisation of production and, consequently, to the disappearance of thousands of small and mediumsized enterprises, particularly in portugal. we note that this proposal makes the mid-term review of the cap a condition from the outset, which shows the hypocrisy of certain delegations in the council.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate our colleague mr izquierdo collado on his excellent report on the commission's white paper entitled 'european transport policy for 2010: the time for choices'. i particularly support him when he insists that the growing liberalization of transport must be accompanied by guarantees, investment, mobility, subsidies, price support and the maintenance of service in island or peripheral regions. in this context, and given the importance of transport for the development of the outermost regions, i would like to stress that the european parliament should uphold the commitments made to the outermost regions in the treaty of amsterdam in this process, thus contributing to economic and social cohesion in europe. i would also like to stress that transport safety cannot be made conditional on profitability and that, as far as road transport safety is concerned, i fully support the commission's objective of reducing the number of deaths due to road accidents by 50% by 2010 (20 000 deaths). i look forward to the proposal of scientific measures at community level to achieve this objective.
in writing. - (pt) the growing attention to road safety represents an added value for portuguese interests. the approval of this report will help to solve many of the problems encountered on portuguese roads, and in particular on some roads in the algarve. i believe that the creation of a european road safety agency, as proposed in this report, is very important, in particular to 'accelerate road safety innovation' and 'provide free access to road safety data and information on best practice in the european union'. i also believe that the european transport fund, another of the measures proposed, is an important pillar of the proper development of road, rail, sea, port and airport infrastructure, in view of the creation of a european network of balanced and sustainable infrastructure. for all these reasons, i am inclined to vote in favour of this report. this report is a good starting point for my country, as it aims at new initiatives that increase the accessibility of peripheral regions.
in writing. - (pt) a realistic approach is inevitable in this area. on the one hand, in view of the distant horizon of 2010, the deadline set by the commission's white paper, and on the other hand, in view of the difficulties of practical implementation of a very wide range of measures with limited resources. it would be good to give transport policy the solvency and credibility it needs. as regards the specific transport of goods, i have long said that priority must be given to the restoration of rail transport, the boosting of short sea shipping and river navigation, to the detriment of the road, which is already extremely congested. many of the problems which are the subject of the rapporteur's concern, such as road safety, the prevention of bottlenecks, mobility and environmental protection, would be greatly reduced by determined action to redress this balance by favouring the modes of transport which are currently the most penalized. the internalisation of external costs, such as environmental costs, can also play an important role in this correction, by obviously penalizing more the more polluting and congested modes of transport, which are also the most likely to cause bottlenecks. that's why i voted for it.
in writing. - (pt) transport is a strategic sector which is essential and indispensable for sustainable development and for the economic and social cohesion of the whole union, because it goes beyond the economic and trade union interests of this sector and its quality has an influence on the whole community. we are definitely in favour of railways in transport in the union, we ask that priority be given to urgent changes in its conditions of expansion, quality and adaptation to the market. we are in favour of responsible liberalization of the management of european railways. we support the institutionalisation of a european transport fund.
in writing. - (pt) the possible delay in the implementation of third generation mobile communications networks and services is now a major risk factor for a sector which has been very weakened since the bursting of the speculative bubble in the usa, and which could affect the communication and information technology sector and, therefore, the economy in general, given the weight of the telecommunications sector and particularly mobile communications in some member states. this is largely due to the high expectations that have been created for the development of the sector and the huge sums collected by some member states through umts licence sales. now they are considering unilateral aid to 'rescue' this heavily indebted sector. beyond this risk factor, consideration should be given to the issues of equal access of citizens to third generation mobile communications, content-related issues, particularly at the level of public service provision, the competencies of further liberalisation of the sector and the effects of radiation from electromagnetic fields produced by mobile telephony. it is essential to further scientific studies in this field.
in writing. - (pt) i am pleased that the european parliament has taken up such an important plan as eeurope 2005, with a view to facilitating the promotion by the member states of their online capacities in the areas of administration (modernisation of public services with a view to ensuring accessibility for all), education (in particular the objective of ensuring broadband access to all educational establishments), health (provision of online health services for the population, broadband information networks between the different points of healthcare provision: hospitals, laboratories and homes) and 'business', without, of course, forgetting the issues related to the technical means necessary to achieve these objectives - the expansion of bandwidth and channels - as well as the delicate problem of information security. although this is a matter on which there is normally a consensus among members, i feel it is important to convey the positive spirit of my vote on this report.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report, and therefore i support the conclusions of the committee responsible on its content. i considered it my duty to give my unequivocal support to the promotion of the capabilities - especially at technical and logistical level - of the member states in relation to the achievement of the objective proclaimed by the european councils of lisbon and santa maria da feira and, subsequently, of barcelona and seville, to make the european union the most competitive society in the world, thus placing it at the forefront of the 'global information society'. this report should also be linked to the van velzen and khanbhai reports insofar as, as it states, it is crucial to promote the beginning of a new era of quality content. the member states will have a special say and a specific contribution to make in this area. to this extent, i believe that it is of the utmost strategic importance to establish priority frameworks for action to promote online capacity, as suggested in the report, particularly in public administration (modernization of public services to ensure accessibility for all), education (ensuring broadband access to all educational institutions) and health (provision of online health services to the population and broadband information networks between different points of healthcare delivery, whether hospitals, laboratories or homes).
in writing. - (pt) this resolution on the preparation of the spring 2003 summit, which stresses the urgency of restoring credibility and implementing the lisbon strategy in order to improve the economic and social model of the european union by 2010, deserves our support despite a political and economic framework for europe that is much less favourable than that which prevailed at the time of the lisbon european council in 2000. we must regain confidence in the lisbon strategy and implement its objectives. this requires a roadmap and the flexible transposition of legislative commitments into national legislation. in the employment and social affairs dimension, the decisive role of the social partners should be emphasised. in addition, member states must adopt measures to ensure greater integration of the most disadvantaged social groups in the labour market, investment in basic and continuing education and training as a vital factor for individual and collective progress, and the fight against undeclared work, poverty and social exclusion. improving the system of mutual recognition of diplomas is also essential to promote greater and better mobility. - mr president, as is well known, the portuguese prime minister signed the letter from the european prime ministers and heads of state, considering it essential to ensure the disarmament of iraq and the implementation of resolution 1441. it is an attitude which the portuguese members of the european people's party support unreservedly. and they support it unreservedly because it is a clear position based on the political tradition of the european democracies, based on the transatlantic alliance with american democracy and, let us also remember, with canadian democracy, australian democracy and the democracy of many other democratic countries in the world. and it is little wonder that today it deserves the support of the overwhelming majority of european countries, both those in the european union and those entering the next enlargement, and the other countries of the continent. however, the most recent events, which have led to a crisis in nato and a threat of vetoes in the security council by the countries of the union, put the unity of europe at serious risk. it turns out that no common foreign policy based on anti-americanism and complacency towards dictators who are dangerous to world peace, such as saddam hussein, is possible. it is therefore worth remembering what we must not forget: - firstly, europe has no strategic defence capability against the new forms of international terrorism, which are being carried out in conjunction with the states which support them; - secondly, the only strategic defence instrument in which european countries participate is nato. if it enters into crisis, it will be europe that will suffer most, more than the united states, in the face of its enemies, because europe cannot defend itself. a crisis in nato will make any common defence policy of the european union impossible; - thirdly, for the enlargement countries, with their recent experience of totalitarian regimes, security concerns are vital. provoking a crisis in nato will be deeply damaging to these countries and make them rely only on bilateral strategic alliances with the united states outside the framework of the european union and nato. and it would be very bad if these countries were threatened with the freedom to make political decisions when they disagree with some, and i insist, with some of the countries of the european union. and finally, the effect of a crisis in nato will isolate europeans, reinforce unilateral tendencies in the united states. if the united states and its allies, including most european countries, have to take military action to implement resolution 1441 without the explicit support of the european union and with nato blockaded, the damage to european alliances will be very difficult to repair. i call on the council and the commission to use the short time they have to prevent any action being taken to force iraq to comply with the resolution without the unity of the countries of europe.
- mr president, in the course of 2002 there was a great deal of debate and legislative work on the subjects covered by the area of freedom, security and justice. for obvious reasons, there was a need to set more ambitious targets on issues such as illegal immigration, border control, the european arrest warrant, asylum and police and judicial cooperation, among others. i do not want to deny that the dynamic of mr antonio vitorino, the commissioner responsible for this area, who i would like to congratulate, has also contributed positively to this development. but we must not forget that these are matters of enormous political sensitivity. we are here invading the traditional boundaries of state sovereignty, which cannot be ignored or underestimated. recent international events have reminded us that the european union is still made up of sovereign states. but it is also the rights and obligations of its citizens that are at stake here and that must be recognized and defined with a sense of responsibility, thus seeking to respond to the needs that the complex present situation imposes on everyone. mr president, in the short time i have, i shall concentrate on the new terrorist threats, which call for action at european level and solidarity at international level. in fact, the way we deal with terrorism today is nothing like the way it was dealt with in the '70s and '80s. we know that today the terrorist threat is not visible and is based on motivations other than political motivation. as a rule, it acts illegitimately, i repeat, illegitimately in the name of a civilization with the aim of bringing it into conflict with our own civilization. the current terrorism is known, it chooses its targets according to the visibility of the results of its action, which makes us all and our institutions possible targets. we also know that he is highly mobile and that he benefits, like all of us, from modern means of communication. we are not unaware that their sources of funding are diverse and often obtained under the cover of promoting respectable causes. and not least, we know that he certainly has access to weapons of mass destruction, especially chemical and biological weapons. in this context, we must find answers that naturally go beyond the national level and even the areas of intervention of justice and internal security, which naturally underlines the importance of our debate. it is clear that the emergence of these new terrorist threats requires action at european level. autonomous action at national level is no longer sufficient to ensure the protection of the population. but these concerns do not mean that we should simply extend the rule of the community initiative and the rule of qualified majority to cover the whole of this area. we believe that this development does not necessarily mean that all union procedures have to be produced or applied in the same way. i am sure that decisions on jha matters will be taken by simplifying the structure of the pillars, without this being a matter of unbalancing the necessary cooperation of governments and national authorities in partnership with the joint management developed by the european union.

- madam president, commissioner, i am of the opinion that, in relation to the global repercussions of drug addiction on public health, crime and insecurity, it is preferable, wherever possible, to develop european approaches. i therefore welcome this proposal for a recommendation and the excellent report by mrs minerva melpomeni malliori. our anti-drug policy has proven inglorious: the trafficking has found its oxygen in prohibitionism, proliferating and making ever greater profits, fuelling organized crime and petty crime, corrupting regimes and humiliating us for our impotence in dealing with it. the deterioration of the health of drug addicts is also a cause for concern, as are the health risks associated with hiv, tuberculosis, hepatitis b and hepatitis c, and the increasing number of deaths from overdoses and poisoning. in the face of this, we may not have absolute certainty about the way forward. but we can't help but change our path. although i believe that the debate in the united nations framework on the impact on public health and crime of the eventual decriminalisation of certain drugs should be pursued calmly, i do not think that this is the priority. the priority is, first of all, to design rational prevention policies based on scientific knowledge of each drug and not on emotionalism and radicalism which, by treating all drugs in the same way, end up discrediting preventive action. secondly, the priority is to develop a policy of risk reduction. i think it is important that for patients for whom drug-free treatments have not produced positive results, methadone replacement programmes should be continued. but it is also important that the experiments in administering heroin under medical supervision to patients with a long history of in the case of the forests, the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the forests are not used as a source of carbon. the un conventions on climate change consider that one of the policies that should be implemented in order to mitigate the effects of climate change is the promotion of forests as carbon sinks, through afforestation and reforestation activities. the kyoto protocol even sets the maximum amount of carbon sinks that can be used by states to meet their greenhouse gas emission reduction targets. in the meantime, given the fragility of the scientific basis for the forest's role as a carbon sink, this kyoto protocol modality was never welcomed by the european union and was eventually accepted as an indispensable concession for an agreement, in particular with japan and russia. now that this issue has been decided, especially after the marrakesh conference, the eu should use forest focus to develop the european strategy for the use of carbon sinks.

in writing. - (pt) drugs are one of the main concerns of european citizens. the fight against drugs requires a european dimension, which includes the adoption of legal instruments against the manufacture and trafficking of drugs, cooperation with producing countries and the promotion of the prevention and control of drug addiction. mr pirker's proposal responds to the growing production and trade of synthetic drugs. it is worrying that most of the synthetic drugs produced illegally come from europe (data from the swiss federal criminal service - 1999 - indicate that the netherlands accounts for 50% of world production). there is an urgent need for effective and rigorous control of the manufacture and marketing of these chemicals, which, although sometimes used legally/legitimately, are frequently diverted to the clandestine manufacture of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. this does not include the lawful trade in such substances, including the production of medicines. i support this proposal, which transforms the current directive into a regulation and simplifies the legislation by making it easier to apply - in a uniform and simultaneous way - (which is all the more important in the context of enlargement). the main objective is to control the trade in drug precursors in a harmonised way and to prevent diversion to the illicit production of narcotic drugs by strengthening cooperation between the competent authorities and economic operators (these must immediately notify the authorities of abnormal orders or transactions), which should be extended to substances not yet listed.
in the first place, the report is a report which is not only a report on the situation in the european union, but also a report on the situation in the world. as if this fact were not serious enough, reports from international bodies such as the international narcotics control board (incb) reveal that the production and trade of synthetic drugs continue to grow. in order to combat drugs effectively, it is therefore particularly important to control the precursors of drugs. but this control is not without obstacles and cannot be achieved by a simple ban on the use of these substances. the use of chemical precursors is not limited to illegal production, and this control will therefore require certain sacrifices on the part of producers of medicines, for example. in this respect, the report seems to strike a reasonable balance. finally, i think it is also essential to adopt measures against websites which market these substances and provide information on their manufacture.
in writing. - (pt) i voted for all four of mrs frassoni's reports, despite the difficulties involved. the use of comitology must be governed by greater transparency of the work of the various committees, with particular emphasis on the need to transmit to the ep the agendas and minutes of the respective meetings, as well as the list of those present, the draft implementing measures presented to the committees, the respective provisional timetables and the results of the votes. in addition, all committee documents should be publicly accessible (except for confidential documents, of course). i therefore agree with the assessment of the constitutional committee that the european parliament does not intend to usurp the commission's own implementing powers: it is a question of establishing a system enabling the commission to exercise its control properly and, if necessary, to challenge an implementing measure with which it does not agree when it is part of the codecision procedure. only in this way will the legislative procedure and the prerogatives of parliament as a co-legislator be fully respected.
in writing. - (pt) after the sinking of the prestige, concerns about maritime safety have been growing. i share these concerns because my country has a large coastline which depends heavily on marine resources. for this reason, and because these problems also affect other countries in the european union, the jarzembowski report on port services deserves our full consideration. as far as the regulations on piloting are concerned, i think it is right to exclude them from the decision. each member state, for reasons of public interest, must be able to maintain the current system, taking into account its local specificities. this report seeks to maintain a certain balance between liberalization of port services and a constant concern for social standards of worker protection, maritime safety and environmental protection in sensitive regions. this balance has already been achieved with the liberalization of air and rail transport. as far as social and labour legislation is concerned, the rights of eu port workers must be protected. i therefore support the rapporteur's view that greater protection should be provided for these workers, not to mention the need to maintain qualified staff in ports, by insisting on training measures for crews.
in writing. - (pt) we broadly agree with the commission's proposal for a directive on ports and maritime transport infrastructure, which aims to create or restore transparent conditions of competition for all ports in the union, in the specific context of the opening up of the market to the various port services. the services covered by this directive relating to towing, mooring, handling operations, including loading and unloading, stowage, transhipment and passenger services, do not give rise to any special remarks. the question arises whether or not to exclude piloting activities from the scope of activities covered by this directive. as i believe that piloting is a service which requires a great deal of experience and is very important for the safety of maritime traffic in ports, i agree with the majority vote in parliament, which i support.
in writing. - (pt) my vote is aimed above all at three points which i consider essential: first, self-handling must not be ably disrupted, opening the door to any kind of opportunism and market distortion, but must be properly limited to operation by the ship's own personnel in conjunction with the competent port operator; secondly, the rules governing the piloting of ships in ports must be kept outside the directive and reserved to national legislation. and thirdly, it is essential to pave the way for the actual definition of clear rules on state aid in this area, as was done in the green paper debates, on which the text of the directive unfortunately still appears extremely poor and empty. finally, if the directive is to result in significant economic changes to the port operating system, it seems to me also essential to provide for transitional arrangements which protect the interests of operators who have in the meantime assumed lasting obligations under national laws and whose economic equilibrium could be disturbed.
in writing. - (pt) the rapporteur recalls the low level of payments and admits the trend towards reducing the share of the eu budget in the community gni-tni. in such a situation, given the systematic increase in priorities and the policy of savings that is being pursued - which are inseparable from the stability pact and involve the systematic practice of cuts, freezes, advances, redeployments and reprogramming of budgetary expenditure - the negative consequences for the implementation of the traditional eu priorities are inevitable, particularly in the areas of social, cohesion and cooperation; the credibility of the budgetary procedure itself is undermined. in addition, there are problems of defining priorities, such as the one assigned to the 'lisbon strategy' or to immigration and asylum issues. the rapporteur even gives in to the need for a change in budgetary policy, particularly when he accepts the current framework of the financial perspective and even the existing limitations at the level of internal and external policies. the commission has also been very active in the fight against terrorism, and has been very active in the fight against terrorism in the past. and palestine is still not a priority...

- mr president, first of all i should like to congratulate mr mann on this report, which makes an excellent contribution to defining the future strategy for employment and social policy in the european union. five years after the launch of this strategy, it is the right time to review experience, identify weaknesses and seek realistic but bold responses to the emerging challenges common to current and future member states and to align them with the objectives of the lisbon strategy. it is indisputable that the employment strategy has contributed to the reduction of unemployment. but today we live in a different scenario, with a european economy in a period of stagnation. this situation requires special attention from the member states. it also requires focusing on clear issues, setting global priorities in the medium term and delivering results. one of them is active ageing as a response to the demographic challenge, without forgetting young people and the most disadvantaged groups. recent experience has shown that the greater the involvement of regional and local policies in national and european policies, the more the employment strategy has to gain. it is never too late to stress the important role of the social partners, civil society and non-governmental organisations in achieving the goal of full employment and better work for all. it is right to highlight in particular the role of small and mediumsized enterprises. in fact, they have been the european engine of job creation. measures to encourage the creation of new jobs and to make life easier for smes will therefore undoubtedly have a positive effect on the quantity and quality of jobs created. i would also like to emphasize and express my full support for the idea of cooperation between university centres, together with the actual practice of an interface between universities and enterprises. finally, a reference to the principle of equal opportunities: a lasting increase in the overall employment rate will only be possible if accompanied by an increase in the female employment rate, and this requires effective measures to improve the link between work and private life.
the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster is a very good one. the economic context of budgetary surveillance has proved to be much less favourable than initially anticipated, reflected in particular in the doubling of the euro area deficit between 2000 and 2001, the 'certainty' that this imbalance would be prolonged and worsened in 2002 and the explicit and real scrutiny of the serious budgetary difficulties experienced in 4 of the member states. the commission therefore drew up recommendations and expressed its intention to issue prior warnings of budgetary irregularities to potentially non-compliant states. this did not materialize, but it did anticipate the actual situation in these countries at the end of the year. the speech by president prodi to this parliament, in which he expressed his concern about the downward phase of the economic cycle but also criticised, without any doubt, the inflexible and dogmatic application of the stability and growth pact without regard to the change in circumstances, was therefore fully justified and consequently advocated the introduction of adjustments and more sophisticated criteria for the application of the pact. since then, many politicians, experts, research institutes, academics and public opinion leaders have spoken out on the subject. the commission itself has followed its president's prudent but bold interpretation by reworking a less rigid and more effective budgetary surveillance framework which is now emerging in conjunction with the principle that the implementation of the pact should make it an increasingly valuable instrument for promoting stability, growth and employment. the report endorses this view in that it considers it to be a step between the strict application of the pact and the necessary evolution towards an interpretative model, which is considered inevitable in the future, which takes into account more sophisticated criteria such as inflation, employment, public debt and its evolution, the financial burden resulting from the ageing of the population and investment needs. finally, the quality of public expenditure is essential to gauge the degree to which the jep is in line with the objectives of the lisbon strategy and the principle of sustainable development agreed in gothenburg. the political prevalence of budgetary constraints and the rigid interpretation of financial equilibrium in the framework of multilateral surveillance have led to a steady decline in the ratio of public investment to gdp in the european area in recent years, with private investment certainly following the same trend. all this coincides with the increased difficulties that the european economy is presenting. the solutions originally proposed or now being revived are not even unheard of in the framework of some developed oecd economies where the 'golden rule' is an essential element not only for consolidating public finances but also for launching and sustaining a process of economic and social development. after the enormous step taken in creating the single currency, the union now seems to be truly paralysed. the excessive restrictions on monetary and fiscal policies, designed to strengthen the european economy and its single currency and to allay the mistrust and fears of the strongest countries in the union, may turn into unexpected constraints which will make the desired recovery entirely dependent on the smooth functioning of the engine of the us economy. the flexibility and rationality advocated are not incompatible with the need to proceed in the true spirit of the stability and growth pact, nor does its public debate weaken the achievement of its objectives. the financial consolidation of the states which accept a common monetary policy and a single currency and reject any form of autarky which would inhibit open relations with the outside world is indispensable and must be pursued. many countries have, moreover, principles and rules enshrined in their constitutions which set more or less rigid limits to budget deficits. this is also essential in the union's policy framework, but such a commitment, to be effective, requires the priority consideration of the interest of the area as a whole (which is truly relevant), and the use of discretionary instruments for the recovery of the less developed regions (countries) may be accepted in exceptional circumstances. otherwise, there is a risk of seeing only the formal fulfilment of budgetary obligations, with the countries in difficulty resorting to the most varied and creative accounting schemes (which also makes their harmonization imperative) with the sole aim of satisfying the commission, as guardian of the treaties, or temporarily deceiving the financial markets by temporarily escaping their natural sanctions. unfortunately, this was the situation in many european economies at the end of 2002. it is therefore absolutely essential to take stock of the current problems of the european economy when assessing the degree to which the objectives set at the extraordinary summit in lisbon have been achieved. it is also necessary to signal to parliament, the council and the commission that a balance can be struck between sound financial consolidation in the countries of the union and the full achievement of these objectives.
- mr president, what surprises me most about this debate is that nothing has shaken the faith of some in the rigidity of the nominal convergence criteria. neither the sharp economic slowdown, the decline in private investment, nor the growing increase in unemployment and poverty are shaking their faith in the tenets of the stability pact, whose fiscal and monetary rigidity has not only contributed to the worsening of the current economic crisis but has also limited the potential for growth in the european union, with all its consequences in the ever-increasing levels of inequality, poverty and social exclusion. this is particularly serious for cohesion countries such as portugal, whose specific difficulties require a dynamic public sector and strong public investment to achieve a high level of real convergence, which is being prevented by the blind application of the irrational criteria of the stability pact. as we know, globalisation should impose greater flexibility in monetary and budgetary policies in the light of the specific needs of each country, and not the rigidity that now prevails, which ends up imposing flexibility in wages and the labour market, weakening monetary policies and subordinating social policies. i regret that the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy has not considered the proposal i made calling on the commission and the council to suspend the stability pact immediately and calling for a thorough review of the economic and monetary policy guidelines in the european union, in particular to take account of the issues of sustainable economic development, employment and the implementation of all social rights through universal and quality public services. the truth is that there is no economic rationale for setting a budget deficit threshold of equal size for countries with different levels of development, nor is there any economic justification for sacrificing everything in the name of zero deficit. it is therefore clear that the fundamental objective of the pact is political. we therefore also regret the proposals which have been put forward here, particularly by the commission.

in writing. - (pt) the report does not address the fundamental question of the demand problem within the european union and does not present any assessment of the economic and employment guidelines to deal with the current economic crisis and the increase in unemployment. the report blames "the rigidity of the european economy", which prevents it from "responding quickly to external shocks". the question is: how rigid are we talking about ? the report does not consider the existing monetary policy to be rigid, imposing the same interest rate and exchange rate requirements on countries with different needs and inflation rates, thus reducing the ability of regions to react to asymmetric shocks, all of which is aggravated by the community budget, which does not provide for redistribution and solidarity between member states. it does not consider the fiscal policy enshrined in the stability pact to be rigid, which conditions public investment, including the application of the structural funds, and calls into question public services and sectors essential for innovation and productivity, such as investment in education, health and research and development. the report stresses greater flexibility in wages and labour markets, which contributes to wage restraint and job insecurity. it called for greater flexibility in the product market, in particular by pursuing privatisation, liberalisation and deregulation of markets. we therefore voted against this report.

in writing. - (pt) eu enlargement will make decision-making more difficult within the ecb, not only because the number of voters on the governing council will be higher, but also because there will be less uniformity of views. it is therefore understandable that the ecb proposed an amendment to its statute to facilitate its decision-making. i think, however, that the proposed solution (i.e. a system of rotating voting rights according to the gdp of each member state) is unacceptable. firstly, because it would put an end to the principle of 'one vote per member' which is currently in force, and secondly because it would hinder the general public's understanding of the eu's monetary policy. i therefore believe that, as part of the necessary reform of the decision-making system within the ecb, a double majority system should be created in which: firstly, each member of the governing council would always have the right to vote and, secondly, proposals would be approved which receive a simple majority of the votes of the national governors, provided that this majority represents at least 62% of the population. the reform of the voting system within the ecb must, however, be completed by the next intergovernmental conference scheduled for 2004.

paiva castle speaks for itself. these decisions have led to a large number of redundancies, thousands of jobs are threatened by the imminent prospect of collective redundancies, the surplus of previous redundancies, with very serious repercussions on the regional economy, in addition to all the indirect effects of the breakdown of services and orders in subcontractor firms, mostly weak small and medium-sized enterprises created from the main project and dependent on it. so we cannot remain indifferent. we cannot ignore, or pretend to ignore, the fact that in many cases these enterprises, particularly in objective i regions, have benefited from community financial support and direct or indirect financial aid from the member states. nor can we ignore, or pretend to ignore, the fact that in most cases the companies which close down, relocate or intend to relocate do not suffer losses but are rather success stories with high productivity rates and recognised product quality, and that the decision to close down is therefore a socially cruel decision dictated solely by external economic reasons. we must take full responsibility for this, bearing in mind that the european union is the most important player in this field in the world and that it must ensure that there is internal discipline in the relocation of companies within the framework of the internal market itself. we therefore express our solidarity with the workers who have been directly or indirectly injured. we consider it unacceptable that a multinational company which has benefited from community financial support in the member state where it has decided to establish itself should be able to breach the obligations arising from that support. we call on the commission and the member states to urge community-scale undertakings to refrain from taking decisions which are harmful to employment without first having considered all possible alternative solutions. we ask the commission to find out what support, both at national and community level, the companies in question have already received and to disseminate it. we must all know what is happening in this area and public opinion must also be able to exercise its control and to impose its sanctions.

in writing. - (pt) i welcome and have supported this outcome of the conciliation process. i fully agree with the determination to improve the protection of health and safety of consumers by providing, as the new directive does, that substances classified as carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic to reproduction and preparations containing these substances are not placed on the market for use by the general public. as is well known, 'placing on the market' entails increased responsibility for ensuring that the product serves the purpose for which it is intended without endangering public health and safety (of persons and property). this designation generally gives the public the impression that certain products are "trustworthy". to do this, this trust will have to be built both through the forecasting and listing of these products or substances - a measure proposed by the commission, which i welcome (it should be borne in mind that the new eu chemicals strategy will involve, among other things, the registration of some 30 000 substances) - and through a preliminary risk assessment of each substance. the control, registration and handling of chemicals and products deserve a discipline that is clear, easily understandable and appropriate to the intended purpose of the use of such products.

- mr president, there is a certain latent conflict between the principle of competition and the principle of cooperation. the european union wants its university education to compete with that of the united states, not only in terms of excellence but also in terms of attracting students from third countries. the more it does so, the more it will reinforce the balance of an essential transatlantic alliance and of western civilization itself. it will also strengthen the foundations of democracy. as far as i know, the universities in the united states have policies for the collection and storage of grey matter which are more in their own interests than in those of the countries from which the grey matter comes. cooperation gives way to competition. the commission's views on this matter are somewhat more moderate, since it is said that it encourages cooperative approaches, that is, that it ends up drawing as a horizon the return to the country of origin of third country nationals who come to europe to graduate. but there are some other aspects which have given the united states a clear advantage, and it is certain that to solve the same problem in europe particular attention will have to be paid to them. among others, the language, the quality of education and the reputation of institutions and programmes, the variety of programmes offered, the recognition of diplomas awarded in the country of origin, legislation on residence, tuition costs and the availability of scholarships. the use of a single language, the high degree of competition between university institutions and the wide variety of their qualitative levels, the systematic concern with recruiting and retaining the 'grey' mass to which i have already referred, the very variation in the price of tuition fees and fees, which are generally quite high, characterize an education which attracts many more students from other countries than that of european universities. in europe, another problem arises immediately with the disproportionate number of students seeking university in the uk, france and germany compared to the other member states. about three quarters of these students seek to enter the universities of the three countries. to this we must add the question of the european linguistic mosaic - which at the level of higher education still has no satisfactory solution in general - with a view to a balanced distribution of the contingents of possible students. it is clear that language learning for university purposes is not limited to the acquisition of rudiments of the language of the host country. and with so many host country language courses being run before attending a higher education course, and so many concurrent courses being opened up by universities to their foreign students, it is obviously utopian to think that the trend currently benefiting the united kingdom, france and germany can be reversed in the short term. this relative scepticism, mr president, is no reason not to vote in favour of the excellent report by mrs marielle de sarnez, nor to applaud the excellent initiative of the commission. but it is a reason for trying to find a solution which is still far from satisfactory for the set of problems i have mentioned and also for calling for a suitable budgetary allocation for this set of problems.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i think we can be satisfied with the work we have done so far in this discharge for the 2001 budget, which has enjoyed a broad consensus in cocobu and has left out only those who, because of ideological prejudice against the european institutions, see this exercise more as a means of combating their strengthening than as an instrument for correcting their mistakes. we have before us a synthesis of problems and recommendations which constitute a real work programme which, although not perfect, i am sure will enable both the commission and ourselves to take significant steps towards improving budget implementation. so let me devote more attention to the work ahead of us than to the repetition of what has been left behind. the modernisation and correction of the community accounting system is our first priority. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very important one. following the measures already taken with regard to data security and data integrity, it is urgent to put an end to the disparate and contradictory accounting systems which, as acknowledged by the director-general for the budget in his last annual report, call into question the synchronisation and coherence of accounting data, and to replace them by a single, readable, reliable and transparent system which can be consulted, accessed, understood and used by all budgetary actors. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. then there is the deeper problem, which is more difficult to correct, namely the systematic under-implementation of the budget, which in 2001 exceeded eur 15 billion, a colossal sum which alone exceeds the total budget of several of the present member states. we would like to stress here that the logic of irresponsibility which often prevails in the community institutions in this area, which always places the blame on others, must end. the commission is responsible for proposing the regulatory framework within which budget implementation programmes are developed; the commission is responsible for making budgetary proposals both in annual terms and in terms of the financial perspective; it is therefore the commission's responsibility to ensure that budgetary programmes are feasible and realistic. if the legislative and budgetary authority wishes to put the commission in front of proposals which it considers unenforceable, the commission has only to assert its right of initiative and refuse to enact them into law. it is true that most community funds have co-decision powers with structures at national, regional or other levels. however, if there are implementation problems on the part of the managing partners, the commission should make them public in a transparent and timely manner, allowing appropriate corrective action to be taken. what is intolerable is that, in the face of profoundly mediocre budgetary executions involving almost all the non-community partners in the management of the programmes, the commission continues to pretend that it is not responsible and that there is nothing it has to do. in this area, we have paid particular attention to the structural aid programme for agriculture in the applicant countries (sapar programme). we are very grateful and look forward to the assurances given us by commissioner franz fischler that he will give the utmost priority to the implementation of this programme. we'll be watching for results. we also feel that we must make every effort to make our colleagues in the interparliamentary delegations aware of the need to speed up the implementation of this programme. finally, i would like to draw attention to the need for urgent action in the commission's relations with the undertakings with which it has contractual relations. it is deeply regrettable that the commission is not even able to keep track of the number of contracts with third parties through which it implements a very substantial part of its own budget and is therefore even less able to establish an appropriate mechanism for ex post control not only of the legality and regularity but also of the transparency and effectiveness of these contracts. it is symptomatic of eurostat, the body on which this parliament has focused its attention in the recent report by our colleague herbert bösch, that it has already been concluded that it is not possible to complete an audit of these contracts within the time limits in recent years, given that they total more than 2000. the so-called outsourcing, i.e. the development of community services by bodies outside the commission, is undoubtedly a policy which must not only be maintained but which must be developed in many cases. but this outsourcing needs more active, coherent and not merely formal supervision. the adoption of this report will thus be more than a point of arrival, it will be a point of departure. i hope that i can continue to count on the cooperation which i have enjoyed so far from the commission services, in particular the directorates-general for budget and agriculture, to whom i would like to publicly thank. i also count on the cooperation of the whole cocobu. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, drug use and trafficking is one of the most terrible scourges of our time. there are few - if any - people in europe who do not know someone in close contact, a relative, a neighbour, a friend, a colleague, a neighbour, an acquaintance, who has gone through the experience of drug use and addiction, with the inherent effects of personal and social dysfunction, human degradation, deteriorating health, impoverishment and, how often, crime and death. the fight against drugs therefore remains a key element of contemporary public policies; it is not time for any government, for any responsible state to slow down in this fight. the three un conventions which form the background to the resolution we are debating today and which we shall be voting on tomorrow are central to this. they represent the high point of a finding that no one can deny: the strategy to combat drugs will only be a 100 per cent success if it is pursued in a coherent and truly global international framework. the 1998 un general assembly action plan is another step in that direction and we are now halfway through the ten-year review period that was then set. the problem is so serious at international level that it is not the time to weaken this statement or any of its instruments. in recent years it has become fashionable in some quarters to say that prohibition policies, summed up in the term 'prohibitionism', have been met with continuing failures and that these failures are acknowledged by the authorities themselves. that's not true! and above all, the impulse for liberalization that this is intended to give rise to is not correct. first, identifying areas or levels of relative failure does not erase the successes achieved or the crucial importance of the adopted international framework of prohibitions as a global safety net; second, identifying areas of failure because we want to increase efficiency levels is not the same as propagating failures to inspire and fuel a surrender in the face of this global threat. and thirdly, therefore, detecting a possible failure is only useful if it is accompanied by a serious diagnosis of its causes, in order to further strengthen the determination in the next phase. it is not difficult to recognize that the main reason why we cannot yet claim 100% success in the fight against drugs, in the line defined by these three conventions, is that this fight is not yet really conducted in a truly international framework. there are still states which, either clearly or subtly, escape the discipline laid down. there are many who devote their energies more to finding loopholes and holes in the framework of the conventions or to creating new ones than to seeking their good application. this report, or rather its explanatory statement, is a good example of this. there are still states, even in the european union, such as the netherlands, which are trying out policies in a different direction, and it may even be asked whether this calls into question the common security framework in the schengen area. they remain territories outside the authority of states where criminal gangs are directly challenging international authority. there are still other territories and areas of activity of a very different nature, in relation to which many states adopt lukewarm attitudes, when they do not deliberately turn a blind eye to the illicit. it is these weaknesses that we must focus our attention on in the run-up to the vienna meeting on 16 and 17 april. and as an informed and responsible parliament, we must not send the union representatives at this meeting a single wrong signal, a single sign of weakness, a single sign of giving up. now, this resolution has got off to a bad start. it began with an initiative which challenges the conventions and framework of the united nations as a whole, although it then seeks to circumscribe its object. mrs buitenweg then tried to make an effort to highlight its content, but she did not erase the source of the misunderstanding of this initiative or its risks. then, in the committee discussions, there were efforts to bring views closer together and to limit areas of disagreement, but despite these efforts, the issue is so sensitive that i thought, on behalf of the uen group, that i should propose an alternative resolution which would give us absolute political security. that is the proposal i am asking the house to support. all ambiguity in this area promotes disaster.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in today's europe, in the world we live in, drugs are often associated with crime, aids, social exclusion and unemployment. drugs are indeed a problem that threatens the health, safety and quality of life of citizens and that is why the european parliament has been committed to finding an effective solution to the drug problem, which is a problem common to all countries and all social groups. the three conventions governing narcotic drugs have already been mentioned here: the 1961 convention on narcotic drugs, the 1971 convention on psychotropic substances and the 1988 vienna convention on illicit trafficking in these substances. these three conventions prohibit the production, trafficking, sale and consumption of a wide range of substances for purposes other than medical or scientific. the rapporteur, mrs kathalijne buitenweg, is basically proposing to amend the 1961 convention on narcotic drugs by reclassifying the substances listed. what the rapporteur wants - and she does not hide it - is to amend the list of prohibited substances so that cannabis can be removed from that list, which, whether she wants it or not, leads to the legalisation of its trade. it is commendable that the member states which have signed these conventions should meet on 16 and 17 april, as the commissioner has already mentioned, to assess the progress made and the difficulties encountered, and to discuss the need for amendments, a process in which new strategies for the fight against drugs or the strengthening of existing ones are always welcome. however, when this report proposes a reclassification of the substances listed, it is intended to give an impetus towards the liberalization of the consumption of certain drugs. and that i cannot accept. i do not believe that support for a drug liberalisation movement can or should be the solution to an effective fight against the growing drug problem. i think it is unacceptable that the idea that the european union is in favour of drug liberalisation should be conveyed in the face of the strategy that has been followed in almost all the member states. the existing conventions must be respected and the means of treatment and rehabilitation of drug addicts must be strengthened. the principle of subsidiarity must be respected, given that there are different drug policies in the various member states. i would like to end by recalling that last month we approved in this house a report by mr pirker on the problem of the growing production and trade of synthetic drugs, in which we approved an extension of the ban to substances not yet listed. no one in the europe we live in would understand that we would have a different approach today.

investment among the candidate countries and, moreover, its gross domestic product represents almost 13% of the total gdp of the 12 candidate countries. it is clear that this remarkable economic performance has undoubtedly weighed in hungary's favour in the course of the accession negotiations, especially if we take into account the speed with which this country has adapted to the mechanisms of a market economy after forty years of planning and that it has certainly borne the social cost that this process has entailed for the most vulnerable. this does not mean, however, that it was easy independence of the judiciary, reducing regional disparities and improving the quality of the environment, and strictly observing the rules governing public markets. we also stress the need to in writing. - (pt) despite the divergent views of the governments of the member states on the unjust, illegitimate and illegal pre-emptive war against iraq, the majority of members insist on strengthening the european union's military capabilities and on the creation of a common foreign, security and defence policy, with all the means at its disposal, which we reject, given that this would seriously undermine the sovereignty of each country and given the prospect of a europe based on the use of force. these members are also promoting closer cooperation with nato, the strengthening, as from 2004, of a military force that carries out autonomous actions and an armaments agency, all of which will be financed from the community budget, which we also reject. we therefore voted against the report. we are for peace and cooperation, not war. conflicts must be resolved through diplomacy, not through the use of force. the arms race not only involves the transfer to this area of resources essential for development and the fight against poverty and social exclusion, but can also lead to new wars and the destruction of humanity, which we reject.
in writing. - (pt) in adopting the subtle method of imposing european centralism, the rapporteur has chosen, although he denies it, to ignore the current historical situation, to ignore the divergent interests of the member states with regard to esdp and to depart excessively from the commitments voluntarily entered into, notably at the european council in helsinki in 1999. the existence of an eu that 'speaks with one voice, loud and clear' would today only be possible by imposing silence on the majority of member states, which would be unacceptable. moreover, in the present context, there is no real basis for pressing for the communityisation of the second pillar on the grounds that it is necessary to strengthen the credibility of the foreign policy objectives. the comparison made repeatedly with the united states of america, a sovereign state and a nation two hundred years old, betrays the option chosen by the rapporteur for the evolution of the eu, an option which i clearly do not subscribe to. the rebuilding of the european institutional architecture starting from the summit is not only a structural paradox but also a complete reversal of the model advocated by the founding fathers and raises fears about the solidity and coherence of what has been built up gradually. that is why i voted against it.
- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the socialist group clearly and unambiguously supports the motion for a resolution under discussion. the socialist group protests with indignation against the monstrous wave of repression that has fallen on those who dare to disagree, to disagree, to think differently and to create freely in cuba. this incredible wave of repression shows, to those who had doubts or illusions, the true nature of the cuban political regime. a totalitarian regime of the orwellian type, that is, imagined by george orwell in his masterpiece entitled "1984". after the liberation of the cuban song, symbolized by compay segundo, ibraim ferrer and his buena vista social club, we thought that the liberation of the poetic word had also begun with raúl rivero, the great poet sentenced to twenty years in prison. and the liberation of the political word with elizardo sanchez and oswaldo payá, here awarded the sakharov prize. but that's not what happened. we were wrong. the cuban dictator has arrested and brutally repressed intellectuals, journalists, political dissidents, members of the varela project, using the pretexts and the usual means of any ordinary dictatorship: spying on citizens, arbitrary arrests, judicial farces and absurd convictions. there are no good and bad dictatorships, mr president. all dictatorships are inherently evil. it is not worthwhile to rank them on a scale of evil and to give sympathy to the dictatorship of fidel castro. it makes no sense for the left to have a kind of pet dictatorship in fidel castro's dictatorship. and i, with this, am protesting! the cynical, brazen and shameless violation of fundamental freedoms and human rights is now a challenge and a provocation that fidel castro has thrown to all citizens and to democratic countries. we must join forces to isolate cuba politically. i do not mean economically isolating, because the economic blockade of the united states has been the best pretext for the cuban dictatorship. i mean isolate them morally and politically. the cuban socialist dissident elizardo sanchez, who spent eight years in fidel's prisons and heads the commission on human rights and national reconciliation, must be supported when he shows exemplary courage in declaring in an interview with a french newspaper and in connection with this wave of repressions that what is at stake in cuba - these are his words - 'is the totalitarian model', which has failed there as everywhere, citing it as an obscene model, adding that the cuban regime is in its terminal phase. times are hard for dictatorships, mr president. i hope that democracy will triumph in cuba and that this admirable people will regain freedom of assembly, association, demonstration, freedom of speech, freedom to travel outside their island. after all, the dreams that were at the origin of a revolution that i always supported, but which was betrayed and denied in its main ideals.
