(pt) mr president, commissioner, i would first like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr manders, on his work, and also mr papayannakis. the adoption of a directive on environmental liability is invaluable. it gives credibility to the environmental legislator, increases the protection of citizens and sends a clear signal to economic operators that pollution does not pay. i therefore welcomed the proposal for a directive with great hope, but i think that, although it is a positive step, it falls short of what is needed. the committee on legal affairs, on the other hand, in seeking to resolve some legal ambiguity, has further weakened the environmental objectives. so as regards the scope of the directive, first of all i accept that damage to biodiversity needs to be clarified, but the solution, in my view, is simply to exclude it from the directive. the loss of biodiversity in the european union is very real and the commitments of johannesburg and gothenburg have to be fulfilled. secondly, i believe that, in addition to damage to the ecological and chemical status of water, damage to its quantitative status should also be covered by the directive, as provided for in the water framework directive. thirdly, i think it is unacceptable that hydrocarbon pollution in maritime transport and radioactive pollution from nuclear power stations should be excluded from the scope of the directive. these activities are among the most damaging to the environment and the international instruments do not fully respond to the prevention and repair of the damage caused by these activities. finally, mr president, i believe that the directive should contain clearer provisions on compulsory insurance, especially for operators with more dangerous activities, so as to avoid that in the event of the insolvency of companies it is not the taxpayer who ends up paying for the damage.
(pt) mr president, commissioner, first of all i would like to congratulate mr sacconi on his excellent report, which is a very good one. although voluntary environmental agreements are welcome in theory, reality has shown that many of these agreements, precisely because they are voluntary, are not implemented and, on the other hand, have often served as a pretext for more ambitious legally binding initiatives not to enter into force. we all remember what happened with the emissions trading directive: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i therefore think it is very positive that the commission has taken the initiative to define clear rules for the recognition of voluntary agreements at community level. i think there are a few rules that must be followed: firstly, voluntary agreements are justified only as a complement to, and not as a basis for, environmental policy. secondly, they should be used only if they can be shown to offer advantages over conventional instruments; thirdly, they should be encouraged only in cases where some of them intend to go further than is provided for in conventional legislation. fourthly, they must be technology-oriented and based on benchmarking criteria: there is no point in voluntary agreements which do not promote the best technologies. finally, i think it is essential that there are deadlines, timetables, well-defined targets, as well as mechanisms for monitoring and implementing these results.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate the rapporteur on the good proposals he has made in his report, the correctness of which has already been confirmed by the support which they have received from the european parliament's delegation during the conciliation procedure. these proposals are aimed at a directive whose merits are also clear. the aim of the directive is to establish and govern a formal system for recording civil aviation events, so that all stakeholders can have access to and be informed about them. it is a matter for all the agents involved in this activity to learn from each other's mistakes, by optimising the educational and positive aspect of bad practices. this helps to establish a safer system for all users. this directive complements the 1994 directive which includes a set of measures on the investigation of civil aviation incidents, which is not likely to produce much result because of the fortunately small number of accidents. the reporting system on which this new proposal for a directive is based has greater potential in terms of the amount of data it can provide. it is also positive that the proposal for a directive provides for a system for member states to delete personal data in the event of a decision to set up a voluntary reporting system for data relevant to aviation safety. in writing. - (pt) in the context of the achievement of the lisbon strategy objectives - to strengthen employment, economic reform and social cohesion in a knowledge-based economy - and the open method of coordination in the field of social inclusion, it is essential to create a common framework for the systematic production of statistics. the aim is to enable a rigorous and timely comparison of the situation between member states as regards income distribution, poverty and social exclusion. this is a very important instrument that was missing. that is why i voted in favour of this recommendation, which accepts the common position adopted by the council on the approval of the european parliament and council directive. this framework provides for the use of common indicators, flexibility in data sources and the integration of new sources into national statistical systems, which will allow for adequate monitoring of the situation and changes in the member states. from 2004, member states will transmit their data annually to eurostat, which will organise methodological studies to assess the impact on the comparability of national data sources and to identify best practices.
in writing. - (pt) i share the rapporteur's view that the council's common position on statistics on income and living conditions in the eu was accepted without amendment, since it was decided not to draw up a report for the second reading. the unanimity achieved in the committee on employment and social affairs also confirms that the council's common position is adequate. if the objective is to produce an annual synthesis report containing community statistics, it is essential that the compilation of data concerning the member states use harmonised definitions and methods. otherwise, there is a risk that a study using heterogeneous variables, which vary from one member state to another, will be obtained and therefore make comparison difficult. the financial contribution from the eu to each member state over four years for the costs of their respective work will make it possible to carry out in 2007 the first edition of a late initiative, further highlighted by the trivial issues constantly dealt with by the eu.
in writing. - (pt) i support this report which deals with a draft regulation which is an integral part of the 'action plan on the statistical requirements of emu'. in order to promote the objectives of the european employment strategy properly, it is important to harmonise the employment data of the national accounts by transmitting these data in the unit "hours worked", in order to clarify labour relations, make the measures consistent and the objectives viable. the european commission's initiative: the future of the european employment strategy "a strategy for full employment and better quality jobs for all" (com (2003) 6 final), has essentially defined three major objectives: full employment, quality and productivity of work, a labour market that promotes integration. the lisbon and stockholm targets for the overall employment rate (67% in 2005 and 70% in 2010, on average in the eu), the employment rate for women (57% and 60% respectively) and the employment rate for older workers (50% in 2010) can only be achieved if both the concrete nature of the employment relationships and the quantitative indicators, in particular the 'number of hours worked', are determined using uniform methodologies.
in writing. - (pt) this report is part of the process of creating an internal energy market in the eu, in accordance with the call of the lisbon european council of 23 and 24 march 2000, reaffirmed at the barcelona and brussels spring councils, for the acceleration of the process of liberalising the electricity and gas markets, which implies greater market deregulation and the intensification of crossborder trade between member states. the report also aims to accelerate the privatisation of public enterprises, given their historical dominant position in the sector, and the process of mergers and concentrations at community level. i have always opposed this process, not only for reasons of socio-economic order, quality and guarantee of the supply of the public service, but also because it is a strategic sector for development, which affects independence, sovereignty and energy security. the commission's proposal aims to adapt the vat rules for gas and electricity to the needs of liberalised markets. the proposed amendments would in fact return the taxes levied to the member states where final consumption takes place, thus facilitating cross-border energy trade. the ultimate objective therefore remains to meet the needs of the european single market in the energy sector.
in writing. - (pt) the situation in the shipbuilding industry is becoming increasingly worrying, as global demand for shipyards fell sharply in 2002. new orders are 60% down on 2000, but in the european union the decline is 77% and this is to be added to the price reduction. one of the main causes of this decline was the eu's unilateral application of the principles set out in the 1994 oecd agreement, which aimed to end aid to the shipbuilding industry. the current temporary defence mechanism has proved insufficient in the face of unfair competition and dumping by south korean shipyards supported by state aid and benefiting from negative margins ranging from 20% to 40%. the eu's share of the shipbuilding market has fallen from 19% in 2000 to only 10% in the first half of 2002, leading to the closure of several european yards, unemployment and the persistent threat of further cuts, as i saw during a visit to the viana do castelo shipyards. it is therefore essential that the eu proposes new mechanisms to preserve and develop the strategic shipbuilding sector through a genuine community programme promoting research and vocational training and taking into account the priorities of modernising the community fleets, ship repair, maritime transport and fisheries.
in writing. - (pt) the european strategy for sustainable development adopted at the gothenburg summit must be combined with corporate social responsibility (csr). companies have obligations beyond the legitimate objective of maximising profits. today, smes and large multinationals must be aware that their success depends on responsible behaviour, both in terms of the environment and respect for fundamental rights and the promotion of social cohesion. it is a recognised fact that social and environmental responsibility enhances competitiveness. thus, corporate social responsibility should be supported and encouraged; the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new guidelines for the european social fund. i would like to stress the importance of:- including gender issues among the principles of csr, including the promotion of women's entrepreneurship and reconciliation of work and private life;- the role of the csr plurilateral forum, which will allow all partners to be heard and help define the limits and challenges facing businesses and share good practices;- the european ecolabel as a quality guarantee for consumers and businesses, as consumers increasingly value csr in their purchasing decisions. the ep should be involved in this process, in particular at the final meeting of the forum and in the exchange of information between the institutions.
in writing. - (pt) this report is nothing but a huge make-up and marketing operation of the employers, at european level, both by the voluntary intentions of the whole process and by the economic and social orientations of the eu, which aim to promote the deregulation of the economy, especially in the labour market, with wage flexibility and job insecurity. in the portuguese case, we could even speak of corporate social irresponsibility, as multinationals close down and relocate their operations to countries with lower wages and more flexible social and environmental standards, putting thousands of workers out of work, jeopardising the development of less favoured regions, breaking contracts with local authorities and states that have provided them with significant public aid and tax benefits. the reality is that many of these companies, which want to promote themselves internationally, have no sense of social responsibility. they benefit from precarious work, fixed-term contracts, late pay and precarious working conditions, with a high proportion of fatal accidents at work. they arbitrarily and illegally lay off workers, impose flexible working hours, encourage child labour and show irresponsibility in the field of pollution. this climate of impunity and non-compliance with the legislation in force must be brought to an end as a matter of urgency.
in writing. - (pt) the resolution on the intelligent energy - europe programme (2003-2006) deserves our support in general because this programme:- seeks to ensure continuity through an energy programme, following on from the current framework programme (1998-2002) in this field, and addressing sustainable development, security of energy supply, energy efficiency, electricity produced from renewable energy sources, among other aspects;- advocates an increase in its budgetary allocations, even if this increase is clearly insufficient (from eur 190 to 200 million), given the strategic importance of the areas covered: energy efficiency and rational use of energy; new and renewable energies; international energy transport aspects, in particular; advocates appropriate control in the development of countries;;- advocates the need to ensure a balance between the full implementation of the programme and the budgetary appropriations; it also proposes to facilitate access for potential candidates. as for the question of the creation of the european agency for intelligent energy, we believe that it is essentially political and concerns the merits of effective policies for research and promotion of energy that have environmental and economic benefits.
in writing. - (pt) i agree with the report in general, although i think that one of the solutions indicated by the rapporteur to increase energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy sources (the creation of a european agency for intelligent energy) still needs to be demonstrated. the creation of an additional bureaucratic body does not in itself guarantee the optimisation of resources. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the possibility of improving the exchange of information between member states and of adopting good practices should rather be considered, without distorting national legal systems or creating artificial structures which conflict with these systems. despite this divergence of views on methodology, i share the rapporteur's concerns about the environment and efficiency, and the conviction that without the involvement of local and national organisations the measures advocated will not be properly implemented. i also think that the special interest and attention paid by the rapporteur to the candidate countries and the adaptations needed when they join the union is very clear.
in writing. - (pt) i largely share the rapporteur's concerns about the need to promote the rational use and supply of energy and the strategic preference for clean forms of energy. in fact, beyond the lower co2 emissions it promotes, the decentralised nature of cogeneration normally prevents the construction of large power generating units, by reducing the environmental effects of their infrastructure and transmission lines. the discussion of this question has made it clear that it is not a fundamentally political matter, but a highly technical one. it did not lead to the expected division between right and left, but rather amplified the different approaches to the problem by the north and south of europe, given their climatic differences. this will have to be taken into account, as will the possibility for member states to submit detailed reports on their national potentials. although it still seems that some technical terms and definitions concerning the use of cogeneration are contradictory, i believe that the principles which guided the preparation of this report are correct overall. i agree with the compromise approach which results from the work done in committee. that's why i voted for it.
in writing. - (pt) i agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary to adopt a regulation on insurance requirements for air carriers and aircraft operators, thus ensuring better protection for users of this mode of transport and extending this protection to all users. i also share the rapporteur's concern about the application of the principle of equality and i welcome the solution he proposes - differential treatment between small and large operators - without which, in practice, these measures could slide this specific market into an oligopoly due to the excessive weight of insurance requirements. despite this agreement in principle, which leads me to vote in favour of this report, i do not hide my doubts as to the possibility of implementing some of the measures which are advocated, for example the verification of the validity of operating licences or air operator certificates, which would require a permanent check on compliance with the requirements laid down.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report, which seems to me to be balanced and to offer a higher level of environmental protection. i particularly welcome the concerns expressed about the 'applicability' of the mechanisms envisaged. since the maastricht treaty, the union has committed itself to ensuring that all its policies protect the environment. for real environmental protection and biodiversity protection, it is essential that economic agents cooperate, since, as the report says, today 'the sources of environmental pollution no longer come mainly from industrial equipment, but reside in multiple economic activities and consumer behaviour', requiring a new, more creative approach to achieve the ambitious and vital goals of better environmental protection. the european commission has been able to move in this direction with its proposal, as has the rapporteur with his suggestions. self-regulation mechanisms between operators and co-regulation, in a kind of consultation with the public authorities, are of course ways to be explored. on the other hand, setting concrete objectives and targets and promoting a simpler and more operational legislative framework, readily understandable by all the actors involved, would certainly lead to greater awareness and more effective protection of the environment.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, in portugal, and more specifically in the algarve region which i represent here, pleasure boats and jet skis are a daily and unavoidable reality given the abundance of bathing areas and their tourist activity. in order to update its directive 94/25/ec (16.06.1994), the european commission decided to keep abreast of technological developments in engines and the latest environmental protection requirements. the original initiative of the european commission to make vessels more compatible with the environmental standards in force is to be commended, in particular:- the emissions of exhaust gases and particles that degrade the quality of bathing water;- as well as engine noise, which harm both the environment and the well-being of the population and holidaymakers. i have therefore followed with particular attention the work which has resulted in the report we are now discussing. i take this opportunity to congratulate mr callanan on the quality of his report, on which i had the opportunity to express my opinion at the second reading of the european parliament in september 2002. i welcome the final results of the conciliation process, in which the european parliament has been able to impose its positions, such as the application of the three decibel sound emission limit to all types of engines. however, i would add that i support the existence of a derogation for boats used for racing and for commercial passenger transport, which are important for the development of tourism, the main activity in my region. as regards competition, i will only mention, as an example, the annual holding in the algarve of one of the races of the formula 1 motorcycling world championship, which attracts thousands of national and foreign tourists to this region.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, about a year ago the european parliament adopted a resolution on the future of tourism in europe, which i was rapporteur for on behalf of the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism, and in which it was expressly proposed that the tourism sector should have a solid legal basis in the future european constitution, so as to enable the commission to intervene effectively in the face of the various problems that arise. as one of the most important sectors of activity in europe, the world's leading tourist region, and one of the sectors with the greatest future in terms of job creation and wealth creation, it is hard to understand the lack of political recognition and means of intervention in the current treaties. in the face of a manufacturing industry which is increasingly moving out of europe, tourism is emerging as a non-relocatable, labour-intensive multi-service activity on which europe can rely today and which it may continue to rely in the future. but should this activity, which is by definition cross-border, be outside the scope of the european institutions? can europe renounce its involvement in one of the most promising sectors for its future development? can the european union be left unable to cope with and respond to the needs of the industries involved in this activity, because there is no legal basis to enable it to intervene effectively? that is the situation we are facing at the moment. in fact, the new constitution presented by the praesidium does not even mention tourism. nor is it proposed that what had been achieved in the existing treaties, which is considered insufficient, should be maintained. we in the european parliament maintain our position that tourism should be expressly referred to as a sector of shared competence between the european union and the member states, as expressly stated in the first part of the constitution and in the policy part of the future european constitution. and we ask: what is the commission doing to achieve this? i would therefore ask the commission what its proposals are for strengthening the legal basis for tourism in the future european constitution.

in writing. - (pt) i support this report because it finally creates the legal instrument that the cooperative sector has been waiting for for too long. i share the wish that the creation of the statute of the european cooperative society should respect the acquired rights of workers and the protection of workers, whether in the original constitution of the sce or in the course of structural changes introduced in an existing sce. the sce must also ensure that workers are informed and consulted, and that they are permanently represented and involved in the management of the sce. the opinions of the workers' representatives must therefore be taken into account in decision-making. finally, i would like to stress: (a) the legislative role of the member states in regulating the status of employees' representatives in the sce and the importance of the principle of protection identical to that accorded to employees' representatives at national level; (b) initiatives on corporate social responsibility which must be encouraged by the workers' representatives when they participate in the management of the sce; (c) gender balance. it is necessary to ensure that the procedures for the appointment, selection or election of workers' representatives promote gender balance.
in writing. - (pt) with the proposal for a directive dealt with in this report, the commission is trying to complete the statute of the european cooperative society with regard to worker participation. apart from the legal and institutional issues involved in this process, the main content of the conciliation of worker participation and rights within the european cooperative society is to be assessed. the rapporteur generally accepts the commission's proposals and only introduces a limited number of new elements, in particular with regard to gender balance, corporate social responsibility and the protection of workers' representatives, which must be at the same level as that granted to workers' representatives at national level. the rapporteur also proposes that the clause allowing member states to withdraw from the worker participation system should a european cooperative society be formed by the merger of two cooperatives be abolished, which would clearly jeopardise workers' rights and should therefore be abolished.
in writing. - (pt) i am voting against the report because i consider that the content directly related to worker participation in european cooperative societies (ecs) goes beyond the scope of article 137. by amending the legal basis, the rapporteur has tried to promote the conferral of new powers on parliament, which do not seem to be in line with the letter and spirit of the treaties. i believe that paragraph 3 of that article - and paragraph 1 (e) of that article, which runs counter to the recommendation of the economic and monetary committee - does not constitute a sufficient and necessary legal basis for establishing the desired participation of workers in the life of these cooperative societies. the use of article 308 is therefore fully justified. furthermore, i consider that the possibility of renegotiating the worker participation regime in the event of significant restructuring following the creation of an sce is potentially incompatible with the abovementioned article. i fear for the soundness and viability of the latter.
in writing. - (pt) while i acknowledge the merits of the delegation to the conciliation committee and the quality of mr callanan's work, i do not think that a sufficiently ambitious result has been achieved in terms of noise pollution, air pollution and the promotion of the quality of water intended for human consumption. i therefore disagree with the derogation for steam boats, the 3 db tolerance for all types of engines and the limit values applied to gaseous emissions in specific inland waters.
in writing. - (pt) the purpose of this regulation is to establish a european legal status for cooperative societies to enable them to operate across national borders in the eu's single market. sharing the same objectives as the statute of the european company (regulation no 2157/2001), this statute of the european cooperative company aims at the adaptation of production structures at community level, thus enabling enterprises of all types to promote the reorganisation of their activities at community level, in other words to accelerate the process of centralisation and concentration of capital of large multinational enterprises - a process which will enable them to overcome the 'obstacles' posed by national legislation to mergers of companies from different member states. as far as companies are concerned, we reject this objective of creating a 'european capital', apart from the socio-economic consequences of such restructuring and mergers, especially for a peripheral country like portugal. as regards cooperatives, which have their own specificities in terms of participation by their members and redistribution of profits, our abstention is due to doubts about the legislative process as a whole and about the aim and content of this initiative by the commission, although parliament has tabled certain amendments to the commission's proposal.
in writing. - the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the permissible sound power level of towed vehicles (com (90) 0173 - c4-0413/90); i dispute the interpretation that the high number of references to national legislation does not undermine the innovative character of the sce. in fact, on a purely hermeneutical level, the concept that a legal framework must be watertight to local specificities to merit this qualification seems to me reductive and i argue rather that it only enriches the organisation and allows a real adaptation of it to concrete cases and realities. the argument of 'completion of the internal market' used to justify the use of article 95 is not better founded since it applies to almost all legislation. politically, it is obvious that the rapporteur and the committees which have delivered opinions are trying to promote the granting of more and broader powers to parliament, on the pretext that this claim is not based on legally valid opinions. i sincerely regret that this is being used as a weapon and as a motive for further institutional conflict. wisdom dictates that before demanding more power, one should make good use of the one one already has.
in writing. - (pt) we believe that policies to protect the environment and natural resources are essential to sustainable development. priority will have to be given to policies and measures focused on prevention, for example by finding ways of researching and supporting access to the best available technologies, with particular attention to the problems and specificities of small and medium-sized enterprises. however, there is a need to strengthen responsibility for repairing environmental damage. i would mention in particular the recent example of the prestige. in this sense, it is important, as part of a wider set of measures and actions, to ensure that heavy industry (in particular heavy industry) accepts its responsibilities for the protection of the environment and natural resources, through correct, fair and effective measures that combat impunity and prevent public finances from bearing the costs and repairing environmental damage due to negligence or to commercial strategies, almost always private, aimed at maximising profit. the current ep resolution improves the commission's proposal (based on its 1983 green paper) on environmental liability for the prevention and repair of environmental damage by challenging the positions of heavy industry (see unice opinion) which characterised the commission's proposal.
in writing. - (pt) the commission proposal under consideration is very important because it aims to create a comprehensive community system for preventing and repairing environmental damage, including water pollution, damage to biodiversity and soil pollution which pose significant risks to human health. after many years of debate and repeated ecological disasters, we have reached the decisive moment for effective prevention and repair of environmental damage, in terms of a real 'separation of waters'. i supported the approach taken by the commission that the concrete institutional and procedural arrangements for achieving the prescribed results should be largely left to the discretion of the member states, in accordance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. in the commission's proposal, however, i consider that the assessment of issues such as the scope of the definition of biodiversity (limited to the natura 2000 network), the compulsory financial insurance/guarantee system (for operators referred to in annex 1 to the proposal), the adoption of an exemption system, the removal of objective liability in favour of the introduction of mitigating circumstances and the exclusion of damage resulting from certain activities is too vague. i therefore disagreed with certain aspects but i feel it is my duty to contribute to the adoption of this directive which, on the whole, is going in the right direction and is a milestone of undeniable importance.

mr president, commissioners, members of the european parliament, you may be surprised to read the first recitals of this report, but in the end it merely states that everyone agrees with the evidence: the dire situation in which the european economy finds itself, namely slow growth, loss of confidence between investors and consumers and rising unemployment, to which i would add the unsustainable levels of income inequality, poverty and social exclusion. it is true that this situation calls for a new approach to the formulation of economic policy decisions in order to achieve the objectives of high growth, full employment, sustainable development and greater social cohesion. but unfortunately, in the face of the evidence, the answer is always the same: to accelerate the process of liberalization and structural reforms, as called for in the lisbon strategy, which is so applauded by the representatives of the employers' organizations, to moderate wages, to bet on labour flexibility and the precariousness of work. let us be clear: the rapporteur's amendments accept and reinforce the guidelines proposed by the commission. the rapporteur himself acknowledges that these guidelines are a repetition of the previous recommendations, but the new approach is just 'more of the same', with even greater intensity when it was essential to make progress. it was necessary to propose a global change in the liberal drift of the economic and social guidelines of the european union. just as we need to question the causes of this situation. and the answer to that question lies in the policies that have been followed up to now. it is enough to look at the present situation to see that it is not by making the labour market more precarious, by reducing workers' rights and by reducing wages that we can help to increase productivity, to combat poverty or to respond to the slowdown in internal and external demand. the interconnection between the economies of the member states and the reduction in purchasing power is well known, as is the need to invest in education, training of people and research and technology to boost productivity growth. this requires, as has been said here on several occasions, that we do the opposite of what the stupid rules of the stability pact imply, which are forcing a reduction in public investment, pushing for the discharge of the state from responsibility in the areas of health and education, and even making it difficult for the structural funds to be used properly in the countries with the weakest economies. just as economic and social cohesion requires a higher community budget, not the lowest proposal in recent years, which the commission has just put forward for 2004, with less than 1% of the community's gross national income. the same is true of the public service and its quality, as the recent struggles of workers across europe have shown. the most striking thing about this report, which closely follows the commission's recommendations in this year's economic guidelines, is therefore its defence of the insistence on increasingly neoliberal measures, despite the serious consequences they are causing. the aim is clear when it considers that wage increases should remain moderate in order to allow profit margins to be restored. the centre of their policies is always profit and not people. that's why he makes the insistent defense of flexible, mobile and cheap labor, without rights, to be used where and how the employers want. it is the precariousness of work in exchange for employment, it is the total devaluation of those who work. i repeat: this cannot be the way. the european union must be a project for the people and not just for the profit of a few, and we must have more respect for those who work. the dignity of workers is an essential step towards increasing the productivity of work.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this new debate on the broad economic policy guidelines is taking place in parallel with the presentation of the employment guidelines and at a time when the priorities defined by the commission for the internal market strategy are known. these initiatives and the instruments and options supporting them are thus expected to be well-connected, as they are geared towards economic recovery and growth, full employment and improved quality of work, social cohesion and inclusion, and increasing the competitiveness of member states' economies and the union's overall economy. the rapporteur's ambition - which contrasts with the timidity of the commission's proposal - is therefore to be supported when he calls for the general guidelines to give priority to structural reforms and when he argues that the commission and the member states should commit themselves to a strictly timed action plan by the year 2010. this joint discussion coincidentally takes place a few days after the ecofin council was informed of the impossibility for france and germany to formally meet the deficit criterion. it is significant that, in the face of new data, the commission has simply noted the fact, not feeling the need to make more stringent recommendations for strong economies such as france and germany. if this is a sign that the time has come for the european institutions to look more at the real conditions of the union's economic development than at the uncritical and sometimes irrational adherence to criteria of questionable scientific value, all is well. discipline and financial rigor are obviously indispensable, but the refusal to use the deficit generated by good investment and accompanied by the containment of lower-quality spending as an instrument of countercyclical policy is utter nonsense. the economic stagnation in europe is severe, deep and protracted and its overcoming requires an active stabilization policy which is not incompatible with long-term fiscal balance. the rapporteur's comments on the stability and growth pact are therefore appropriate. public deficits should be assessed with flexibility, taking into account the level of each state's overall debt, public investment needs and the requirements of ageing populations. the creation of a budgetary reserve fed during periods of growth and used during periods of recession will be a good measure, not least because some of the present difficulties stem from the commission's excessive tolerance of the expenditure of some states in a period of positive economic performance. finally, it would be useful if the report could make a recommendation to introduce a mitigated golden rule in the assessment of excessive deficits. the commission would be responsible for identifying the investments and public expenditure needed for the lisbon strategy in order to bring coherence and harmony to all policies, instruments and objectives resulting from recent economic policy initiatives.
in writing. - (pt) the european central bank (ecb), the symbol of the monetary orthodoxy that characterises europe, is one of the least democratic institutions, not only because its policies escape democratic control, but also because it is the only community institution where not all the member states are represented at the level of the executive board. the recent changes to the decision-making process, by introducing a rotation system, have removed the permanent voting rights of the members of the central bank's board of governors, further excluding certain countries, such as portugal, from the monetary policy decision-making process, which we contest. we therefore hoped that the replacement of a member of the executive board, in this case mrs gertrude tumpel-gugerell, an austrian, would help to change the current situation. however, if we analyse the new member's answers to the parliamentary questionnaire, we find his unconditional support for the monetary and budgetary orthodoxy currently in force. for example, it considers that the main contribution it can make to the economy is the implementation of the stability pact and insists that the ecb focus on price stability. which means nothing's gonna change.
in writing. - (pt) we are increasingly concerned about money laundering, which is the source of funding for international crime and terrorism. we know that there are crossborder movements of cash, because there are no controls to monitor these movements across the community border. the money laundering directive provides for supervision of transactions by financial institutions with a value of eur 15 000 or more, but does not mention cash flows. this directive should be supplemented by other measures, for example by introducing controls on the flow of cash across the community's external border, by creating uniform rules, by closing gaps and by trying to balance the requirements of these controls with the requirements relating to the protection of the internal market and the free movement of capital. it is imperative to establish a community approach which respects, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the freedom of member states to choose the procedure. the definition of the objectives and the rules to be followed is a community matter, but the manner of implementation must be left to the discretion of each member state.
in writing. - (pt) the absence of control mechanisms on the free movement of capital, the creation of instruments to circumvent prudential rules and the presence of large sums of money in tax havens contribute to the weakening of the financial system and facilitate the laundering of money derived from crime, including drug, arms and human trafficking, thus highlighting the role of organised crime in contemporary capitalism. the world bank estimated in 1995 that money laundering was worth between 300 and 500 billion dollars, not including estimates of tax evasion. more recently, the imf has been putting forward a value of between 2% and 5% of world gdp, or between $600 and $1.5 trillion. it is therefore clear that the fight against money laundering requires a political will to control and tax effectively the movement of capital at international level. this proposal, although limited, is a step in the right direction in that it encourages the harmonisation of customs procedures to not only supervise cross-border transactions by financial institutions but also to control cash flows above eur 15 000. so she's taking our membership.
in writing. - (pt) from an agricultural point of view, 2001 was marked by the rapid spread and scale of the foot-and-mouth disease epidemic in the eu, particularly in the united kingdom. we remember the burning of wood and the slaughter of animals, which, in addition to their environmental, economic and public health consequences, have caused widespread social disruption in the countries affected. two points stand out clearly: health policy cannot be determined by commercial issues and a control strategy which only provides for the preventive slaughter of sick animals, without taking account of new scientific advances, is ethically unacceptable. this epidemic, combined with the other food and health crises that have ravaged the eu (bse, dioxins, sewage sludge, nitrofurans, etc.), shows the failure of the current model of agricultural development and the consequences of an export-based cap on falling prices and opening markets. the transport of live animals, the closure of local slaughterhouses, the absence of border controls and the elimination of local production are just some of the current problems. hence our overall support, which highlights our budgetary proposal to create an agricultural disaster fund, which the rapporteur partially recognises as justified when he proposes the creation of a community fund for animal diseases.

mr president, social and employment policies suffer the consequences of economic policies. that is why it made no sense to have a debate on the economic guidelines separately, as is unfortunately happening, despite all the efforts made by the rapporteur to prevent that from happening. the commission's spring forecasts foresee gdp growth in 2003 to be no more than 1% in the euro area, with negative consequences for employment, which will fall by 0.1%, and imply a worsening of unemployment, which will reach an average of 8.8%. this should be a wake-up call for changes in community and monetary policies, in particular a review of the stability pact to give full priority to public investment and other measures to promote employment and social inclusion. but instead, the same solutions are insisted on, making it difficult to achieve credible employment strategies and social inclusion objectives. so, while i have the greatest doubts about the achievement of the objectives and targets proposed in this report, given the known positions of the council, the commission and most of the governments of the member states on the possibility of changing the economic guidelines and any revision of the stability pact to give priority to growth in quality and entitled employment and social inclusion, i stress the positive, albeit insufficient, proposals aimed at improving the employment strategy. i also stress the insistence on the member states to set quantifiable national targets to be included in the first national employment plan they draw up in accordance with the new guidelines, the need for debate in national parliaments and the need to contribute to achieving better results, not only in terms of job creation but also in terms of reducing unemployment, equal opportunities and social inclusion. however, the current reality required much more. the accelerated growth of unemployment resulting from the liberalization and privatization of key public sectors, from the restructuring and relocation of multinationals, from the growing difficulties and lack of support for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, from the insistence on the predominance of monetary policies and restrictive policies that curtail public investment and prevent the growth of the purchasing power of workers, pensioners and pensioners, from the increase in the retirement age, which penalizes workers and does not free up the creation of jobs for young people, must be stopped. but neither the majority in this parliament nor the council accept such proposals. on the contrary! in general, they insist on policies which aggravate the present situation, as we saw in the previous session during the debate on economic policy guidelines and as we see again here when we want to go a little further, as our rapporteur, mr herman schmid, has tried to do. it is of course good to advocate improvements in working conditions, but it is not enough to propose an overall reduction of only 15% in the rate of occupational accidents and 25% in high-risk sectors in all member states by 2010, especially for a country like portugal, which has the highest rate of occupational accidents mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the employment policies of the member states must focus on clear priorities in the light of the current economic context, the requirements of an enlarged european union and a better implementation of the lisbon strategy. lifelong learning, the work of older people and the fight against undeclared work are priorities which should be highlighted, as the rapporteur rightly points out. while stressing the importance of consensus priorities, this report takes a less appropriate approach to some aspects, namely: first, the stability pact: the implementation of the employment strategy is the responsibility of the member states, which must ensure that adequate financial resources are allocated, respecting the need for sound public finances in line with the broad economic policy guidelines and the stability pact. the stability pact is an essential instrument to ensure the sound management of the public finances of the member states and to ensure sustainable growth and the smooth functioning of economic and monetary union. reference to the pact and its implementation is therefore essential in the context of the european employment strategy. secondly, immigration as a response to the overall strategy of job creation must be rigorously framed. the recruitment of immigrant workers must be done with discretion. it is necessary to verify that the conditions laid down by the applicable rules on entry, residence and employment are fulfilled in order to avoid disorderly immigration. illegal immigration into member states is subject to extremely disparate national regulations and has been increasing in recent years, reinforced by trafficking in human beings and the activities of smugglers. it should be left to each member state to define the skills profile and the number of workers it intends to recruit on the basis of the needs of its labour market, demographic trends and its capacity for integration. the fight against undeclared work must also be strengthened, reducing labour costs and making job creation less costly. thirdly, the setting of targets, such as reducing unemployment or increasing the participation of women in the labour market, must be demanding but achievable, and account must be taken of the different starting points of the various member states. these targets should be considered in terms of progress to be made and not in terms of levels to be achieved. otherwise we risk making them unacceptable and putting them into practice in the national employment plans. finally, i would like to congratulate commissioner antónio vitorino, who has very well expressed the need for a balance between security and flexibility as essential factors for competitiveness and productivity in europe.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the agreements we have discussed today are important and positive, as has been pointed out by both the commissioner and mr hernández mollar, who has done an excellent job on behalf of the committee on civil liberties in this area. it is the first time, as has been pointed out, that extradition and judicial cooperation agreements have been concluded between the european union and a third country. and it is good that cooperation between the united states and the european union is being strengthened to enable a more effective fight against crossborder crime and the proper protection of our democratic societies, our common values and our citizens. i am one of those who criticise the secrecy surrounding the negotiations and the fact that the council, excluding this parliament, has tried to classify the text of the agreements as confidential. it is impossible to understand this attitude when it is a matter which will directly affect the fundamental rights of our citizens. fortunately, the council has backed down on this absurd and unacceptable classification. we are dealing with two agreements with which we are in general agreement, but there are aspects which it is essential to secure. firstly, the treatment to be given to the united states, which can never be identical to that reserved to the member states of the european union in the framework of the european arrest warrant, since they are not subject to community law or even to the convention on human rights or even to the european rules on data protection; secondly, the primacy of an application for the execution of the european arrest warrant or an application to appear before the international criminal court over any application for extradition to the united states; in writing. - (pt) i agree with the rapporteur's position, which, while agreeing with the substance of the proposal, advocates its rejection on the basis of the legal basis. the draft directive does not, in fact, aim to establish substantive conditions for removal, but only concerns the mutual recognition of decisions on removal already adopted. in other words, it does not specifically cover community expulsion decisions based on a standard adopted under article 63 of the ec treaty, but expulsion decisions adopted on the basis of national law. it is therefore a directive dealing with the applicability of a decision and not a directive laying down substantive law in the field of removal. the court of first instance held that the national court had not been entitled to rely on the principle of mutual recognition of decisions adopted on the basis of national law.

the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, my voice is not helpful but i will try to be clear. the commission presented its legislative proposals for further reform of the cap last january. apart from major adjustments in some sectors, the main innovations in the proposals are the so-called dissociation and modelling of direct aid paid to producers. the aim of the dissociation is to convert the present aid into a single aid per holding, which would be dissociated from these productions and their quantities. from then on, farmers would always receive this amount, regardless of what they cultivated in the future and could even not cultivate anything as long as they kept the land in good agronomic condition. by modulation, the commission intends to apply a rate of reduction of aid, which would reach 19% in 2012; about two thirds of the money thus released would finance future reforms and about a third would be set aside for strengthening the second pillar of the cap - rural development. only farmers receiving less than eur 5 000 a year would be exempted from this reduction in aid. the proposal now before the house was adopted by a large majority in the committee on agriculture and rural development on the basis of a compromise proposal submitted by the rapporteur and negotiated with all the political groups. the essence of this commitment, which is intended to become the european parliament's position, is as follows: first, support only a partial and gradual dissociation of direct aid but limited to the arable crops and male cattle sector. as a consequence, all other premiums would continue to be awarded on the basis of the current model; secondly, support for a much more limited modelling of only 6% in less-favoured regions and 8% in non-less-favoured regions, with the revenue thus generated to be used mainly to strengthen the second pillar. farmers earning less than eur 7 500 would also be exempt from the application of modelling. with this position the european parliament is trying to send some political messages. the first is that it unequivocally supports a reform of the cap which introduces greater economic rationality, which facilitates its application in an enlarged european union and which helps to unblock the negotiations in the world trade organisation. the second message is that such a change must be made with prudence and realism. in fact, our position is that the total dissociation of aid as proposed by the commission, which seems an interesting model in theory, in practice presents considerable risks and ignores the reality of european agriculture, the great instability of markets, which always require management and protection instruments at the border, and the enormous heterogeneity of european agriculture with enormous differences in yield and competitiveness and, consequently, with profoundly different impacts in the application of a dissociated system of payments. the third political message is that the risks of production abandonment following the introduction of a decoupled system of aid are particularly serious in the most peripheral and disadvantaged regions with lower productivity and therefore less competitive. parliament therefore proposes a lower rate of modulation in these regions, that no separate system be applied in the outermost regions and that the special situation of all these weaker regions be taken into account in order to continue to provide their farmers with alternative production methods. fourthly, parliament also wants to say that it is not justified at this time to decide on such a high rate of reduction of aid to finance future cap reforms. this is because the cost and timing of these reforms are not known. fifthly, parliament's commitment to supporting the strengthening of the second pillar of the cap, particularly by financing new actions in the field of food quality and safety, should also be emphasized. finally, it is also worth recalling that it is proposed that, from 2007, the future system of unbundled aid will no longer be based on the historical criterion but will be based on two major criteria: the area and the employment of each holding. finally, the european parliament is thus contributing to the adaptation of the cap to new needs and emerging realities, but it is doing so in such a way as to avoid or minimise the risks of abandonment of production, increased unemployment and the creation of other serious imbalances in certain agricultural systems, particularly in the most disadvantaged and peripheral regions. it is therefore hoped that the council of agriculture ministers, which has the final say, will share parliament's concerns and force the commission to amend its proposal during the negotiations under way. (applause) i would like to thank
mr president, the commission's proposals do not serve the interests of agriculture and could have serious consequences for family farming and small and mediumsized farmers if some of their essential assumptions are not revised in the meantime. instead of correcting the present imbalances in the distribution of aid between countries, production and producers and paying particular attention to the specific features of countries such as portugal, it is mainly aimed at securing the freezing of the community budget in the context of the enlargement process and taking another step towards liberalizing the agricultural sector worldwide, taking into account the forthcoming world trade organisation negotiations. one of its basic principles is to establish aid on the basis of historical references of recent years and to assume its dissociation from production, which, from the outset, benefits the largest producers and the most advanced agricultural countries and condemns the most backward, small and family farming to their present situation. in addition to accelerating the process of concentration of production and land, it will make permanent the current inequalities in the distribution of aid, in which portugal is greatly handicapped, encourage productive absenteeism and speculation on the agricultural land market, promote unfair competition between productions with and without entitlement to aid and create new conditions for entry into the sector, particularly for young farmers. we cannot accept that a policy of support for production should be replaced by a policy of social 'help'. we want another reform of the cap and we regret that this mid-term review has not been used to do so. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not undermined by the excessive deficit. among the most worrying is the report by mr arlindo cunha, which comes dangerously close to the proposal by commissioner franz fischler. in fact, not only does it not make any real modulation proposals, it accepts the disconnection of production aid from certain arable crops and cattle payments. what was important was guaranteed by protecting the internal market, that consumer safety and food sovereignty were promoted taking into account portuguese conditions and specificities. we will continue to fight for these goals.

mr president, commissioner, i would first like to congratulate mr alexander de roo on his excellent report and on his ability to engage with the shadow rapporteurs. i should like to begin by saying that, according to the data of the european environment agency, if we are to reduce our carbon dioxide emissions, it is essential that we invest in maritime transport. but this commitment to maritime transport to solve the problem of climate change cannot be made at the expense of acidification by sulphur dioxide emissions. it seems to me therefore unacceptable that the efforts that have been made on land to reduce sulphur dioxide emissions have not been followed up at sea and i therefore welcome the excellent initiative of the commission, although i think it should be more ambitious. firstly, with lower maximum sulphur limits, so i fully support the 0.5% limit; secondly, by extending the zones for reducing sulphur dioxide emissions to areas other than those covered by the marpol convention, and for this it is essential that the commission should push for the extension of the reduction of these emissions to the mediterranean, the north-west atlantic and the black sea in the marpol convention; and thirdly, i think it is important that what we are doing on climate change to reduce the economic costs of complying with the kyoto protocol can also be applied to the acidification problem. if we are going to reduce the cost of complying with the kyoto protocol in europe by eur 1 300 million, then a similar sulphur dioxide emissions trading system should also be applied to enable us to reduce the cost of meeting these targets.
mr president, this proposal for a regulation on the management of atlantic waters has suffered a major setback with the presentation, at the last fisheries council, of a compromise proposal by the current eu presidency which, in the name of non-discrimination between member states and invoking the end of the transitional period for the full integration of portugal and spain into the common fisheries policy, seeks to eliminate the division between their fishing zones, making it difficult to take measures to control fishing effort and calling into question the guarantee of the sustainability of resources in portuguese waters. this proposal would mean the liberalisation of access to the zone between 12 and 200 miles of the exclusive economic zone for spanish vessels, with the creation of a large fishing zone without borders, which, given the size of the spanish fleet, would not only have devastating effects on fisheries resources, with serious consequences for portuguese fishermen, but would also make the resource conservation measures put in place by the portuguese state unfeasible. hence the importance of maintaining the division of the ices statistical fishing subareas ix and x and the cecaf divisions. and it cannot be said that this is discrimination between states. discrimination exists when we want to consider situations that are different and specific as the same, as is the case with portuguese fisheries. it is therefore necessary to take account of the specific regime of access to portuguese and spanish waters by their vessels without a time limit. finally, i would like to mention the specific situation of the outermost regions and the need to maintain the existing derogations for access to their exclusive economic zone, as provided for in this report.
mr president, we are faced with a very difficult debate which must be approached in a democratic spirit but which is sensitive to all the parties involved. of course, the principles of sustainability in the exploitation of marine resources, based on scientific criteria - we all agree on this - must be respected, but the principle of non-discrimination must also be applied, although this must be properly crossed and complemented by the equally important principle of relative stability. i would like to thank the members who, together with my colleague ilda figueiredo, voted in favour of my amendment on access to water in the azores. in fact, as has already been said, this is a very delicate situation, with a very difficult biological balance, and we must be very careful in accessing these waters, since the fish are concentrated in a very small part of them, on the highest peaks of the sea. secondly, i would also like to support the commission's intention, as expressed in this proposal for a report, to maintain the specific regime for access to water between portugal and spain, which was decided in 1995 by mutual agreement between the two countries and which was supported by the commission and the council. we hope that this arrangement can continue, because it is the best way to maintain responsible fishing and a climate of peace in the fishing community between the two countries.

in writing. - (pt) the action plan proposed by the commission does not take into account the impact of the fisheries council decisions of 16-20 december 2002 and does not address the difficulties of the sector or the consequences of the restructuring (shredding) measures and the plans for the rebuilding of stocks, which, according to the commission, would involve the loss of 3 000 jobs per year until the end of 2006, in addition to the expected loss of 8 000 jobs per year, resulting from the crisis in the sector and the modernisation of the fleet. it is unacceptable that the commission proposes to finance the action plan through the reprogramming of the structural funds under the fifg and that it presents the possibility of using the mid-term review of the structural funds to try to obtain additional resources from other structural funds. we agree with the rapporteur that additional funds are needed to offset the socio-economic consequences of the reform and the stock replenishment plans, and the commission must use the flexibility instrument or a revision of the financial perspective. we agree with the rapporteur that special attention needs to be paid to small-scale fisheries. the commission admits that 'the financial support measures for small-scale fisheries have not produced the desired effect on the protection of this sector'. this is why we insisted in the 2003 budget procedure on the creation of a specific support programme.
in writing. - (pt) the failure often blamed on the old common fisheries policy (cfp) should make the whole union aware of the importance of having a thoroughly studied evaluation, which could potentially form the basis of a new approach, and that this approach be reflected, if possible, in the new cfp. to do this, it would be crucial to articulate appropriately the interest in the conservation of fisheries resources and the impact of each cfp option on tens of thousands of people, their jobs and their families. this is precisely the subject of this report and the action plan to deal with the consequences of the negative effects of restructuring in the fisheries sector is the appropriate basis from which this study should be carried out. with this in mind, i support the rapporteur when he:- considers that the commission's assessment of the socio-economic impact of the cfp reform is still highly theoretical, that it does not provide sufficiently concrete answers to the problems currently facing the fisheries sector;- argues that the economically weakest enterprises, which could be the most affected by the reform, deserve solidarity and support from the european union;- stresses the need for a serious and detailed debate on the model of fisheries that the european union should follow and reaffirms the importance of a positive approach. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - (pt) taking advantage of the change from unanimity to qualified majority voting (treaty of nice) for the council decision on the 'status of members of the european parliament', the ep is again insisting on a proposal which contains aspects with which we do not agree. among other things, we do not agree with the creation of a monthly parliamentary allowance, equal for all members, regardless of the countries they represent. meps are elected in national constituencies. they are bound and must continue to be bound to these constituencies. the creation of a single parliamentary allowance is part of a federalist conception of the mandate of an mep, aimed at transforming the current national mep into a future 'european mep', a vision which we do not share. moreover, as we have pointed out, the social realities of the eu countries are very different, making it inevitable, with the implementation of this measure, the existence of situations of deep inequality and disparity between the level of wages of workers and elected representatives and holders of public office in different countries, as in the case of portugal, which would be completely incomprehensible. the salary of an mep must therefore be based on the salary of members of the national parliaments in the country where he or she was elected. that is why we are voting against this report.
in writing. - (pt) following the explanation of vote given yesterday, i could not vote otherwise in this final vote, because my reservations are reservations of principle and substance, since they are interwoven with the overall nature of the european institutions. that is why i voted against this report again. but i would like to express my surprise - and my disagreement - that under the pretext of establishing a system of equality for all members and a single status, the possibility of separate systems and differentiated privileged situations for certain members is still maintained. it is sufficient to mention, for example, the possibility for certain re-elected members to be able to maintain, at least for a new parliamentary term, the option in favour of a different salary system. however, apart from the fact that this is absolutely unsustainable in the political framework of the new statute, it could lead to a very negative and completely unsustainable situation, since it would represent double discrimination: on the one hand, it is a different system from that of members of the other member states; on the other hand, it would be a system of discrimination against members of the other member states. and, secondly, it is also a different system from that applied to other meps elected in the same member state. i do not know what surprises me more: the fact that this absurdity was adopted or the fact that even the european commission agreed to it...
