in writing. - (pt) once again, the majority of meps decided to defend the complete liberalisation of the natural gas sector and to accept the positions defended by unice in relation to the objective of the so-called 'lisbon strategy'. the ep's proposal on the role of national regulatory authorities (nras) and a 'european' nra, which will have the task of completing the internal market and ensuring effective competition, is an example of this. this highlights the objective of transferring to so-called 'independent' entities a whole range of competences that should be devolved to democratically elected national institutions. in other words, for the ep, the national state would not even have a regulatory role, which would be the responsibility of the so-called regulatory authorities and the european commission. the intention is so brazen that it has aroused the council's resistance. in general terms, the aim is to impose competition rules on all sectors of the public service, encouraging privatisation, undermining the guarantee of security of supply, investment capacity, equal access to the best prices and quality service, and this will lead to a regression in the rights of all workers in the companies of the sectors in question. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. it should be noted that our proposal was rejected by the majority of meps, including those from the ps, psd and cds-pp.
in writing. - (pt) the liberalisation of the electricity sector is another objective of the 'lisbon strategy'. as in the gas sector, the ep has been the voice of the interests of the european employers' confederation, unice. energy is a strategic sector fundamental to the sovereignty of any state. this guarantee will be called into question by the current liberalisation. in a few years' time, the electricity sector - the rapporteur says so - will be dominated by 5 to 8 companies in the eu, which will of course belong to the more economically developed countries. attempts to impose competition rules and encourage privatisation by jeopardising security of supply, investment capacity, equal access to the best prices and quality service will lead to a regression in the rights of workers in the companies in the sectors in question. hence the presentation by our group of a proposal to reject the common position and the various amendments which seek to minimise the negative aspects of the recommendation, in particular with regard to ensuring compliance with public service obligations, respect for the environment, the specific nature of the outermost regions, and the protection of domestic and small consumers. significantly, the majority of meps, including those from the ps, psd and cds-pp, rejected the rejection proposal.
in writing. - (pt) some of the amendments tabled indicate that the increase in installed nuclear power capacity in europe is essential to comply with the kyoto protocol. this argument lacks rationality and objectivity. all the available evidence indicates otherwise. between 1990 and 1999, the european union already reduced its greenhouse gas emissions by 4% and could reach the remaining reduction level by 2012 (4%), thanks to low-cost measures. according to the european commission, it is possible to meet the kyoto protocol by applying measures costing less than eur 20 per tonne of co2. the commission's proposed measures for the european climate change programme and the framework directive on emissions trading do not include the promotion of nuclear energy.
in writing. - (pt) we are aware that this regulation, in conjunction with others such as the regulation on traceability and labelling, is a step towards lifting the moratorium on gmos. the pressure from the us, which has now lodged a complaint against the eu with the wto, and from the big biotechnology multinationals, which are seeking an end to the moratorium and freedom of trade in gmos, is becoming increasingly evident. nevertheless, the proposals in this report, as in the first reading, make significant improvements to the text. an agreement on this could be important in speeding up the process of ratifying the cartagena protocol on biosafety and biodiversity. the proposals also aim to ensure that imports of gmos cannot take place without the prior written consent of the importing country and that the signing of agreements and conventions cannot lead to a lower level of protection than that provided for in this regulation and the protocol. they also require the exporter to respect national regulatory frameworks and guarantee the public's right to information, which is why they deserve our support. as the report states, the precautionary principle should be taken into account and it should not be made conditional on commercial considerations, given the possible impacts of gmos.
in writing. - (pt) in the absence of strong and integrated legislation on genetically modified organisms (gmos) that can provide guarantees for consumers and industry, the processes for granting marketing authorisations at eu level have been suspended for three years. i welcome the legislation on traceability and labelling of gmos, as it makes it possible to register and monitor the movement of gmos on the market, as well as food and feed produced from these organisms. this allows the consumer to make his own choices and facilitates the procedure for withdrawing a product if this proves necessary.
in writing. - (pt) as you know, the overall objective of the cartagena protocol on biosafety, approved on 29 january 2000, is to ensure an appropriate level of protection in the safe transfer, handling and use of genetically modified organisms (gmos) resulting from modern biotechnology, which may have adverse effects on the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity, also taking into account the risks to human health and their impact especially on transboundary movements. however, in line with the position of the portuguese government, i consider it important to now regulate this at european level, in order to guarantee the overriding interest in this area: a high level of consumer protection. i therefore welcomed the adoption of the council's common position - and the reconciliation of positions which avoided the conciliation procedure - and, as such, the forthcoming entry into force of clear, technically safe rules which would put the eu in a different position from that which, because of the dispersion of the rules, led to the anti-gm moratorium which led the us to lodge a complaint with the world trade organisation.
in writing. - (pt) in response to the prestige accident, the commission announced a series of measures to minimise the risk of future accidents involving vessels such as the erika and the prestige. the commission proposes three fundamental amendments: the introduction of a provision requiring that crude oil and heavy petroleum products be transported only by double-hulled tankers; the accelerated withdrawal of single-hulled tankers; the introduction of a new system of transporting heavy fuel oil and heavy petroleum products by tankers with a double hull; and the introduction of a new system of transporting heavy fuel oil and heavy petroleum products by tankers with a double hull. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment and the environmentally sound use of energy from renewable sources. i therefore fully support this proposal for a regulation, which i consider extremely positive and timely in order to guarantee greater safety in maritime traffic, greater control of oil transport and more effective protection of the marine environment, measures which i have long advocated. this is of vital interest not only to a member state like portugal, which has a huge maritime border and which includes extremely vulnerable island territories, such as the archipelagos of madeira and the azores, but also to the whole of the european union.
in writing. - (pt) we have no shortage of substantial and even compelling reasons for adopting progressively more demanding measures in the field of maritime safety. the occurrence, in a very short period of time, of two major disasters - erika and prestige - and the confrontation with the variety and gravity of their consequences, has shown us all the urgent need for a decision in this area. we are all aware of the intolerable conditions under which many ships continue to carry dangerous and highly polluting cargoes. in this sense, this new proposal is particularly timely in line with the long-announced requirement for a double hull. moreover, as the european commission study has shown, the rapid phase-out of single-hull vessels, as proposed, will not lead to a substantial reduction in oil capacity and, as the rapporteur says, the capacity and international recognition of european shipyards could even benefit them from building new vessels. i also agree with the rapporteur when he says that the solutions now proposed by the european commission must be extended to the international maritime organisation, and that the necessary negotiations must be promoted with great firmness in this context. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) the protection of juveniles is a priority to ensure the conservation of fish stocks and their long-term sustainability. improving technical catch measures should therefore be seen as an essential component of the common fisheries policy and should be considered together with the remaining instruments for the fisheries sector. we therefore agree with the rapporteur's proposals, in particular when he says that fishermen, as the parties concerned by these measures, and those with the most in-depth knowledge of the matter, should be fully involved in the process of defining these measures. moreover, we have always advocated strengthening the social dialogue with the sector, as our proposals in the opinion we drew up in the context of the 2003 budgetary procedure demonstrate. however, we continue to believe that regional advisory councils will not be the most appropriate instruments to ensure this participation. the common fisheries policy would have had to be decentralised. we agree with the rapporteur that the technical errors in the drafting of this commission proposal, in particular a regulation consolidating legislation with extremely technical and sensitive matters, call into question the commission's technical competence in these matters and increase the level of mistrust of fishermen towards the commission.
in writing. - (pt) this proposal by the european commission, which consolidates existing regulations and introduces, in part, new measures, particularly in relation to cod and hake, is important. the court considered that the existing technical regulation was right to allow member states to take measures in certain urgent cases and in relation to their own vessels, subject to the proviso that they could not be less stringent than the conditions laid down by community law. i share the rapporteur's regret that these provisions are not retained in the present proposal. like the rapporteur, i hope that the commission will quickly rectify this omission, as well as the omission of any reference to regional advisory councils (racs). the commission must understand that a sustainable and viable fisheries sector is only possible with the confidence and cooperation of fishermen and taking into account the views of those concerned. moreover, this omission goes against what commissioner fischler promised fishermen in a speech in london, when he asked them to 'be present, participate and be effective actors in the fisheries management process'. i think things would be even better if more of the amendments tabled in plenary had been adopted. nevertheless, for the reasons which have been briefly set out, i voted in favour in the end.
in writing. - (pt) it was necessary to send a clear signal to the council presidency, given that the compromise proposal supported by the commission and promoted by spain, which aims to create a single atlantic area for the management of fishing effort, without the division of the current conservation areas, not only does not serve the development of a sustainable fisheries policy, but would also produce adverse effects, in particular for portugal, in terms of the conservation measures under way and at socio-economic level, both for the fleet and for the regions that depend on this sector. that is why we have contributed to the approval of amendment 20 to this report and we fully support it, given that it proposes the maintenance of the current regulations for a period of ten years, after which the scheme would be reassessed. we would like to say that, despite the fact that all the other amendments to the regulation have been rejected, the committee on fisheries has approved our proposal to raise the limit of access to the exclusive economic zone of the azores and madeira to 200 miles. the council must also take this proposal into account in the compromise negotiations.
in writing. - (pt) the adoption of amendment no 20 by a very large majority was decisive, as it allowed the european parliament to send a clear signal as to the respect of essential principles and valid agreements previously established. it was decisive because the amendment strongly rejects obscure political maneuvers, deceptively dressed in a legal device and clearly based on a wrong basis, in order to serve the interests of one member state - spain. this would clearly harm the conservation of fisheries resources in particularly sensitive areas of the european coast. it would also be completely unacceptable for a revision of the regulation to leave out the careful conservation efforts made by certain member states, namely portugal and ireland, in these same sensitive areas. it is therefore difficult to understand the restrictions that have long been imposed on fishermen in these countries, while paradoxically opening the door to a further waste of fishery resources. i also strongly support amendments nos 8 and 13, which dealt properly with the specific problems of the azores sea, which concern the interests of europe in general and the azores in particular. but in the end it was not necessary to vote for them. i hope that the commission and the council will understand - and respect in substance - the very clear signal sent by parliament and respect the voice of those elected by the european citizens.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the question of workers' financial participation in companies is a very controversial one. recent events related to the collapse of several companies that had employee participation schemes are indicative of the potential risks linked to this system. the enron case and others like it show how necessary it is to study the consequences of applying existing systems, to look more deeply at the various alternatives to participation, whether associated with retirement savings plans, or linked to participation in capital, profits or purchase options. past experience has shown not only the risks but also the many doubts about the incentive that job creation can provide and the dangers of using it to undermine the application of labour law and workers' rights, particularly in the areas of wages, organization and working hours, equal opportunities for men and women and maternity and paternity rights. everyone should be aware of the increasing volatility of financial markets. the report also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the european union's financial instruments are used to the full, and that the european parliament is given the opportunity to make its views known. obviously there are various types of financial participation which may even give rise to certain management schemes. but the discussion is not so much about the 'how' as about the fundamental 'goal' of the proposal. it cannot be allowed to interfere with the process of wage formation and to push for greater flexibility in the labour market. mr winfried menrad sought to establish some rules, particularly as regards collective bargaining, arguing that wage increases should not temporarily coincide with negotiations on financial participation or that worker participation should be an additional element and should not replace the normal basic wage or other components of wages such as the pension scheme. of course, any membership of participation schemes will always be voluntary and can never lead to any discrimination between workers or jeopardize other forms of participation in the life of companies, particularly in the area of workers' trade union organisation.

mr president, i would like to make a brief point of order on a very important directive on cells and tissues, which we voted on here a short while ago in the first reading in a report by our colleague mr peter liese. we have had the unpleasant news that the council, at its meeting this week and on a proposal from the commission, has hardly considered parliament's proposals. i would ask the presidency to convey the following message to the council: we need this directive and parliament's rights must be respected. either the council will relax its position or, most likely, we will be thrown into a laborious conciliation process in april or may, which is very inconvenient. it is therefore very important that the council, in this directive, respects parliament's positions and makes its position more flexible when the second reading begins in september.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the commissioner for her speech, which shows the commission's commitment to tackling this serious public health problem in collaboration with the member states, which have the competence in health matters. in fact, the number of breast cancer cases has been increasing at an alarming rate in the european union. as an example, i would point out that in portugal breast cancer is the leading cause of death among women over 45. every year, in my country, there are 3,500 new cases and every day five women die from this disease. however, there is real political will and concrete measures to improve this situation. i therefore thank and congratulate the rapporteur on her excellent report which alerts us to the alarming numbers of this particular type of cancer both in europe and in the world, and calls on us all to act urgently and to make the fight against cancer one of the key priorities of health policy in the european union. we are faced with the challenge of drastically reducing the death rate from breast cancer in europe, but also of eliminating disparities between member states in the quality of health care and, therefore, in women's chances of survival. to do this, we must act at several levels: - first, prevention and screening: it is urgent to promote awareness-raising campaigns demonstrating that early diagnosis of the disease increases the chances of cure. the member states should therefore put in place two-yearly screening models for women aged 50 to 69, as recommended in the european guidelines on mammography screening;- second: diagnosis. in all member states it should be ensured that women are informed of the results of a mammogram within five working days and, after diagnosis, do not wait more than four weeks to start treatment; women with breast cancer should be treated by interdisciplinary teams that have received and continue to receive appropriate professional training. to get through the treatment phase as well as possible, patients should have access to psychological support, physiotherapy care and social services. after treatment, the medical and emotional follow-up phase is essential. and finally, i'd like to end on a note of hope by saying that one day we will be able to fight and eradicate this disease. so let us make good use not only of the €400 million for cancer research available under the sixth framework programme for research, but also of the new action programme in the field of health 2003-08, to develop innovative initiatives and projects.
i think the chairman of the committee on budgets is right. the amendments we have adopted are clearly intended to ensure that everything is finally compatible with the budget. so i would say that there will be enough room for manoeuvre on this matter to change, say, the wording if necessary, so that it is so.
in writing. - (pt) this report on the financial participation of employees is an essential contribution to overcoming the capital versus labour dichotomy. employees who participate in the profits or capital of the enterprises will be more motivated, more productive and, consequently, will promote a better competitiveness and profitability of the enterprise. moreover, financial participation contributes to the achievement of two objectives: the realisation of the european social model and the increase in employment. it is a good report, and i therefore vote in favour. i share the principles set out for the financing of the financial participation model, namely: voluntary participation, the need for clarity, transparency and simplicity of schemes, the exclusion of disproportionate risks for employees, the prevention of pro-cyclical effects linked to changes in the economic situation and the compatibility of schemes with the mobility of employees. i regret, however, that the european commission has proposed few solutions for smes, whereas there is a need to carry out studies on the different forms of participation in smes and to consider alternative solutions.
in writing. - (pt) following recent statements calling into question the reliability of the controls carried out in the various member states, it was essential to update the rules for the organisation of official controls on products of animal origin, particularly in the case of fresh meat, shellfish and milk. i welcome the proposal for a regulation and would like to highlight, among the new rules, the role assigned to veterinarians, the increased intensity and frequency of checks, the scientific basis of the checks and greater flexibility in relation to small businesses.
in writing. -(pt) the proposal for a directive is part of the process of reworking community legislation on general food hygiene rules, health policy issues related to the placing of products of animal origin on the market and official controls of products of animal origin. administrative simplification and, at the same time, the maintenance of high standards in this area are of particular importance, since it has already been demonstrated in the clearest possible way that the level of hygiene of the products offered to the consumer has not been systematically uniform or reliable. the measures advocated by the proposal will therefore promote greater accountability of all actors in the food chain, which will encourage consumer confidence, which has been strongly shaken by the recent crises. therefore, the consistency and transparency of the application of this new legal framework will have to be promoted, without forgetting the specific needs of small producers, who are generally further away from the centres of dissemination of information and adoption of legislative amendments. i think the european commission should consider the amendment proposed by the rapporteur, which emphasises the need to allow member states to adapt to the new rules. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - (pt) the european union is currently in the process of deregulating the use of smoke flavourings in foodstuffs - in some member states there are restrictions, while in others there is no legislation on the matter. it is therefore necessary to define the legislation in order to harmonise the authorisation procedure. i also welcome the development of a positive list based on the latest scientific knowledge and on the guidelines formulated by the european food safety authority. it is to be hoped that the precautionary principle - the basis of all european food policy - will also apply to each new use of smoke flavourings.
in writing. -(pt) i voted in favour of the report which stresses the importance of clarifying the rules on human health. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's suggestion that medical devices should be reclassified, apart from the technical issues. it provides a legal framework and distinguishes between pharmacologically active and non-pharmacologically active medical devices. i also support the proposal to encourage member states to take the necessary measures to ensure that single-use devices are not reused. finally, i also decided to support the report in that it considers it essential to include explicit provisions on public access to documents. the dissemination and promotion of information to citizens, particularly on this issue, should be encouraged as a priority, in order to ensure citizen participation and to follow up our commitment to increasing the level of consumer protection.
in writing. - (pt) we voted against this report because it accepts, albeit in a slightly nuanced way, the principle of decoupling production aids, does not make any real proposal for modulation and setting a limit to the aid paid under the cap and, in some respects, is worse than the original proposal. the report does not propose partial decoupling but, in practice, full decoupling of aid for arable crops and male bovine animals. the same report reaffirms the compulsory national co-financing of rural development measures and gives modulation an optional character, which calls into question not only the principle itself but also the community redistribution of savings, thus harming portuguese interests. the modulation proposal sets out a differentiation in the level of reductions to be made for less-favoured regions and raises the exemption threshold to eur 2 500. however, the proposal fails to differentiate between producers and instead penalizes medium-sized producers in comparison with large producers. we regret that our proposals were not accepted, in particular the proposal on modulation, the proposal on the doubling of the special amount of aid paid to farmers receiving less than eur 5 000 and the proposal on the exemption from reductions for farmers receiving less than eur 10 000, which would be financed up to a ceiling of eur 100 000 per farmer.
in writing. - (pt) the reasons why portuguese farmers complain about a profoundly unfair cap are not new. it is constantly said that portugal and its agriculture are the last beneficiaries of the cap in the european union. by voting for the amendments to reject the proposals put forward by the european commission as a whole, i wanted to express politically the dissatisfaction of the portuguese people and the feeling of disappointment with the commission's initial proposals, which do not even constitute the outline of a satisfactory response. however, i recognize the excellent work done by mr cunha and the need for reform of the cap, both for financial reasons - determined by the wto negotiations - and because of the demands of consumers and the need to meet a new type of demand - less productivist and more oriented towards the rural world. i believe that the european parliament's position has the merit of moving the reform towards a more reasonable, balanced and fair position, namely a gradual and cautious reform. i would also like to leave the benefit of the doubt to commissioner fischler, who, at the end of the debate, assured us that the commission would henceforth support mediterranean products, just as it would other products. this is why i supported the bulk of parliament's proposals, whilst abstaining in the final vote.
in writing. - (pt) rural development seems to be the panacea for all the ills and imbalances of the various types of agriculture in the eu. but it is also part of the cap's strategy of fiscal saving and liberalisation of agricultural markets, in connection with enlargement and the negotiations within the world trade organisation. the aim of market mechanisms is to support prices and thus incomes, ignoring the need to remedy deep-seated injustices. without farmers and agricultural production, rural development is impossible. the commission proposal does not increase the appropriations allocated to rural development but transfers part of the appropriations from the markets pillar, which implies a renationalisation of part of the cap costs. the proposals contained in this report are, on the whole, positive, although the substance remains the same. our vote reflects the improvements introduced, namely: support for the less favoured regions, young farmers, women in rural areas, promotion of agricultural products, an increase in the amounts of aid provided for under the various instruments, and our proposal to increase compensatory payments to the most disadvantaged regions by eur 100.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate our colleague karl erik olsson on the excellent report on the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1257/1999 on support for rural development by the european agricultural guidance and guarantee fund (eaggf) and repealing regulation (ec) no 2826/2000. i support this report, particularly on the need to help create the conditions for the development of agriculture in the weakest and most difficult regions of the european union. in this way, it is possible to prevent the rural exodus of these populations, to encourage the protection of the landscape and therefore of the environment, while trying to improve the living standards of the populations of these regions. i would also like to stress that the european parliament must systematically support the development of an agricultural policy which respects the environment, giving priority to support for farmers who respect community rules and young people who want to set up as farmers. it should be noted that this is also a way of stimulating employment in europe.
in writing. - the present proposal for a regulation on the cereals sector highlights the strategy of the recent cap reforms: lower prices and gradual deregulation of the markets. the compensation of income is partial, with direct aids covering 50% of the price reduction. this strategy encourages the concentration and intensification of production and the increase in the size of farms, which accelerates the desertification of the rural world. in addition, the 45% reduction in the price of cereals resulted in an increased budgetary cost of €630 million. we supported several of the rapporteur's proposals, including the inclusion of rye in the list of cereals eligible for intervention and the references made in defence of community preference, but we reject the principle of decoupling production aid for the cereals sector. we also reject aid to the potato starch sector, which supports large agro-industrial groups from only certain member states, whereas it is necessary to regulate and encourage the production of potatoes for consumption. a comprehensive reform of the cap is needed. this reform should guarantee similar levels of aid and market regulation for mediterranean products. without this, it will be impossible to redress the profound injustices in the distribution of aid and, moreover, we will send a misleading message to producers in regions and countries with climatic conditions suitable for other productions.
in writing. - (pt) this proposal for a regulation calls for the common organisation of the market in dried fodder to be phased out, starting with the 2008-2009 marketing year. the commission's justification is based on environmental issues, namely the use of fossil fuels for dehydration and even the use of irrigation. but environmental issues can be solved by other means, such as plans to reduce the use of fossil fuels, natural soil drying or the use of renewable energy. however, we must look at this sector more as a source of vegetable protein production, for which the european union has a growing deficit, already reaching 35 million tonnes of soya equivalent. in other words, the eu meets only 23% of its vegetable protein needs. the situation will only worsen with enlargement. the disappearance of this production implies the need to import, mainly from the united states, 2 million tonnes of soybean meal equivalent, with all the risks that this implies in terms of contamination by gmos. this is why, despite taking account of the environmental factor, we have voted in favour of the rapporteur's proposal to maintain the current common customs tariff, strengthen market instruments and increase total aid to eur 68 per tonne from the 2004/05 marketing year.
in writing. - (pt) the rice sector is going through a difficult period, given the imbalances caused by the simultaneous increase in domestic production and imports, the latter being due to the preferences and customs reductions of recent years. this situation will tend to worsen with the reduction in customs duties linked to the implementation of the 'everything but arms' initiative, the new round of wto negotiations and the risks of 'triangulation' and abuse of the inward processing regime. there is also a conflict of interest between the southern producing member states and the northern consumer member states in europe, whose preference for consumption is for the indian rice variety, for which the eu is largely in deficit. this proposal for a regulation is unacceptable. the commission proposes a 50% reduction in the intervention price for a basic price of eur 150 per tonne, a compensation for this reduction of around 88% of the compensation applied to cereals under the previous reforms and a quantitative limit. in doing so, the commission ignores the specificities of this monoculture, which is concentrated in regions with specific characteristics and no alternatives. the commission also forgets that this crop has the highest costs in the agricultural sector in terms of investment in machinery, equipment and installations, which are generally specific. forcing rice farmers to switch to other crops would therefore put them in serious economic difficulty. we are therefore abundant in the sense of the rapporteur.
in writing. - (pt) in this proposal for a regulation, the commission proposes to extend a reformed milk quota system until the 2014-15 marketing year, with no projection for the future. the maintenance of the quota system is essential to guarantee milk production throughout the european union and to ensure the income of producers. the end of the quota system, as the large surplus producing countries would like, would lead to the liberalisation of the sector, greater concentration of production and a sharp fall in prices, which would primarily harm small and medium-sized producers in the least productive and most disadvantaged regions. it is therefore necessary to approve general quota increases for all countries and to take concrete measures to combat the concentration of production, whether regional or in the hands of a small number of producers. however, account must be taken of specific situations, such as in portugal, more specifically in the outermost region of the azores, where it is essential to guarantee an increase in quota in order not to penalise a sector with significant socioeconomic influences in a region marked by major structural disadvantages.
in writing. - (pt) milk production is of vital importance in the most disadvantaged regions. it is therefore essential that minimum prices cover labour and production costs and that family farming and rural holdings are protected. the transfer of production rights without land and the fall in prices, together with the absence of concrete measures for regions with specific difficulties (closure of collective milking rooms, absence of aid for the costs of transporting milk to inland or mountainous regions, etc.), led to a concentration of production and the disappearance of thousands of farmers, especially in portugal. we reject the commission's proposal to reduce the guide prices by 28% for the next five marketing years. the absence of measures to combat the concentration of production and the speculation on the economic value of milk quotas is unacceptable. similarly, no updating of the fat content to better reflect the actual average was planned. we agree with the rapporteur on her proposals for an increase in intervention prices compared with the commission's proposal, for full compensation for price cuts through direct payments and, above all, for an additional subsidy of eur 5 per tonne for the less-favoured regions. but we reject the abolition of indicative prices.
in writing. - (pt) the concept of multifunctional agriculture is now more on the table than ever, especially in the context of the current cap reform. it even seems that some have just discovered the multifunctional nature of agriculture. however, agricultural production has always had positive externalities for rural development, contributing to job creation, the development of other upstream economic activities, land use planning, and the protection of the environment, landscapes and cultural heritage. therefore, policies to promote a large and dense network of small and medium-sized family farms and the development of local and regional markets are essential. it is clear that the current cap, despite the reforms it has introduced, is the main culprit in the end of multifunctional agriculture through the gradual liberalisation of agricultural markets. for this reason, we agree with the rapporteur that concrete measures in the field of the cap should be put in place rather than 'statements of intent', which is not the case in the commission's proposal on the cap. we support the proposals put forward by the rapporteur, but we regret that she has not shown greater ambition.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate our colleague, mrs rodríguez ramos, on her excellent report on the multifunctionality of agriculture and the reform of the common agricultural policy, which i support, particularly as regards the defence of a european agricultural policy capable of taking into account the multiple functions of agriculture; the commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of life in rural areas, including the maintenance of the population in rural areas, land use planning, the protection of the environment, landscape and cultural heritage and the introduction of the concept of territorial cohesion. i would also like to stress that the european parliament prides itself on acting in respect of european diversity, which means that in the case of agriculture we must also consider the non-commercial aspects, with a view to the harmonious development of the european union.
in writing. -(pt) i believe that multifunctional agriculture must be part of the cap reform process and that it is important that the council and the commission take up this concept. the social, environmental and territorial impact of agricultural activity has not received the necessary attention from the community institutions, which have focused agricultural policies mainly on their qualitative and economic aspects. in reality, it is a principle of elementary justice to point out that the public goods and positive externalities, which are difficult to quantify, resulting from conventional agricultural activity largely supplant the economic benefits directly derived from agriculture. for this reason, particular attention should be paid to the rural population, concrete measures should be adopted outside the rural development framework and the maintenance of agricultural activity should be encouraged and supported, taking into account the importance of farms at local level. we must also reorient production towards sustainable and high-quality development. i also agree with the rapporteur's interpretation that account must be taken of the irreplaceable presence of a reasonable number of farmers who must have the means to continue to ensure a human presence and proper management of rural territory in the face of the unforeseen vicissitudes of competition in a market in full liberalization. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) we do not agree with the content of various points in the resolution and certain of the wording chosen, including the point on the mention of a 'judeo-christian and humanist culture of europe' or the point on turkey's commitments to nato. the resolution lists issues of extreme importance, such as the ban on the activities of the various political forces, the issue of amnesty for political prisoners, the practice of torture and other forms of violence and repression, the control of the military over the political life of the country or the military occupation of northern cyprus and the non-application of un resolutions relating to the occupation. the day before yesterday, my group in this parliament organized an initiative on the situation in turkey, in which various human rights organizations took part. one of the main ideas highlighted in this initiative - despite the occasional constitutional and legislative amendments which were considered positive by these organisations, some of which have no practical application - is that there is a need to continue to denounce the violence and arbitrariness of the turkish authorities and that solidarity with all those who resist and struggle should be strengthened. we will continue to support all initiatives in this direction.
in writing. -(pt) according to the conclusions of the lisbon european council, the open method of coordination should make it possible 'to disseminate best practice and to ensure greater convergence of national policies in the light of the main objectives of the european union'. however, the way in which the open method of coordination has been applied so far reveals some weaknesses. hence the need for clarification, particularly in the definition of the fields of application; the mobilisation of all national actors so that the process is not limited to the participation of an elite; the commission has also proposed that the method of coordination be used with other community instruments, so that it is complementary to legislation and not 'legislation in disguise'. it is therefore appropriate to support the recommendation that an article on the open method of coordination be included in the future constitutional treaty, which should define and set out the contours and procedures. i also welcome the need to consult the committee on women's rights and equal opportunities on matters within its remit and acknowledge that it would be useful for the european commission to carry out a study on the effectiveness of the method. the measures proposed will certainly contribute to the improvement of the open method of coordination, which is why i voted in favour of this excellent report.
in writing. -(pt) i voted in favour and welcomed the initiative taken by the committee on employment and social affairs. i agree with the rapporteur that (as is the view of the four working groups of the convention) the open method of coordination should be more precisely defined and included in the treaty. the national reports should indicate how civil society, the social partners, local, regional and national authorities and parliaments have been consulted. i have always defended and stressed the unparalleled importance of the participation of national parliaments and peoples (specifically the persons concerned or targeted) at local level in the formation and manifestation of the 'community will'. the reason is that the latter does not correspond to the federalist vision of a putative 'european will' but is rather the result of a 'will to understand', a meeting of dissimilar interests, a convergence of values and objectives. the sharing of best practice, combined with the open method of coordination, is therefore a path that should be improved, explored and extended to other areas as well, given the positive impact on employment policies. this approach would allow for genuine convergence and collective enrichment, without resorting to the more or less binding nature of the legislative act. finally, i also supported the proposal to ask the commission to draw up a study on the effectiveness of the open method of coordination.

in writing. -(pt) sport is an activity with countless virtues, such as the development of group spirit and mutual aid in team sports, the use of leisure spaces, the obvious health benefits, the possibility of raising awareness of the importance of respecting the rules and raising ethical awareness, among other examples. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption. in keeping with the old maxim 'a healthy mind in a healthy body', sport should start at school and it is essential that all, men and women, should enjoy the same and appropriate conditions for sport. the low presence of women in sport decision-making mechanisms within sports federations and associations is not a problem specific to sport, but in this particular case too, the issue must be properly addressed. the participation of women must be encouraged by the union, even if certain proposals seem to us to constitute an excessive interference, either at the level of the competences of the member states or at the level of the own organizational capacity of sports associations - in short, a double violation of the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. - (pt) the incidence of breast cancer has increased at a steady rate. the report, which has just been approved, argues that prevention, early detection, diagnosis, treatment and monitoring of the disease need to be improved. according to who, in the european union, 216,000 new cases of breast cancer were recorded in 2000, of which 79,000 were fatal. this type of cancer is most common in women, affecting one in nine women and is the most common cause of death among women aged 35-55. the risk of developing breast cancer is 60% higher in western europe than in eastern europe. hence the proposal to put in place the conditions for a 25% reduction in the mortality rate from breast cancer in the european union by 2008. member states are invited to propose that all women aged between 50 and at least 69 years should undergo a mammogram every two years, in accordance with the european guidelines on quality standards for mammography screening services, as only eight of the 15 eu member states currently have national screening programmes. all women with breast cancer should have the right to be treated by multidisciplinary teams. that is why we voted in favour.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate the rapporteur on this important and timely report. in fact, the figures from the international agency for research on cancer confirm this. according to the same figures, in 2000, more than 79 000 women died of breast cancer. in addition, the comfortable majority obtained in the committee on women's rights and equal opportunities, with only two abstentions and no negative votes, confirms the accuracy and relevance of the content of the report. among the proposals made by the rapporteur, i would highlight the inclusion of the fight against breast cancer in health policy priorities, the implementation of a biennial screening model for all women aged 50 to 69 and the regular participation of doctors and paramedical staff in complementary vocational training actions. another determining factor would be a clearly defined objective in terms of research into a treatment for this type of cancer, among others. i am one of those who believe that cancer is still the real 'evil of the century' and must be our priority.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are faced today with a significant setback for peace and the rule of law in indonesia, reflected in the breach of the ceasefire and the resumption of hostilities in the province of aceh on the one hand and the renewed tensions in irian jaya or west papua on the other. indonesia is one of the largest countries in the world, and it has the particularity of having added to the problems caused by geography and history, and in particular by the process of decolonization - which has already been mentioned by mr mayer, and which is the root of the problems of the former aceh sultanate - the problems caused by brutal repression and dictatorship and by the indonesian expansionist character which has gone through the annexation of irian jaya and the military conquest of east timor. these last two facts help us to understand the seriousness and complexity of the situation we face today in this country. the decolonisation of east timor, which followed the fall of the suarto dictatorship, was a historic step in reversing this internal expansionist logic which is characteristic of indonesia, as well as the attitude of the western world which had supported, by action and by omission, the conquest of this small and young nation in south-east asia. as we know, this was not a peaceful action and could only be successful if external military force was used, since the united nations proved incapable of dealing with the indonesian armed reaction on its own. in view of this, and recognizing that it is therefore pointless to always stand against any armed action, everything leads us to believe that we are in a situation where, as our joint resolution points out, everything must be done to put an end to the armed conflict and to reopen the dialogue between the indonesian government and the separatist movements in aceh, as well as the representatives of irian jaya. in addition to taking all the necessary measures to restore the ceasefire in aceh and dialogue in irian jaya, we must also establish a foreign policy for indonesia based on respect for human rights, minorities and inter-ethnic and inter-religious dialogue. and these principles have to be superimposed on geopolitical calculations or economic interests, which are always bad advisers in these circumstances and which have given us such bad results in the past, and they must also be superimposed on deterministic calculations about territorial integrity or rights to self-determination, which are sometimes difficult to trace in the first place.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by congratulating the commissioner on his reassuring words and approach to this delicate issue. the textile industry will face a major challenge from 1 january 2005: after that date all wto members will have access without quantitative restrictions, i.e. almost freely, to the markets of the european union, the united states of america and canada. in line with the doha development agenda, the aim is to steer international trade liberalisation to the benefit of the least developed countries. in these countries the textile sector is very important. i would like to highlight india, pakistan and china. china is a case in point: the world bank forecasts a doubling of its textile exports in the next five years. as the commissioner has said, this sector is also of great importance in the european union, employing two million people and generating a turnover of 200 billion euros. after enlargement, the number of employees will exceed two million and a half thousand. this industry is one of the most traditional industries in the economic structure of my country. portugal is one of the largest textile and clothing producers in the union. its exports account for more than one fifth of total national exports. portuguese textile products are present on the main world markets, notably the markets of the european union and the united states. the portuguese textile and clothing industry is composed mainly of small and medium-sized enterprises, the overwhelming majority of which are concentrated in the northern region. in this context, it is essential to reflect in depth on how to minimise the negative effects on european union businesses and maximise the opportunities arising from the liberalisation of markets. the aspects that will enable european textile companies to compete in the open market must be strengthened. research and technological development, information technology, training and vocational qualification are the only possible outlets for preserving and increasing the weight and importance of the textile and clothing sector in the european and world economy. the institutions involved must ensure conditions of competition and respect for international trade rules, in particular by combating poverty wages and child labour, advocating the improvement of social and health benefits, guaranteeing fundamental labour rights and adopting measures against fraud, among others. in the particular case of portugal, multilateral negotiations must be conducted within the framework of the doha development agenda, which should result in tariff harmonization and the removal of non-tariff barriers, thus allowing practical market access. we are aware of the great challenge we face and we believe that the future negotiations should be conducted with rigor and without haste in order to strike a balance between the doha commitments on development and the interests of the textile and clothing industry in the union.

mr president, i think we can all agree that the sustainability of fisheries resources and measures to conserve them are essential for the fisheries sector. however, a common fisheries policy cannot be applied blindly: take into account the local and regional specificities of the various fisheries, fleets and sector-dependent regions of the various member states and the populations involved. the participation of fishermen and their associations is therefore essential, their experience is vital. but it is also this specificity which implies, for the correct application of the common fisheries policy, that it is essential to guarantee flexibility to the member states in the application of measures to manage fishing effort, to take account of the local pilot projects developed by the fishermen themselves - as the rapporteur points out for the mediterranean. this also implies the ability of states to apply conservation measures, since they are the ones who know the situation of resources best. another aspect is the strengthening of research, since conservation measures and the assessment of the state of resources must be taken on the basis of sound scientific advice and with the involvement of fishermen and their associations. this requires a strengthening of research, as the rapporteur also proposes in his text for the mediterranean. we also support the delegation of responsibility for the management of coastal fisheries, and not only, in the member states, as well as the promotion of solutions found at local level to reduce fishing effort, taking into account the principle of subsidiarity. i think this is a good way to go in other areas, like the atlantic. for example, small-scale coastal and artisanal fishing is very important in portugal, as it is in the mediterranean. we therefore agree with the rapporteur when he argues for the need to create specific measures to support it - as i have also argued in my opinion on the 2003 fisheries budget - and we stress the need for the fifg to promote small-scale fishing. i also stress the importance of taking into account measures for the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources, similar to those we advocate for the mediterranean in various areas of the atlantic, in particular the 200 miles of the portuguese coast and the outermost regions. i would also like to stress, as the rapporteur does, that the degradation of fisheries has other causes, namely pollution and shipping, and that is why the sector is often also a victim in this process. finally, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am glad i am not wearing a hood, but my voice is a little weak when i speak of the mediterranean, which is a call to us, to the sun, to the beaches, to the holidays. the history of the mediterranean is a very rich and complex climatic, physical, cultural and political history. i recently read that the mediterranean sea dried up completely five million years ago, as evidenced by the salty sediments that lie at the bottom of the ocean. it is true that the mediterranean sea, as a result of tourist pressure, as a result of a rapidly growing population in north africa and pollution, is not threatened today as it was when this climate cataclysm completely dried up this beautiful sea. however, the mediterranean's fisheries resources are in many cases being overexploited. this is the conclusion of the most rigorous scientific research, although there is no scientifically proven risk of rupture. and while there is no risk of rupture, there are threats and there is reason to fear that the mediterranean's resources will also suffer the same depletion that has occurred in other maritime regions. and that's why action is necessary. if it is true that delegation and responsibility in the member states and the pursuit of local solutions to reduce fishing effort is to be welcomed and is a good principle, which could possibly be applied on certain atlantic coasts - in writing. - (pt) the next olympic games will take place in the territory of a member state for the first time since the creation of the schengen area and its integration into the union. we are defining a specific community measure, which establishes a system of exemption from the visa provisions for members of the olympic family participating in the 2004 olympic games in athens. the purpose of this regulation is to facilitate the task of the member state responsible for organising the next olympic games, greece, while giving it the means to honour the commitments it has made under the olympic charter. temporary derogations are provided for in respect of certain provisions of the community acquis on visas. they are limited in scope, proportionate, technical and fully justified by the exceptional nature of the event. members of the olympic family who, by reason of their nationality, are subject to a visa requirement shall remain subject to that requirement. the intention is only to facilitate the application procedures and the form in which visas are issued (the organising committee will simply have to provide a list of participants to the services responsible for issuing visas in greece). in addition, no conflict is created with the fundamental principles or security standards of the schengen area (the greek authorities must verify that all the required conditions are met before issuing a visa).

in writing. - (pt) i congratulate mr wijkman on his excellent report, both for his insightful reading of the key role played by energy in development policies and for the paths he highlights, always marked by the central concern to improve the living conditions of the poorest. this concern and the adoption of practical, realistic and effective measures are a challenge to the creativity of the peoples of the european union and an imperative for humanity. we must break the energy-poverty dichotomy - the basis of the commission's two proposals - because 'where energy is lacking, poverty grows and a vicious circle is set in place'. i share the rapporteur's concern about the lack of a clear financial commitment from the commission to support the diagnosis. however, i think we are moving in the right direction. even from a purely economic point of view, any support that can be given in the energy sector is clearly an investment for the future. for every one of us. this is one of the areas where development policies can have a more lasting and visible effect.
in writing. - (pt) as stated in the implementation plan of the johannesburg world summit for sustainable development, 'oceans, seas, islands and coastal areas are an integral and essential component of the planet's ecosystem and are of crucial importance for global food security'. the protection of the marine environment, in particular the conservation of its biodiversity, must be considered a priority. in addition, additional actions are needed in the field of marine environment protection, a genuine coastal policy and the promotion of sustainable use of the seas. we therefore agree with the rapporteur that a strategy in this area must incorporate the precautionary principle, the development of protection and conservation measures, an integrated approach to all human activities that have an impact on the marine environment, an integrated approach to the management of fishing effort and a regional approach that takes into account the diversity of regions and respect for their 'ecological characteristics and socio-economic aspects', without forgetting the other causes of marine pollution. therefore, we consider that the recent commission proposal on the management of fishing effort in the atlantic ocean calls into question the conservation objectives and, in particular, the capacity of portugal to undertake conservation measures in its exclusive economic zone.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate the commission on the communication it has presented. i believe, however, that this communication should have based its analysis on the conservation of fish stocks and not on a vague notion of sustainability. the analysis does not sufficiently address the impact of fishing on the protection of the marine environment. in addition, the communication does not sufficiently define the quantified objectives to be achieved or the timetables to be respected. i therefore hope that the commission will propose as soon as possible a draft strategy for the protection of the marine environment which presents a comprehensive response to the challenge of promoting sustainability in the marine environment at global level, both by coordinating and consolidating the various existing legal texts and by encouraging the establishment of monitoring and evaluation bodies at european and global level. this strategy should be accompanied by an action plan for the protection of the marine environment, including objectives, resources and timetables. finally, i would like to draw attention to the role of the european union in international negotiations on the conservation of the marine environment: it is essential that techniques which lead to bycatch (leaving drifting very long nets which end up killing non-target species such as whales, seals, birds and turtles) are severely restricted at world level.
in writing. - (pt) the unanimous decision of the committee on the environment, public health and consumer policy confirms the almost irrefutable nature of this own-initiative report. i share his views and i voted for it. i believe that a harmonised european marine strategy is appropriate; the need for such a strategy has not been demonstrated. furthermore, the idea that the lack of detailed information is no excuse for avoiding precautionary measures - especially when there is no doubt that biodiversity has declined - is, unless applied blindly, an excellent principle for taking action. the rapporteur's request that the european union take a decision to join the arctic council is also helpful - the current members of the arctic council are the united states, canada, iceland, norway, russia, denmark, sweden and finland. if the eu became a member, the euro-atlantic understanding of environmental problems would certainly be improved and the eu could participate in an important forum, especially for the protection of the northern marine environment. as for the commission's belief that maximum sustainable yield should be defined in terms of stock sustainability and not economic sustainability, i think a more balanced approach is needed: a strategy for the protection and conservation of the marine environment with, at the same time, the definition of mechanisms to increase economic sustainability. the best thing to do in the face of such a compromise is certainly to realize that the policy thus defined is always successful.
in writing. - (pt) as i said in my explanation of vote on the markov report, one of the main problems with the structural instrument for pre-accession (ispa) - the 2001 development programme for the eight acceding countries - is that there are still difficulties with the procedures for using the appropriations. the ispa programmes are a kind of cohesion fund for the countries that will soon join the european union and are intended to improve basic infrastructure in the field of the environment and transport. in this context, as the rapporteur has stressed, it is important to invest in good administrative training for staff from these countries who will be managing structural fund aid next year. this will avoid bureaucratic delays, which lead to bottlenecks and additional delays. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the application of the principle of equal treatment for men and women in matters of employment, vocational training and promotion, and working conditions, is based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women. otherwise, there is a risk of severe paralysis in the coming years, offset by last-minute liberality which is not consistent with the ideas of rational and structural development.
in writing. - (pt) the sustainability of the fisheries sector depends on the sustainability of fish stocks, which must be considered as public goods. we therefore subscribe to the fao code of conduct for responsible fisheries, which states that measures should be introduced to minimise pollution, waste, discards, catches by lost gear or by non-target species. the development and use of more selective and environmentally friendly fishing gear and techniques is needed, as is effective protection of juveniles. the fao has estimated that between 17.9 and 39.5 million tonnes of fish are discarded each year by commercial fisheries, which is between 2 and 5 times the eu's fisheries production, which is completely unacceptable. we generally agree with the objectives of this report. however, we believe that a solution will only be found when effective decentralisation of the common fisheries policy is implemented and allows fishermen, scientists and public authorities to play an active role. at the outset, as the rapporteur has said, this can be achieved through the regional advisory councils, as provided for in regulation 2371/2002, by formulating a strategy for the disposal of waste.

the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the environmental protection of the european union's coal industry. a ton of carbon will have a price in the market and whoever is able to produce the same with less carbon dioxide emissions will win. the adoption of this directive is therefore of enormous political value: it will give credibility to our international leadership, which is essential if we are to convince russia to ratify the kyoto protocol, it will make it possible to correct, as from 2005, the poor performance of most member states in complying with kyoto and, above all, it will reduce by 35% the economic cost of implementing kyoto in the european union. although we welcomed the commission's proposal from the outset, which we regarded as positive, parliament felt that it should be given greater ambition. i believe that this was achieved with the second reading agreement concluded with the greek presidency, with the excellent cooperation of the commission and which will be voted on tomorrow. this agreement has two major advantages: firstly, it avoids the conciliation and thus the possible postponement of the start-up of the system from 2005 to 2006; secondly, although i do not accept all the amendments tabled by parliament, the compromise reached incorporates our most important proposals. let me highlight the main innovations introduced in this agreement. firstly, the definition of a national ceiling of emission allowances in line with the kyoto objectives. this ensures that a quantified objective is achieved through the system, and avoids the risk of over-allocation. secondly, the opt-out clause will be applied to installations but not to activities, thus ensuring that the liquidity of the system and the balance of the internal market will not be affected. point 3 allows the system to be extended to other sectors, in particular transport, chemicals and aluminium, in the context of the revision of the directive. point 4 - the auction is included in the method of allocating emission allowances, albeit unfortunately in a non-harmonised way, from the first period onwards. point 5 - the appropriations for clean development projects and joint implementation of the kyoto protocol will be linked to this directive but will not replace the priority to be given to domestic action. point 6 includes an opting clause allowing states to extend the system to other installations and other activities. point 7 is the extension, albeit on a voluntary basis, of the system to other greenhouse gases besides carbon dioxide from the second period of the directive. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. finally, i would like to highlight the inclusion of benchmarking criteria in the allocation of emission allowances in the member states. i therefore believe that the european emissions market, with this agreement, has become more ambitious environmentally, more economically efficient, with less risk of distortion of competition and more compatible with other national policies already in place. i would like to end by thanking the cooperation of the council, in particular the greek presidency, the commission, which was inexhaustible in the arbitration between the council and the commission, and especially my fellow shadow rapporteurs, because i believe that only their collaboration and support has allowed parliament to be united. and only the united parliament has allowed this agreement to be so positive.
