in writing. - (pt) as the rapporteur has said, the prospectus directive is one of the pillars of the action plan for financial services, which is an integral part of the lisbon strategy, which aims to integrate financial markets by 2005. it is therefore understandable that the report considers that 'it is essential to reach a consensus and to ensure a rapid adoption of the directive under consideration', as 'the latter will contribute to the creation of a legal framework that will strengthen the conditions for raising capital via europe's financial markets'. in other words, in addition to the refinancing guarantee for (large) companies, the directive aims to promote greater liberalisation of investment and capital. in this context, the amendments introduced by the rapporteur at the level of the common position adopted by the council are intended to make the regulation more flexible, to speed up the process of approving the prospectus and to reduce the powers of autonomous decision of the member states and national legislation. in concrete terms, the state's ability to determine the criteria defining a qualified investor and to reduce the time taken for approval of the prospectus has been restricted by the introduction of the concept of approval by default. the directive even considers it disproportionate that the competent authority carries out on-the-spot inspections to ensure compliance with the directive. it even advocates raising the threshold for investors below which the publication of a prospectus is no longer compulsory. in short, the directive calls for liberalization. hence our rejection.
in writing. - (pt) i largely agree with the rapporteur's concern to strengthen the conditions for raising capital on the european financial markets. i believe that the transparency and clarity of these markets, which are the result of the process of simplification advocated, constitute a valid reason for the establishment of minimum regulatory standards at community level. such measures could contribute to the creation of a legal framework to strengthen and facilitate the raising of capital on europe's financial markets and to improve standards of investor information, thereby serving the interests of issuers, investors, operators and the markets themselves. i note the rapporteur's sensitivity to the need to lighten certain regulations in order to adapt legislation to market requirements and fluctuations and to reduce the burden on small and medium-sized enterprises. in particular, it would like to remove the requirement to keep a 'register' of bodies considered to be qualified investors and allow smaller regional banks to issue bonds without having to bear the costs of drawing up a prospectus. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) in line with the guidelines of the lisbon strategy, this proposal for a directive aims to establish the coordination rules to guarantee the free movement of goods in the field of public supply contracts and the achievement of freedom of establishment and freedom to provide services in the field of public works and services contracts. the proposal argues that non-discrimination, in particular on grounds of nationality, must be ensured and competition facilitated by better harmonisation of existing national procedures by opting for the most economically advantageous proposal. the authors of the proposal impose national rules, generally of a technical nature, which are subject to criteria of non-discrimination and compatibility with the objective of opening up public procurement. in doing so, however, it is forgotten that, while the transparency of public contracts is essential, these same contracts can be an important instrument of economic policy, even if they are awarded in a positive way in favour of small and mediumsized enterprises. regional development can be taken into account, the achievement of social and environmental objectives, such as working conditions and employment protection, or the production methods themselves can be encouraged by inserting special provisions in the contract. the most economically advantageous factors may not be related to the lowest price, but to job creation. which explains our rejection of the proposal.
in writing. - (pt) public procurement of works, services and supplies by open tender represents more than 14% of european gdp. despite this, the public procurement sector has benefited little from the creation of the internal market. while these directives are essential for the balance of the internal market and for crossborder procurement, the main advantage of these directives is rather the possibility of encouraging sustainable development. it is essential to include environmental and social objectives in public procurement. unfortunately, neither the proposal for a directive nor the report by our colleague mr zappalà gives public bodies the right (let alone the obligation) to choose a particular service or product in a public procurement on the basis of its sustainability. i therefore support the amendments to give such a right to public entities. it is difficult to accept that the eu recognises in its european strategy for sustainable development and in the commitments made in johannesburg that it is fundamental to integrate environmental costs into economic activity, and that it prohibits member states from basing their procurement policy on this same principle.
in writing. - (pt) this directive, in line with the guidelines set out in the lisbon strategy, is intended to complement the general directive laying down the coordination rules for public procurement by meeting the specific requirements of the procurement procedures in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors. these reports are largely part of the more general philosophy of liberalising and privatising public markets and services, which was given new impetus at the last spring council, particularly in these basic sectors. these reports also have a link with the forthcoming wto negotiations, not only because of the general agreement on tariffs and trade - gatt - but also because they address the issue of the opening up of public procurement, which is on the doha agenda and to which the eu attaches such importance. however, since these are sectors of major socioeconomic importance, we cannot leave them to the whims of the market, thus obeying the principle of open markets and non-discrimination and limiting the power of the member states and national administrations. that is why we reject this proposal as well.
in writing. - (pt) this common position of the council, although it falls short of some of the proposals made by the european parliament, improves the current legal framework for genetically modified organisms, even though we know that it will be a new attempt to justify the lifting of the moratorium, which should be maintained. the compromise reached, although far from perfect, ensures that all foodstuffs for human and animal consumption containing, based on or produced from gmos will now be subject to a more consistent and uniform authorisation procedure, and that this authorisation will be valid for a maximum of 10 years. in addition, mandatory labelling is extended to all genetically modified foodstuffs, irrespective of the detectability of gmos. the possibility for member states to take appropriate measures to prevent accidental contamination of conventional and organic crops by gmos is also enhanced, although effective control measures after the release of gmos into the environment are difficult to envisage in a context of the removal of borders and the free movement of goods. nevertheless, i regret that the thresholds for accidental or technically unavoidable contamination by gmos not yet authorised have been maintained at 0.5%, even for a transitional period. this is an area where 'zero tolerance' should apply.
in writing. - (pt) the problem of genetically modified organisms (gmos) raises seemingly contradictory questions. on the one hand, we have the question of scientific and technological research, particularly in terms of its practical application in the activities of daily life, for which we should continue our efforts to support and encourage. on the other hand, we are faced with the risks inherent in anyone whose work focuses on scientific research into food and the food standards that should be guaranteed to citizens - all of which require continuous attention and caution. my position on this report is based on the absence of conclusive evidence that such genetic mutations are absolutely harmless to human and animal health. gmos arouse in me the reserve and caution of any person concerned about the common good. i would, however, not like my position to be seen as an obstacle to scientific progress, which is always desirable and should not be subject to insurmountable legislative obstacles. however, i stress the need to respect the different life forms and the strict codes of ethics governing the handling and use of such delicate and complex substances.
in writing. - (pt) this regulation complements the community system for the authorisation and control of gmos: a mandatory labelling system for all genetically modified foodstuffs intended for human and animal consumption. we know that its approval is a further step towards lifting the current moratorium, which should be maintained in view of the risks associated with the release of gmos into the environment and the coexistence of gmos with conventional and organic crops. the us biotechnology industry is exerting strong pressure to open the european market to gmo imports and thereby to impose acceptance of these technologies, especially in developing countries. we have seen this in the recent speech by president bush at the meeting of the association of the biotechnology industry in washington. in his speech, the us president accused the eu of contributing to hunger in africa by blocking imports of gmos and demanding the lifting of eu restrictions. at the same time, the united states refuses to ratify the cartagena protocol on biosafety. the united states and the multinationals want to control not only farmers but also the agricultural and food policies of the member states. their joint pressure strengthens the prospect of lifting the moratorium and abolishing the traceability and labelling system. the latter thus becomes a first line of defence in the fight against and in the mobilisation of consumers and farmers against gmos and their release into the environment.
in writing. - (pt) in the absence of strong and integrated legislation on genetically modified organisms (gmos) that can offer guarantees to consumers and industry, marketing authorisation procedures at eu level have been suspended for three years now. i welcome the legislation we have just adopted on the traceability and labelling of gmos, as it facilitates the registration and tracing of the movements of gmos on the market, as well as food and feed produced from gmos. this will enable the consumer to make informed choices and the procedure for withdrawing a product from the market has been facilitated, should such a withdrawal be deemed necessary. however, the proposal for a directive contains certain provisions which may open the way to falsification, consumer deception and distortion of competition. rules should be clear and simple. therefore, i supported the amendment proposals which aim at: enhancing detectability; ensuring coexistence between gmo and non-gmo crops; implementing traceability and corresponding labelling exclusively for gmos and products for which the presence of genetically modified dna or genetically modified proteins has been detected, and not for all products.
in writing. - (pt) we believe that it is essential to develop measures that help reduce the volume of municipal and industrial waste and promote its recycling and reuse, using rational and integrated solutions. packaging plays a particularly important role in this process, as do incentives for the use of biodegradable materials. however, the definition and implementation of such measures will have to take account of the reality and interests of each country. it is therefore difficult to understand why european rules should be loosely transposed into different national laws when they do not take account of differences between member states. therefore, while i share the concerns expressed in this report, particularly in the development of preventive measures, i cannot help but wonder about the viability of the proposed timelines and targets for product recycling. i would reiterate that the effectiveness of an environmental policy depends on the will and efforts of the national institutions, which are responsible for drawing up the policy and mobilising resources, but also for directly involving industry in the reduction of packaging waste. however, the public also has a role to play in protecting and enhancing the environment. the latter requires a continuous effort to educate, raise awareness and mobilize people about the current problems and the solutions to be put in place to solve them.
in writing. - (pt) the first and most important aspect of the policy for the recovery and recycling of materials is prevention. prevention of packaging waste requires the producer to base his decision on the type and quantity of materials used on a life cycle analysis of the products and to quantify its environmental impact from design to disposal. in this way, he can internalize environmental costs into the final price of the product. unfortunately, the directive proposed by the commission has not gone far enough in waste prevention. the second key requirement is the definition of legally binding objectives. in this respect, the directive is more ambitious in that it sets targets for the recovery and recycling of packaging waste, in particular for the following materials: glass, paper, plastic, metals and wood. however, these objectives can only guarantee behavioural change if they appear credible and thus achievable. i therefore support the objectives set out in the common position and i disagree with the objectives put forward by the rapporteur. i particularly object to the proposal to bring forward the recycling and recovery deadlines for portugal, greece and ireland from 2012 to 2009. it should be recalled that these three member states have characteristics which make it more difficult to achieve the objectives of recycling and recovery of packaging waste, in particular in terms of the dispersion of the territory (outermost regions) and the populations.
in writing. - (pt) i agree with the rapporteur's position in general. fortunately, there is a broad consensus among all citizens on this issue, expressed in particular by the almost unanimous vote at first reading. it is essential to promote the recovery of packaging waste, its recycling where possible and the prevention of its production. the union's strategic objectives set out in lisbon and, more particularly, the environmental dimension added and transformed into sustainable development in gothenburg, make it compulsory to adopt measures and policies capable of combating waste and environmental degradation. it is recognised that environmental protection is, in the long run, the only guarantee of protection for citizens and consumers. i must, however, like several colleagues from the committee on the environment, public health and consumer policy, express my concern about the proposed shortening of the time-limits for member states to transpose the proposal for a directive. it considers that a more realistic approach, such as that suggested in the common position, is preferable, depending on the treatment, recovery and recycling units that actually exist on the ground. the achievement of the objectives, which are of interest to all of us, requires a credible and sustainable strategy.
in writing. - (pt) we consider that the continuation of the fight against the destruction of the ozone layer, the greenhouse effect and the global warming of the planet that results from it is a priority and an urgency. to combat this, either we must increase the use of alternative and renewable energy sources, which enable us to reduce the consumption of fossil fuels, or we must implement measures to reduce emissions from polluting industries and their effects - which requires investment in research and the application of new technologies - in order to contribute to the objectives set out in the kyoto protocol. however, we reiterate our rejection of the creation of a "trade in emission allowances" - which would make it a commodity - allowing the most developed countries to buy "pollution allowances" from the least developed countries, guaranteeing the former their status as "privileged polluters" and favouring the non-development of the latter. moreover, recent data from the united nations indicate a trend towards increased emissions from industrialised countries. this report is part of this perspective, accepting greenhouse gas emission trading, which is seen by some as a tool to achieve the objectives of the kyoto protocol. we think that is not the right approach.
in writing. - (pt) i welcome this proposal for a directive, which is the first step towards the creation of an international market for the trading of greenhouse gas emission allowances, an area in which the union has been a pioneer - before the international regime provided for by the kyoto protocol came into force in 2008. the excellent work of the rapporteur has made an important contribution to this process. the directive will create a market for greenhouse gas emissions within the eu by introducing emission allowances for industrial complexes, which will be allocated by the member states' authorities. the amendment proposed by the commission is particularly welcome. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the allocation of emission allowances for the period 2005-2012. the adoption of this directive will mark the beginning of a new era in the culture of responsibility, both for business and for the state, bringing together operators and politicians on a path that citizens are keen to see them take.
commission. - mr president, i have tried to do this as quickly as possible. it is very welcome that parliament sometimes gets ahead of the agenda. it changes our usual reflexes and i'm very happy about it. i thank you for inviting me to take stock of the important timetable for the fifth wto ministerial conference in cancun in september. our position on the substance is well known: we want the doha development agenda to succeed, pursuing three fundamental objectives for the european union. the first objective is to support economic growth, which we need in europe and in the world. the second concerns the framing of more open markets through multilateral rules, to allow for a better articulation between our commercial interests and the values of our societies. the third objective is the integration of developing countries into the international trading system, which is the main objective of this round of negotiations. we do not conceive of it in rhetorical terms, but in very concrete terms. each of the parts of the negotiating programme must have added value for development. we are only weeks away from the cancun conference; the time is therefore running out for the success of this conference and the preparatory process must be intensified. the necessary political impetus should be given in several areas, namely agriculture, access to industrial markets, investment, competition, trade facilitation, public procurement. in all the areas i have just mentioned, arrangements must be made to prepare for the final negotiation. in other areas, such as geographical indications, the link between trade and development, and dispute settlement, we hope to obtain, at the cancun conference, initial results, probably modest, which will have to be amplified in the final agreement. so there is still a lot of work to be done. we feel that these objectives are achievable and that the complexity of the issues is not the issue, but rather the political will. this is true of a subject which i have not mentioned and which will be important for the cancun conference: the problem of access to medicines in poor countries. on this point, as you know, the united states blocked the decision last december, despite the balance we had reached around the world trade organisation table. there seems to be some development, but it is not confirmed and it is clear that the us position will have to change in order to get a comprehensive agreement in cancun. let us consider each of these without going into too much detail. first, there is agriculture. we need a complete set of procedures and a date for the submission of tenders. in this respect, the agreement reached last week at the agriculture council strengthens the hand of your negotiators. this agreement clearly marks the beginning of a new era. whether for farmers, consumers or taxpayers, this progress will lead to better use of resources, greater transparency, improved quality and protection of the environment, and animal welfare, which are the various concerns expressed on this point. this reform also sends a clear signal to the rest of the world that we are largely turning our backs on an old system which has generated certain distortions of trade. the new agricultural policy is more favourable to trade, as the developing countries wanted. so, after the opinion of your parliament, the agriculture ministers have granted your negotiators, franz fischler and myself, a credit line which we will not make public - we are not naive - but which we will use within the limits of what is necessary and justified. this credit line will only be opened if we are sure of obtaining counterparts. i am thinking, for example, of the disciplines that need to be put in place for other support systems, in particular the american system, which we know has a detrimental effect on trade, and i am also thinking of the protection of geographical indications. for all this, counterparts will be needed, no one should be mistaken on this point. there is no question of unilateral disarmament, as my colleague franz fischler has very well said. we have done our duty in the agricultural field. it is now up to our partners to take the initiative, particularly the americans, who have reintroduced a system of distortions in recent years. secondly, access to the market for industrial products. this is a major objective of the doha agenda. trade must be as open as possible so that the greatest number of people can benefit from these advantages. our aim is to ensure that developing countries have better access to our markets, that is to say, those of the developed countries, but also to enable a significant reduction in the barriers to trade which may exist between developing countries. the importance of the south-south dimension of market access should not be lost sight of. thirdly, the so-called singapore issues, namely competition, investment, trade facilitation and transparency of public procurement. we must determine the terms of the negotiations in order to launch them formally. this objective remains one of the union's priorities. these issues are inseparable from the single commitment. we will resist the temptation to remove one or the other, because it would upset the balance of the whole cycle. we must therefore agree on the modalities. fourthly, the issues of importance to developing countries, namely special and differential treatment and implementation. we are seeking to increase flexibility with developing countries, in the direction of their desires and wishes, without creating a kind of two-speed wto. in this respect we are ready to move forward, to draw up a framework agreement or even a set of guiding principles to be adopted in cancun, in order to ensure greater attention to these issues, i repeat, which are important for the developing countries. as regards trade and the environment, which are sensitive issues in this house, we should take a decision at the cancun conference on the wto observer status of multilateral environmental agreements and on the deepening of discussions on other environmental issues. you know our programme in this area: greater coherence between multilateral environmental agreements and international trade rules. this is why we have asked, for example, that the secretariats of multilateral agreements and unep, which acts as the secretariat for certain types of multilateral agreements, be granted observer status at the special sessions of the committee on trade and environment, which take place in geneva and are devoted to this issue. we also believe that the cancun ministerial conference should decide to further discuss voluntary environmental labelling. this is an opportunity for constructive dialogue in favour of trade in environmentally friendly products, especially those from developing countries. i would like to conclude by saying a few words about our working methods, that is to say, the relationship between your parliament and the commission in this area. as always, we are working closely with parliament to prepare the cancun conference. we have, in a sense, anticipated a number of positive outcomes of the convention in this area, since the text currently on the table proposes to give parliament almost the same rights as the council in matters of trade policy, namely co-decision for the adoption of laws implementing trade policy, the right to information throughout the negotiation of international agreements, the right to give a favourable opinion on the outcome of the negotiation - which corresponds to the alignment that those of you who have been looking at this issue were seeking. so i think our joint efforts have paid off. it is no doubt that in some respects the text is still a bit muddled and that it can be improved. i think there are still some pockets of consensus, which some of you have continued to rightly question. nevertheless, progress is being made and european democracy will clearly win, if the text of the convention on this point is not weakened by the intergovernmental conference. it is in this spirit that we will work together for the cancun conference. as you know, a delegation of members of the european parliament will be with us in cancun, as they were in seattle and doha. i'm personally delighted. we also support the idea of a parliamentary conference of the wto, because the parliamentary contribution can only strengthen the legitimacy of the negotiator. to achieve the results i have just described, which, as i said, are ambitious and achievable, we must work hard until the cancun conference. we'll do it with you. this dialogue and these debates are necessary, because we know that we will not have your support if we do not. that is why we are looking forward to the resolution which, as i understand it, will be voted on tomorrow.
- mr president, the difficulties at this crucial stage of the negotiations leading up to cancún do not allow for an easy ministerial meeting next september. these difficulties are largely due to the present world trade system, its tendency towards liberalization and its often negative effects on the fragile economies of the least developed countries. north and south have not benefited equally from this system. it is therefore essential to give full consideration to the most important issues raised by these countries, and it is essential to put a stop to this trend, at least until an effective assessment of their results is made. the development agenda cannot be a meaningless designation, but must set an unmistakable will and direction. it is also essential that the clause on special and differentiated treatment for developing countries, with which the european union is to establish a strategic alliance, be given real and substantial substance. we all know the key issues at stake. i shall confine myself to brief notes on three of them: medicines may be or are already a key issue. the united states has blocked the agreement, and has been putting pressure on some countries to give up the right to import generic medicines. it would be appropriate to stress and emphasise that the right to health should prevail over any commercial interests; the commission has also been active in the field of the environment, and has recently launched a new programme for the protection of the environment. the dramatic increase in agricultural subsidies for the united states does not make it any easier to reach an agreement, but the european union can still take an important step, in particular by contributing to the eventual abolition of all export subsidies; finally, as regards access to the industrial market, the textile and clothing sector deserves particular attention, given its vulnerability and the concessions already made, especially in the bilateral context. we can accept some specific measures in this area aimed exclusively at the least developed countries, but always taking account of this important group and its potential for employment.
- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to leave you with two notes on the strategy for cancún next september. the first is that the doha declaration is very clear about ensuring the best balance between the trade and non-trade aspects associated with trade. in this respect, issues such as the precautionary principle, food safety, the basic rules on gmos and respect for designations of origin and geographical indications are decisive. it must be said that it is completely unacceptable for a number of third countries to use our geographical indications and designations of origin linked to a culture, a territory and a history as generic or semi-generic products. the production and sale of products under the designation 'porto wine', 'wood', 'champagne', 'parma ham' or 'manche cheese' or other in the united states, australia, canada and new zealand is unacceptable because it means the misappropriation of a commercial advantage that does not belong to them. the second point is to remind ourselves that the recent reform of the cap gives us all the conditions for a more aggressive stance in the negotiations, not only in defending the whole dossier of protection of geographical indications and non-trade concerns, but also to try to impose a wide range of rules, namely disciplining export credits, public trading companies and the abuse of food aid and the de minimis clause; to get all the rich countries to give the 49 poorest countries in the world the same conditions that the eu gave with the initiative 'everything but arms'; to make a clear distinction between the developing countries and the poorest countries in the world, which is no longer realistic to put on the same level as countries like india, malaysia, indonesia or south american countries and dramatically poor countries like mozambique, chad or burkina faso, or most of the acp countries. in addition to agriculture, this is also the case, for example, in textiles and clothing, where the complete opening up of the community market to products from the first group of countries would destroy hundreds of thousands of jobs in the european union, particularly in the poorest and most backward countries such as portugal, greece and spain, or the new countries of eastern europe. it is therefore hoped that cancún will provide a fundamental balance between all these dimensions, or else globalisation will be rejected by our society.
- mr president, i too would like to reaffirm, first of all, my total readiness to make possible all proposals which are really aimed at improving cooperation and optimising the use of airspace, ensuring higher levels of safety. however, as has already been pointed out, particularly by commissioner loyola de palacio, this is a delicate matter - technically, institutionally and politically - and it requires a great deal of realism and a great deal of common sense. in my speech here last september, at the time of the first reading debate on the organisation of the single sky, i had the opportunity to mention the aspects which concerned me most in the commission's drafts and in the proposals also adopted in the committee on transport. i cannot help but stress that these concerns have largely disappeared in the presence of the fairly balanced common position adopted by the council, especially as regards the functional blocks. and that is why i cannot help but distance myself once again from some of the amendments which have been adopted in the committee on transport, since they are totally at odds with the consensus reached in the council and also with the commission's now more balanced position, which i of course welcome. i think it is really untenable, in particular, to insist on a proposal to create functional blocks which override the will of the member states, because the community has no competence in the field of airspace management or any other, and, very especially, it has no such competence when the military side is involved, as is the case in this case. furthermore, there are no known or foreseen to date any irreconcilable conflicts between member states in the definition of cross-border airspace blocks. the european union has already adopted a declaration guaranteeing the necessary cooperation between the civil and military components in order to fully implement the concept of flexible use of airspace.
- mr president, commissioner, we are today considering, at second reading, a package of proposals aimed at creating a single european sky. i fully agree with the aims of the proposals under consideration, but i have some concerns about their content, which i cannot but express to this house. these concerns relate, on the one hand, to the absence of a legal basis within the common transport policy to deal with certain matters, including those of a military nature, and, on the other, to the excessive and disproportionate limitation of the sovereign power of the member states over their airspace. in this context, let me make three points which i consider to be fundamental. the first concerns what i consider to be an attempt by the commission to make the airspace of the member states a community space by immediately creating a single european flight region on the basis of which so-called 'functional blocks' would be created. on this point i fully support the council's common position that the determination of functional blocks is a matter for the member states alone and cannot be changed by the european union. secondly, and on military matters, the commission's proposals provide for the possibility of imposing rules on the management and use of airspace for military activities. once again, i agree with the common position adopted by the council, which seems to me much more balanced and balanced in that it recognises that a more efficient use of airspace depends on closer cooperation between civil and military entities, that is to say on the uniform application within the single european sky of the concept of flexible use of airspace. this objective should always be pursued in accordance with national competences. finally, i would like to refer to the question of airspace management and express my total disagreement with an approach which tends to equate this management with any economic service comparable to the liberalised telecommunications or transport markets, under the supervision of a european regulatory body. i therefore believe that each member state should be able to appoint the service provider within its airspace with complete freedom, under the supervision of national supervisory authorities and without subordination to any other entities.
- the regulation in question has as its stated aim the protection of air passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or considerable delay of flights. however, the proposal under discussion does not fully meet this objective and the amendments tabled weaken the council's common position, which in some respects is already a step back from the commission's proposal. we are aware of the current difficulties facing airlines (and therefore believe that a balanced solution must be found); but we cannot accept that this argument excludes passengers travelling under package tours from the scope of the regulation, diminishes their protection in the event of flight cancellations or removes the possibility for the passenger to opt for the right to reimbursement or re-routing in the event of a long delay. we acknowledge the existence of 'extraordinary circumstances' which may lead to the conclusion that airlines will not always be responsible for flight delays or cancellations. however, such 'circumstances' should be limited to, inter alia, weather or safety problems, in order to avoid that passengers' interests may be prejudiced by purely economic or commercial criteria.
- mr president, the notoriety of the mandate of the ecb under the presidency of mr duisenberg is acknowledged, and it is respectable that this institution is convinced that its monetary policy is the most appropriate for the short-term recovery of the european economy. the bank's recent changes in monetary strategy are generally regarded as very positive and as a real step forward. it is, however, undeniable that europe's economic recovery is not visible on the immediate horizon and that all the policy changes that have been developed have been anticipated by the markets and directed towards functions and balances that, in the short term, can contribute little to that recovery. in fact, gdp growth in europe is forecast to reach around 0.7% in 2003 and to grow by only 1.6% of gdp in 2004, meaning that the ecb is cutting its growth forecasts by 0.9% in 2003 and 0.8% of gdp in 2004 in one fell swoop. in the face of the false dilemma of growth or stability, the ecb cannot resign itself to its main institutional design - price stability - while ignoring the fragility and contradictions of policies aimed at achieving other objectives such as economic growth and employment; the commission's proposal for a directive on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of their employer is a very good one. the bank also has good reason to believe that the starting point for monetary policy has been wrongly set at 2% inflation and is not in line with the potential growth of the european economy. the european central bank must therefore help to find answers and solutions to the following fundamental questions: have the structural reforms carried out in the economies of most european countries been sufficient? if not, what further contribution can monetary and fiscal policies make to overcoming the current economic stagnation? are the current monetary policy constraints and fiscal constraints imposed by the stability and growth pact which the ecb has supported compatible with the necessary reform of the european social model, without calling into question their essence and the distinctive nature which they assume in the framework of european development policy? does the current appreciation of the euro fully correspond to the fundamentals of the european economy and is it a proactive element of economic recovery or, on the contrary, can it trigger a serious deflationary process? what can the ecb contribute to overcoming the structural reform gap needed to achieve the objectives of the lisbon strategy? will these objectives be achievable within the time limits initially envisaged with the monetary and fiscal policies that have been developed and with the apparent choice of national states for a minimum level of economic coordination? the level of the ecb's responsibility in the face of the economic crisis and the active cooperation to overcome it depend on the balance of choices and the effectiveness of the responses to the problems mentioned. without prejudice to the positive balance sheet of the bank's activities, as the rapporteur, mr blokland, does, the ep must, within its functions and powers, draw attention to the problems that exist and encourage all the institutions to overcome them.
- madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to focus my speech on the euro payments area. the introduction of the single currency was a huge success, but if there is general satisfaction with the introduction of banknotes and coins, the same cannot be said for the functioning of the euro payments area. in fact, the euro has been our currency since 1999. for four and a half years the euro has been the currency of eleven countries of the union and the national currencies have been nothing more than sub-multiples still in circulation. but the european banking system, during this period, was resistant to the recognition of this new reality. there are 12 countries with the same currency but the banks functioned as if it were an international zone. the euro payments area had no real existence. it is only a year since electronic cards were able to be used in the euro area as well as in the issuing countries themselves, and only this week it has become possible to make bank transfers under the same conditions as those applied within each of the respective countries. and while this measure is excellent for citizens and smes doing business in the euro area, the limit per transaction of eur 12 500 is ridiculous and unjustifiable. if there is a technical infrastructure to transfer the same currency from one country to another and if the cost is minimal because it is a virtual transaction that is processed by computers, why is there such a low limit? the cost of a 12 500 euro operation is the same as that of a 50 000 euro operation, as will be possible from 2006, or would it be that of a 100 000 euro or more operation? i would even say that forcing a company to make 10 partial transactions of eur 12 500 to make a payment of eur 125 000 only increases the costs for companies and banks. i therefore think, and i conclude, that it is essential to make the euro area work effectively by reducing bank charges to the levels they are at national level. do not forget that, as far as currency is concerned, our country is the euro zone. what does the commission intend to do to improve the functioning of the euro payments area?

in writing. - (pt) this report stresses the need to make gender budgeting a systematic tool to integrate the gender perspective into community and national budgetary procedures. i was convinced that i should support him. gender budgeting means, in the context of budgetary policies, that revenues and expenditure are assessed and restructured in all programmes and projects to ensure that women's priorities and needs are taken into account, with the ultimate aim of achieving gender equality. a campaign to raise awareness among the public, national governments and parliaments should be launched, including through the development of a guide on the instruments and methods for introducing a gender perspective in public budgets. finally, i agree with the creation of a european network of gender budgeting subjects and experts, which would be linked to the network of parliamentary committees responsible for equal opportunities. this would help to develop and disseminate good methods and good practice.
in writing. - (pt) the need to design public budgets in a gender perspective with the ultimate aim of achieving gender equality in practice stems from the fact that we consider the budget not to be a neutral instrument but to reflect the division of power existing in society. the budget is therefore the result of political choices and becomes a key instrument for defining the model of social and economic development and the criteria for redistribution within society. thus, any equality policy must be reflected in the way budgets are drawn up at the most diverse levels. as the rapporteur points out, in order to achieve the principle of equality, governments and public administrations must analyse gender issues, reduce inequalities between men and women, taking into account the fact that men and women play different roles in society and the economy and that, therefore, economic policies have a different impact on them. by voting in favour of this report, we also underline the importance of the implementation of the beijing platform for action and the provisions to be defined in the budget of the european union itself, with a view to implementing the proposals made in mrs ghilardotti's report.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate mr lisi on his excellent report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of a flight. i support this report, particularly the option of a single distance criterion for compensation in the event of delays or for the passenger to be seated in a lower class. i would also like to stress that compliance with the measures provided for in this regulation, in particular with regard to compensation in the event of non-compliance, implies that the organisation of air carriers will have to be seriously and profoundly reviewed, which is why it would be appropriate to extend the deadline for the entry into force of this regulation by a few months.
in writing. - (pt) food additives are already regulated. apart from sweeteners and colours, the bulk of these additives are largely derived from natural raw materials. these substances - the e's appearing on the packaging of foodstuffs - are necessary for processing and processing by the agri-food industry; they are used, for example, to preserve and stabilise mixtures, to enhance the taste or to improve the appearance of the product. hence the importance of this report in the wider discussion on food safety, as various food and veterinary crises (bse, foot and mouth disease, sewage sludge, dioxins, nitrofurans, etc.) have significantly undermined consumer confidence and made more evident the need to change the production model. consumer perception of food additives has deteriorated, despite the risk assessment and the concept of the acceptable daily intake. today, the scientific and technological means exist to improve production methods and to protect against inappropriate use, guaranteeing the precautionary principle. stricter requirements on labelling and packaging are needed to ensure the necessary information. we therefore agree with the rapporteur. the commission should undertake a general assessment of the use of food additives, basing future authorisations on three criteria: technological necessity, a high level of protection of human health and labelling that does not mislead the consumer.
in writing. - (pt) the consultation procedure under review allows the european parliament to assess the needs of the eu budget for 2004 and to reach agreement, inter alia, on the level of expenditure on agriculture and fisheries. against the background of enlargement, this budget advocates greater economic, social and territorial cohesion, while showing a very limited increase in appropriations. i should like to comment on some of the financial forecasts for agriculture and fisheries. i welcome the significant increase in amounts, especially for rural development, although this increase is mainly for future members. the budgetary efforts devoted to health protection, consumer protection, food safety and environmental criteria for quality agriculture are also positive. i wholeheartedly support the creation of a special heading for farmers affected by emergencies and disasters such as foot-and-mouth disease, swine fever and other diseases. as in the case of the common agricultural policy, this budget shows a relative increase in the amounts for fisheries. however, i do not agree with the sharp cuts in research and the structural funds for fisheries. this is why we must strengthen the control and use of each member state's quotas, avoiding penalising those who respect them and letting offenders get away with it.
in writing. - (pt) it is worrying to note that the implementation of commitments at internal policy level fell to 10% on 30 april 2003, from 24% in 2002, and that this is due to the budget chapter related to research and technological development, which is a priority given the weaknesses of the eu. there is also a downward trend in the implementation of commitments in the social fields, in particular in the chapters relating to the social dimension and employment, education and youth, whereas these priority areas already have low resources. in addition to a lack of political will, the causes of this situation include bureaucracy, opacity and rigid rules on the use of the amounts. the argument of low execution cannot be used to justify cuts in sensitive areas. it is not acceptable that amounts relating to the social dimension and employment are not needed at a time when unemployment is rising in the eu. i regret that the rapporteur has not dealt specifically with the fisheries issue, in particular the programme for the conversion of the fleet formerly active in morocco and the lines relating to the social dialogue with the sector. this would have been important in view of the reduction envisaged in the preliminary draft budget for 2004 and the lack of a definition by the council of the financing of the reform of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. - (pt) in the context of its power to monitor the implementation of the eu budget, the european parliament analyses the amounts for 2003 in this report. it aims to ensure that eu financial resources are used effectively to achieve the objectives set out in the policies and to ensure continuity with the budget for the following financial year. i therefore share with great concern the conclusions of this report, which once again draws attention to the problem of committed and unused funds. this is particularly worrying when one knows that part of these funds are covered by the n+2 rule (which requires that the funds committed are used by the member states within 2 years after the year of the initial authorisation, otherwise the funds are lost). this situation becomes even more unacceptable and shocking when it occurs in the application of the structural funds and in the internal policies of the eu. i therefore support the presentation of a transparent, frequent and detailed statement of commitments not fulfilled, cancelled and lost due to non-use, as well as an assessment of the financial impact of losses. this valuable data will have to be presented by budget heading and by member state. i also support the simplification of the rules for submitting applications for structural funds, in particular through improvements in the timing and application of the funds. these measures will have to be adopted during the mid-term review of the structural funds.
in writing. - (pt) it is understandable that little importance is attached to the european parliament's reports on monetary policy. instead of engaging in a genuine critical analysis of the conduct of monetary policy, they repeat the same arguments, regardless of the economic climate. it is therefore not a happy conclusion that the ecb has responded correctly to economic and financial developments. the whole thing is still wrapped up in the dogmas of service, support for the stability pact and flexibility of the labour market. it is well known that a rigid monetary policy implies that adjustments made to overcome economic shocks have an impact on wages and employment, influencing domestic demand and increasing inequality, poverty and social exclusion. it can only be seen that the current eu recession and the differences in inflation rates show that a single monetary policy cannot effectively meet the needs of member states with different levels of economic development. i therefore reiterate the need for a thorough review of the monetary and fiscal policy guidelines, the rigidity of which has not only contributed to the failure to exploit the potential for economic growth in recent years, but is also the main cause of the current recessionary period, which is accompanied by a worsening of unemployment. that is why we voted against it.
in writing. - (pt) i deeply regret that parliament did not ask for a report on the first results of the introduction of euro banknotes and coins, as requested in my first motion for a resolution on the effects of the introduction of the euro (b5-640/2002), which is annexed to today's report. while underlining the success of the whole operation and stressing the expanded competences for the euro area, this report acknowledges its disappointment at the inflationary pressures of the changeover to the euro, especially in the services sector, and calls for an investigation into financial irregularities, just as i do in my resolution. the commission and the ecb acknowledge that the impact was higher than the 0.2% forecast but significantly lower than the effects reported by consumer organisations and by some national central banks' inflation information. however, the report does address the evolution of bank fee and commission payments in the euro area. a full assessment is needed to identify excessive increases, including in domestic payments, and illegal charges for cross-border payments, which penalise consumers and increase the cost of transactions. the banks cannot claim that consumers and smes are paying for their lack of profit on foreign exchange transactions. i therefore welcome the adoption of my amendment.

mr president, the serious forest fires which have broken out in portugal this year have also affected agricultural and urban areas, destroyed houses, factories, schools, electricity and telephone lines and other equipment, caused the death of 18 people, left many families homeless and without any property, killed livestock and game, deprived some 45 000 people of income and wages. it was a huge catastrophe that aggravated portugal's already difficult economic and social conditions, and we have therefore asked the european union for support and solidarity from the very beginning. according to recent estimates, more than 400,000 hectares have burned, representing about 5% of our territory and 11% of the forest area, and in some municipalities more than 80% of the forest area has been burned, with estimated losses of more than one billion euros. this situation requires special support measures, and the budget proposed by the commission is clearly insufficient, as commissioner michel barnier said during his visit to portugal. in addition to the condolences and solidarity with the families of the victims and all those affected by this catastrophe, in addition to the appreciation of the efforts of the firefighters and the population for their determined action in fighting the fires despite the scarce resources available, it is necessary that the amount to be mobilised by the european union solidarity fund be at least equivalent to the request made by the portuguese government, i.e. more than 52 million euros. but the gravity of the situation requires that there be other extraordinary complementary measures, both at the level of the reprogramming of the structural funds and through the various existing community programmes, making the rigid processing dimensions and difficult to combat. this also requires more effective prevention measures to be promoted at community, national and local level and greater attention to public health in europe. the common agricultural policy itself, leading to the disappearance of thousands of farms and farmers in recent years, particularly in my country, has contributed to the complete dismantling of the traditional relationship of complementarity between forest area and agricultural area in the areas of small land, increasing the desertification of the rural world and thus contributing to the promotion of conditions which favour the existence of large-scale fires. the cap revision measures will tend to aggravate this situation, which requires a rethinking of the measures taken. we call on the commission to continue to work with the national authorities, both in minimising the environmental impact and in supporting the affected populations, but also in reforestation, supporting all fires and stress that this disaster shows the irrationality of the criteria of the stability pact in relation to the socioeconomic reality of portugal, when, in a situation requiring heavy public investment, it is conditioning it. we therefore urge the commission and the council to review the stability pact, in particular by immediately excluding from the budget deficit calculation all public expenditure and investment related to this catastrophe.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the context of this joint debate on economic and social cohesion, we are given the mastorakis report on the second interim report of the commission on european cohesion policy. i would like to express my support for the ideas expressed by the rapporteur, whom i would like to thank for the outstanding quality of his work. for a member state like portugal, regional policy and cohesion policy have played and continue to play a key role in its development and full integration into the european union. i am glad that certain european regions, including some in portugal, have left the cohesion funds on their own merits. it is without doubt the best example of the success of this community policy. however, it should be borne in mind that while there are already significant differences in the levels of development between some european regions, with enlargement these differences will become even more marked. in order to achieve the full realisation of its cohesion policy and thus reduce regional development disparities, the european union should continue its support to existing member states in a sustained manner. and at the same time, develop the regions of the future member states in a balanced way. in the face of this dual challenge, the european union has an obligation to provide the funds needed to meet the new needs of this situation. the current ceiling of 0.45% of community gdp can therefore never be subject to any budgetary cuts. for this reason, and because cohesion policy has proved to be a success in portugal, i reject the renationalisation of this development instrument. i welcome the fact that the commission has created a transitional system for regions subject to the statistical action of enlargement which are no longer eligible as a result of the opening up of objective 1 to the less developed regions. finally, i cannot but support the creation of a new objective 2 based on criteria of regional competitiveness, in accordance with the guidelines of the lisbon summit.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i shall confine myself in this debate to highlighting the paradox facing economic and social cohesion policy. the paradox is also well established in both reports under discussion, and i congratulate my fellow rapporteurs on the excellent work they have done. in fact, while the challenge of enlargement is the greatest ever for this community policy, it is easy to see a weak and even reticent political will towards the urgent need to revitalize this fundamental pillar of the european construction. instead of revitalizing, we sometimes talk of renationalizing, instead of more resources and more solidarity, we talk of national selfishness. but despite this environment, i have not yet lost hope in visionary and supportive political responses of the kind that were given on the occasion of the great european challenges of the completion of the great internal market and the achievement of economic and monetary union. so, on the occasion of each of these challenges, the resources allocated to economic and social cohesion policy have been doubled. now, with enlargement, this ambition is needed to meet the enormous regional imbalances that enlargement has created, particularly because the future solidarity policy will also have to take account of the cohesion deficit that still exists in the present european union of 15 countries, a deficit that is even at risk of worsening as a result of the dynamics induced by enlargement and the likely unequal distribution of its benefits. it will make perfect sense that whoever gains the most from enlargement will also contribute the most to the financing of european solidarity. but this hope is also based on the commission's position, and in particular on that of commissioner michel barnier, who, fortunately, against all odds, has not given up his belief that an effective economic and social cohesion policy at european level is possible, with a minimum level of financial resources, more simplified, decentralized and effective and with a greater contribution to the objectives of cohesion by the other community policies, a cohesion policy which must improve its response to the needs of island regions, mountain regions, regions with low population density and, of course, the outermost regions.
the rapporteur. - mr president, the draft we are going to vote on in the co-decision procedure concerns a fundamental change in the vat system applicable to travel agencies. the need to adopt this legislation urgently arises from the profound changes in the tourism sector over the last thirty years and from the numerous exceptions and derogations currently in force in a sector where profit margins are very low. the main changes concern the possibility for companies to deduct vat when attending conferences or incentive tourism and electronic bookings, where it is necessary to protect european travel agencies from competition from outside the community. i only hope that the unanimity which has been achieved in parliament's committee on economic and monetary affairs will also be achieved in the council.
in writing. - (pt) i have decided to support this report, which aims to replace several previous directives on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens or mutagens at work. as the legal services department advisory group noted, this proposal respects the spirit of the codified texts by simply compiling them in a single document and including the formal changes required by the codification process. i think that this 'codification' is an appropriate measure to encourage better regulations on worker safety, which is essential in the european context. it is clear that risks such as those discussed in this proposal, which are so often hidden, must be avoided. in other words, it is better to avoid them than to make changes in response to these dangers. better to prevent than to compensate. this proposal clearly goes in that direction. in line with the lisbon agreement, it is not only aimed at more jobs but also at better quality jobs.
in writing. - (pt) i welcome the unanimous approval of this recommendation by the committee on constitutional affairs. as has been stressed, care must be taken to ensure that the use of 'comitology' does not detract from our faithful respect for the co-legislative powers and legislative procedure of parliament. this will prevent the subsequent adoption of legislative provisions by means of implementing measures other than the co-decision procedure. the task is primarily to establish a system enabling parliament to exercise correctly the powers of control conferred on it and, if necessary, to challenge any implementing measure with which it disagrees, where those measures originate in the codecision procedure. parliament has always advocated greater transparency in the work of the various committees, in particular by emphasising the need to forward to it the agendas and minutes of committee meetings, attendance lists, draft implementing measures submitted to committees, provisional timetables and voting results. in addition, all committee documents - except for classified documents - should be made available to parliament and the general public.
in writing. - (pt) in recent years, all aspects of the tourism sector have undergone profound changes. observers have noted an increasing number and variety of services offered and an increasing number and variety of customers. in view of these historical changes, it has become imperative to carry out a rapid revision of the special vat regime applicable to travel agencies in force since 1977. i therefore wish to express my full support for parliament's report and congratulate the rapporteur, mrs torres marques. i fully agree with the approval of the changes to the vat system for travel agencies, which involve taxing tour operators established outside the eu when they offer their services to european consumers. this measure will eliminate unfair competition affecting the european tourism sector. it also deals a blow to tax evasion by european companies claiming to be established outside the eu and not charging vat to consumers. when these adjustments have been made, the european tourism sector will be able to compete on a fair and equal basis in the highly competitive world travel market, creating a situation which can only have positive consequences for our consumers. tourism in the algarve can therefore only benefit from this new system.
in writing. - (pt) in recent years the labour market has changed substantially, which requires a change in our information collection procedures. the labour force sample survey proposed in this report will enable us to take even more effective action to create jobs. the features of this survey, which include six new variables and the option to differentiate between structural variables, will help us to better understand the labour market and to define future economic and employment policies. in order to achieve the objectives set out in the lisbon strategy - in particular in terms of employment and labour flexibility - and with a view to the entry into force of so many provisions related to the european employment strategy, i voted in favour of this report, which endorses the commission's proposal to strengthen this important survey tool.
in writing. - (pt) in voting in favour of this report on the organisation of a sample survey of the labour force in the community on a quarterly basis, i would like to highlight the six new variables introduced: the continuous collection of wages or salaries, the responsibility of management, the participation of public employment services in the search for the current position, overtime during the reference week, the contract with a temporary employment agency and the lack of childcare services. all these variables will improve the availability of comparable statistics on the level of employment and unemployment trends and describe the structure of labour market participation of individuals and households. this greater understanding will undoubtedly contribute to achieving the objectives of the european employment strategy and to more effectively adopting measures implementing the lisbon strategy. these measures are eagerly awaited by european citizens.
in writing. - (pt) as i said in my explanation of vote on the frassoni report, i agree with this reform of what is known as the 'comitology' procedure. greater transparency in the exercise of the commission's implementing powers and adequate scrutiny by parliament will undoubtedly enable the community to adopt intervention measures more effectively and appropriately. greater involvement at this stage of the procedure, rather than mere control, will give citizens better guarantees as to the pursuit of the objectives and principles prevailing when the basic instruments are being designed. this participation will also ensure greater convergence with the intentions of the legislators.
in writing. - (pt) in order to meet the political wish expressed in tampere and laeken to apply the principle of mutual recognition of decisions in criminal matters ('which should become the cornerstone of judicial cooperation in both civil and criminal matters within the union'), we approved at this plenary session several proposals containing measures to implement this principle. in this context, the principle of non bis in idem is undoubtedly one of the urgent preconditions for the mutual recognition of decisions in criminal matters and for the strengthening of legal certainty within the union. this is a general principle of criminal procedure, which contributes to strengthening the rights and freedoms of citizens, in particular with regard to procedural guarantees. it shall be recognised at international level and within the different legal systems of the member states; it is intended to preserve the right not to be tried or prosecuted twice for the same offence. the purpose of this framework decision is to provide the member states with common rules of law concerning this principle in order to ensure uniformity in the interpretation of those rules and their practical application. this principle must therefore be applied horizontally in the member states so that citizens are not tried or prosecuted twice for the same offences.
in writing. - (pt) i note with satisfaction the restrictions introduced by the rapporteur on the european commission's sphere of competence and freedom of action, which limit and adapt its right to intervene in the field in question. i have, however, abstained from voting on this report because i consider that its conclusions are based on a legal decision which i do not approve of. the report was drawn up after the decisions of the court of justice in its judgments of 5 november 2002 had been made public. these judgments resolved the conflict of jurisdiction between several member states and the european commission in a positive manner. in view of the imprecise and even deficient nature of the legislation in force in this field, the court of justice took the decision, which has become customary for it by reason of repetition, to confer on the commission the competence which it claimed. although this is not a new phenomenon, it is nevertheless regrettable that the community institutions have for the most part interpreted the principle of subsidiarity in such a way as to concentrate powers in a top-down attitude, thus undermining the ability of the member states to conclude contracts independently and denying the very aims and origins of this basic principle.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report because i feel that the european community and its member states could benefit from more intensive and diversified trade relations with the people's republic of china, particularly in the field of maritime transport. in this respect, i welcome the commitment to ensure non-discriminatory treatment of vessels flying the flag of the other signatory and to allow the establishment of subsidiaries, branches or representative offices. these measures will foster the strengthening of trade relations, as well as increased contacts and understanding between civilizations, which could ultimately be beneficial for both parties. it is also important to preserve the bilateral agreements previously concluded between member states and the people's republic of china in all areas not covered by the agreement proposed today, and to preserve those agreements in their entirety whenever their provisions are more favourable.
in writing. - (pt) i support this important report. no one can doubt the need for more precise estimates of the risks involved in the granting of loans by banks. it is therefore essential to adopt a new agreement (bale ii). in addition, it has been demonstrated that the existence of clear international rules governing minimum capital requirements (base i) contributes to financial and legal trade security. an evaluation of the new system is therefore essential. as the rapporteur warns, we may well be entering a procyclical phase characterised by limited bank credit and even an economic recession. this could put an end to bank lending, especially to small and medium-sized enterprises. this will penalise business founders the most and could threaten the future potential of the european economy. without underestimating the positive effects of the new agreement (in particular the prospect of increased possibilities for the use of collateral), the commission must therefore, in the directive following the basel ii agreement, pay particular attention to the current situation of the european economy and to the rapporteur's calls for a spirit of greater democratic legitimacy in the drafting of these rules. it should also be alert to its warnings about the possibility that us financial institutions which are not covered by the agreement but operate in europe enjoy certain unfair competitive advantages over european banks.
in writing. - (pt) the european union must pursue the fundamental objective of promoting economic and social cohesion. since the structural funds are one of the main tools for achieving this objective, they must be maintained at their current levels. the rapporteur makes some important remarks, which we agree with, in particular the following: - his opposition to the renationalisation of structural policy, which is an essential pillar of european unity, and his defence of the less-favoured regions, which must remain the top priority of the structural funds; - his assertion that the regions which will no longer be eligible for objective 1 as a result of the purely statistical effects of enlargement will not suffer from these statistical effects. all the relevant measures must therefore be taken to redress this injustice, without reducing the funds allocated to these regions. as regards the rapporteur's recommendation that the current minimum proportion of 0.45% of the community's gross domestic product should continue to be allocated to the structural funds in the coming period, the only problem is that this amount is clearly insufficient to ensure economic and social cohesion, especially given that the union will welcome during enlargement countries whose per capita income is on average around 40% of community levels.
in writing. - (pt) i voted for this report and i particularly welcome the judicious inclusion of a series of 'warnings' relating to the union's current cohesion policy. if these warnings are heeded, they will enable us to make safer and more effective progress in harmonizing the levels of development between the different regions of europe. in other words, we will be able to pursue the ultimate goal of cohesion. i hope that the commission will examine in depth the proposals set out, from the specific requirements of the outermost regions of the union (where cohesion policy has already proved to be a valuable driver of development) to the need to simplify the rules for implementing regional policy (by reducing the bureaucracy inherent in payments, for example), and to rationalize the objectives in the light of their real effectiveness. a particularly sensitive aspect is the artificial increase in the gross domestic product of some european regions which is a direct result of the enlargement under way. many, including myself, have called on the european commission to devote considerable attention to this issue, and i am convinced that the positive responses i have received from the commission to my written questions on this subject will ultimately form an integral part of future official policy.
in writing. - (pt) regional and cohesion policies play a substantial role in european integration. objective 1 regions must therefore retain political and economic priority and receive increased attention. regional inequalities that appear as a tangible result of cohesion policies call for a redefinition of the priorities of these policies. the community policies associated with the cohesion fund must be progressively regionalised and their renationalisation must be prevented.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, in the european union, along with all the problems related to the world of work, maritime workers are also a problem that cannot be ignored. in the absence of qualified national or community labour, shipowners are forced to resort to workers from outside the community. in order to facilitate the use of seafarers from third countries, the commission has put in place a programme of training and recognition by the member states of diplomas issued by third countries. in this connection, it should be noted that more professional information means more maritime safety and the prevention of incidents. given that many maritime accidents are human-caused, it is essential to ensure a high level of training for the crews of european vessels. the proposal under consideration provides, for example, for english to be used as the working language if the crew and the authorities on the ground do not speak another common language. i therefore believe that the recognition of training in a third country must be based on the evidence that there is insufficient supply of european staff for certain posts. without taking away the merit of this training proposal, i would like to take this opportunity to draw the attention of the commission and parliament to the importance of continuing vocational training for national and european seafarers. i therefore agree with the rapporteur, mr poignant, that we need to make the maritime professions more attractive as a means of combating unemployment and to aim at strengthening the human resources of a sector in crisis. in my view, the european union lacks an action programme to promote these professions.
