madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, regulation 1408 is over three decades old and was created to coordinate the social security laws of the member states. its main objective is to ensure that workers moving within the european union are not prejudiced in their social security rights. over the years, this regulation has undergone several changes which have made it very complex, and the social security systems of the member states have undergone very positive developments, as is the case in my country. these circumstances lead to the urgent need to reform this regulation. the commission's proposal, which is being welcomed, sets out very clearly the objective to be achieved: to coordinate social security systems with a view to enlargement. it is a question of coordination, not of harmonization, but of modernising and simplifying the regulation. in this context, important progress has been made in several areas, particularly with regard to the rights of the unemployed, pensioners, frontier workers and their families. the list of social security schemes covered by coordination has also been extended and measures are envisaged to tackle the problem of double taxation. the rapporteur has indeed been working on the reform of this regulation. so i congratulate you. but i must say that some of the proposals he has put forward raise difficulties, difficulties which led to the epp's unfavourable vote in the committee on employment and social affairs. i shall now mention one of them, which concerns the definition of the concept of family: each member state recognises a particular concept of family in accordance with its national legal system. it is therefore not legitimate to impose on the member states any family model.
mr president, commissioner, madam rapporteur, i think it is appropriate to begin by recalling that the first reason for the existence of this agreement was the withdrawal of greenland from the european union. and i think it's also important to remember the reasons why this abandonment took place. it was because it wanted to impose on this small and outermost community an expropriation of its inalienable right to exploit the 200 miles of its exclusive economic zone, which is now clearly enshrined in international maritime law. this is perhaps the greatest misunderstanding that pervades the european union, and it has already caused us serious problems in the past and continues to threaten our future. the fact that in small areas, such as the north sea, which are well defined by national borders, the european institutions have jointly organised the exploitation of highly migratory surface fish species was a sensible choice. it is no longer acceptable to move from individual cases and solutions to common ownership of fisheries resources in the light of a purported community law. the same article of international maritime law that defines ownership of marine biological resources also defines ownership of mineral resources, in particular fossil fuels. the same european community which has sanctioned the application of this clause to delimit the ownership of undersea fossil energy mines in the north sea by the various states wants it to no longer be valid when it comes to biological resources. in other words, we would be dealing with a right which is valid only for the defence of the interests of the central european states, where gas and oil are found, but which is no longer valid when it comes to defending the interests of peripheral states or outermost regions within europe, around which there are large maritime areas with significant resources. in the ten-year period which, according to our position, should now be opened up for the european institutions to reflect on the status of the western waters, it is necessary to thoroughly review the question of access to waters, to adapt european legislation to the major principles of international maritime law and to examine the best ways of safeguarding a sustainable fishery in the atlantic.

in writing. - (pt) today we are examining the mid-term review of the fourth fisheries protocol between the european union and greenland, which entered into force in january 2001. the protocol provides for compensation in excess of the fishing rights allocated, totalling almost €43 million and €28 million respectively. it also proposes a partnership for sustainable development taking into account the crisis facing the fisheries sector. however, for portugal, the key issue remains the loss of historical fishing rights in greenland waters after accession to the eu and the existence of 'paper quotas' which were allocated in accordance with the principle of relative stability but which are not used by the fleets of the member states signatories to the protocol. in 2000, only 54% of the fishing opportunities allocated were used, despite the financial effort of the protocol. without calling into question the principle of relative stability, we must therefore ensure that these unused quotas can be used by the fleets of other member states. in any case, special attention must be paid to the portuguese fleet. it is fair to say that the financial aid we are giving greenland because of the crisis it is going through cannot be included in the financial compensation for the fisheries agreement, because that would overburden the budget line concerned, which is already suffering from serious shortcomings. this is why the elements of this agreement which are not related to fisheries should be separated.
in writing. - (pt) this extensive study shows that, given the size of european shipping, our continent is lacking in qualified seafarers from the member states. hence the need for the european union to recruit seafarers from third countries. the proposal under consideration seeks to create a framework of training requirements for seafarers from third countries to carry out activities, which would be supervised by the european maritime safety agency. this initiative therefore reinforces the importance of maritime safety, which the recent sinking of the prestige has once again highlighted in a dramatic way. in this sense, the whole proposal to guarantee the highest possible level of qualification for seafarers must be welcomed, as must the proposals to introduce a uniform working language and to simplify the recognition procedure, which, according to the professionals in the sector, is excessively complicated. finally, i agree with the alarm signal raised by the rapporteur for an opinion, who reminded the commission and the council that parliament has already repeatedly called for an action programme to promote maritime professions to be presented. if, as has been argued on various occasions, maritime transport must be promoted and improved, in particular to replace heavy road transport over long distances, it is essential to implement an action programme to promote maritime professions.
in writing. - (pt) the minimum level of training for seafarers should, in my view, be the exclusive responsibility of the fishermen's unions, in accordance with their respective regulations. fishing is extremely important for coastal populations, both in terms of employment and in terms of family income. compulsory training should therefore not be a barrier to access to the sea and rivers, but a requirement for the sustainable development process at local level and for participation in a process of rebuilding marine fauna and flora.

- mr president, mr sylla's report provides an excellent opportunity to remind us that immigrant populations living in the european union are particularly vulnerable and are the main victims of the violation of fundamental rights. the measures aimed at creating a genuine and coherent community policy on illegal immigration have been delayed in their adoption, which is incompatible with the urgency and seriousness of the problems facing these people. on the other hand, measures to ensure security or to control illegal immigration, which are usually repressive in nature, have proved more likely to generate consensus among governments than positive or integrative measures. progress was made in 2002 with the adoption of several instruments which constitute the first steps towards a common policy on asylum and immigration. the directive on minimum standards for the reception of asylum seekers, the refugee directive, the dublin ii regulation and the family directive are of particular importance. however, these instruments are not sufficient to resolve the legal and social fragility of many thousands of immigrants who have settled in our countries and whose situation is extremely precarious and exposed to all kinds of abuses. a key instrument still awaits final approval by the council: the european long-term resident statute for immigrants who have resided for more than five years in the territory of a member state, which will offer them the right to a range of benefits on the same terms as nationals. mr president, overcoming these deadlocks is crucial to a real increase in the level of protection of fundamental rights in the union.

in writing. - (pt) access to water is essential for life, health, nutrition, well-being and development. therefore, water should not be regarded simply as a commodity, but as a public good. the fact that 1.7 million people lack access to safe drinking water, leading to 30,000 deaths a day from related diseases, is particularly shocking. while the shortage of drinking water in developing countries has worsened, the privatisation of water companies is nonetheless proceeding rapidly, particularly following the conditions imposed by the world bank and the international monetary fund for loans and structural adjustment programmes that weaken public services by causing under-investment in the sector. liberalisation or privatisation of water companies has helped deprive poor communities of access to water and has led to higher prices. a serious assessment of the socioeconomic and environmental effects is therefore required, as well as guarantees that articles vi and xxi of the general agreement on trade in services are revised, in order to protect the right of each developing country to freely decide on its method of water supply. the creation of a european water fund is in principle a good initiative as long as it supports the water policy of the beneficiary countries by guaranteeing public ownership and management so that everyone has access to water, without discrimination.
in writing. - (pt) more than 2.5 billion people in developing countries lack access to safe drinking water and 3 million die each year from waterborne diseases such as typhoid fever, dysentery, cholera, hepatitis, malaria, trachoma, fluorosis and japanese encephalitis. we need to ensure that the monterrey and johannesburg water targets (a 50% reduction in the number of people without access to safe water and sanitation by 2015) are implemented as quickly as possible. however, it is equally important to encourage the €700 million european water initiative launched in johannesburg. finally, i welcome the proposal to set up a european water fund to help the acp states.

in writing. - (pt) although the rapporteur was able to propose several interesting and valuable strategies in response to the challenge of 'how to help developing countries to take advantage of trade', i felt obliged to abstain from voting. the observation that the key to development lies in trade liberalisation should, rather than leading to enthusiastic applause or violent condemnation (both leading to ideological disputes with short-term effects), at most be a starting point and a frame of reference. in view of this undeniable truth, the best approach is to link trade relations with developing countries to certain obligations. in other words, it is better to impose conditions on the aid provided by the eu and/or its member states to those economic agents who, by buying raw materials or selling goods and services, establish trade relations with developing countries. these conditions would imply the obtaining of immediate related benefits. in practice, this could include mandatory technology transfers, the establishment of local capacity, the supply of medicines, the construction of basic infrastructure, the provision of services to reduce debt management costs, etc. history tells us that it is ineffective to try to change the 'economic' climate by imposing legislative restrictions.
in writing. - (pt) the figures for the health situation in developing countries are tragically telling. this emergency requires rapid, strong and effective european support. first, it should ensure that the most developed countries increase their contributions in order to fully comply with the commitments made at the monterrey summit (the millennium summit) and the johannesburg summit (the sustainable development summit). second, it should raise the standards of aid effectiveness and transparency through a strategy that respects precise objectives and timetables, is monitored and evaluated, ensures that available programmes and goods are distributed fully and continuously, encourages the use of local human resources, thus avoiding heavy dependence on foreign technical assistance, and builds local capacity. third, it should send clear messages to markets through european legislation and strategies implemented within the world trade organisation so that in the long term, ever-increasing quantities of medicines are made available urgently at affordable prices in developing countries. fourth, it is time to extend the debt relief initiative to more countries.
in writing. - (pt) this report clearly shows the relationship between poverty and disease, disease and poverty. the statistics on health in developing countries are appalling: 28,000 children under five die every day, 2 million people die of tuberculosis every year, 1 million die of malaria, and so on. the spread of aids has also reached tragic proportions: 25 million africans are living with the disease, a quarter of them have died from it, and 10 percent of people aged 15 to 50 are afflicted. i support the proposal for greater investment in health in developing countries and effective monitoring of outcomes. the efficiency of this investment should be maximised by a simultaneous strategy of good allocation of resources. i would also like to stress the urgent need for a more productive debate on access to medicines for communities in developing countries, given that the scale of the disaster calls for more creative, bold and determined responses. i therefore agree with most of the report. however, i abstained in the final vote, as i deplored the rapporteur's failure to resist the temptation to include in the final resolution a paragraph written in this ideological coded language, like that of other reports produced by this parliament, which simply aims to inscribe european development policy in the international pro-abortion movement.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report which recommends, in general terms, a 'strengthened culture of consultation and dialogue' with non-state actors (nsas) as a means of increasing the effectiveness of the european union's development policy. interaction between different actors - local, institutional and other, such as civil society - is increasingly important at national and international levels. this is one way of getting the response we urgently need if we are to help the world's less favoured regions. after this general observation, however, i must point out, in the light of the rapporteur's comments on the increasingly significant reductions in community aid to the various ngos, that the participation of non-state actors does not in itself guarantee the effectiveness of development policies. we need to encourage greater participation and involvement from actors who do not support ideological or programmatic campaigns or promote their own agendas, but whose objectives are truly generous, selfless and altruistic and whose actions therefore give a more concrete and tangible result. it is therefore incumbent upon us to put the "quality" of participation above the quantity.

in writing. -(pt) the initiative of the republic of austria, motivated by the need to respond to "a dramatic increase in asylum seekers" in that country "contrary to the european trend", is part of the logic of building "fortress europe". the initiative aimed to establish a list of third states considered safe for them to assume responsibility for examining an asylum application, assuming that the country responsible for examining the application was the country through which the applicant had entered the union. among the countries on the proposed list, switzerland is the only non-eu and non-schengen country. it can therefore be inferred that austria was primarily targeting the candidate countries with which it shares a border. however, as the rapporteur points out, a fundamental principle is at stake here, namely that the geneva convention allows every asylum seeker to have his case examined individually. therefore, even if a list of 'safe third countries' could be drawn up, an asylum application could not be automatically rejected given the provisions of the geneva convention. furthermore, under the principle of subsidiarity, a regulation would not be the most appropriate instrument to use in relation to such a vital aspect of the sovereignty of the member states.
in writing. -(pt) i support the rapporteur's arguments because i believe that the scope of the austrian initiative is indeed limited. the rapporteur points out that this regulation would apply only to switzerland, which clearly does not sufficiently justify the establishment of such a legal instrument. at the same time, the inflexible nature of the proposal does not provide for any mechanism for revising the list of 'safe states' and adding or removing countries. this could lead to the paralysis of the ab initio system without any benefit to asylum seekers or law enforcement. the rapporteur notes that the underlying problem with this austrian proposal is that there is a 'dramatic increase' in asylum applications in austria, which is regrettable. however, this is where i disagree with the rapporteur, because i have to say that i consider it normal and even positive for a member state to try to assert its rights and solve its specific problems, even if this may sometimes run counter to the abstract principle of 'community interest', which is very often elusive when it comes to security and justice. i also support the rapporteur's assertion that the concept of safe european third countries should not be covered by a separate regulation, but should rather be considered within an overall approach established by the framework of the asylum policy directive.
in writing. -(pt) as expected, mr trichet, president-elect of the european central bank (ecb), reaffirmed and strengthened the current economic 'triangle' of the european union based on price stability, the stability pact and the 'lisbon strategy', despite the increasingly evident incompatibility of this 'triangle' with economic growth and employment. in his questionnaire replies, mr trichet reiterates that price stability is a precondition for growth, "by maintaining a small increase in unit costs of production" - in other words, by wage control, reductions in real wages and productivity increases, but only for employers in this case. mr trichet also mentioned the consensus of european governments on the 'lisbon strategy' and the need to emphasise the approach based on structural reforms, by which he meant liberalisation, by increasing the flexibility of the labour market and by gradually privatising pensions. finally, it reaffirms the 3% threshold of the stability pact, arguing that no government has asked for it to be amended and that the commission has demonstrated its necessity. this is rather ironic, given that france is on the verge of failing to meet this same requirement for the third year in a row. mr trichet also favours amendments to the ecb's voting procedures, which essentially exclude countries like portugal from the financial decision-making process. that is why we voted against this report.
in writing. -(pt) unemployment is one of the main problems in the candidate countries. in six of the 12 candidate countries, unemployment is above 10%, leading to social exclusion and poverty. economic and monetary policies that promote economic growth and employment are therefore necessary and should be encouraged by the public and cooperative sectors. this unemployment can be attributed to the rapid destruction of planned economies, linked to waves of privatisation and the total opening up of markets, which has led to serious disruptions not only in economic activity but also in public services themselves, particularly in the area of social security. this same transformation is confirmed in the explanatory statement of the report, which says that it has "inflated the ranks of the population at risk of poverty" and led to the increase in "precarious employment relationships, such as temporary work". the commission's communication therefore aims to transpose the european employment strategy in its 'post-lisbon' form into the candidate countries. the latter do not seem to need greater flexibility of employment and greater mobility. once again, the solution lies in a thorough review of the european union's well-established neoliberal economic and monetary policies. the european union should redouble its efforts to achieve social and economic cohesion.

in writing. -the commission proposal aims to implement measures relating to the supply of natural gas following recent or imminent crises, in particular those caused by us attacks on countries such as iraq. there are so many relevant questions that it is impossible to deal with them all in this talk. the commission is even trying to appropriate the right to intervene in the workings of the member states, an ambition repressed by parliament, which thus ensures that the member states retain their prerogatives in this area and in relation to their international obligations. as the documentary filmmakers suggest, the substance of these documents is not explicit, but implicit, the key point being that world oil production has more or less peaked, or even exceeded this maximum stage, and although natural gas production may indeed continue to increase, it will not peak until about 25 years at best, both facing an inevitable decline. in view of these facts, the establishment of a european hydrocarbon supply monitoring system to address this major problem could play a role, particularly in relation to our knowledge of the state of world stocks and essential research into other energy sources such as renewable energy.
in writing. -(pt) as with the concerns raised by the karlsson reports which deal with different substances, there is no doubt that it would also be beneficial to start aligning measures to ensure the security of natural gas supplies. the forced harmonisation proposed by the european commission is a different story altogether. this harmonization is expressed in a power which the commission would like to have for itself: 'to monitor closely the quantity of new contracts for the import of gas from non-community countries' (article 6 (1) of the proposal). unfortunately, the commission's proposal is based on the idea that, in a competitive market, security of supply cannot be left to the responsible sector, an argument which it takes too far. for my part, i agree with the rapporteur who says that market operators - in other words, market players and member states - are perfectly capable of guaranteeing security of supply. recent studies confirm this. for this reason, i was forced to abstain. i feel that the european commission should respect the legal nature of the proposed legislation - a directive - and therefore suggest general minimum safeguards and precautions which can then be adopted by member states and operators in this sector, with sufficient flexibility to adapt to the specific circumstances of each country and with the political freedom to enact concrete legislation in this context.
in writing. - (pt) as in the mombaur report on natural gas supply, the substance of this report does not lie in its explicit concerns but in its underlying ones, i.e. that world oil production has more or less reached or even already exceeded its maximum level and that natural gas production will undergo the same evolution in a short time. the report proposes various measures which are also palliative measures. this approach does not go to the heart of the matter and does not address the more general problem of our declining oil production capacity. while the european parliament's amendments 2 and 5 emphasise the need to reduce oil demand through the development of renewable energy sources, experts agree that what we really need is a sustainable reduction in energy requirements. different experts say that it is necessary to align demand with supply capacities, to reduce demand in line with the rate of resource depletion in order to avoid any imbalance. it is not enough to say that we "have to" diversify and reduce demand. we must find an objective basis for assessing this decline. one of the most pressing and essential requirements is to set a target for reducing consumption, similar to kyoto, but without making it a mystery or a story.
in writing. -{pt) i voted in favour of an amendment whose adoption by a majority means that the european commission's proposal has been rejected. it was really the best solution and it will save us a lot of trouble and conflict. it was only a matter of time before i came out against all the aims of the proposal, which do indeed address serious current concerns. the problem, however, is that the european commission used these concerns to mask an attempt to almost assert its rights to directly interfere in the management of energy resources in the member states and to influence the market on its own behalf. the rapporteur is nevertheless trying to 'limit the damage': he proposes more realistic transitional periods (2007), he leaves it to the member states to decide what percentage of stocks can be held by private or public companies and he removes the power to intervene in the event of a significant price increase (this power will only be retained in the event of a major supply disruption). however, after all that had happened in the competent committee of the european parliament and after the various amendments had been tabled, reinforcing the opposition to the ever-wider ambitions of the commission, it was a predictable outcome and a happy outcome, especially in view of respect for the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. -(pt) i am glad that this report has had the fate it deserved after the european commission's proposal in the other karlsson report was rejected. i hope that the decision taken in plenary to refer the matter back to the committee responsible will improve the text of the proposal for a directive. if the legislative process is to continue, more realism will be needed. in particular, it is very important to take into account the heavy economic and financial impact of the decision to increase the minimum stock level from 90 to 120 days, which will result in intolerable and unjustifiable management costs for many member states. the best strategy might be to leave this issue as it is and to focus primarily on promoting genuine mechanisms for linking stocks, encouraging a community of interests and interconnecting trans-european energy networks.
in writing. -the consultation procedure, the purpose of which is to amend regulation (ec) no 40/94 on the community trade mark, may seem insignificant. however, this is not the case. there is in fact a link between community trade marks and designations of origin or geographical indications which recall the limiano cheese case, the pont de lima case and the wine case. that is why amendments nos 1 and 2 to this report seem dangerous to me. although he says that a trade mark cannot, under any circumstances, be at the same time a geographical indication or an appellation of origin, the rapporteur also says that the geographical indication or the appellation of origin can be included in the mark when the products covered have the right to indicate it. the problem is that this can lead to trade protection of trademarks belonging to the same operator, usually a company, thus threatening the designation of origin, as in the case of limiano cheese. that is why we abstained.
in writing. -(pt) the initiative of the federal republic of germany to adopt a directive on transit assistance in the context of air removal measures - which means the expulsion by air of persons accused of being 'illegal immigrants' - is one of a series of provisions and measures aimed at building a 'fortress europe'. as the group of honourable members whose name is inscribed in the 'minority opinion' section of the report has described, the real purpose of this initiative is to try cynically to improve and make more efficient the machinery for expelling people accused of 'illegal' stay with the least possible resistance. the introduction, through an amendment, of a clause to safeguard the rights set out in the european convention on human rights and fundamental freedoms will not change the fact that the status quo now de facto, if not de jure, violates the right of men and women to immigrate in search of a better life. it is impossible and even intolerable from a human point of view to put thousands of men and women in a tragic situation by applying repressive measures designed to increase security.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. transit assistance in the context of removal by air is a sufficiently important issue to justify the establishment of a code of conduct and clear provisions on the rights and responsibilities of transit states and escorts accompanying third-country nationals during removal. the 'legal vacuum' in which both the member states and the escorts accompanying persons in the process of deportation found themselves did not help in defining their roles and responsibilities. i cannot, however, support the minority arguments which irresponsibly advocate the removal of all restrictions at the frontiers. moreover, if i may say ironically in one of the rapporteur's proposals, i do not consider it 'inappropriate' to refer to third country nationals as 'persons', because that is what we all are, regardless of our nationality. this is precisely why it is legitimate to introduce clauses prohibiting transit if a third-country national is at risk of inhuman or degrading treatment, torture or the death penalty or if his life or freedom is threatened because of his race, religion, nationality, membership of a certain social group or political opinions.
in writing. -the parliamentary committee has incorporated some of our proposals into the report. among them:- the need for member states to have at their disposal the appropriate means to carry out the checks, which will be achieved by increasing the number of inspectors and improving their working conditions and methods; - the importance of having qualified seafarers to ensure that the required preventive maintenance of ships is carried out; - the existence on board ships carrying dangerous substances of systems to deal immediately with minor pollution; - the development of safe port facilities equipped with the necessary means to implement appropriate emergency plans. however, other important proposals were rejected, including the following: - to submit a proposal on the social, living and working conditions of seafarers. these conditions shall be complied with on board the vessel; - delegate the authority to allocate competences to companies with the technical expertise required to carry out the work and which are independent of the shipowners; - set up a european parliament committee of inquiry. however, the majority of the votes in the plenary session were in favour of the establishment of a temporary committee, which in a way shows that our position has been established. that is why we voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) the sinking of the oil tanker prestige off the coast of galicia on 19 november 2002 caused an ecological and economic disaster of a very large scale, to which, i am pleased to say, parliament has devoted its full attention from the outset. a parliamentary delegation, of which i was a member, went to galicia in march of this year to see for itself the extent of the disaster. i therefore share the concerns expressed by the commission and the members of this house about maritime safety. i call on all parties to commit themselves firmly to the vital field of maritime safety, because the quality and safety of ships sailing in european waters and of european vessels worldwide depend on it, as does the protection of europe's coastline and citizens from further disasters. safety is our business and requires our full attention! i also speak as a representative of a region where many shipping lanes between america and europe converge and which is therefore extremely exposed to this type of disaster. the island of porto santo has already suffered the terrible consequences of such accidents. hopefully these measures will ensure that my region and all the others will never have to experience this again.
in writing. - (pt) i supported this report and approved it in the final vote in accordance with my intervention in the debate. it is absolutely deplorable that the socialists and other left-wing members rejected the proposal for an oral amendment tabled by the rapporteur himself just before the vote on a sensitive point - amendment no 11 on the creation of a temporary committee - which would have allowed for a wider consensus on the final drafting of this excellent and very comprehensive report. unfortunately, the european left is more interested in petty political chicaneries, serving the interests of internal chapel quarrels in spain, than in the effective pursuit of the common interest. the adoption of amendment no 23, whose partisan tone is evident, proves this. i voted in favour of the report and amendment no 11 in the original wording of the rapporteur. the portuguese coast is very vulnerable to such situations. this is true both for the continent (which was almost hit by the prestige disaster) and for madeira and the azores. we clearly need to be at the forefront of maritime safety, which is why we need to make substantial progress in this area. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur once again on his excellent work.
in writing. - (pt) the quality of water in seas and rivers in europe and around the world is crucial for the well-being of people. political decision-making in this area must not be hesitant, fragile or ambiguous. the council, the commission and parliament must have a common, clear and uncompromising position so that disasters like the prestige cannot happen again. never again! we cannot and must not underestimate the need to strengthen the hulls of ships, to control their routes (navigation corridors), to have a high level of professionalism among their crews, to move the navigation corridors to the open sea and to use the corridors correctly.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the convention enthusiasts want the new treaty to be signed on 9 may, the date on which we recall the schuman declaration of 1950. but let's hear it for robert schuman! in exact words he said this: "europe will not be achieved by a coup, nor by a joint construction, but by concrete achievements which first create a de facto solidarity". i repeat: it will not be achieved by a coup, nor by a joint construction, but by concrete achievements that create de facto solidarity. now let's look at what we have in front of us. we have a convention and, as giscard d'estaing has told us here, there were 1 800 speeches, thousands of amendments, but not a single vote, not a single vote. it was undemocratic, neither in its basis nor in its process, and it went far beyond its mandate. what would it mean, then, as the rapporteurs intend, to impose their conclusions as definitive, above the powers and responsibilities democratically attributed to the igc alone? it would be a coup against robert schuman. we have taken another look at the conventional text that is being forced to become a constitution. and what do we see? we see the attempt to make europe at one stroke, by upsetting long-established balances through a new construction of the whole. schuman again. and let us remember what happened a few weeks ago at the preparatory meeting of the igc in riva del garda. several states and several nations have made important reservations to the text of the convention, which the uen takes up in its proposals for amendments to this report: the composition of the commission, the presidency, the place of christianity, etc. in the face of these criticisms, the german minister oskar fischer abruptly threatened the financial perspectives for 2007 to 2013, which the press interpreted as an unfortunate budget blackmail. what is this? what is this? it is to refuse to take concrete steps to build up a de facto solidarity which is what schuman recommended on 9 may 1950. the majority of my group therefore recommends that the igc, whenever it remembers 9 may, should really take its inspiration from the schuman method. i ask the italian presidency not to allow the language of threats, of conditioning, of blackmail between member states and to favour broad freedom, equality and openness in the debates. we must not allow the haste and pressure of some to shake off the democratic shiver to spoil the magnificent construction begun in the treaty of rome.

in writing. - (pt) i regret that the european parliament has not approved our proposal to reject this proposal for a directive, which opens the way to the patentability of software programmes, despite the adoption of innumerable amendments to this directive. the european parliament is thus doing a disservice to innovation and technological development. we seem to be living in a time when everything is susceptible to being commercialized, owned by someone and used for personal enrichment. some would like to see this commercialisation not only affect production but also knowledge, life itself. we live in an age where discovery, which is part of our common heritage, is confused with invention. this directive opens the way for the patentability of human knowledge, which we reject. although some positive proposals were accepted in the final vote, most of the proposals we tabled were rejected, which we regret. we will continue to fight against this proposal for a directive and against the interests of the large multinationals which it seeks to satisfy.
in writing. - (pt) during the debate in plenary, my colleague mr mussa said that intelligence could not be patented. i fully agree with this principle, because we cannot forget that software is the result of a mental operation which allows a human being to have a series of instructions executed by a machine devoid of intelligence. it is therefore a product of the human mind which, if patented, would risk reducing the capacity for research and innovation, given the number of patents already registered, notably by the large us groups. the latter would thus have a kind of "intelligence monopoly". in addition to the fact that this is a highly complex technical issue, we are sensitive to the economic and political consequences, which concern mainly small and medium-sized software design companies. we therefore voted against, despite the adoption of a few amendments which go in the right direction.
in writing. - (pt) the patent is an instrument which serves to protect the intellect and to promote creativity through the legal protection of a creation in the strict sense. the legislator in this field must never forget this principle. in other words, the patent should not be used to do the exact opposite. the intellectual property itself cannot be patented, nor can patents be used to curb creativity and, at the very least, create 'crimes of intellectual property' or 'crimes of free creation'. the patent cannot be reduced to a mere trophy for the first to arrive at the competent authority with an application for registration, but a reward for the one who has actually created something new and an incentive to continue creating. the proposal for a directive, which does not apply to the european patent convention, allows the patentability of ideas implemented by computer programs. it therefore goes far beyond the protection already afforded by copyright and would lead to the crystallization of 'intelligences' and the perverse establishment of a barrier to technological development itself - as well as to economic and social development. the text has been slightly improved by the adoption of a few amendments in plenary - some of which were tabled by me - but that is not enough to get us to vote on it. i therefore voted against. i would have preferred that the proposal be rejected and that work be resumed on another basis, as i also proposed.
in writing. - (pt) the purpose of this proposal for a decision is to ensure the financing of community actions to be carried out in support of consumer policy for the years 2004 to 2007, in accordance with the objectives and actions set out in the european strategy for consumer policy, approved in 2003. the aim is to support organisations and bodies working in the interests of consumers at community or national level, with a budget of eur 72 million. while i believe that the financial package should be more substantial, i support this initiative, which was voted unanimously in the committee on the environment, public health and consumer policy. it aims to strengthen the objectives of a high common level of consumer protection, effective enforcement of consumer protection rules, greater participation of consumer organisations in community policy-making and the integration of consumer protection objectives into all relevant areas of european union action. it also called on the commission to ensure that the european parliament and the council were able to reach agreement on the draft directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a dispute between the commission and the consumer. on the other hand, there needs to be a clearer definition of organisations that are genuinely working in the interests of consumers and not just being spokespersons for industrial lobbies.

in writing. - (pt) the commission has long wanted to create a community framework for the taxation of energy products. this compromise by the council is therefore a significant step in that direction, allowing agreement on a comprehensive directive on energy taxation covering all types of energy. the rapporteur is, however, very critical of the minimum levels of taxation that have been adopted, the exemptions and the tax reductions that are being proposed. we have serious reservations about this directive. we are in favour of reducing the tax burden on workers, but the solution does not involve 'environmental taxation' of energy or pollution. it involves rebalancing the taxation of labour and capital. secondly, this type of indirect taxation is ultimately paid by the final consumers (users). it does not take income into account and penalizes low-income families. the effects of the large increases in taxation on the productive fabric, especially that of the most disadvantaged regions, must also be assessed. in addition, the underlying polluter-pays principle raises serious concerns, as it allows those with economic power to pollute, which is evident in the liberal philosophy of emissions trading. the central issue should be not to pollute. environmental protection and the fight against environmental dumping must be achieved through appropriate regulation and effective enforcement, involving strong state intervention and investment.
in writing. - (pt) the european parliament has just taken an important step towards greening energy taxation in the european union by giving the green light to the directive restructuring the community framework for the taxation of energy products and electricity. i hope that the council will now react in an equally constructive way and that it will not again oppose the veto which prevented the revision of the same legislative text in 1997. one of the most important objectives of sustainable development policy is to internalize environmental externalities in the economy. in other words, the price of products must reflect their true environmental cost. the price signal is fundamental for both producers and consumers to reorient their choices towards sustainability. unfortunately, we are still far from this reality: buying green is still a luxury and selling green is not yet profitable enough. i support the rapporteur in advocating more ambitious and binding rules, including reducing taxes on production using renewable energy sources and increasing levels of taxation on fossil fuels for transport.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to deal with climate change and the growing environmental risks, using taxation as an additional instrument. despite the rapporteur's reservations about the council's proposal, which he considers to be inadequate, i believe that this proposal reflects the broadest possible consensus within the council, knowing that this issue must be approached with caution and in a spirit of seeking consensus. my vote therefore relates to the legislative body of the report, because i do not entirely share the rapporteur's concerns, which are set out in the explanatory statement. we are particularly divided on the end of the rule of unanimity on these matters or on the tightening of community requirements for the taxation of products. while it is clear that there will be a need for greater coordination between member states to address growing environmental challenges, the focus should be on the application of the polluter-pays principle rather than on the imposition of artificial consensus.
in writing. - (pt) the fisheries agreement with the government of mauritius expired on 2 december 2002. the parties agreed to start renegotiation of the protocol annexed to the agreement. however, this negotiation was postponed in view of the fact that the government of mauritius is currently assessing the state of its saltwater fish stocks. the parties therefore proposed an extension of the current protocol by one year, while maintaining the conditions of access and the allocation key between member states. the eight portuguese longliners will thus continue to benefit from fishing opportunities. the extension is therefore necessary and i support it in this context, while criticising the delay in submitting this protocol to parliament's consideration. the central question, however, is to create the conditions for the conclusion of a new multiannual agreement as soon as possible. my vote in favour does not mean that i support all the rapporteur's positions.
in writing. - (pt) the ageing of the population and the ever-decreasing employment rate among the elderly are threatening the viability of pension schemes. we urgently need to reform social protection systems. member states should cooperate in the field of pensions through the open method of coordination, so that divergences of interpretation arising from bilateral agreements can be reduced. studies of pension systems show that the key to success is to balance economic and social concerns, as macroeconomic, social and employment policies are interlinked. the european employment strategy and the european social fund make important contributions to the promotion of permanent employment and the recruitment of older workers. member states must adopt measures to discourage early retirement and to encourage active ageing, together with enterprises, workers and the social partners. finally, member states must eliminate all forms of discrimination based on sex from their pension systems and eliminate existing differences in the level of pensions for women, which are still lower than those for men. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) the commission's communication on sustainable and adequate pensions analyses the first reports on national pension strategies submitted by the member states. the commission's analysis covers the adequacy of pension schemes, their financial sustainability and the need to modernise them. i welcome, of course, the fact that member states have already started their reform processes and that some have already implemented important reforms. that is the case in portugal, and i am happy to say that. there is also a clear awareness of the need for further reforms to preserve the long-term sustainability of pension systems, combined with sound public finances. it is of the utmost importance to eliminate from this debate the demagogic language and the untimely rhetoric which presents itself as the 'standard bearer of the defence of workers'. the unsustainable situation of many national pension systems is due to demographic change and it is certain that if nothing is done it will cause serious harm to all retired workers, both present and future. like the rapporteur, i welcome the close cooperation between member states in this area. moreover, as i also agree with most of its conclusions on three fundamental objectives - adequacy, financial sustainability and modernisation of pension systems - i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) i can only welcome the draft convention on the future of europe and its work, which is a historic milestone on the road to european integration. i welcome the desire to bring the union closer to its citizens, to strengthen its democratic character and to improve its decision-making capacity, in the context of enlargement. i welcome the (though timid) strengthening of the union's role and capacity to act internationally, in the face of the challenges of globalisation and increasing interdependence. i welcome the fact that, for the first time in the history of european integration, national parliaments are playing an active role in the development of european legislation. the union acquires legal personality and the long-awaited disappearance of the pillar structure is finally achieved. i welcome the call in mr gil-robles' excellent report for consultation of european citizens by referendum, if possible on the same day as the european parliament elections. i regret the disappearance of the rotating presidency of the council and the absence of reference to the roots of our common culture and history.
in writing. - (pt) i voted against amendment no 78 tabled by the group of the european united left/nordic green left in accordance with the voting instructions of the group of the party of european socialists. however, i consider that, in essence, the amendment in question is correct because it points out one of the weaknesses of the draft constitution presented by the convention to the intergovernmental conference. indeed, this project is not very innovative in the field of european economic governance. in particular, it does not define how national economic policies should be coordinated and does not revise the objectives of the european central bank to link them more closely to growth and employment policies.
in writing. - (pt) this report reiterates its support for the work and results of the convention, which we reject. as we have pointed out in the past, the undemocratic methods and processes by which the convention was drawn up have contributed to the drafting of a text which merits our categorical opposition. in the terms of this text, an increasingly aggressive form of capitalism will take place, society will be structured along neoliberal lines, everything will be commercialised and people will be further devalued. the social aspects which the text promised to defend will be relegated to the background and we will slip further down the path laid down in the maastricht and nice treaties. this is a real attack on the principles of the constitution of the portuguese republic. it is a threat to sovereignty both in legal and institutional terms, and in the concrete areas of citizens' fundamental rights and freedoms. it is an attempt to throw into the dustbin of history any possibility of alternative paths to european integration. instead of making the pursuit of peace, development and economic and social cohesion on the basis of high levels of social protection for all absolute priorities, the text defines peace simply as a possibility and not as a central objective. it is taking the profoundly militaristic nato path, linked to us imperialism. we hope that the next intergovernmental conferences will reject this proposal for a convention and seek alternative ways of responding positively to the current problems.

in writing. - (pt) the commission's proposal for a directive aims to protect investors (by introducing harmonised rules governing the activities of authorised intermediaries) and to help investment firms operate at european level. as a framework directive, it merely sets out high-level general obligations to be complied with by the authorities of the member states. it is not intended to impose a particular market structure but to be flexible enough to adapt to the different market structures in place in different countries, and to enable and promote innovation in a context of cooperation between national authorities. it clarifies and completes the list of financial instruments admitted to trading on regulated markets or between investment firms; it updates and harmonises the regulatory conditions to be met by investment firms, both at initial and subsequent authorisation levels, and strengthens the practical implementation of the 'single passport' for investment firms, while reaffirming and extending the principle that firms must be able to operate throughout the eu on the basis of authorisation by and supervision by the competent authorities of the home member state. the proposal touched - and touches - on sensitive and delicate points, as the debates in the committee have shown, but in view of the balanced compromise position proposed by the rapporteur, theresa villiers - whom i warmly congratulate - i voted in favour of it.

- the next item is the report (a5-0257/2003) by mr della vedova, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the proposal for a council regulation on the control of concentrations between undertakings: 'ec merger regulation' (com (2002) 711 - c5-0005/2003 - 2002/0296 (cns)).
the commission has already adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of accidents at work. the reform in question is the result of a review process which began in 2000 and which forms the basis for the new proposal for a regulation which i hope will soon be adopted by the council so that it can enter into force in time for the forthcoming enlargement. the aim of the reform is not to question the merits of the current system. we are proposing a number of significant improvements to the current system, mainly with a view to improving the system in terms of transparency and consistency of merger control. at the same time, in addition to the regulation, we are improving the decision-making process at the commission, ensuring that investigations into proposed mergers are more accurate, more focused and better supported by sound economic analysis and take full account of the rights of the parties concerned by the merger and of third parties. we are also aware that the court of first instance requires a high standard of proof from the commission. this has obvious implications for the way we work. the package of measures to reform merger control includes the proposal for a new community merger regulation and a draft communication containing guidelines for the assessment of horizontal mergers. in recent months, in addition to the preparation of these documents, a number of measures have been adopted concerning the staff and internal organisation of the directorate-general for competition, including the introduction of a new figure - the chief competition economist - and procedures such as the peer review group to ensure greater precision of control during analysis. the proposal for a new merger regulation is characterised by three main elements: first, the clarification of the concept of dominant position in the context of the assessment of the possible effects of mergers on competition; secondly, questions of jurisdiction, in relation to which we propose to streamline the system of referrals between the commission and the member states; thirdly, many procedural changes have been proposed to increase the flexibility of the investigation and notification periods for mergers slightly, and to align the investigation powers provided for in the merger regulation with those established in regulation 1/2003 which, as you know, concerns the application of articles 81 and 82 of the treaty.
mr president, the commission has proposed a new regulation on mergers in the wider context of the updating of the legislation on the infringement of competition and the consequences that such infringement may have for the full functioning of the single market. this is a highly sensitive area in which legal certainty, administrative procedures, transparency, control and appeal of decisions and the active, dynamic and timely involvement of all the interests represented in companies must be strengthened. the merger of undertakings is an economic and legal process which is fundamental to the dynamisation of markets, business restructuring and the growth of economies. it cannot and should not be regarded as a process which inevitably leads to abuse of a dominant position. a very clear distinction must be made between what constitutes an investigation into the infringement of competition following allegedly irregular behaviour and what constitutes the natural control of a merger, which in principle must be regarded as legitimate and in accordance with the rules governing the market. the amendments already adopted by the committee and those which will be tabled in the plenary, in particular by the socialist group, are therefore of fundamental importance. competition is not, in the community legal order and the political philosophy which determines it, an end in itself, but rather an instrument through which the major objectives of the union can be achieved and made concrete. it is therefore necessary to be extremely cautious about the european union adopting a criterion of substantial reduction of competition (used in other jurisdictions and in particular in the united states), and it is certain that the position of the parliamentary committee and the rapporteur will eventually reflect this caution. it is also significant that the majority of the economic operators consulted expressed reservations and apprehensions about the adoption of a new criterion, especially in view of the fact that the abuse of a dominant position criterion has worked well so far. the effort made by the commission, following the green paper of december 2001, in presenting this proposal for a regulation is very commendable and should generally deserve the support of parliament. it is, however, essential, in line with the report under discussion, that some amendments be introduced to improve the text by emphasizing legal certainty and, in particular, by highlighting the role that the employees of the companies joining should have in the study of the whole process and in providing not only relevant information but also guarantees of economic and social success of the operation under consideration.
- the next item is the report (a5-0311/2003) by mr rack, on behalf of the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism, on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the minimum safety requirements for tunnels in the trans-european road network (com (2002) 769 - c5-0635/2002 - 2002/0309 (cod)).
commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, you all remember the very serious fires in road tunnels in france, italy, austria and switzerland in 1999 and 2001. in order to ensure that such disasters do not happen again, or at least that they do not have such dramatic consequences if they do, the commission sent you a proposal for a directive earlier this year to establish minimum safety requirements for tunnels. it was also encouraged by several resolutions adopted by your parliament, notably after the fire in the gotthard tunnel in october 2001. the commission proposal covers all road tunnels over 500 metres in length on the transeuropean network, i.e. about 500 tunnels. the tunnels of the trans-european network are used by motorists of all nationalities and it appears that the consequences of fires can be considerably reduced if people in such a situation have standard safety equipment and uniform information on the best course of action to take to protect themselves. the proposal contains technical requirements and organisational requirements. the most important measures can be summarised as follows, without listing all of them. long tunnels will need to be equipped with a range of high-performance equipment, in particular emergency doors and advanced ventilation systems. automatic incident detectors will have to be able to inform the tunnel operator of potential hazards. the commission also proposes the installation of uniform safety signs, easily understandable by all users. all the technical measures proposed seem to us to be necessary. some were surprised at the very technical nature of the proposal, but if one compares the envisaged requirements with the technical rules established by international bodies or at national level, it can be seen that they are necessary to cover the essential aspects. organisational roles and responsibilities will now have to be clearly divided between the main stakeholders, which are the administrative authority, the tunnel operator and the safety manager. the measures will apply to new tunnels, but also to existing tunnels, which will have to be brought into conformity according to a timetable spread over 10 to 15 years. member states with a higher number of tunnels than the european average will have a longer period to bring the old tunnels into conformity with the directive. this is a long-term task for the engineers responsible for tunnel safety in the member states and it is important that the directive is approved as soon as possible. i also know from the contacts we have already had with some of you that we can count on you to reach a rapid agreement with the council on this matter.
mr president, let me also begin by emphasizing the quality of arlindo cunha as a member of parliament and as a european citizen and also how much he will be needed by this parliament and the committees on agriculture and fisheries. however, since he has gone to portugal to take up an important post in charge of a large portuguese region, the north of portugal, i hope that he will be very successful in these functions. and i do not have - being from a different party from that of mr arlindo cunha - the same problems as those shown here by mr struan stevenson, the chairman of the committee on fisheries, who, as he is not a member of the british labour party, has shown some distance from the policy of the british government. i have no problem with that, but it is a question of style: on the one hand the british style and on the other the lusitanian, the iberian style. let me also begin, mr president, by emphasizing how correct and balanced i find the report by mr cunha and the commission's communication. i would like to be as sober as commissioner fischler, who basically said that he agreed with the report and that it confirmed the content of the commission's communication. it's a fact. there seems to be no fundamental difference of opinion between us on this matter. i would say that the diplomacy that the european union has developed in the fisheries sector is an interesting diplomacy, which has led, as mr struan stevenson has also said, to a very interesting and very original model of fisheries agreements, which we can even consider exemplary and which can perfectly well serve as a model for other countries in their relations and negotiations on long-distance fishing. i would say that this diplomacy must continue to develop without any complexes in order to defend the interests of the european union's long-range fleet. this fleet cannot be considered to be portuguese, spanish or french, but it must be understood as a fleet of the european union, since the commission is the only interlocutor, the only actor in these international relations. mr president, i support the report by mr arlindo cunha and also the content of the commission's text. i hope that the european union's long-distance fisheries will continue to develop along the three lines of conservation of resources, solidarity with the poorest people and equity towards those working in the fishing industry. i would like to conclude by saying that we must fight against illegal fishing, against flags of convenience, which are sometimes the worst enemies of fishing and of genuine fishermen.
mr president, i also join in congratulating our colleague, mr arlindo cunha, and congratulating him on the work he has done here in the committee on fisheries and the committee on agriculture. i would like to mention this report, and to say that international fisheries agreements are undoubtedly a very important part of the common fisheries policy, ensuring the maintenance of fishing activity in many regions of the european union - more than 30 000 direct jobs - helping to reduce the community's trade deficit in fishery products and providing more than 20% of total community catches, and therefore we must give them our full support. studies show that one euro invested in these fisheries agreements generates economic activity of 3 euros, creating a benefit clearly outweighing the cost. it is therefore important to improve and strengthen this component, even taking into account the conclusions of the fisheries council of october 1997, which have already been discussed here. and this is all the more important because there are those who are questioning these agreements. however, i would like to point out that the commission should take account of some important aspects of these agreements. and one of those central issues is the question of its funding. it is true that there must be coherence between the common fisheries policy and development policy, but it must not be forgotten that these agreements are essentially trade agreements: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. and so more partnership agreements must be developed, also taking into account, in an equitable way, the interests of the various countries and their respective fleet segments. i would like to conclude by saying that it is not understandable that there are agreements in the european union with different conditions, as the rapporteur has pointed out: in some countries, shipowners pay for fishing licences; in others, they pay nothing. it is therefore necessary to solve not only this problem but also the question of paper quotas and the possibility of temporarily transferring unused fishing rights. i hope that, thanks also to the support we give to mr arlindo cunha's report, the commission will also take account of the proposals he makes in his work.
mr president, on the middle east conflict, we continue to see positions taken that either side with israel against palestine or condemn the israelis in favour of the palestinians. some of them have their reasons. the unwavering right of defence of innocent israeli populations and the natural aspiration of the palestinians to freely shape their future are naturally among these reasons. where reason certainly does not lie is in the terror to which both peoples of that region are voted. in our view, it is still on the road map that there is still some hope for peace between israelis and palestinians. this initiative, which involves not only the belligerents but also the united states, russia, the united nations and the european union, must be improved but cannot be abandoned. its objectives, which are to end the conflict by 2005 by eliminating violence and terrorism and allowing the peaceful coexistence of a future palestinian state alongside israel based on an effective democracy based on tolerance and freedom, which, we must admit, has not yet been implemented, remain valid. it is absolutely vital to go back to the step-by-step method, expecting each party to fulfil its obligations to the other at each stage. what we cannot accept is the present reality. the positive steps are few, very few, and those that have been taken have been met with violence. if the conditions for the emergence of strong bonds of mutual trust are not created, we will not only continue to see the death of innocent civilians, but the day will soon come when hope itself will die. the status quo is therefore unacceptable. the european union is therefore obliged to step up its pressure, together with the other relevant partners, to make a possible and lasting resumption of the peace process. unlike other colleagues who have spoken here, we have serious doubts that the solution lies in the deployment of an interim military force on the ground, composed of armed forces from a coalition of countries. we obviously do not accept the erection of a wall separating the two territories. what does not seem acceptable is the attempt to replace it with a human barrier, albeit one that is well armed, organized and legitimized by the international community. it would also be a classic military response which would not solve a typical urban guerrilla situation. in our view, what is needed is to make it clear to the palestinian authorities that the despicable suicide attacks on israeli civilians must stop once and for all, and that the full force of european diplomatic pressure must be used to this end. on the other hand, it is essential to ensure that the israeli democracy's response is contained and to warn the neighbouring countries in the region to refrain from harbouring and supporting terrorist groups whose bases continue to feed and engage in criminal activities. as we have said repeatedly, there is no good terrorism, just as there is no bad terrorism. no form of terrorism can be justified. it's not justifiable. no reason for committing it can be tolerated, unless we are recognizing its legitimate purposes. wherever terrorism resides, wherever it intervenes, whatever form it takes, it is also the european union's duty not to waver in its fight against it. we are convinced that the resolution of the middle east conflict would deprive international terrorism of a powerful ideological ally.
in writing. as i saw during a recent visit to palestine, the israeli government, despite criticism and protests, continues to build settlements and the wall of shame, the military occupation, the destruction of infrastructure, housing and other equipment, targeted killings, the keeping in israeli prisons of more than seven thousand palestinian prisoners, including some 340 children, and the constant violation of the most elementary rights of the palestinian people, attacking syria and practicing genuine state terrorism. it is therefore with frustration and indignation that we hear the statements of european officials demanding respect for the law. how can we demand that president arafat and the palestinian government take action against terrorist acts if israel is militarily occupying palestine? the european union must take practical initiatives and measures. the 'euro-mediterranean eu-israel association agreement' should be suspended, as called for in the ep's resolution on the 'situation in the middle east' of 10 april 2002. the commission and the council must take the initiative within the un to demand compliance with the un resolutions, recognise the right of the palestinians to dignity and to an independent state, send international observers and a un-led intervention and peacekeeping force.
