in writing. - (pt) i believe that it is essential to improve the coordination of the legislative process. this is why i largely agree with the interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament, the council and the commission, which aims to improve the quality of legislation through a series of new initiatives and procedures. among these, i would like to highlight the creation of indicative timetables for the different phases leading to the final adoption of each legislative proposal, as well as the attempt to ensure better synchronisation of the processing of dossiers at the level of the preparatory bodies of each branch of the legislative authority. i welcome the reference to 'self-regulation', which is outside the union's mandate and allows private partners to adopt common guidelines at european level for themselves and among themselves. the draft agreement also addresses the question of better transposition of community law into national legislation. the institutions undertake to ensure that all directives include a legally binding deadline and as short a transposition period as possible. in my view, the result of this agreement is quite balanced and fulfils the objective of improving the quality of community legislation. i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. - (pt) we are of the opinion that a space policy based on cooperation between member states should be based clearly and unambiguously on the non-proliferation of weapons, the peaceful use of space and the rejection of the arms race in space. that is why we have always denounced and criticised the united states for proposing the creation of a national missile defence system, which will militarize the use of space and trigger an arms race, with terrible consequences for the future of all humanity. not only does the report not criticise the militarisation of space, but it goes so far as to give a central role to a 'european agency for armaments, research and military capabilities', proposing a partnership with the european space agency and underlining 'the dual character of civil and military activities' in space. the resolution also supports the military use of satellite systems to carry out what it euphemistically calls 'peacekeeping operations', which means paving the way for war operations. the resolution therefore runs counter to the spirit of united nations general assembly resolution 49/74 of 15 december 1994 on the prevention of an arms race in outer space, and in particular to article 4 thereof. that is why we voted against the resolution.
in writing. - (pt) the tendency towards greater concentration and centralisation of capital is inherent in the capitalist system and is driven by the primacy of competition and the increasing liberalisation and internationalisation of capital. the emphasis on this intensified inter-capitalist competition, linked to the permanent revolutions in production processes generated by technological developments and economies of scale, leads to the law of survival of the fittest, the elimination of competitors and the creation of increasingly oligopolistic or even monopolistic markets. competition policy, in particular merger control, is an attempt by the system to self-regulate and avoid the vicissitudes of economic cycles and the negative influences of dominant or concerted positions on markets. however, it is clear that it cannot reverse this general trend. in the light of the current liberalization processes and the extent of market integration, there has nevertheless been strong pressure to amend regulation no 4064/89, which was perceived as too restrictive in relation to the need to create powerful, internationally competitive industrial groups. the commission's proposal thus goes one step further with new concepts of concentration at community level. the rapporteur wants to go further. it wants a narrower concept of concentration, by minimising control or opposition to a concentration. in view of these facts, we also reject this report.
in writing. - (pt) like the rapporteur, i welcome the european commission's intention to carry out a thorough review of the community antitrust or competition system. in this context, this proposal for a regulation is a further important step forward. several recent decisions of the european court of justice have highlighted the need to clarify and simplify competition rules, particularly in the light of the competitive environment in other regions of the world. in general, both the courts and the business community stress the need to take into account the requirements of a free and dynamic market, which should not be unduly burdened by long and cumbersome procedures for transactions that are in no way illegal but are part of the normal functioning of a free market. a regulation of the various aspects of community competition law - in particular the rules on state aid, mergers, abuse of a dominant position or concerted actions aimed at distorting the market - should never lose sight of the requirements of an open and free economy that wants to be regulated, nor of the appropriate level of eu intervention in companies and member states. this level, as we know, is governed by the principle of proportionality in this area. since the rapporteur has succeeded in introducing both these concerns, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) in responding to the attacks of 11 september 2001, the european union showed its solidarity with the united states' objective of preventing and combating terrorism. however noble these aims may be, the ends do not justify the means. the united states has adopted a number of measures to strengthen border controls, such as requiring airlines to provide passenger name record (pnr) data. in march this year, the european parliament considered that it was unacceptable for such data to be transmitted if it could not be guaranteed that an appropriate level of protection and compliance with the community rules in force was being respected. the commission's conclusions indicate that the data protection provided is not sufficient: the objective justifying the collection and storage of data remains unclear; the number of data appears excessive and disproportionate; the data are retained for an excessive period; the united states has not complied with any obligation; and there is no recourse for passengers or the eu itself. it is therefore essential that any transmission of data in breach of community rules should cease. we need to determine what data can be transmitted and ensure that there is no discrimination or retention of data beyond the period of a passenger's stay. passengers should be fully informed in advance and should always have access to a prompt and effective redress system.
in writing. - (pt) the current situation, where the us authorities have access to the personal data of passengers on transatlantic flights (pnr or 'passenger name record') from computerised reservation systems (apis or 'advance passenger information system') is unacceptable. this situation violates the right to the protection of personal data, including the community directive in force, as the resolution actually states: - the objective remains vague; there is a risk that the data may be used for other purposes, including transmission to other us government departments; - the number of data required (39) is incomprehensible and disproportionate; - the retention period for data (6/7 years) appears unjustified; - passengers have no means of effective control or extrajudicial redress; the us threats to withdraw landing rights from airlines which do not comply with its requirements are also unacceptable. we demand that the right to the protection of personal data be fully respected and that we do not give in to american demands by seeking to establish exceptions to the rules in force in europe. the compatibility, in the light of these same rules, of the proposal to introduce the so-called european union passport containing electronic chips has, however, still to be debated.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, forests represent a priceless and irreplaceable heritage of humanity and all living beings. protecting and preserving them is a survival imperative. we all know the importance of forests for the balance of the earth's globe, for biodiversity and for economic activities, in addition to the aesthetic and environmental values they contain. europe is concerned about the future of forests and must start by setting an example in protecting its forest areas, whether in the mediterranean or the nordic countries, since the problems of forests know no borders. the forest focus regulation aims to build on the experience of the two previous regulations and to create a long-term monitoring system to assess the state of the forest ecosystem in the european union. it also reveals a great ambition: to cover areas such as pollution, climate change, biodiversity, natural resources and soils. it's all right, man. the regulation had, however, two weaknesses: first, it reduced the financial envelope to such a high level of ambition that the commitment was only softened; the second weakness was the sacrifice of the fire prevention strand which had been transferred to rural development programmes. the resumption of the firefighting dimension is appeasing to us, and there is undisputed progress. the commission's promise that when it presents its communication on the forestry strategy, due by the end of the year, it will include a proposal on fire protection planning was not enough for us. we are still very much alive in the images of the gigantic fires of last summer, which left a trail of desolation in portugal in particular, a trail which will not be easily erased from memory and landscapes.
mr president, forest fires are a plague that destroys thousands of hectares of forest each year in the european union, particularly in the southern countries. we know that this year not only has the rule not been broken, but the situation has reached tragic proportions in the southern countries and in particular in portugal, where 20 people have died, where 45 000 have lost their sources of income, and where it is estimated that more than 11% of the forest area has been burned, with a total of more than eur 1 300 million in direct damage. this disaster illustrates the need for the european union to support measures to combat forest fires, particularly in the field of prevention. this is what the european parliament understood by a large majority in its resolution of 4 september 2003 on the consequences of the summer heat when it called not only for a financial increase in the forest focus programme but also for the inclusion in it of appropriate preventive measures to ensure the continuity of the measures provided for in regulation 2158/92, which expired on 31 december 2002. i would also like to point out that not all the fire prevention measures included in this regulation are covered by the forestry-related measures provided for in the recent regulation 1999/1257 on rural development. it is important to continue the preventive measures which the present situation makes even more urgent. our colleague the rapporteur rightly insists once again on the inclusion of the first reading amendments on prevention, which were then rejected by the council. it mr president, with the scourge of the fires that struck portugal last summer, devastating more than 10% of the national territory, it has become more evident that much of the disaster could have been avoided with effective prevention measures. it is worth recalling the old popular saying "prevention is better than cure". during his visit to the burnt-out regions, commissioner michel barnier himself drew attention to this fact. it has become abundantly clear that instruments are needed to monitor, but above all to prevent, the factors that are deteriorating forests. only a study of the causes and effects of fires will allow a relentless fight against them. prevention measures are therefore aimed at reducing the size of burnt areas, combating the causes of fires and monitoring forests. the european union cannot simply monitor fires and intervene after the disaster has occurred. a real policy of prevention is needed. however, it is not a question of imposing undesirable measures on portugal, but of developing concrete and vigorous measures which are part of the national forestry strategy that is being developed. i therefore argue that prevention should be an integral part of the forest focus programme, irrespective of the existence of the rural development regulation. when it comes to a subject as important as the forest, one of europe's treasures, one cannot afford to save a few pennies. for this reason, and with a view to financing these prevention measures, i have already advocated an increase in the budget of the european union through the financial perspective up to 2006. any preventive measure is only really operational if it is provided with sufficient financial resources. finally, i could not conclude this speech without congratulating the rapporteur, encarnación redondo jiménez, on the sensitivity with which she has dealt with this subject, which is so sensitive for portugal.

mr president, in this joint debate on the second railway package, the european parliament is once again showing its support for the liberalisation of the railways and thus promoting greater competition in this sector in crisis. in this context, i believe that rapid liberalisation of the railway sector in all member states favours this type of transport as a credible alternative to combat the exceptional growth of air and road transport with its harmful consequences for the environment and land use planning. i believe that this liberalization can only be understood in the broad sense, i.e. greater competition in both freight and passenger transport, both in national and international traffic. this liberalisation will give any community railway undertaking equal access to the infrastructure of all member states for commercial purposes. but as i have already said, we must combat a widespread prejudice: the liberalization of rail transport does not invalidate the increase in safety standards. this railway package provides for the strengthening of safety standards, in particular by harmonizing the working and resting times of train drivers and other staff carrying out safety tasks. if technology allows for very high levels of safety, there is no good reason for legislation to be lagging behind by imposing standards that are less protective of passengers. the introduction of a black box on trains is another safety measure which i fully support. if this mechanism has demonstrated its clear advantages in the air and road sectors, in trucks and buses, i see no reason why this technique should not be applied to railways. in insisting on this priority of safety, i also express my support for the creation of a european railway agency, allowing greater madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, my first words will of course be to congratulate our rapporteurs neena gill and jan mulder. i should like to say that we are now facing the last budget to be voted on in this parliamentary term, and attention is increasingly turning to the multiannual financial framework which will guide our budgetary policy in the medium and long term, a framework on which the commission is discussing the grounds for its adoption and on which parliament itself will have to give its opinion. the report on this subject commissioned by president prodi raises some reservations. and, of course, the crucial question of economic and social cohesion. the budget of a federal state - as we increasingly want our budget to be - must have as its main feature a redistributive character. in a democratic, politically cohesive and socially responsible europe, this redistribution must be carried out with economic and social cohesion as the main objective. in fact, the same is true in the member states with a more federal structure, such as germany. the view taken by the sapir report, that there is a conflict between cohesion and growth, seems to us to be ideological and wrong. good cohesion policies are necessarily good policies for economic growth, just as bad cohesion policies are also necessarily bad policies for economic growth. the problem with the present functioning of the community budget is precisely that budgetary redistribution is sometimes made to the benefit of the most central countries and regions and even of large companies or multinationals, as in the case of subsidies for the disposal of products or export refunds, and these are the points that need to be reviewed more rigorously. these are the mechanisms and distortions which must be tackled by the next financial framework, and never economic and social cohesion, which must remain the great guiding political principle of the community budget.

mr president, despite the recognised competence of commissioner michel barnier, one of the most intriguing phenomena in european policy is undeniably the persistence of a significantly low level of implementation of the structural funds as measured by the rate of implementation of payment appropriations. this is all the more strange when the first objective of structural policy is sustainable development within the union. it is true that the persistence of a large and growing amount of unpaid commitments does not necessarily imply that all the ultimate objectives of cohesion policy cannot be achieved. it is necessary, moreover, that they be - and that they be done quickly - so that at least a good part of the remainder to be liquidated is not lost in the bureaucracy of the institutions or in the political and administrative incapacity of the governments of the member states. the fact that blame can and should be shared between the two decision-making levels is a logical consequence of the unequal distribution of implementation in the countries of the union and the various structural funds. making regional policy and the management of the structural funds more effective depends therefore on good national policy choices, but it also depends on regulations and the elimination of unnecessary bureaucratic requirements. the report acknowledges the role of the commission in introducing simplification measures, but also challenges the inadequacy of these measures and rightly proposes their re-evaluation. cohesion policy is on the agenda and its review has become irreversible with the publication of the sapir report. without now anticipating a political discussion, it is important to stress that the quickest and easiest way to make policies obsolete is to make them incomprehensible and unenforceable by applying the appropriate dose of bureaucracy and regulation. it is therefore essential and a matter of priority that the commission reinforce and emphasise its strategic role in setting priorities, leaving the bulk of responsibility for the implementation and management of funds to the member states. i therefore welcome the report by mr giovanni pittella, i recognize its opportunity and i support its proposals.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, no one today dares to question that the structural funds have been and continue to be a crucial instrument for reducing regional development inequalities. it is therefore very difficult for me to see that the funds available and unused amount to eur 91.6 billion, or the equivalent of the annual budget of the european union. at the end of the 1994-99 programming period, there were still some 300 erdf programmes which had not submitted any type of payment request. under these conditions, these values highlight the aberration. my only consolation is that portugal is one of the best member states in implementing the funds. in the context of the community support framework ii (csf ii), which has only just been completed, portugal has exemplary implementation rates: 99.6% for the erdf, 98.3% for the esf, 100% for the eaggf and 90% for the fifg. taken as a whole, portugal's implementation rate is 94.2%, well above its european partners. similarly, csf iii, which covers the period 2000-06, remains very problematic for the european union. once again, portuguese values are on the right track, according to the interim evaluation reports. (closed) the causes of such under-execution are known: long and complex programming, unreliable payment provisions and overlapping of different programming periods. the council, faced with the importance of the amounts to be used, has come up with solutions which, in my view, are too cautious. i am convinced that such measures will not have the effects that are expected of them, and some of them will even be counterproductive. the commission should be responsible for setting the priorities for the compliance of actions and monitoring implementation, leaving the member states with sole responsibility for the implementation and management of structural actions. moreover, this under-implementation of the structural funds seriously damages the image of the european union with its citizens. finally, as a portuguese and an algarve, i hope that the next csf-iv 2007-13 will continue to integrate the algarve as a region benefiting from structural actions, even in the context of an enlarged europe. if not, i think it is legitimate to demand a fair solution that will enable these regions, which are not eligible solely because of the statistical impoverishment of the enlarged european union, to be supported in their efforts towards convergence.
i also regret, mr president, that the structural funds have been under-utilized by some 22 billion euros. the concern is heightened by the fact that payments to be settled in the period 2000-2006 already amount to over €76 billion, and are at risk of being cancelled under the n+2 rule, which is regrettable given the high levels of unemployment and poverty in some member states, such as portugal, and the shortcomings in social facilities and infrastructure that are essential for social inclusion. since economic and social cohesion is a central objective of the european union and the structural funds are therefore indispensable to promote real convergence and constitute a redistributive factor at the level of the community budget, their non-use not only undermines this objective but may contribute to exacerbating existing regional inequalities. the causes of this situation must therefore be tackled, whether by solving the bureaucratic problems by means of simplification and decentralisation measures, or above all by revising the budgetary constraints imposed by the stability pact, and not forgetting that the structural funds are even more important at a time when the enlargement of the european union is being prepared. the policy of economic and social cohesion therefore requires that these procedures be revised in order to make effective use of all the funds.

in writing. - (pt) i share the rapporteur's view that ratification by or accession to the 1996 hague convention by member states will improve the protection of children's rights in matters of parental responsibility so that, as the rapporteur states, 'the best interests of the child remain the primary consideration in all decisions relating to children'. i welcome the proposals to ensure that the convention enters into force as soon as possible. i reject, however, the federalist ideas underlying this report. i must stress in particular how ironic and inexplicable it is to suggest that member states need the council's authorization to ratify or accede to this convention.
in writing. - (pt) i agree with the rapporteur when she says that the establishment of a harmonised and standardised judicial area is an extremely important element in the advancement of european integration in the area of parental responsibility. this proposal is an interesting step in that direction. in fact, it is intended to allow member states to ratify or accede to the hague convention in the interests of the european union, thus overcoming the technical obstacle that only sovereign states can be signatories to the convention. the importance of all this lies in the fact that the hague convention deals with jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition, enforcement and cooperation in matters of parental responsibility and child protection measures, and has already been the main source of inspiration for the future council regulation on parental responsibility, which the council continues to discuss. however, i do not share the rapporteur's view when she seeks to base her arguments on article 24 (2) of the charter of fundamental rights. the consideration of the best interests of the child should be invoked because of its intrinsically high value and not because it is required in a text which, in any event, has no legal value today. however, since it is a question of ensuring that in all judicial decisions concerning children, their best interests remain a primary consideration, i support the rapporteur's proposals.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate mr pittella on his report. it contributes to the complex debate on the structural funds. i would nevertheless like to draw attention to two points where the rapporteur's approach differs from mine and which have led me to table two draft amendments which i ask the house to support. the amendments are as follows: - amendment to paragraph 23 of the motion for a resolution: i would like to stress the importance of mentioning the principle of legitimate expectations in relation to the eligibility of advances granted by the member states to final beneficiaries and their inclusion in refund applications received before 31 december 2002. the principles of solidarity, flexibility and efficiency are complementary and not competitive. - amendment to paragraph 35 (b) of the motion for a resolution: in accordance with the principle of simplification, and on the basis of one of the objectives of improving the use of the funds, i propose that arrangements be made to analyse whether a combination of the funds and centralisation of their management would improve their effectiveness. this will depend on the course of events, which will enable us to decide at a later date whether such an analysis is appropriate.
in writing. - (pt) this report is a thorough and worrying examination of various issues related to the implementation of the structural funds. these funds constitute a system of redistribution of wealth through the community budget with a view to reducing disparities in development between member states and increasing economic and social cohesion. over the years, they have made visible progress towards these goals. there is no doubt, however, that the backlog in the implementation of the funds and the corresponding initiatives and instruments is getting worse. this is due, in large part, to two factors. firstly, it is very common for funds to be actually available only when the next programming period has already begun. on the other hand, the procedures are long and complex. the european commission must therefore address these issues in greater depth and consider more ambitious changes to procedures to combat the late approval and implementation of programmes and the unreliable nature of financial forecasts. in line with the objectives of the lisbon 2000 strategy, the effectiveness of the structural funds must be strengthened and coordination between the various community services and national and regional administrations must be improved. as the report suggests, it is very important to strike a balance between desirable simplification measures and the controls needed to achieve economic and social cohesion, while keeping in mind the current enlargement challenge. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - (pt) i cannot agree more with the proposals of both the committee of independent experts and the european parliament that a single directorate-general should be fully responsible for the implementation of the structural funds in each member state. this would improve coordination between the various community services and the national and regional administrations concerned. i would also like to stress the need to give more money to the quality of projects and the real impact of the structural funds on the regions concerned.

mr president, history shows that europe would benefit from speaking with one voice and from having common diplomatic and military instruments. at a time when europe is trying to build institutions capable of embodying a collective destiny, the war in iraq has laid bare the immense distance still to be covered. the introduction of a new figure, the minister for foreign affairs of the european union, with one, two or three hats, in the colourful language of mr berthu, into the draft constitution gives us reason for hope. will the organ work? will this one get strong content? i hope so. we cannot accept that there are two separate and distinct elements in the construction of europe: the economy, which is adapted to integration, and politics, in its strong and classic sense, which is hostile to it. in reality, this dichotomy does not exist and is not part of the nature of european construction. when questioned, european citizens overwhelmingly support a common foreign and defence policy. the european legislator does not therefore run the risk of being accused of taking an avant-garde attitude, divorced from public opinion, if he moves towards a europe of defence and security. the european citizens want to feel secure against threats of external or internal violence, but they do not want to be vassals of any unilateral power, even if it presents itself as an ally. perhaps all of you dream of the project of perpetual peace of immanuel kant but know that the road is arduous and the angelism in history is expensive.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, once again we are faced with a measure in the context of the creation of an area of freedom, security and justice - which is intended to respond to the concerns of citizens' daily lives - the great objective we set ourselves to achieve and where all citizens should see their integrity protected, have access to justice and see their rights guaranteed, regardless of where they are and as easily as if they were in their own country. it is important to establish minimum standards for state compensation and to facilitate access to compensation in cross-border situations, so as to provide an ultimate guarantee for the victim when he or she cannot access compensation from the offender or by other means. we know very well that victims are often unable to obtain full compensation from the offender, either because he does not have the necessary means, or because he has disappeared, or because he has never been identified. we want to avoid that, because of the profound disparities between the systems in the various member states, there should be unjustifiable differences in the compensation to which citizens are entitled simply because they have been the victims of an offence in one place in the european union rather than another, which is inexplicable, especially in the light of the existence of a common area of freedom, security and justice. i therefore welcome this proposal for a directive, as well as the report by mrs roberta angelilli, which does not seek to harmonize but rather to establish minimum standards, allowing member states who so wish to maintain them or introduce more generous provisions for the victims of the disaster. the principle of territoriality should be applied first, so that the member state on whose territory the crime was committed is responsible for the payment of compensation, with the victim having the additional right to lodge a claim for compensation with an authority of the member state in which he or she resides in order to avoid secondary victimisation. i would stress that the principles of social justice must be respected, requiring each member state to compensate not only its own nationals but also other victims of violence on its territory, such as migrant workers, students, tourists and others.
mr president, commissioner, mr president of the committee on fisheries, dear rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, i would ask our colleagues catherine stihler and struan stevensen in particular to extend my words of deep solidarity to the fishermen of shetland and all of scotland, and indeed all the regions of europe directly affected by this tragedy. the precedents we know, particularly in newfoundland, do not reassure us. and the possibility that we have crossed the point of no return, the point where even the most radical measures will not allow a sustainable cod fishery for the future, is a possibility we cannot rule out. i can only say, ladies and gentlemen, that while we are sympathetic to the victims of the disaster, we must also take the necessary measures to prevent the destruction of our biological resources by an irrational common fisheries policy and to prevent this tragedy from being repeated in many other parts of europe. contrary to the democratic will of this parliament and contrary to the views of the scientific community throughout europe, the council, with the active collaboration of the commission, has recently liberalized access to most of the azores exclusive economic zone and is now threatening to liberalize the use of predatory gear, including bottom trawling in much of this exclusive economic zone. with this measure the commission is taking a step which could lead to a repetition of the tragedy we have seen in the north sea, in the parts of the central atlantic that have been protected from devastation until today. we therefore urgently need a new fisheries policy which transposes into community law the rules of international maritime law, the right of property as recognised by the european charter of fundamental rights, and the precautionary principle, which is always stated but never practised. we need a fisheries policy that does not simply give obituaries after approving conditions that do not allow or encourage sustainable fishing. in writing. - (pt) the draft budget for 2004 confirms the trend towards a reduction in the size of the budget, especially since 1997. this draft budget represents less than 1% of the community's gross domestic product, whereas it is the enlargement budget, with increased needs for economic and social cohesion, and whereas the eu is currently experiencing an economic recession. as a result of agenda 2000, the restrictive financial framework of the copenhagen council and the consequences of the constraints imposed by the stability pact, which directly affects budgetary implementation, the budgetary procedure has become a grocery store where trifling matters are discussed and a policy of transfers, cuts and redistribution of funds is applied. all this affects the transparency of the budget. we regret that the creation of a budget line for reconstruction in palestine, with a budget of eur 20 million, has been rejected, given the deterioration in the living conditions of the palestinian population and its infrastructure. however, we welcome the european parliament's approval of our proposal to ask the commission to maintain the level of funding for east timor, given the continued reconstruction needs and international commitments to the country. this is to redress the injustice of the 70% reduction proposed by the commission, which has eliminated the specific budget line for east timor.
in writing. - (pt) the community's criminal justice system has always focused on the perpetrator of the offence and on the imposition of penalties based on the offence committed. the victim is given little importance, subject to different national compensation systems, which have serious difficulties in coordination and application in specific cases of cross-border crime. it is therefore important to establish minimum standards which define the concepts of 'victim' and 'offence', determine who may be entitled to compensation in the event of the death of the victim and lay down the terms and forms of payment. i think it is particularly impressive that the rapporteur considers it essential to guarantee compensation. this is essential not only to mitigate, as far as possible, the harm and suffering, but also to alleviate the social conflict produced by crime and to facilitate the application of a rational and correct criminal policy. a society which claims to be a guarantor of individual rights should also guarantee the protection of its citizens in their individual dimension. i warmly congratulate the rapporteur on his excellent work. i voted for his report.
in writing. - (pt) as the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices) pointed out at the end of 2000, cod stocks are seriously threatened by collapse in the north sea. this poses a serious threat to the environment and the sustainability of resources, but also to fishermen and the fleet sectors affected by these catches. in december 2002, the council proposed a definitive recovery plan for these stocks with the aim of ensuring that cod stocks are restored to the precautionary levels recommended by the experts within five to ten years. in addition, there must be a balance in the planned actions, taking into account the socioeconomic consequences. this requires measures to compensate for the costs incurred by fleet sectors and the fisheries regions that depend on these catches, as well as ensuring the full involvement of the main stakeholders in the recovery of stocks, i.e. fishermen. it should also be clear that the necessary funding for these measures must be secured, while the flexibility instrument must be mobilised or the financial perspective revised.
in writing. - (pt) the commission's proposal to develop a recovery plan for cod stocks in the north sea and adjacent waters is in response to data showing that these stocks are on the verge of depletion. this would reduce fishing activities, affecting fishing communities on the west, east and north coasts of ireland, northern scotland and the islands to the north and west of scotland. these are peripheral and extremely vulnerable areas, given the limited scope for diversification of the local economy and limited access to markets. therefore, as this report seeks to balance the need to pursue established objectives of restoring stocks with the socioeconomic impact on the fishing sector and the communities heavily dependent on this activity, i could only support it. i believe that the emphasis in this report on flexibility and local participation - particularly that of fishermen and regional advisory councils, as suggested by the rapporteur - in the recovery plan seems to me indispensable in this respect. the call for a report on the impact of industrial fishing on cod stocks, which is still controversial, is also interesting.
in writing. - (pt) i regret that my group's proposal to amend this common position, which was approved by the european parliament in plenary, has been rejected. the majority of parliament and the council both want the sector to be liberalised and extended to include national rail freight networks, although the members of this house are more pressed for action. parliament stressed that freight services (international and national) and international passenger transport should have access to rail networks from 1 january 2006. the council proposes that date for international freight services and 1 january 2008 for the opening of all member states' infrastructures for use for all types of rail freight services. it does not provide for international passenger transport. the council calls on the commission to present, by 1 january 2007, a report on the application of the directive, in particular as regards the functioning of the various organisations involved; the evolution of the market, trends in international traffic, the activities and market share of all the players; the overall impact on the transport sector; the impact on the level of safety in each member state and the working conditions in the sector by member state, which parliament does not want to accept.
in writing. - (pt) i agree with the proposal by the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism, which, following the line of the rapporteur, supports the acceleration of the opening up of the railway market, proposing the beginning of 2008 as the deadline for the full liberalisation of national passenger services. i also support other amendments which make a positive contribution to the revival of the railway sector and which establish a balanced relationship between the modes of transport of goods and people within the framework of the principles set out in the white paper on european transport policy. i hope that this is a further step towards the goal of a genuine internal railway market, which will also make it possible to reduce the intensity of traffic on our roads, especially the huge volume of goods carried by large heavy goods vehicles.
in writing. - (pt) when considering the railway package which is being put to the vote today, and which i fully support, the geography of the european union must always be borne in mind, not forgetting the peripheral territories of the current member states and the new 'enlargement' countries. portugal cannot remain outside the system of transeuropean rail networks. the portuguese government is undecided, but the union must not be so permissive and must focus on respecting a timetable for overall infrastructure within the union.
in writing. - (pt) the purpose of this directive is to introduce community safety objectives (csos) and community safety methods (csms). the council considered that they should ensure the maintenance and improvement of a high level of safety and its improvement, in so far as this is reasonably feasible and taking into account the competitiveness of the rail transport mode. this criterion of competitiveness, together with that of the proper functioning of the internal market, is the basis for the whole content of this directive. we voted against many of the amendments because the objective of greater railway safety will not be achieved by the european parliament's proposals, which only define minimum standards at european level and prevent member states from establishing different national standards unless they are agreed by the others and do not affect the free movement of trains. once again, the european parliament is adopting a maximalist position which we reject.
in the case of the railways, the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the safety standards are not exceeded. that is why i voted in favour of this report. i have long argued that rail should be given priority over road in all these areas, especially for the transport of large volumes of goods over long distances. the good safety indicators of european rail transport consistently confirm this argument. such a policy would automatically relieve our congested and accident-prone roads and highways. the liberalisation of rail services will do much to help this, although the supervision and monitoring of safety rules, including the maintenance of infrastructure, should be a matter for the public authorities. as i said in the first reading vote, i also support the introduction of a safety certificate for railway undertakings and infrastructure managers, the appropriate training of all staff, full access to safety information for all railway undertakings and the adoption of a single working language for international rail transport.
in writing. - (pt) the full implementation of this proposal for a european commission directive, which aims to speed up the implementation of interoperability between the various players in the trans-european rail system, is also directly linked to the creation of the european railway agency, which is the subject of the savary report. this is a good reason to add to the already long list of valid arguments in favour of the creation of the european agency and will lead to a high level of technical harmonisation. the valuable contribution of this agency will make it possible to ensure better coordination of the investments of the different member states in cross-border projects, to ensure the application of technical specifications for interoperability (tsis) developed by the european association for railway interoperability (aeif) and to financially support their application. the fact that parliament's committee has proposed very few amendments - only six, and very slight ones - to the council's common position is a good indication of the general consensus reached on this matter.
in writing. - (pt) i am pleased that the council has accepted the european parliament's proposal to involve workers' and users' organisations in the work of the agency, in particular its administrative board, but they must be able to be chosen by the structures they represent and not appointed by the commission. naturally, parliament wants representatives of workers' organisations to be involved in the working groups which will later go on to draw up recommendations, and not just in the consultation process which follows, as suggested by the council. contrary to the commission and parliament's proposal, the council proposes that the agency's management board be composed of one representative from each member state. parliament maintains the proposal to limit the council to only six representatives, which we reject. as regards the six representatives of railway undertakings, infrastructure managers, the railway industry, trade unions, passengers and freight customers, the council supports the commission's proposal that they be appointed by the commission.
in writing. - (pt) the vote in the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism - 44 votes in favour and only 2 abstentions - clearly illustrates the benefits of the creation of a european railway agency, which would cooperate with the european commission in better coordination between the various actors involved in the railway system and in the creation of a standing committee that stimulates the debate through recommendations and opinions. the creation of this agency is further justified by the increasing liberalization of the sector and the future issuing of uniform safety rules in all member states. furthermore, provided that they are properly disclosed, the agency's consultation, proposal and observation activities can lead to greater awareness, both in the member states and among european citizens, of the enormous benefits offered by rail transport. i agree with the view of the committee on transport, which wants to involve road operators in the work of the agency. however, i disagree when, as regards the composition of the agency, the committee rejects the idea that the council's representation on the agency's management board covers the whole spectrum of member states. this representation could be substantial and should at least include all countries with large rail networks and/or that are part of the trans-european networks.
in writing. - (pt) i am concerned about the emergence of this lucrative but odious phenomenon which threatens the physical integrity of people. it has become a privileged area of activity for organised networks that exploit the differences and gaps in the laws of the member states, at the expense of the most vulnerable groups, such as children - the number of kidnappings in brazil and guatemala is shocking - and people living in conditions of extreme poverty. with the enlargement of the eu in 2004, action at european level has become even more urgent, as there is a potential risk of new lucrative trade routes emerging, in particular through and to hungary and the czech republic. an integrated community approach is needed, and the definitions of offences associated with trafficking in organs and tissues of human origin and the corresponding sanctions must be harmonised. an element of extraterritoriality should be introduced to prevent individuals from seeking to purchase organs illegally outside the territory of the union. we need to look at the underlying causes of this crime: the acute shortage of organs available for transplantation, which is largely due to a lack of public information. various studies indicate that the vast majority of citizens say they are ready to donate their organs after death, but only a small percentage express their formal consent.
in writing. - (pt) since the proposal under consideration is based on the idea that the human body should not be a source of profit. i therefore voted in favour of this initiative by the hellenic republic. i have always rejected any act which threatens human integrity, especially when it comes to cases of easy enrichment at the expense of vulnerable third parties. i also welcome this initiative, because i have to admit that it is easy for these traffickers to operate in eu countries because of the free movement within the community area. the rules must be very clear, all these illegal activities must be sanctioned and punished. however, trade in organs and tissues of human origin is legitimate when it takes place for medical purposes, within a very narrow and strictly regulated framework. i therefore support the rapporteur's amendment under the framework decision, which should be 'illegal trafficking in organs, parts of organs and tissues of human origin', because i believe that this legitimate and strictly regulated trade is appreciable and legal (for example, in the case of semen, blood and its derivatives). i also think it is good to urge the commission to create databases: one for legally available organs - accessible to the whole medical profession in the eu; and another, pan-european, of patients waiting for a transplant... in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this important report. in the wake of the european commission's communication, it brings back to the european agenda today and once again the decisive question of europe's future industrial policy, especially in the context of the current enlargement process. the industrial policy of the union is currently undergoing a change, faced with the consequences of the euro and enlargement. a new approach to industrial policy is needed, which should be based on the following priorities: maintaining efforts in education, training and skills; reducing tax barriers; increasing investment in research and innovation; ensuring the quality of infrastructure (transport, communications and energy); facilitate business financing and social dialogue; make business creation procedures more flexible, etc. only if these different aspects are respected will it be possible to achieve the objectives set out in the lisbon strategy and to move towards harmonisation within an enlarged europe, based on the current union's labour rules. finally, it is imperative to strengthen, promote and support the entrepreneurial side of industry, always seeking economic efficiency as well as social and human efficiency. as the committee on industry, foreign trade, research and energy has drawn up a balanced report, i voted in favour.

mr president, commissioners, members of the house, in the committee on fisheries we have examined and debated the commission's proposals for an action plan to be implemented from 2003 to 2005 to ensure that access to and exploitation of fishery resources are controlled throughout the fishing chain and are subject to a single regulatory and control procedure applicable to both catches and the transport and marketing of fishery products, a system which should produce comparable results, irrespective of the nationality of the executor and the competent national inspection service. there is a broad consensus in the european parliament and in the fisheries sector on the need to improve coordination at community level of inspection and surveillance activities, to streamline resources, to establish priorities, particularly in areas where greater cooperation between member states is needed, in particular in international areas managed by regional organisations in which the european union is a contracting party. it is also considered positive that progress is being made in measures to harmonize processes and objectives, building on the experience gained in the various countries over the years, particularly in the field of cross-border cooperation, while always bearing in mind the role of the national authorities in monitoring and evaluating inspection and surveillance activities in dialogue with the sector and the national authorities, without losing sight of the different regional realities and without calling into question the functions of each member state. as has been stressed on several occasions, the effective implementation of the common fisheries policy implies first and foremost that fishermen support and respect fisheries regulations, which will be improved by the participation of fishermen's organisations in the decision-making process at all levels. and that is one aspect which we think is particularly important. but equally important is that measures are taken to make more effective use of national means of inspection and surveillance in selected fisheries and stocks, which should be the subject of analysis and debate among all parties involved, including fishermen's, producers' and shipowners' organisations, and national authorities. however, we draw attention to the high costs of using new technologies which are important for this mr president, the reduction of administrative obstacles to the free movement of vehicles and persons and the establishment of a direct link between the annual road tax to be applied to passenger cars madam president, the spread of unemployment, precarious employment and poverty and social exclusion calls into question the notion of a europe that is a champion of social justice and solidarity. it is known that in the european union there are more than 15 million unemployed and some 60 million people living on less than 60% of the national average income, problems that affect mainly women, but also older people with very low pensions, migrants, children, disabled people and workers with precarious and low-paid work. and this situation is made much worse when we look at the situation of the candidate countries which will be members of the union from may next year. the worsening of this economic and social situation calls for different measures than those already adopted, since there is a tendency towards an increase in disparities, a weakening of cohesion and some backsliding in the policy of equality between women and men. the current situation requires that we no longer regard the implementation of the stability pact as an absolute priority but rather suspend it in order to review its irrational criteria for nominal convergence, that we end the primacy of monetary and competition policies and put the response to serious social problems, the implementation of the social policy agenda and an effective public investment policy on the agenda to create the 15 million jobs that are missing in the european union. so, as i said in my recent report on the implementation of the social policy agenda, which this house adopted last september, the serious problems of unemployment and poverty - including persistent poverty - must be given priority in all community policies, particularly in competition policy (and as the commissioner responsible for the common agricultural policy is here, at least if this is to help look at agricultural issues and also change policy there to combat poverty and social exclusion), not forgetting the structural funds and the stability pact. we regret that the commission not only does not comply with the nice social policy agenda, but also continues to fail to provide for the presentation of new initiatives in areas already requested by the european parliament, insisting on their rapid elaboration. it is a long list which my colleagues have already mentioned here, but which we also approved here at the last part-session on 3 september and which i subscribe to again, and i am in agreement with all the questions which have been raised here. i would stress the need for effective measures, for mechanisms of intervention in the area of relocation of companies, for directives on article 13, both on the rights of women in all areas other than employment and on the rights of disabled people. it is urgent to overcome the delays in improving the directives aimed at promoting health and safety at work, especially for women. it is urgent that the proposals which this parliament has already adopted be implemented.

in writing. - (pt) it would be useful to establish common standards for all member states concerning the respect and protection of the individual rights of suspects, accused persons or persons convicted in criminal proceedings, as proposed by the commission in its green paper. the laws must be understood and justice must be predictable, and as we know, an arbitrary approach will always result in unpredictable justice. furthermore, ignorance of the law does not justify breaking the law and does not benefit the perpetrators, who must know that there are criminal proceedings. this is even more important if the person concerned is a foreign national. i therefore agree to adopt common minimum standards on procedural guarantees, which will strengthen the trust of the persons concerned in the judicial authorities and the trust of the various officials of each member state in the judicial system of the other states. what really made me turn against this report - in its final formulation - is that it encourages standards that go far beyond the 'minimum', for example, the translator register, 'compensation' in the event of insolvency or the intervention of a psychiatrist. in other words, i do not agree with the recommendation for an extremely long list of changes, which would ultimately lead to greater safeguards for foreign nationals than for national nationals. i therefore regret that i had no choice but to vote against the report.

in writing. - (pt) the decision to draw up an own-initiative report on promoting women's participation in what is known as the 'new information society' was a good decision. i particularly welcome the following: - this report condemns the fact that the policy of developing new icts focuses largely on economic aspects and that the control of these icts is left primarily to the private sector, without an assessment of their social consequences or any real measures to promote equal rights for men and women. as the report says, this gives the false impression that everyone can take part. - this report warns of the risk of social exclusion due to the inability to use ict - the so-called digital illiteracy - which affects women to a large extent. - this report recognises the need to pay particular attention to women, in particular older women, unemployed women, women with low incomes, women emigrants, women from ethnic minorities and women with disabilities. however, i do not agree with the non-critical tone of the report towards the neoliberal policies advocated in the 'lisbon strategy' and the 'employment guidelines', thus turning a blind eye to the main causes of inequality and social injustice, of which women are the main victims.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report for the sole reason that i believe that the european union must focus its policies on promoting access for all to their legitimate rights, in particular those relating to knowledge. in this context, women should not be discriminated against - nor men. i regret, however, that the text cannot resist the temptation to give in to populism and feminist rhetoric under the cover of so-called neutral language. he is so intent on serving a radical agenda of ideas and language that he doesn't even realize how utterly ridiculous he is, because of his pretentious stereotypes and utter stupidity. take the rapporteur's irony for example. it explicitly expresses its desire to combat stereotypes and then suggests overcoming the social exclusion of girls and women - migrant women, women with disabilities, the poor, single mothers and farmers, women from ethnic minorities and older women - by providing different models of the roles that "successful, independent and happy women" can play in the field of information and communication technologies. is anyone taking this seriously? i also share the report's concern about linguistic diversity on the internet and i believe that this is a universal factor of social exclusion, even if it should be said that in this area men and women are on an equal footing.
in writing. - (pt) i support mrs honeyball's report because i think it shows the support that the european parliament gives to the commission so that the commission can open a real debate in the council on the essential tax harmonisation in the automobile sector. this proactive attitude is what the vast majority of european citizens want, because they associate excessive paperwork and high administrative costs, as well as the fragmentation of the car market, with the difficulties in consolidating the internal market. i would add that the essential environmental dimension, which this report deals with in depth, requires a new approach to car taxation.
in writing. - (pt) as the rapporteur quite rightly points out, the parliament already declared in 1998 that it was in favour of strengthening the internal market in this area and fought to put an end to double taxation - in particular through the registration tax - by supporting the european commission's proposal. the council has not yet taken a decision. the council did not give its opinion despite the fact that most citizens agree on the need to establish fairer conditions for the purchase of a car within the european union. look at portugal, for example, where a tax - the car tax - makes the final purchase price much higher than in other countries of the european union. the proposal to link the level of taxation to co2 emissions and the much-needed greater harmonisation of market conditions are to be welcomed. the report also notes that tax competition between member states is useful and can help to promote the eu's dynamic economic development. furthermore, i must point out that this subject does not objectively fall within the eu's fields of competence - see article 95 (2) of the treaty establishing the european community. since these ideas are much more than mere recommendations, i have decided to vote against the report.

madam president, two notes in this package deserve particular attention: the first concerns the double standards in the way the lisbon strategy is dealt with: the commission has been asked to take action to ensure that the member states do not lose sight of the social dimension and that the member states do not meet the objectives of employment, social inclusion, equal rights and opportunities, but when it comes to liberalising sectors of economic interest, the commission is required to bring infringement proceedings against member states which have been late in the liberalisation process, as in the clegg report on telecommunications, without even bothering to ask whether public services are guaranteed for all citizens. that is an unacceptable position. the second note concerns the increase in the financing ceiling from 10 to 30% of the total investment costs of a project at the stage of implementation, but without any increase in the total budget, which is problematic because it means that there will be fewer projects involved when it is necessary to ensure balanced development. that is, the poorer countries should not have any greater difficulty in obtaining financed projects. the increase in the ceiling must therefore be accompanied by an increase in the overall amount.
the commission's initiatives on the tax harmonization of motor vehicles and fuels are, in general, justified and positive. they are right because they are an essential element for the proper functioning of the internal market, seeking to eliminate or alleviate the anomalous situation of the heavily segmented car and fuel markets, and they are positive because they systematically value an approach to the environmental impact of motor traffic. transport and mobility are now key factors in the pricing of goods and services and it is therefore essential that they do not constitute
