in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the number of radioactive sources currently existing in the european union requires special care and attention in their management, packaging and handling. in addition, it is crucial that sources which for various reasons are beyond the control of the member states are detected and eliminated. the creation of the traceability system proposed by the commission could help to avoid exposure to ionising radiation resulting from improper source control and to ensure that safety is controlled. the aim of the proposed system is to prevent any malicious use of these sources and to enable their control within the european union by facilitating their harmonised management at european level, the continuous monitoring of their life cycle and the safe exchange of these sources between the countries of the union. i share the rapporteur's view that the responsibility of the supplier, the technical expert, in the life cycle of the various sources he makes available should be emphasised. i also approve of the obligation to control possible crossborder movements of the relevant sources, both within the european union and towards third countries, and the establishment, in accordance with the judicial and criminal traditions of the member states, of a system of harmonised sanctions to be applied in the event of infringement of the rules.
in writing. - (pt) the decision to set out the information to be displayed on signs at external border crossing points was first taken in 1994 in the context of the schengen system. the aim of this initiative is to update these indications and to establish uniform minimum indications to be displayed on the signs. the excellent report by mr deprez deserves our full support and it deals with the question of external borders, which was the weak link in the system. i would like to emphasize four main points: - the choice of the system of separate checkpoints, a welcome step given the differences in the control requirements for community citizens, for nationals of the european economic area or the swiss confederation and for nationals of third countries; - the fact that there should be no difference between the signposts for eu nationals and for nationals who enjoy the same rights when crossing borders - these signs should be as clear and simple as possible; - the fact that the authorities of the member states are obliged to affix signs in other languages or with other characters, particularly in multilingual countries, in those using an alphabet with specific characters or in those which are likely to receive many travellers using languages with specific characters. - the application of these measures not only at airports but also at land and sea borders.
in writing. - (pt) this is a set of measures relating to the crossing of the external borders of the member states and the control of persons at these borders, and these measures are, in my view, entirely justified. the system of separate checkpoints for citizens subject to community law at authorised crossing points at the external borders of the european union is fully justified. the signs must be clear and easy to understand ('eu'/'not eu'). in addition, the authorities of countries whose nationals are treated as eu nationals, such as iceland, norway and switzerland, must identify their nationals when they cross borders. words should also be avoided on signs where symbols are sufficiently explicit. finally, the authorities of the member states should be explicitly authorised to affix signs in other languages or with other characters, in particular in multilingual countries, in those using an alphabet with specific characters or in those which are likely to receive a large number of travellers using languages with specific characters. these measures are consistent with their objectives; so i decided in their favor.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this report, which proposes to open a recruitment procedure for civil servants for the countries which are to join the european union as part of its enlargement, scheduled for 1 may 2004. however, we would like to emphasise our disagreement with the european institution's choice to hire these new officials at a salary level which will be lower than that of current european union officials, as they will be integrated when a salary scale is introduced which is more unfavourable to new recruits, irrespective of their country of origin. the decision was obviously based on budgetary choices, which are always mentioned in connection with social issues but which are never taken into account when it comes to subsidising large european companies or providing european defence with military equipment.
in writing. - (pt) this proposal for a decision aims to provide an answer to the administration chapter of the eeurope 2005 action plan, in particular through the 'programme for the electronic exchange of data between administrations (ida) contributing to the creation of pan-european e-administration services in support of cross-border activities'. ida programmes are designed to encourage cooperation between national public administrations and between these administrations and the commission, and 'help' in the application of legislation, community programmes, control procedures and the 'open method of coordination'. however, this apparently technical programme and its instruments raise doubts as to the attempt to pave the way for federalism, encourage european integration and create the idea of a 'european public administration', in addition to the underlying objectives. in any event, the communication does not address the issue of 'e-government' at all. since the internet can ensure easy contact with administrations and provide services directly to citizens, we must constantly ensure universal access and improve the quality of services. it is clear that the internet should not be seen as a substitute for hosting services, nor can we accept that it be used to centralise services, as this would have direct consequences for service provision and territorial cohesion.
in writing. - (pt) i welcome the commission's proposal and the excellent work of mrs read. as i have said on several occasions, a knowledge society, one of the objectives of the european union, requires practical action to promote telecommunications infrastructures - the internet in particular - which promote interoperability and widespread access to new technologies for all eu citizens. i am also pleased to note the impressive results achieved under the ida programme - on cross-border coordination and cooperation between public administrations. secondly, i would like to welcome the new programme to succeed it for the period 2005-09 and which is called 'interoperable provision of pan-european e-government services to public administrations, businesses and citizens (idabc) '. in fact, exchanges between national authorities and community institutions are of crucial importance, both in operational terms - they represent a valuable source of information and cooperation for the staff of national public administrations and allow for greater efficiency - and in terms of guaranteeing citizens' rights, as they make relations between national and community public authorities more transparent and direct. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the commission either argues that harmonization is necessary at european level or, on false grounds of environmental protection, raises the taxation of diesel where it is lower than that of petrol. we rejected this proposal by voting against any amendment leading to an increase in the tax on diesel fuel. we would not object to higher taxes being levied on the large road haulage companies, which are big consumers of diesel fuel. it would be logical for them to contribute to the depreciation of the road network which the states provide them free of charge, which gives them an advantage over rail transport. but if that were the aim, it would be the profits of these companies that should be taxed in order not to penalise individuals, including those with the lowest incomes who are often forced to travel by private vehicle because of the lack of adequate public transport.
in writing. - (pt) the commission proposal aims to achieve gradual upward harmonisation of excise duty rates on commercial fuels and to separate the tax regime for commercial use from the tax regime for private use. the commission claims that it wishes to correct distortions of competition within the internal market and protect the environment in accordance with the 'polluter pays' principle. the proposal for a directive must be seen in the context of the strategy presented in the white paper on 'european transport policy for 2010: the time to make choices', which calls for a review of the distribution of the tax burden between 'users' and 'taxpayers' and for the 'real' cost of transport to be passed on to 'users'. in order to achieve this objective, the commission states that 'the use of transport infrastructure should be progressively taxed and the coherence of tax regimes improved'. in a broader context, the commission is seeking to establish, within ten years, a european tax system that includes registration and traffic taxes, a sound infrastructure charging system and the harmonisation of fuel taxes. the proposal for a directive also lays down minimum excise duty rates for unleaded petrol and a central rate for commercial fuels. given our disagreement with most of these proposals, we supported the rapporteur's position to reject the commission's proposal, which was accepted by parliament.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of the rapporteur's opinion, which reflects that of the parliamentary committee responsible, so that the commission's proposal is rejected. in my view, this proposal, which the commission justifies by claiming that the environment must be respected and that unfair competition within the internal market must be combated, leaves much to be desired in terms of efficiency and could have negative consequences for the current member states and, above all, for the new member states. we need to look more closely at the idea of introducing two categories of taxes on petrol and to see the rate for private cars - non-business fuel - quickly aligned with the rate for unleaded petrol, in order to take account of the consequences of these measures for the industrial sectors concerned. i am aware that there are cases of 'oil tourism', but i do not think that the scale of the problem justifies full harmonisation. a certain degree of tax competition could even be beneficial, since the proposed strategy of harmonisation would in most cases lead to higher taxes. as i come from a peripheral region of the union, i can only hope that geography will be taken into account in future proposals. in reality, portuguese drivers are probably not affected by 'oil tourism' in the same way as german or belgian drivers are supposed to be.
in writing. - we are in favour of research development and therefore of its funding. in the spending of the european institutions, it is certainly not research and development spending that is a problem, as long as it is not just used as a pretext for subsidies to private companies. we see, however, that research expenditure, together with social expenditure, is the one most readily cut, at any rate in france, to increase aid and subsidies to large employers. the whole approach set out in this report is to consider research as a competitive element only, between europe and the united states or between individual firms. the report itself is forced to note that private companies, which are mainly concerned with their own profits, or even short-term profits, neglect investment in research. in reality, there is a contradiction between the pursuit of profit and scientific research in the interests of society as a whole. we did not vote against this report because we are in favour of public research receiving much more funding than it currently does, but we also did not want to endorse this subordination of research to the race for profit.
in writing. - (pt) sustainable and increased investment in research is the best guarantee of success in achieving the objectives which the european union has set itself, which must lead to the creation of a knowledge-based economic area which is more dynamic from an economic and cohesive point of view. it will therefore be one of the best investments in the future of the citizens of the union. the commission's communication sets more ambitious targets than before, proposing measures to raise eu research expenditure to 3% of gdp, with one third of this to be financed from public funds and two thirds from the private sector. at present, this figure is only 1.9%, which is far from the percentages observed in the united states (2.7%) and japan (3%), and reveals significant differences within the union itself. to achieve this, investment in research will need to grow at a rate of 8% per year, in addition to the necessary budgetary increase in view of the forthcoming accession of ten new countries. that's my point too; i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the linkohr report denounces the fact that research expenditure in europe is too low. we are obviously in favour of increasing research funding. but this report justifies this increase by unacceptable arguments. it never mentions the usefulness of research to improve living and working conditions or to safeguard the environment. the only criteria for research funding are europe's competitiveness and its assertiveness. the proposed method for this is research conducted on a competitive basis, which is more conducive to the commercial interests of private enterprises. the report notes that not all research activities are producing the expected positive effect on european economies; it therefore advocates the establishment of a european system for developing criteria for efficiency and success and for evaluating research against these criteria. the research and scientific community in france and other european countries is mobilizing against the drastic reduction in public funding and the forced orientation of research towards the most immediately profitable areas. together with them we defend freedom of research in the name of the public interest. i therefore voted against this report on dangerous logic.
in writing. - the liberalization of the telecommunications sector has led to the most serious crisis in its history. the policy of widespread privatisation, a direct consequence of the choice of deregulation and competition, has led to a monstrous indebtedness of operators, seeking at any price - and at any price - new market shares, building parallel and competing networks, such as mobile, in a dubious waste of resources. this was accompanied, it should be recalled, by massive job cuts and a jeopardising of the whole notion of public service. the report presented here by mr clegg is in favour of taking a further step in this direction. i can only vote against it. a different policy is needed, based on the satisfaction of social needs. telecommunications must be defended as a public service, which requires control by the state over policy and the choices of operators. we stand for the following principles: low tariffs for the services most used by the majority of the population; free measures for the poorest; coverage of the entire territory by mobile networks and high-speed internet as part of the public service; the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.

in writing. - (pt) i support the report by mr lisi recommending the adoption of a joint text agreed in the conciliation committee and updating the council directive on the control of major-accident hazards involving dangerous substances. we are particularly pleased that the following amendments of parliament have been accepted. the aim of the proposals is:- to extend the scope of the directive to cover dangerous substances such as potassium nitrates, which were responsible for the explosion at a factory in toulouse in 2001 that killed 30 people and injured about 2000 others; - improve the training of all personnel working in a potentially hazardous installation, including subcontractors, with priority given to the first emergency measures to be taken in the event of an accident; - improve information to the public, with particular emphasis on the creation of a spatial planning databank which will ensure the compatibility of hazardous sites with sensitive areas to be assessed; - ensure that operators of hazardous installations draw up publicly accessible safety reports containing maps, images and equivalent descriptions. given the introduction of considerable improvements in the common position, which has allowed for much greater progress than the second reading could have allowed for, i support... in writing. - (pt) the purpose of this regulation is to transpose into community law the amendments adopted by the international maritime organisation (imo) and incorporated into a new chapter of the international convention for the safety of life at sea (solas) after 11 september 2001 and in view of the need to protect ships and to improve maritime safety against possible attacks. this will ensure that international measures adopted by the imo for national shipping are applied uniformly in the european community. these amendments to the solas convention and to part a of the international code for the safety of ships and port facilities (isps code) contain mandatory provisions which are open to various interpretations and adaptations by member states. part b of the code consists of recommendations, but the commission proposes that some of these become binding provisions. member states will only be able to adopt specific provisions for ports which are used only occasionally for international traffic, although one provision provides for a possible exemption from the obligation of pre-entry security checks for ships engaged on a regular service within a member state or between two or more member states, subject to the adoption by the latter of a national plan for the application of the provisions of the regulation. in addition, the report establishes a single national authority responsible for the safety of ships and port facilities, gives the commission responsibility for controls and evaluations and entrusts the european maritime safety agency with a role to assist the commission in carrying out its tasks.
in writing. - (pt) the commission has put the proposal on the table today to incorporate into community law the provisions adopted by the general assembly of the international maritime organisation, the final version of which was adopted in london in december 2002 by the international diplomatic conference of the governments signatory to the international convention for the safety of life at sea (solas convention 1974). this is a very important convention. in practice, the principles applied to air transport are transferred to maritime transport, with member states having to draw up national maritime safety plans defining safety standards and designating a competent national authority, which will be the sole responsible authority in this field and which will have the specific task of ensuring the safety of ships by issuing certificates. i am aware of the enormous vulnerability of this sector and, taking note of the security measures advocated in the report for ships and port facilities, which are the ship-to-port interface, but not for ports as such, i urge the commission to persevere and to come forward with a legislative initiative to regulate the security of community ports. i share the rapporteur's concern about the financial implications of these security measures and i agree with his request to the commission to present a study on this subject. i voted yes.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this proposal. improving the security of networks at community level, whether public or private, is becoming increasingly necessary, mainly because of the concerns of citizens, businesses and economic operators in general, given the real 'explosion' of the internet. the almost infinite amount of information available on the internet, together with its surprising capacity for data transmission, has given users easy and frequent access which, as we know, is a breeding ground for criminal activities, often designed to damage the system, which calls into question its reliability and security. the commission proposal provides in particular that 'this agency shall facilitate the application of community measures relating to network and information security and shall ensure, through the assistance provided, the interoperability of information security functions in networks and information systems, thus contributing to the functioning of the internal market', which i fully agree with. i also believe that this agency must be designed to actively seek solutions to the problems created by cybercrime, which means, of course, looking very closely at the particular situation of increased risks and exposure that our children are facing.
in writing. - (pt) almost one in four europeans (for a total of about one million a year) will die of cancer. this is a huge burden, both in human terms for people living with cancer and their loved ones and in terms of resources used for the diagnosis, treatment and care that the disease requires. therefore, the fight against cancer through the 'europe against cancer' programme, which was set up in 1985, has been a european priority for a long time. according to the rapporteur, my friend and colleague, mr mussa, who during the debate received the enthusiastic support of the non-attached rapporteurs from all groups, 'it is therefore crucial to develop the actions undertaken by the union through the following means:a) health information and training of the european citizen;b) the introduction of already validated screening;c) periodic quality controls of screening;d) the study of the feasibility of new screening methods. the commission's communication enables europe to confront together the common, cruel and socially destructive pathologies. the urgency of strategic action directed at european level against cancer is demonstrated by the worrying epidemiological data.' in this context, my vote was not only in favour but also enthusiastic and i hope that this recommendation will be adopted because, although it is not legally binding, it is a real political priority.
in writing. - (pt) i would like to congratulate mr mussa on his excellent report on a subject which is of great concern to us - cancer and its early detection. it is a terrible disease, one of the leading causes of death, directly affecting many citizens and, consequently, their families. we also know, especially from published studies, that nearly one in four europeans will die of cancer. although this is a non-legally binding recommendation, this proposal should be considered as a political priority. the overwhelming majority in the plenary is an indication of this: 528 votes in favour and only 6 against. i would also like to express my satisfaction with all the support that has been given to this proposal in the parliamentary committee, particularly through proposals for secondary prevention measures which facilitate early diagnosis and which therefore include less aggressive and more tolerable therapies. i also welcome the very clear commitment to promoting a thoughtful and determined attitude towards screening programmes, as well as the commitment to an information campaign designed to teach people to self-diagnose.
in writing. - (pt) this proposal for a regulation aims to respond, within the current framework, to the need to register and ensure the traceability of movements of ovine and caprine animals in order to improve the identification of infected animals in the event of an epizootic. this is the system which the european parliament itself recommended in its resolution of 17 december 2000, on the basis of the report of the temporary committee on foot-and-mouth disease and, in particular, on the priority of identification. while important, these measures do not solve the problems facing our agricultural model. above all, it is necessary to reduce transport and especially the export of live animals to a minimum, to combat the disappearance of local slaughterhouses, to encourage local production and short distribution channels, to combat the policy of under-investment in veterinary inspection services and to take account of the problems created by the elimination of internal borders. this regulation raises three important questions for producers, especially small producers: the proportionality of the administrative and bureaucratic burden, the possibility of respecting the deadlines and the payment of costs. the report proposes some simplifications of the system, such as the extension of deadlines, the involvement of the community in the future electronic identification system and the financing by the community of all the costs of creating individualised identification systems. only in this way will we be able to avoid an increase in the number of producers leaving the sector.
in writing. - (pt) the proposal for a regulation establishes a system of individual and batch identification and, for the species concerned, provides for the possibility of using an electronic identification system. the aim is to improve the identification system and to create a computerised system for recording the movements of sheep and goats in order to enable rapid and accurate traceability, which is essential for monitoring diseases, potential problems or incidents affecting public health. since the effectiveness of this technology has not been adequately tested in all member states and since it is neither practical nor economical to apply it in all situations, i think it is important that the commission should draw up a report on the experience gained in this area, a report which would analyse the economic implications of the electronic identification system before its introduction on a universal and mandatory basis. i share the rapporteur's concerns about the timeliness and feasibility of the proposal on the table. i agree with the amendments he has tabled and i can confirm the concerns he has raised about the large skilled workforce, which is aging rapidly and has a very low income level. these farmers may have to leave the profession because of the increased costs borne by producers, which is a sufficient reason for the union to cover the costs of introducing the individual identification system. i voted yes.
in writing. - (pt) although progress has been made since the last report, all member states were late in responding to the questionnaire (portugal and ireland took over a year). progress has been made in the development of waste management plans, although some countries do not have such plans or do not implement them, and as a result, several infringement procedures for non-compliance with the directive have been initiated. the objective of stabilising waste generation at 1985 levels is not affected, as no reduction measures have been defined by the member states and/or the commission, which urges member states to intensify separate collection of recyclable waste and to have sufficient recycling and recovery capacity as well as incineration capacity with energy recovery in the absence of better treatment alternatives. we strongly support the positions presented in the report and the measures proposed, particularly those which would ensure that countries are self-sufficient in waste treatment and that the directive is respected and revised, especially as regards the conditions for the recovery, disposal, control and use of waste, on the basis of minimum criteria which take into account the environmental impact of these operations; the gaseous and other emission regulations must be equivalent for all processes.
in writing. - (pt) i welcome this commission proposal, which i believe meets the expectations of the citizens of the european union both in terms of increasing levels of environmental protection and efforts to treat, recycle, recover and transport waste. the belief that environmentally responsible waste management is crucial is now, fortunately, widely accepted. this is evidenced by the impact that the transport of waste (and polluting products), especially by sea and inland waterways, has had recently in the media. in the field of waste today, operators - whether they are simply transporters or those responsible for treatment, recycling or recovery - must be obliged to comply with the highest possible safety and protection standards and procedures. to this end, control regulations must also be developed, depending on the type of waste being transported and how it will be treated once it has reached its destination. i also agree with the proposal for a red list (more dangerous substances) and a green list (less dangerous substances). finally, i would like to stress that in this area it is essential to share information and best practice constantly because of the frequent scientific and technical doubts about the fate of certain types of waste.
in writing. - (pt) while it is worth saying that the debate on the prioritisation and funding of scientific research at community level in the context of the sixth framework programme is not only about the important issue of funding of stem cell research, i share the position of my group that: - attempts to prevent community funding for stem cell-based research, especially embryonic stem cell research, carried out in member states that allow this practice should be rejected; - national legislation in eu member states that rejects this possibility should be respected; - the objective of pursuing, in a regulated manner, research to alleviate or cure diseases, in particular those caused by the degeneration of specific cells, such as parkinson's disease, alzheimer's disease and diabetes, should be confirmed. since this is the case, i reject any direct or indirect attempt to limit or even more or less completely prevent community funding for research in this field.
in writing. - (pt) when it comes to issues related to the use of community funds, but affecting areas which, in terms of their respective legality or illegality, fall within the sphere of national legislation and for which the member states adopt divergent responses, the european union must refrain from providing funding at all. otherwise it would be in breach of the principle of subsidiarity. the question is not whether the european union prohibits or authorises something that does not fall within its sphere of competence; the aim is not to interfere indirectly, by financial means, with exclusive national competences and to prevent taxpayers' money from being spent to finance programmes and activities which, in their own member state, are prohibited or constitute illegal acts. by not respecting this guideline, the commission proposal clearly breaches the principle of subsidiarity and that is why i voted against it. as regards stem cells and the hopes raised by research in this field, i suggest that, without prejudice to what each member state does with its own financial resources, all european research funding should be directed to adult stem cells. this is not an ethical or legal problem and experiments on this type of cell have already produced very encouraging tangible results, which is not the case for embryonic stem cells. i commend the rapporteur, mr liese, for his efforts to reach a compromise on a limit, and for the clarity of his final statement rejecting the proposal on the grounds that a majority would once again make it impossible to adopt.
in writing. - (pt) the report covers key aspects of the important issue of soil protection, which should be taken into account in future resolutions, but it will be difficult to meet the proposed timetable. some objectives, especially for portugal, will be difficult to achieve, bearing in mind the reality of the portuguese situation and various scientific and technical issues, in particular the presentation by the commission, before july 2004, of a thematic strategy for soil protection which will define the problems, the qualitative and quantitative objectives and the means by which they can be achieved, the timetables and the general principles of evaluation and control. the presentation of such a strategy will require the cooperation of the member states and, given the current state of the work of the working groups set up for this purpose, it will be difficult to achieve all the objectives set in time. similarly, although there is a need to produce what has been called a 'scientific soil catalogue' - a need felt by various researchers and specialists in this field for a long time - and this needs to be supported, the proposed timetable nevertheless seems to be very tight. the attempt to harmonise soil analysis methods in order to obtain comparable data would be even more difficult. finally, the implications of these 'concerns' for agricultural and environmental policies must be assessed, particularly in social and economic terms, in order to avoid rendering the agricultural sector unsustainable.
in writing. - (pt) erosion, decline of organic matter, pollution, waterproofing (caused by the construction of housing, roads and other infrastructure), silting (caused by mechanical pressure resulting from the use of heavy equipment, overgrazing, sports activities), decline of biodiversity and salinisation (excessive accumulation of soluble salts of sodium, magnesium and calcium), as well as floods and landslides are major threats to the soils of the member states. in this area, despite the fact that there is no specific european policy dealing with this issue, actions undertaken in the context of other policies, such as environmental, agricultural, regional, transport or research policies, have a clear impact on soil protection, which is more than necessary. i voted in favour of this report, although i think the commission has overstepped the principle of subsidiarity by proposing legislation in this area. despite the fact that this strategy has only just been announced, we would be right to ask what would be the added value of european action beyond the exchange of information, knowledge and best practice. we might also ask why it is necessary to study the issue of urbanisation and regional planning, given that the issue of land varies enormously from one member state to another and even within the same member state.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the principle that when it comes to environmental issues we must always try to raise the standards. the environment knows no borders and affects everyone. data provided by member states on waste treatment, recovery or recycling processes must be more reliable and provided more quickly. i fully agree that member states should have an obligation to develop waste management plans or to improve existing ones, mainly to promote measures designed to encourage the prevention and reduction of waste generation. i must, however, express my dissatisfaction with the general tone of the report when it recommends giving the commission more powers to impose sanctions and levy taxes in environmental matters, asking that infringement proceedings be initiated according to the higher or lower quantity/quality of data provided by the member states. it is essential that such action, which should focus more on control, monitoring and prevention and less on penalties, be based on reliable data, particularly as regards the nature of the waste treated. as the rapporteur himself points out, however, the first harmonised statistics will not be available until 2006. we will therefore not have the elements which we objectively need to assess the 'relative' dimension of waste treatment in the european union.

the rapporteur. mr president, i do not intend to reopen the debate. i only want to reply to mrs patricia mckenna when she said that this report represented a victory for the arms industry lobbies. the vulgarity of the statement did not even merit a response. but the insinuation of the honour it represents leads me to make this protest. i have nothing against the naturally divergent views of the honourable member. what i cannot accept is your insinuation that there is an alleged relationship of subservience or even representation of the interests of this sector of activity. i'll know exactly what to do if there's a conflict of interest, mr. president. this insinuation is not only offensive but also false and completely out of the high political context in which this debate has been taking place. the statement made by the honourable member and the ethical disregard it contains are therefore with the person who made it.
the schengen agreement was signed in 1990 and the need to strengthen controls was recognised in order to prevent threats to the security of our citizens from entering the community, such as organised crime, terrorism, trafficking in human beings and drugs, illegal immigration and others. the application of the principle of free movement and the abolition of checks at national borders have increased the importance of checks at external borders. we know that free movement within the territory of the schengen states is a freedom which requires in return not only the strengthening of the common external borders but also the rapid and efficient exchange of information in the context of border controls and police cooperation. in this context, the sis, the schengen information system, has been playing a very important role, which is to be given greater relevance with the creation of a second generation of sis, which has been designated sis ii. sis functions as an information system enabling the competent authorities in the member states to search for and obtain alerts on persons and objects. it is currently operational for thirteen member states plus two other states - iceland and norway - and it is intended that it will soon become partially operational for the united kingdom and ireland. the sis is the largest database in europe and has a dual function: in the area of public policy and security, and in the area of immigration, providing support for measures to compensate for the free movement of persons. the proposals which have been put to us for the creation of sis ii are intended to extend the capacity of the system and to introduce new possibilities at technical and research level, taking advantage of the latest advances in information technology. the council envisages that it could enter into force in 2006. the creation of this new system is intended to address three major issues. first, enlargement, so that the new member states can be integrated, for which we need to have the capacity to integrate more users, more member states, but also new categories of users. there is already agreement in the council to allow new authorities access to sis, but it is not yet known which authorities. second development: the current system includes functions which concern two categories of information (people and objects). the aim is not only to increase the categories of data to be introduced, new objects and functions, but also the processing capacity of this information, the interconnection of alerts, the modification of their duration and also the archive, the transfer of biometric data, in particular photographs and fingerprints. no decision has been taken by the council on which new categories of objects or persons to include. third and lastly, in view of the increase in the number of functions and users, the system should be more homogeneous, more flexible, more secure and with higher performance, easily managed and with controlled costs. it is therefore legitimate to consider that we are not talking here about a limited compensatory measure introduced to facilitate the free movement of persons, as provided for in the schengen convention, in particular in articles 92 and 102. indeed, a presidency note of february 2002 even argued that 'the sis may be used for police information purposes in the broad sense'. the character of the sis has thus undergone a metamorphosis, albeit imperceptibly; the question remains as to what exactly the future purpose of sis should be, or how this broad sense referred to by the presidency could be defined. and i think that only when the question of the definition of the objectives of the sis has been answered in a clear and politically acceptable way will the debate on topics such as new functionalities or new users be able to give a full answer. proposals for the introduction of new functionalities, new users, new architecture, new synergies, in particular with the visa information system, new management and even location are still being discussed. these proposed amendments obviously have repercussions for data protection and the protection of citizens' fundamental rights. we reiterate that any decision taken must always be accompanied by the highest standards of data protection, in particular the requirements laid down in article 118 of the schengen convention, so that the right balance between security and freedom is always sought. i hope that this report will help to make the debate on sis ii more transparent, to emphasize the need for this parliament to follow the process, to underline the need for its management to be ensured by community bodies and to ensure that the greatest effectiveness is always accompanied by the desirable and necessary strengthening of the issues of data protection and safeguarding the rights of citizens.
madam president, the proposal for a recommendation to the council on the second generation of sis gives us the opportunity to express our serious concerns about the development of the schengen information system. the sis was initially introduced as a limited compensatory measure in the context of the free movement of citizens. it is, however, becoming an instrument of police cooperation, as the council is gradually adding new functionalities and giving various authorities access to its database. as the schengen joint supervisory authority points out, the proposed development of sis and the creation of sis ii constitute a fundamental change in the nature of the system itself: while sis only alerts the designated authorities in cases where an individual on file crosses a schengen border, sis ii is likely to become a multifunctional investigative tool. this is the transition from a reactive security logic to an active security logic. the prospect of a new system that would enable authorities to share information on millions of individuals for different purposes, probably using the most advanced technologies, including biometric data analysis, obliges us to reflect on the impact that this new system may have on the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens. in particular, the right to the protection of personal data, recently reaffirmed in article 8 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and incorporated in the draft european constitution drawn up by the convention. it is true that the need to improve cooperation in the fields of justice and home affairs and, in particular, the linking and cross-referencing of information between different databases is one of the objectives of the european union that the member states have committed themselves to pursuing. we all understand the need for efficient information systems to meet the challenges posed by international terrorism and crossborder crime, but such action can never jeopardise the fundamental principles on which the union as a community of law is founded. the balance between privacy and security cannot be altered by the adoption of information and communication technologies created as governments' response to the increased risks of new and dangerous criminal phenomena. when available technologies threaten the integrity of personal information worthy of protection, it is imperative that appropriate legislation be adopted to address the potential for abuse. the report by mr carlos coelho, and i take this opportunity to congratulate the author, contains a number of proposals which are generally in the right direction: the need to hold a real public debate on the objectives of sis ii; the need to develop sis ii in a democratic and transparent way, enabling citizens to have access to more information about the system and the possibility for the persons concerned to access and rectify their personal data; the merging of the various existing databases which makes it possible to create a coherent and comprehensive data protection regime; the thorough analysis; new access authorizations granted to new authorities; the creation of a european agency for the strategic management of sis, controlled and supervised by the european parliament.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we have seen the realization of european citizenship through a series of events such as the introduction of the euro or the abolition of internal frontiers within the community. in situations like these, it is visible that they exist and that they complement national citizenship. however, there are areas where visibility of implementation is reduced. the structures created by the community to promote european citizenship exist, they are financed by the community, they may even have work done, but they do not reach the general public. the lack of knowledge of the work carried out in the various institutions is profound, but because of the lack of transparency, bureaucratic processes, and a clear distancing of european citizens from the institutions that are supposed to represent them or from bodies set up to serve them, there is no real knowledge of what is going on. we have been surprised recently by surveys which show that european citizens are completely unaware of the work of the convention, despite the large sums of money invested. i myself was rapporteur on the euro two years ago, a very interesting community service which is essential for mobility and the promotion of crossborder employment, and i have noticed that the public is generally unaware of it. well, after more than two years, although this was one of the areas strategically identified in the resolution we voted on, pointing out the need for a great deal of information work, almost everything remains substantially the same because of failures on the part of the commission and disinterest on the part of the member states. it is therefore essential to take action. on the one hand, more transparency should be required from the bodies receiving community support. i agree with mrs rühle that the investments made by the european union in informing and promoting its citizens should be publicised, particularly on the websites of the organisations receiving these funds. it is a way of diluting the idea of a europe of eurocrats only and distant from the citizens, making them aware that such a europe is directly involved in the daily lives of each of us and making it possible for citizens to participate in social and political life. the community institutions are not without responsibilities and can improve their delivery by simplifying the procedures for submitting proposals for applications to community funds for civic promotion, promoting easy access to documents through user-friendly systems, strengthening the intermediary structures between themselves and citizens, and by really listening and opening up. this is the right time to encourage citizens to participate in the construction of the european union. the intergovernmental conference is preparing a new treaty with constitutional aspirations which will have a major impact on the future of european citizens. so i challenge you all: the european parliament has already made a number of proposals to the council and the commission, and it is not the council that has made the proposals. consultation is required in all member states on the future treaty. in this way we can all contribute to the real exercise of active european citizenship. it is pointless to tell our fellow citizens that they are also european citizens and then spend our lives telling them to 'shut up'. it is not right to proclaim european citizenship from maastricht and then shut it up altogether by imposing a strict vow of silence on it. we cannot have the idea that european citizenship is very interesting and good as long as the citizen does not remember committing the sin of asking for the floor. we are therefore committed to active european citizenship.

mr president, i first of all welcome the holding of this debate, which i had requested in september, before the recent decision by the european union's finance ministers not to apply sanctions to france and germany for breaching the stability pact. in practice, they have given reason to our complaint that the nominal convergence criteria are unreasonable, with the known disastrous consequences of economic recession, worsening unemployment and poverty, as is the case in portugal. we have said here many times that this stability pact is useless. in the debate last october we reaffirmed that we agreed with the statements of president prodi and commissioner lamy when they said that this pact is stupid, like all decisions that are rigid; that this pact is a crude instrument of economic governance and should be replaced by something more intelligent, given that the 3% rule is medieval. unfortunately, they have not been consistent with these claims and have not put forward a proposal for the revision of the pact. they were determined to move forward with the excessive deficit procedure against france and germany, as they had done with portugal. the inevitable happened: germany and france did not accept the commission's proposal. of course the commission said that it was continuing to apply the treaty and that it 'reserved the right to examine the consequences of the council's conclusions and to decide on possible action'. but does anyone believe that she will do something against france and germany if the governments of these countries have not agreed? no, and we all know that. the question remains, why maintain a pact that makes no sense? it is well known that the text adopted by ecofin merely imposes the rules previously announced by the german and french governments, thus accepting that three consecutive years have passed without meeting the maastricht criteria. and certainly if they need more they can go up to four or five years... we know who is in charge of the stability pact, who is using his power and strength in the european union, even though there is no new constitutional treaty yet. it is noted that it was germany which demanded the stability pact, with its unacceptable nominal convergence criteria. but he did so, as we now see, to exact his compliance from others. not for you. the commissioner pedro solbes can now say that the council's decision 'does not respect the rules and the spirit of the stability pact'. will you resign because you're being disqualified like this? of course, france was more realistic, stating that the council has another way of applying the stability pact, thus making its non-compliance effective, although advocating changes through what it called the "enrichment" of the stability pact. a thesis that others have defended here today. it is true that some have said that the pact is not dead, but that it is frozen, frozen until the moment when the rich and powerful countries consider that it can be unfrozen because their problems are solved. we know that the governing council of the european central bank also advocated the adoption of the commission's proposals. are you also resigning because you were overtaken by the council? for our part, which has always been against this stability pact, we have long been advocating its suspension in order to review its stupid nominal convergence criteria, which do not take account of the reality of each country and its different degrees of socioeconomic development, which confuse productive expenditure with non-productive expenditure in the calculation of the budget deficit. but one thing is certain: the hypocrisy of those who, as in portugal, use the argument of the stability pact to justify anti-social policies has now become clearer. let's bury this pact! let us look for alternative policies that give priority to employment, quality public services, sustainable development and the well-being of the people!

the driving force behind community europe to being a factor of instability. the stability pact is dead at the moment, at least as far as the sanctions part is concerned. this is an indication that community europe is without direction". i don't intend to contribute to the debate on whether or not the stability pact was stupid. we saw how, in a few days, those who thought he was smart decided not to respect him and those who thought he was stupid protested when he was forgotten. i accept that other indicators are needed and that the mechanisms applicable to boom cycles may be qualitatively different from those which should be respected in recession cycles. but i am sure of one thing: mechanisms are needed to discipline public finances in the interests of the euro and of europe. what is not acceptable is the double standard: that for some it is obligatory what for others is excusable. what is harmful to european unity is the feeling that what is not tolerated by the small is tolerated by the big. what is unacceptable is to see who has sinned by making disparaging and disparaging comments about those who have honored the commitment they have made. the attitude of the french and german finance ministers towards the courageous policy of budgetary restraint of the portuguese government was regrettable. what is worrying is that the slip in compliance with the rules of the pact could lead to higher interest rates, as has been admitted by commissioner pedro solbes. this is a worrying scenario for households and businesses that are heavily indebted. madam president, our aim should be to strengthen the instruments of european integration and not to weaken them, especially in the context of the debate on the new constitutional treaty and the completion of enlargement.
madam president, as you will know from the various initiatives that have taken place in this parliament this year, mr oswaldo payá, who was awarded the sakharov prize last year, should have been with us on 1 december. unfortunately, the cuban authorities didn't let him come, they prevented him from coming. he sent a message to parliament asking me to read it. i read that message in its entirety at the foreign affairs committee meeting. i shall not repeat it here, i just want to put it on the record. it is a strong message, a moving message, in which he notes the difficulties faced by the democrats in cuba, but also notes the continued determination of the varella project (i would draw the attention of all colleagues to this fact) and denounces the fact that he has been prevented from travelling. he denounces the situation in the concentration camps and the prisoners, the very topics we would like to hear from him and be able to debate with him. it also calls for the european union's moral support for cooperation, which we will certainly not deny, and states that the european union's constructive dialogue must be with the whole of cuban society. i therefore ask the president of parliament and the conference of presidents to return to this matter, since the invitation of 13 november was not accepted and it is very important that we get oswaldo payá to go free until we can tell him what is going on in his country.
mr president, commissioner, rapporteur, as our colleague herbert bösch reminds us in his careful and exhaustive report, it is now three and a half years since the present head of olaf took office, an institution which has grown to the point of having 364 staff. the time for expectations, transitions and adaptations is therefore over. the time has definitely come for balance, evaluation and accountability. the audit of olaf seems to me to be essential, just as it seems to me to be essential that we evolve from the current additional figurine of a 'supervisory committee' to a body of control, evaluation and decision-making in the last instance. our committee on budgetary control has always regarded olaf as a working instrument of a european prosecutor's office, an institution which the growth and sophistication of european transnational crime makes increasingly necessary. the outcome of the present intergovernmental conference will therefore be crucial. until it is framed by a european prosecutor's office, we have to ask ourselves whether it is wise to continue investing in police techniques that olaf is legally unable to pursue at the expense of audit techniques that are the basis of the fight against all financial crime and that no financial investigation body can afford to do without. the poor performance of olaf in the recent eurostat case was necessarily contributed to by a lack of understanding of basic communication and information concepts and the balance of interests involved. but it was also the absence of auditors, whose techniques must always be at the heart of the fight against irregularities or financial fraud. these are times of rigour, of demand, of work, of professionalism, of balance, of reasonableness and common sense, and that is what we expect to see from olaf.

for certain fishing areas, especially in andalusia and, to a lesser extent, in the portuguese algarve. it is true that the commission and parliament have managed to approve a plan to support the
