mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in order to overcome its limited fisheries resources, the european union has developed, among other measures, the conclusion of agreements with third countries for the use of foreign territorial waters in exchange for financial compensation. in 2002, the european union concluded such an agreement with mozambique, seen by many as the perfect agreement, balancing cooperation and mutual interest: the community fleet will be able to fish in mozambican territorial waters for the next three years, with financial compensation of some eur 4 million. this balanced agreement does indeed have ideal conditions. first, because it covers species whose resources are abundant in mozambique: shrimp and tuna. secondly, because it takes into account the development of local fisheries through the training of mozambican crews. thirdly, because the community compensation was earmarked for specific objectives in the fisheries sector. fourthly, because there will be monitoring of the implementation of the agreement, with particular attention to the health aspects of catches. i join the european parliament, through its rapporteur, mr stevenson, in demanding that it receive the annual report on the application of the agreement and the conditions for its implementation, which will enable this institution to follow up this strategic agreement for the common fisheries policy of the european union, and thus to be kept informed, before any negotiations, when the agreement is renewed. i would like to conclude by expressing my great satisfaction at the conclusion of this very balanced agreement. i am convinced that, unlike the previous agreement, mozambique will have no reason to denounce this text.
mr president, i too would like to welcome the return of community fishing vessels to mozambican waters. i am portuguese and i make this statement without any colonial nostalgia or any recollection of those times, but i feel that this return of community vessels to mozambique's waters also demonstrates the democratic maturity that that country has reached and the normality of diplomacy that has been established between that country and the european union. in fact, as has already been said, this agreement has mutual advantages, it is even the culmination of the drawing up of fisheries agreements with third countries that the commission and parliament have been working on over time. this agreement is the result of a lot of thought and experience which is worth applying in future to cases similar to those in mozambique. in this respect, the president of the commission described this agreement as a model - i agree - and it could be the basis for future agreements with third countries, poor countries, underdeveloped countries, which will find in a scheme and a system such as the one contained in the agreement the best way of defending their interests and of supporting their fisheries in an ecological, scientific and economically advantageous way. i must therefore congratulate the commission on the very good results it has achieved in its diplomatic relations with mozambique, and i must congratulate the chairman of the committee on fisheries on the excellent report he has produced.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to congratulate mr cashman on his report, which has received widespread support in the committee on civil liberties. as mr cashman has said and as commissioner bolkestein has stressed, the very logic of freedom of movement will make it ever more urgent that we adopt rules in these areas, since the free movement of citizens within the community will multiply the cases which are already occurring and which deserve our attention. it is incomprehensible that, in the event of the death of a community citizen in a member state other than his country of origin, more complex formalities should be applied, longer deadlines for burial or cremation should be set and the costs should be higher. this is clearly against the logic of the community. as such, measures must be taken to simplify or even harmonize the procedure for repatriating the body of a deceased person in order to make it more in line with the community logic, which of course is not taken into account in the international agreements governing this matter, either the berlin agreement of 1937 or the strasbourg agreement of 1973. these agreements, being relatively old, do not take account of the current situation in europe and have therefore become obsolete in many respects. moreover, those agreements introduced indirect discrimination by applying them mainly to 'non-nationals', which is contrary to the fundamental principle of community law of non-discrimination and thus violates essential rules of community law. it is then for the commission, as guardian of the treaties, to verify their compatibility and to take the necessary measures to ensure that they are respected. finally, it should be noted that not all the member states have ratified these agreements, which means that there is a considerable disparity in the measures applied by each of the member states.
madam president, commissioner, mr president of the court of auditors and other members of the court, allow me to join in the congratulations already addressed to this court for the excellent work it has done, but also allow me to highlight two special reports on export refunds which are indeed exemplary and speak volumes about the quality of what the court of auditors has produced in recent years. in clear language, without succumbing to the hyperbole and bureaucratic metaphysics which we unfortunately still find in some texts of this court, we see here the repetition of a diagnosis already made in 1990. the export refund system is extremely complex and highly permeable to fraud, and does not comply with the most basic rules of transparency. in 13 years, nothing essential has changed in the way this business is run, which concerns a very small number of interests and companies whose names the commission is adamant about keeping secret. the commissioners come and go, reforms pass, export refunds, but they stay and challenge everything and everyone. three years after the commission exposed the network that counterfeited tens of thousands of tonnes of butter across europe and after being urged to defend europe's financial interests as well as the rights of citizens and farmers, it still refuses to take any action against any of the offenders, in effect giving preferential treatment to the large dairy companies involved in this scandal over that which it reserves to any farmer whose milk production exceeds his quota. these are the practices and realities that it is essential to combat and that it is useful to see stamped out with efficiency and diligence, as has been the case with these court reports on export subsidies. so once again i would like to congratulate the court of auditors on the work it has done.
madam president, measures to facilitate the simplification of procedures and formalities are positive, and in this particular case of health care provision they are even more important because they will help to facilitate the free movement of people. it is important that these rights should be extended to as many people as possible, and it is therefore positive that the creation of a european health card for all people travelling, studying, working - and also for their family members - in any member state of the european union has been achieved, thus replacing the forms currently in existence, but without containing data that jeopardises their privacy. i also think it is good that information is made available to all citizens about the rights they enjoy in this field in the various member states and that this is properly ensured. i would therefore like to congratulate my colleague, mrs anne elisabet jensen, on her work. i hope that there will be very direct access to all health care for citizens in the various member states of the european union, and that this will happen as soon as possible, within the timeframe that has been set. i also hope that today's vote will help to ensure that this timetable is not exceeded and that the health card will become a reality during the next year.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european union cannot be just an area of free movement of capital, goods and services; it must also be a europe of free movement of citizens without prejudice to their rights. the entry into force of the european health insurance card will be a major step towards achieving this fundamental objective. the barcelona conclusions of march 2002 had already agreed to the creation of a european health card as a way of removing obstacles to geographical mobility. the aim is therefore to facilitate the free movement of persons within the european union. support for this report now is a necessary condition for us all to benefit from this community progress in 2004. i congratulate the rapporteur, anne elisabet jensen, on her good work. i also commend the commission for its diligence and commitment in achieving this ambition, as well as the very positive cooperation of the council. the entry into force of the european health insurance card will result in the harmonisation of the rights of insured persons and their family members, whether they are travelling, studying, on secondment, looking for a job or are international transporters. all citizens will have the right to benefit from benefits in kind by having recourse to medical care during their stay in the territory of a member state and by avoiding the complicated and bureaucratic procedures which now involve the intervention of various bodies. to create the conditions necessary for the adoption of this card, the regulations implementing social security schemes, in particular regulations 1408/71 and 572/72, must first be amended. i am pleased to note the agreement reached with the council on the revision of regulation 1408/71. the adoption of this single, personalised instrument will eliminate the various forms currently in force, harmonise the rights of insured persons and simplify formalities. the existing forms will, however, be phased out. such amendments require adequate information to be given to insured persons about the rights and obligations arising from the new legislation and it will be for the member states to ensure that such information is given to their citizens. the creation of the european health insurance card is thus an ambition that has become a reality, but it is also a symbol of europe and a tool that reinforces the feeling of belonging to the european union.
in writing. - (pt) this draft amending budget proposes to reduce payment appropriations for the structural funds prior to 2000 by eur 5 billion and ratifies the agreement in principle which the european parliament reached with the council during the budgetary consultation of 24 november 2003. the commission justifies this reduction by problems in the processing of payment applications and by budgetary under-implementation compared with member states' applications. however, it remains to be seen how these payments will be executed in the future, taking into account that less than €1 billion was committed in 2004 for programmes prior to 2000. the fact is that, if there are almost €13 billion in commitments remaining to be settled from programmes prior to 2000, these commitments must be fully implemented and not cancelled, in accordance with the principle of the objective of expenditure, in order to guarantee the principle of economic and social cohesion. more than a concern about implementation, it is an attempt to respond to the constraints of the stability pact, thus reducing the contribution of the member states to the budget of the european union, in particular that of large countries such as germany and france.
in writing. - (pt) the programme for the conversion of vessels dependent on the fisheries agreement with morocco was approved two years ago, after the agreement was not renewed, making eur 197 million available to the two fleets affected, those of portugal and spain. in the opinion of the committee on fisheries which i drafted for the 2003 community budget, i expressed my concern about the implementation and financing of this programme. the commission proposal aims to amend the basic regulation in order to facilitate the implementation of the current programme, in particular by broadening the eligibility criteria for beneficiaries and extending by 12 months the deadlines for granting individual compensatory payments. this flexibility, which i support, must be extended to the co-financing of national early retirement schemes and to individual compensation payments linked to a social conversion plan, as proposed by the rapporteur and adopted by parliament. i would like to emphasize the proposal to include measures similar to this regulation in the framework of the regulation on structural aid to the fisheries sector when recovery plans are adopted or fisheries agreements are not renewed. this could help to mitigate the socio-economic consequences when severe restrictions are imposed on fishing opportunities.
in writing. - (pt) the european union's fisheries agreement with morocco ended in 1999. since then, morocco's demands have made it impossible to conclude another agreement. as a result of this non-renewal, the community fleet has been subject to a large number of restrictions. the situation affected 400 vessels and 4,300 fishermen. this sector did not need this to reach a tipping point, as the main countries affected were spain and portugal, and in particular the algarve. the community fleet must not be the silent victim of the impasse in the negotiations with morocco. the fishermen did not choose to convert their vessels and the restrictions on fishing were imposed on them. some were forced to put their ships to rest while others had to find another direction for their activities. sustained socioeconomic support measures are therefore needed to alleviate the disastrous effects of this failure to renew the agreement with morocco. the union has an obligation to help save this sector in crisis. the proposal provides for greater flexibility by extending the deadline for granting aid and removing certain restrictions. from now on, fishermen will be able to receive payments irrespective of whether the vessel they worked on is scrapped or exported. the aim is to ensure fair treatment of all fishermen and to include as many of them as possible in the community fleet.
in writing. - (pt) this proposal for a regulation is intended to maintain the current aid scheme for the marketing of certain fishery products from the outermost regions, which has been in operation successfully since 1992 and is one of the objectives of the posei programmes. the proposal aims to compensate for the additional costs of disposing of these products by financial compensation for production, processing and marketing, taking into account the costs induced by insularity, remoteness of the market, the small size of local markets, topography and climate. in this sense, we agree with the rapporteur not only on the approval of the current system but also on the transfer of the legal basis from article 37 to article 299 (2) of the treaty establishing the european community on the specific characteristics of the outermost regions. the permanent nature of this system must also be guaranteed, since the constraints on these regions are permanent. however, i regret that the budget for the programme was reduced from €17 million to €15 million per year for the period 2003-2007, when it should have been increased. the rapporteur's amendment no 3 is questionable, since the flexibility required in regard to under-utilisation of the available amounts may jeopardise the key to their distribution among the member states.
in writing. - (pt) i fully support the regulation under consideration which, in view of the specific characteristics of the outermost regions, will allow the continuation of the system of compensation for the extra costs incurred by their isolation in relation to the production, processing and marketing of fishery products, by providing it with a budget of eur 15 million per year for the seven outermost regions. this is an attempt to ensure that regional economic players in the fisheries sector benefit from production and competition conditions identical to those existing in the continental market. the european parliament also supports the permanent nature of this compensation system, given the permanent nature of the constraints linked to the specific nature of the outermost regions.
in writing. - (pt) i fully support this proposal for a regulation. the specific problems affecting the outermost regions are well known, particularly those linked to the marketing of their products outside their territory. they face additional costs, which include transport costs as well as energy consumption, insurance and packaging related to transport. they also face higher operating costs than those on the mainland (cost of fuel, lack of qualified technicians for ship maintenance and repair, delays and additional costs in delivering spare parts from the mainland, and blocking ships at berth in the event of breakdowns or storms). the latter make their products more expensive and less competitive than those of producers in the acp countries or of continental community producers. i therefore think it is quite right to encourage compensatory measures for the marketing of important fishery products. they also continue the system originally introduced in 1992 and implement the objectives of article 299 (2) of the treaty establishing the european community.
in writing. - (pt) during the review of the common fisheries policy in december 2002, the council considered that the outermost regions deserved special treatment, particularly as regards the management of the community fishing fleet. the commission's proposal is in line with this, but does not address the real problems of the regions concerned, which have a non-industrial fleet and small businesses, which have made it impossible to take full advantage of existing support for fleet modernisation and renewal. it is therefore important to ensure that this process of modernisation and renovation can continue without constraints arising from community legislation. the rapporteur's proposals improve on the commission's proposal. first of all, they propose a more appropriate legal basis, article 299 (2) of the treaty establishing the european community, which recognises the specific constraints affecting the economic and social situation of the outermost regions. they also extend the provision on public aid for fleet renewal for a further two years, until 31 december 2006. the rapporteur also calls for a report to be drawn up on the evaluation of the application of these measures, in order to examine whether they should be continued beyond 2006. it is regrettable, however, that the necessary increase in structural assistance from the fifg has not been taken up.
in writing. - (pt) in view of the specific characteristics of the outermost regions in the field of fisheries (the non-industrial nature of their fleet, the small size of their market, the small size of their enterprises and the delay in the modernisation and restructuring of their fleet), the regulation under examination will exceptionally allow, by way of derogation from recently adopted rules for the union as a whole, the granting of financial aid to the outermost regions for the modernisation and renewal of local fishing fleets. this derogation is essential for the outermost regions and may be even more valuable if the council accepts the following parliament proposals:- public aid for fleet renewal should be possible until the end of 2006 instead of december 2004;- an evaluation of these measures should be carried out in order to consider whether they should be continued beyond 2006;- advances on aid should be allowed up to 14% instead of the current 7%.
in writing. - (pt) this resolution does not go much further than the positions held by parliament on the so-called 'european governance', a euphemism used by federalists of all stripes to designate the evolution towards the creation of a future european government - the european commission 'obviously' - with 'european' social partners, for what has been called 'european public opinion'. in the external sphere, it means representing the european union in international organisations through the proposed minister for foreign affairs, who would head a common european diplomatic service. the consideration that 'the recent failure of the wto conference in cancun shows the need to reform the wto's rules, working methods and decision-making mechanisms' is also important. in other words, faced with a new setback in the neoliberal capitalist agenda, its representatives are trying to find procedures that will circumvent the position adopted by some countries to defend their national interests against the big capitalist powers, more particularly the european union. however, i welcome the requirement for openness and transparency in the use of experts and the publication of the composition of committees and working groups consulted by the commission in preparing its proposals, which will certainly put the emphasis on the role of unice (the union of confederations of industry and employers of europe).
in writing. - (pt) in line with previous reports, the first element considered in this report is a set of measures designed to simplify and improve the regulatory environment. i would stress the intention to strengthen the objectives of transparency and simplification of legislative processes, decision-making and citizen participation, which are essential to make community legislation more accessible and understandable. the european commission proposes to simplify the content and form of the legislation in force by reworking the existing legislation. this would be a positive action, although the process needs to be monitored to ensure that no significant element of the community acquis is lost and that democratic legitimacy is not compromised. the 'citizens' criterion', which would be used to assess the impact of proposals on citizens' daily lives and could lead to information or compensation measures, can be beneficial to people and help to increase their interest in community issues, such as increasing participation rates in european integration. in my view, it is equally important to create a single internet portal for all institutions, through which citizens can follow the decision-making process from start to finish and the use of external experts. despite the positive points i have just mentioned, i abstained because i think the report has adopted a 'federalist' and 'one-state' approach...
in writing. - (pt) i welcome the european commission's initiative to adopt measures to reduce air pollutant emissions from ships. shipping is largely responsible for pollution in coastal areas and also contributes to global warming. contrary to what many people think, ships may prove to be one of the most polluting modes of transport, a fact that has been exacerbated by increasingly stringent legislation on fuels used by road vehicle engines. hence the importance of adopting identical measures for marine engines as well. however, i do not think that the measures proposed by the commission meet the objectives which the initiative seeks to achieve. without running the risk of falling into a utopian programme, i think we could go a little further, in line with what the rapporteur proposes, towards the development of a more audacious plan. as the report also points out, the commission proposal also fails to provide the necessary link with the fifth and sixth eu environment action plans. it is therefore logical to improve the text by adopting a position which is in line with what already exists on this subject in community legislation. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - (pt) i support this report, which aims to give new impetus to the fight against corruption, detailing what has been done and what needs to be improved and identifying areas where the union needs to focus its efforts in the fight against corruption. globalisation, combined with other factors, has led to an increase in cross-border trade. corruption in a member state is therefore no longer a purely national problem, but is becoming a transnational problem, which will be better tackled by joint action by the union. the union must be determined to introduce and implement an anti-corruption culture at all levels of political activity, in the public and private sectors and at national and community level, as corruption is a threat to a law-abiding society, distorts competition and hampers economic development. i would like to remind you, bearing in mind the recent eurostat case, that in addition to the corruption perpetrated by representatives of the community institutions, there is another worrying problem: the loss of citizens' confidence in the process of european integration. the role of european bodies responsible for promoting cooperation between member states to eliminate corruption is essential. coordinated action by these bodies (eurojust, europol, olaf and the european judicial network) will strengthen the actions undertaken by national police forces and facilitate transnational investigations by sharing the information capacities of the member states.
in writing. - (pt) this report, which proposes interesting approaches to the prevention, regulation, control and monitoring of corruption in various fields, such as political and administrative activity, public procurement, and international trade, among others, has positive aspects. it can, however, be criticised for:- a degree of federalism, which we do not support, illustrated for example by the fact that it defends the european arrest warrant, the increase in the powers of eurojust and europol and the ill-defined, cumbersome and unjustified creation of a european prosecutor's office;- a certain confusion between measures for transparency and measures for standardisation (customs), while paying less attention to the interests of the peoples and nations; - a highly administrative, bureaucratic and federalist approach, which is not very participatory and would exercise little political control over the major economic and financial powers, in particular overseas investment companies, banking operations, clearing houses, in other words, genuine money laundering institutions. that is why we abstained from voting.
in writing. - (pt) despite the rapporteur's concerns, in particular that these appropriations cannot be used to finance repatriation policies - in particular to pay for special flights that take 'illegal immigrants' back to their country of origin - and the introduction of amendments to minimise the negative effects of the regulation, the fact is that the regulation is intended to 'encourage the signing of readmission agreements' with third countries. in fact, as the rapporteur points out:- 'it is clear that the commission's intention is to create an instrument which could provide a counterpart for third states which would agree to sign readmission agreements'; - "the promise of support and financial aid can provide an incentive for third countries to sign these agreements and to make them accepted by their public opinion" and he adds "even if, at present, the total transfers that third countries receive from their immigrants in the european union is much higher than all the aid going through eu financial support programmes". in other words, it is another instrument designed to support the eu's repressive immigration policy, by trying to guarantee financial compensation to the countries of origin of "illegal immigrants" so that they sign readmission agreements.
in writing. - (pt) i warmly welcome this commission proposal which implements the decision of the barcelona european council of march 2002 to introduce a european health insurance card. the card will not change existing rights and obligations and is intended to simplify access to treatment in the visited country and, at the same time, to guarantee to the institutions financing the health system in that country that the patient is fully insured in his/her home country and that, therefore, the institutions of his/her home country will duly reimburse all costs. i therefore believe that this measure gives substance to one of the most important principles underlying the european union, which is to guarantee a high level of health protection for all citizens throughout the union and to contribute to the free movement we all want by removing barriers and obstacles to the geographical mobility of european citizens. finally, i believe it is of the utmost importance to encourage actions that ensure that beneficiaries of health insurance schemes are sufficiently informed of their rights and obligations under this regulation. and this starts with the need to ensure that citizens are informed of the introduction of the map.
in writing. - (pt) this commission proposal to amend the organic farming regulation is mainly aimed at clarifying terminological problems, whereas the concept is being used incorrectly by supermarket chains and certain multinational agri-food companies. the proposal also aims to strengthen controls on all operators at all stages of production. however, the proposal fails to meet expectations in this sector, which now has almost 150 000 farms, representing 4% of the cultivated area in the union. in this context, i agree with the rapporteur when she says that organic farmers, who are the main actors in this form of production, must play an active role in this procedure for amending the regulations. i also agree that labelling should not be ambiguous in terms of the name and that is why the derogations granted to certain brands, such as danone, for example, should be abolished immediately. the labelling and rules must clearly be the same, also for imported products. i very much regret that the report does not address the issue of gmos, in particular the so-called 'coexistence' or genetic pollution issues and that it also neglects the support and protection of organic seeds. the introduction of gmos will challenge the choice of organic farmers, with the economic risks arising from this pollution affecting their eligibility for existing aid and no clear definition of the responsibilities of the polluter is given. in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of the report because i think it is essential to explain to consumers what organic products are and to tell them what organic products are. given the growing demand and interest of many farmers in the application of good practices which are healthy and respectful of the environment, the commission's proposal amending regulation (eec) no 2092/91 to monitor the development of organic farming in the european community is fully justified. i agree with the measures proposed by the rapporteur, particularly with regard to the fight against any ambiguity in the name, which could lead to confusion and misunderstanding of organic products among consumers. in fact, there is a growing need for certainty as to the terminology in the different community languages identifying the production methods of organic products, which must be labelled with a symbol immediately recognisable to every citizen of the union, the labelling being precise, whatever the origin of the product. similarly, biodiversity must be preserved, crops and products must be protected and any pollution of organic crops by genetically modified organisms must be avoided. in this respect, it is important to protect and support organic seeds.
in writing. - (pt) this report approves the new fisheries agreement with mozambique, which will last for three years and provides for a fishing quota of 1 000 tonnes of deep-sea shrimp and 535 tonnes of by-catch and fishing opportunities for 35 freezer tuna seiners and 14 surface longliners, the main beneficiary of which will be the spanish fleet. the overall financial compensation was set at just over eur 4 million per year. it should be noted that the first agreement, signed in 1988, was denounced by mozambique in 1993, which considered that it was no longer suitable for the development of its fisheries sector. i am in favour of this report, although i have three reservations. firstly, portugal will only gain 150 tonnes of shrimp (and 80 tonnes of by-catch) and licences for five surface longliners, despite the needs of its fleet and despite its fishing traditions in mozambican waters. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the fishing industry, which is the main source of income for the fleet. finally, we must support the development of the local fisheries sector, not only under the provisions of this agreement but also in the framework of our policy of cooperation and development with mozambique.
in writing. - (pt) the proposal for rationalization of rates must be examined in the context of the current process of establishing a definitive vat system, based on taxation in the country of origin and on a harmonised timetable, with the least possible derogations, for the taxation rates of the different member states. this idea, which was put forward by the member states in view of the potential effects on their tax policy, has the support of the european parliament. it is however strange that in this case the parliament has adopted a more realistic position, in particular by considering that this is not the right time for further harmonisation and by supporting the council's intention to extend the experimental application of reduced vat rates to certain labour-intensive services. commissioner bolkestein refused to put forward this proposal at the last ecofin council on 25 november. however, as regards reduced rates, and keeping in mind the concept of fiscal sovereignty, it should be recalled that member states must maintain the necessary flexibility in the implementation of social and cultural policies, in particular when they establish reduced vat rates. secondly, since a minimum rate already exists, member states must have the power to set rates in accordance with their policy choices regarding tax redistribution and the financing of national budgets.

in writing. - (pt) i voted against the first case and abstained on the second part of point 9 because:- it is not clear whether the naples conclave will give rise to the idea of a commissioner per member state. in fact, the alternative to what was agreed at the convention, on the basis of the requirement of one commissioner per state, will result in the reappearance of the requirement of two commissioners for the most populous states, which not only differentiates between states - the large states counting as two - but also favours the creation of a concentration of powers in the hands of twelve commissioners from these states to the detriment of the others; the amendment advances a false idea of equality which is in my view more likely to be achieved by the rotating equality where each member state can choose whether or not to belong to the college of commissioners, with or without voting rights, on a rotating basis depending on the specific composition of successive commissions. this gives countries equal opportunities in terms of time, with no country having more rights than another.
in writing. - (pt) i voted against because the compromise resolution is seriously unbalanced. the european parliament must now adopt an objective, realistic and impartial position, instead of insisting on an intransigent position and false 'negotiating positions' - the parliament does not take part in any negotiations. we should contribute in a responsible way to a visible consensus, instead of stubbornly insisting on a so-called 'consensus of the convention' which, as everyone has understood, does not exist. i was particularly disappointed that amendments nos 8 and 9, which i tabled on behalf of the union for a europe of nations group, were not adopted. rejecting the step forward made by the naples conclave towards the solution of a commissioner per member state, on an equal footing and with full status, makes little contribution to the success of the igc and reveals an unexpectedly reactionary mentality on the part of the parliamentary majority - especially when, unfortunately, real nonsense is being poured in its place, such as the idea that "the allocation of a commissioner per member state risks giving it an intergovernmental character" (!?). as for the lack of support from the italian presidency for a balance, given its proposals to move beyond the differences on the preamble by explicitly referring to the christian or judeo-christian heritage of europe, while at the same time confirming the secular nature of the european institutions, this simply proves the intolerance and prejudices underlying the political resistance to the growing demand for social change that millions of european citizens are calling for.
in writing. - (pt) i agree with those who have stressed that the creation of pilot programmes for 'tripartite contracts and conventions between the community, the states and regional and local authorities' can only be interpreted correctly if we take into account the intentions underlying this action. in fact, the proposed objective - through 'formally coordinated actions' aimed at 'improving policy implementation', in other words, establishing community standards which can only be applied in specific ways which take account of very different and specific realities - is already contained in the treaties, in particular through the application of the principle of subsidiarity and through a much simpler and more appropriate process, which is to define objectives to be achieved, leaving member states to choose how to achieve them through a directive. thus, the underlying idea behind this initiative is not the crucial need to fight ultra-bureaucratic or highly centralised procedures or to really increase the power of local authorities to manage their own domain, but simply to raise local authorities to the level of direct partners of the european institutions in implementing their directives, in an attempt to succeed the states as the national interlocutor. the support and warm congratulations of the ultra-federalist constitutional affairs committee of the parliament are therefore due.
in writing. - (pt) i abstained from voting on this report because i feel that the reasons given by the rapporteur for 'deploring the lack of genuinely effective links between the european institutions, in particular the commission, and the territorial authorities of the internal, regional or local type in the member states' are not sufficient to justify the launching of 'tripartite contracts and conventions on objectives'. in fact, like mr berthu, i believe that the community legal system already has a mechanism which allows us to achieve the same result by different means, the directive. in fact, this legal instrument, which is closely linked to the principle of subsidiarity (although only in the application of the means) could be an option for the areas proposed, which are economic development, environmental policy, transport, agriculture and fisheries, the state itself remaining the sole and direct interlocutor of the european institutions. i think that the measure advocated to raise local authorities to the level of direct partners of the european institutions is part of the well-known process of european centralisation and the de-emphasis of the states. and i predict that, if the practice of concluding such contracts spreads, the complexity of interinstitutional relations will increase disproportionately, as will the related bureaucracy. it will lead to chaos. i acknowledge the commission's caution in proposing the adoption of experimental pilot programmes, which will be the subject of a future evaluation report.
in writing. - (pt) in accordance with the ec treaty, the community and the member states are obliged to adopt measures to combat fraud and protect the community's financial interests. in 2002 alone, irregularities and fraud amounting to some €2 billion were detected to the community's detriment, and this may be just the tip of the iceberg - with obvious economic repercussions - underlining the need to step up the fight against corruption. i share many of the rapporteur's criticisms and concerns about the evaluation of olaf's activities. as the rapporteur states, 'the eurostat case has highlighted weaknesses in the office's investigation activities', in particular the fact that the investigation dragged on for years and that the rules to protect the persons concerned by the investigations were not respected. i therefore agree with the need to guarantee greater autonomy and greater resources for olaf, in particular for an increase in the number of investigators. however, some fundamental issues, which underlie many cases of irregularity and fraud, in particular concerning the outsourcing of commission services, need to be addressed. i also have serious reservations about the need for a european prosecutor, a step in the process of creating a european public prosecutor's office, supported by europol, eurojust and olaf.
in writing. - (pt) the transparency of decision-making processes, which i have always advocated, cannot disappear when it comes to the adoption of legislative acts. the increasing complexity and number of competences conferred on the institutions and bodies of the european union require greater vigilance over the adequacy and legitimacy of the use made of the heritage of european citizens, which is embodied in the budget. i therefore welcome the commission's evaluation report on the activities of this body. we need to pursue some of the approaches put forward by the rapporteur, such as closer coordination between the control structures of the different institutions, a better definition of olaf's rules of procedure and the definition of a clear policy on the priority of investigations. it is also worth highlighting an aspect that is often only superficially addressed - with enormous consequences for the success of olaf - namely the receptivity of institutions and bodies to warnings and reports issued by olaf.
in writing. - (pt) there are currently no provisions governing the repatriation of dead bodies from one member state to another in a uniform manner throughout the union. in the absence of such provisions, the crossborder transport of remains is governed by two instruments of international law, the berlin agreement of 1937 and the strasbourg agreement of 1973, concluded under the auspices of the council of europe, to which only a part of the member states have acceded and which are in many respects obsolete. the rapporteur is of the opinion that, on the basis of these agreements, in the event of the death of a community national in a state other than his country of origin, the procedures are more complex, the time taken for burial or cremation is longer, and the costs are higher than if the death occurred in the country of origin of the deceased. this is why, and given that there are in some member states significant immigrant communities from another member state, as is the case in portugal, for example, we need to enhance the value of measures that could address the specific needs of these communities, in particular with regard to the range of issues addressed in the report.
in writing. - (pt) the legislative differences between the national legal systems of the various member states of the european union place the relatives of persons who have died in a member state other than their own in a particularly difficult situation. the necessary formalities, which are inevitably more complex in such cases, the longer deadlines and the higher costs faced by the victims' families make an already painful and very delicate moment even more sad. moreover, the instruments of international law applicable to such situations are inadequate, given the current levels of mobility of citizens, an aspect which is of greater importance for the free movement of persons within the intra-community area and which increases the likelihood of such situations occurring. i particularly agree with the rapporteur that free movement is hampered by this legal framework, in particular because equal treatment between community and national nationals is not fully respected. as i believe that the rapporteur's proposals are going in the right direction, providing for the adoption of concrete measures and putting an end to the inaction of the european commission in this area, i voted in favour of this report.

the rapporteur. - (nl) mr president, i apologize for the delay, but we are still trying to reach a compromise in extremis in order to achieve a qualified majority. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, representatives of the council and the commission, ladies and gentlemen, i thank you for your excellent cooperation in this particularly complex and difficult matter, which is legally thorny and politically sensitive. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this, but i am saying that it should be involved in the negotiations. we have already consulted with the council, and i see some possibilities here, at least if parliament dares to vote by qualified majority on a package which i have just distributed, because i think that is indeed a minimum requirement of the large groups. i thank you for having decided to postpone the vote until wednesday, because all the translations were not yet ready. they are now, but i have a little more time to reach these compromises now. and in the end, it's a great thing. the whole procedure proved to be very difficult. parliament had to vote to appoint the committee which would deal with this matter on the merits and i think this is a first in the history of this parliament. it has revealed some sensitivities, sometimes even some tenderness. i think that the text approved at first reading is relatively balanced. unfortunately, the council has again considerably reduced it by introducing a very large number of 'mays', that is to say, that member states 'may' take measures. my view is that instead, it should be more like "must". i think it would be good for both the environment and the economy if we could create a level playing field instead of creating this patchwork of environmental legislation in europe that will not benefit either the economy or the environment. these conditions of equality are paramount. in the discussions on the previous report, i noticed that many of my colleagues were only talking about the fact that in lisbon it was agreed that europe should become the most competitive knowledge-based economy in the world. to do this, we must have the courage to take decisions that transcend the national interest and go beyond certain political issues that we would like to achieve. because in the end, it's the result that counts, not that i can go and say to my constituents, "look how brave i was to propose this. i may not have gotten any results, but i did offer it". i would regret that we were unable to reach a qualified majority, at least on a number of key points, so that we had room to persuade the council to replace many of these 'maybes'. fortunately, the joint proposal incorporates many of the texts which were in the text adopted by parliament, albeit weakened by these 'maybes', and i think that last week the committee on legal affairs and the internal market adopted several relevant texts. in particular, the financial guarantee with a fixed maximum amount and the mandatory financial guarantees that are possible over a given period. it is useful and necessary to be able to guarantee the possibility of insurance cover. with unlimited liability, no insurance company will want to take out a policy that they would not have introduced themselves. i am afraid that we would then have a sector that is totally out of control, and i do not think that this would work for our economy or for the environment. we then recognised once again the responsibility of the state, the role of the public authorities as a "safety net". all member states must be obliged to examine carefully the authorizations issued, but also to control them. we need that authority. in addition, an amendment on a mitigation system, a system where factors are weighted, was rejected. as an amendment was approved on more far-reaching defence measures, total exemptions and exceptions, unfortunately it was not accepted. since it has been proposed again, i hope that we will obtain a qualified majority on these three important points and that we will also be able to introduce it in europe. i think the environment will benefit, and our economy will too, because we will have minimal harmonisation. this is good for the environment, because the environment knows no borders. in the internal market which we want to optimise, there are no frontiers for our companies either, so i think that minimum harmonization is an excellent starting point, which is good for both the environment and our economy. if we fail to achieve a qualified majority on these points, i think that on the eve of the elections this parliament will be ashamed because we have given the council a free hand to clarify the details of an extremely important point, which i would regret. i hope that we will avoid this embarrassment and that we will be able to find a qualified majority, particularly on the points i have just mentioned. i'll shake heaven and earth to that end and we still have all day tomorrow to do it.

in writing. - (pt) due to the economic activities and jobs it generates, milk is a strategic product for the azores economy. it represents 80% of the regional gross agricultural product, 25% of national milk production and guarantees an income to about five thousand highly productive producers. since the 1999-2000 marketing year, production has reached 500 000 tonnes, and even 523 000 tonnes during the 2002-2003 marketing year. without the derogations, producers would have had to pay additional taxes for exceeding quotas and many of them would have gone bankrupt. in view of the specific characteristics of the azores, their milk quota should be increased, in particular because there is no economic alternative in this outermost region. the agreement reached at the agriculture council in luxembourg on 26 june 2003 still does not meet the needs of the azores. the introduction of an additional quota of 50 000 tonnes from 2005-2006 until the 2014-2015 marketing year and the derogation from an exemption threshold of 23 000 tonnes for additional levies are not sufficient. the fairest course would be to convert this derogation into a quota and to ensure that it is permanent. the portuguese government itself has recognised the need to increase the quota by 100 000 tonnes, but has unfortunately agreed to a much lower level.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the specific circumstances and needs of this very beautiful portuguese island region - the autonomous region of the azores - where the dairy sector plays a key role, must be taken into account. the process of stabilising the milk and milk products market must continue, while ensuring that azorean producers have a reasonable period of time to adapt to the constraints imposed by the legislative instruments and that their traditions and ways of life are respected, in a general context of understanding the specific difficulties linked to their ultraperipheral situation. in view of the situation in the azores, it seems to me essential to grant this region an additional quota and to extend this derogation temporarily. in coordination with national and regional authorities, the union must promote the spread and adoption of both viable alternative production methods and other forms of profitability of agricultural land without condemning it to abandonment and desertification, in the interests of the economic and social cohesion so much proclaimed and rarely observed. without this effort, unemployment, loss of character and emigration due to the eventual decline of the dairy sector could threaten the azores, as has already happened, notably at the time of the 'orange crisis', which deeply affected the archipelago in the 19th century.

in writing. - (pt) i support this proposal and the work done by the rapporteur, mr pirker, and i congratulate the council on having taken account of most of the proposals put forward by the european parliament at first reading. the aim of this initiative is to convert directive 92/109 into a regulation, so as to simplify the legislation and make it easier to apply uniformly and simultaneously. this simplification is even more important with the enlargement of the union. without it, the 25 member states would have to provide for national implementing measures for each amendment to this directive or its annexes. the aim is therefore to harmonise the monitoring of the trade in drug precursors and to prevent their diversion to the illicit production of narcotic drugs. it also aims to facilitate the legal trade of precursors used in the internal market for legal and legitimate purposes such as the production of medicines. in the face of the growing production and trade of synthetic drugs, it is essential to establish effective and rigorous controls on the manufacture and marketing of these substances, which can be diverted to the illicit manufacture of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. at the same time, there must be close cooperation between the competent authorities and the economic operators in the chemical industry.

in writing. - (el) the proposal for a directive setting high standards of quality and safety for human tissues and cells fills a significant gap in community legislation in order to ensure a high level of quality and safety for tissues and cells intended for transplantation or for any other use that needs to be precisely defined. it will also produce comparable levels of quality and safety in all member states. on the basis of my group's positions, i voted against amendments nos 1, 3, 4 and 38. i voted for amendment no 2 and amendment no 58. the european parliament should not restrict the operational scope of the directive for reasons of conservatism, but should preserve high levels of safety and quality.
in writing. - (nl) the lifting of the anonymity of sperm donors is the least controversial point of this proposal. however, the correction of defects and diseases in the human body by means of tissues and cells remains a sensitive issue. the conception of children for the purpose of disposing of embryos by means of abortion in order to obtain human repair material is rightly met with strong opposition, there is also a dislike for the commercial exploitation of people to sell their body parts for money, as blood donors have long done in america. i support rules to prevent the production of human material by these means, but i do not support attempts to make the rules stricter, to the point of banning stem cell research, for example. if it turns out that defects and diseases in the human body can be corrected by stem cells, it would be foolish to rule out this solution right away. the same criteria should apply to organ transplantation, which will be the subject of a separate text. i respect the view that man should not take himself for god in matters of creation, but if we follow this line of reasoning to the end, some aspects of health care also become illegal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report and i am glad that a large majority of the house did the same. the compromise reached with the council and the commission means that the directive on the establishment of quality and safety standards for the donation, procurement, testing, processing, preservation, storage and distribution of human tissues and cells is now ready for rapid adoption and implementation. this is excellent news for the fight against a number of incurable diseases, which can increasingly be combated by the transplantation of human cells and tissues, and offers new hope to many of our citizens. of course, these therapeutic practices and medical research must be governed by transparent and strict regulations, which aim both to minimise risks and to ensure compliance with ethical principles. the result in this respect is rather satisfactory. the principle of gratuitousness and voluntary giving is thus enshrined. the principle of non-commercialization of the human body is also recognised, to avoid it being seen as a mere source of profit.
in writing. - (pt) the proposal aims to integrate european markets, to harmonise the conditions for restructuring companies, to strengthen the legal certainty of crossborder takeovers in the interests of all interested parties and to ensure the protection of minority shareholders in the context of these operations, thus increasing the transparency of structures and defence mechanisms. this proposal for a directive is the third and i have given my support to it because what we have here is the result of efforts to overcome many obstacles and lively debate in the context of institutional cooperation and consultation, which i welcome. indeed, by strengthening the internal market and the vitality of european competitiveness - especially in relation to the us - we will gradually improve our own financial services, which foster a healthy competitive environment among european operators, in a framework of fairness, transparency and sustainable growth. i also believe that the main obstacle to the adoption of the directive in 1989 and 1996 - the effect of takeovers on employment and, more generally, its social repercussions - must remain at the heart of regulatory concerns. this is the only way to understand the scale of the union's struggle to achieve genuine corporate social responsibility. it is also the only way to achieve the objectives of economic dynamism and competitiveness, focused on creating more and better jobs, and on developing greater social cohesion.
in writing. - (pt) i voted against the report and the proposal for a directive, which was adopted by 325 votes to 221 with 7 abstentions. while some harmonisation of eu countries' rules governing financial markets is necessary to promote the internal market and hence growth, the takeover bid directive is not going in the right direction. if the directive is adopted, the swedish system of a and b shares will continue to be an exception. the directive must be revised after five years, with the obvious risk that the swedish system will be challenged again and abolished once and for all. the scheme which provides for class a and class b shares is open and non-discriminatory. it is based on freely concluded contractual acquisition agreements. there is no evidence that the system of differentiated voting rights prevents takeover bids. in principle, it can also be argued that the forms of ownership do not have to be decided at eu level, nor does the ownership right in question, or the long-term social responsibility of the shareholder in a limited company. i also voted in favour of the amendments which aim to give employees the opportunity to express their views on a takeover bid through a consultation of their representatives by the company's board of directors.

in writing. - (pt) although the compromise which the european parliament is proposing to the council introduces some amendments to its proposal of 3 and 4 june (on taxation and privileges and immunities, for example), it retains aspects which we disapprove of, such as the fixing of a parliamentary monthly salary which is identical for all members, regardless of the country they represent. the question is not whether a statute for members of the european parliament should be established. as we have said, the members of this parliament are elected to represent national constituencies. therefore, they are, and must remain, bound to these constituencies. this means that meps' salaries must be based on the salaries of national parliamentarians in the country in which they are elected. similarly, we cannot ignore the very different social realities in each country of the european union. the granting of the same parliamentary salary to all meps will lead to situations of profound inequality and disparity in different countries, such as portugal, between the salaries earned by workers and those earned by political representatives and public office holders. that would be completely incomprehensible. that is why we are voting against the report.
in writing. - (pt) we supported the rejection of the commission's proposal which, in the name of combating distortions of competition in the internal market and protecting the environment and on the basis of the polluter-pays principle, seeks to achieve a gradual upward harmonisation of excise duties on petrol and diesel for business purposes and to separate excise systems for these fuels from excise systems for private fuels. the proposal for a directive, which the european parliament had already rejected, is part of the strategy presented in the white paper 'european transport policy for 2010: time to make choices', the aim of which is to redistribute the tax burden between 'users' and 'taxpayers' and to make 'users' bear the 'real' costs of transport. the commission proposed 'to introduce a gradual tax on the use of transport infrastructure and to make the tax system more coherent'. it also proposed the creation, within 10 years, of a european tax system which establishes registration and traffic taxes, a 'smart' system which makes it possible to levy taxes on infrastructure and to harmonise excise duties on fuels. it also sets minimum rates for the special tax on unleaded petrol and a central rate for business fuel. however, given our disagreement with most of these proposals, we supported the positions to reject the commission's proposal, which is a new development.

in writing. - (pt) i welcome the work that has been done in an area which is of growing concern to european citizens, namely the protection of the environment and the liability of economic operators for damage caused to the environment. i therefore consider it justified, necessary and useful to oblige operators to take the necessary measures to deal with imminent threats of environmental destruction and to establish compensation mechanisms for the damage caused. i also share the idea of distinguishing between certain high-risk commercial activities for which all environmental damage is covered and for which objective liability applies and other commercial activities for which only damage to protected species and natural habitats will be covered if intent or negligence can be proven by the operator. the realistic and balanced solutions we are able to provide in this area will help to achieve the objective of preventing and remedying environmental damage and protecting the economic and competitive interests of the companies concerned; these solutions will also help to achieve the objectives set by the community for achieving sustainable growth and development.

in writing. - (pt) there are benefits to wearing a seat belt, mainly to prevent people from being ejected from vehicles. various studies of road accidents have shown that many passengers die after being thrown out of the vehicle, while those who remain in the vehicle usually survive. we can therefore legitimately consider that the use of seat belts is socially beneficial in that the wearing of a seat belt contributes significantly to the reduction of the number of deaths and injuries in accidents. it should also be remembered that this report adopts a commission proposal which should be considered in the light of the amendments to the council directives of 1974, 1976 and 1977 on the improvement of road safety. we can reasonably expect that the commission's proposals contained in this package of measures will produce positive results. however, at a time when the percentage of road fatalities remains high, safety measures should be increased for all vehicles - not only for light vehicles (category m1), but also for minibuses and coaches (categories m2 and m3) as well as for light commercial vehicles and heavy commercial vehicles (categories n1, n2 and n3). road safety must be a priority. it is for all these reasons that i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - (pt) improving transport safety, which is the reason for the very high number of victims each year, is one of the european union's priorities and this problem has given rise to numerous reports drawn up by the european parliament and the publication of a white paper. i believe that by extending the obligation to wear seat belts, the commission proposal, which the rapporteur also approves, contributes to greater safety for passengers and that is why i supported this report. it concerns in particular minibuses, coaches and light commercial vehicles, medium commercial vehicles and heavy commercial vehicles. however, this measure only minimizes the effects of road accidents and i would like to see investment in other, genuinely preventive actions to reduce the percentage of road deaths more effectively through a reduction in the number of accidents. i propose, for example, that large investments be made in schools and civic education, but also in promoting a culture of responsibility and respect, in improving roads and motorways, which are becoming increasingly congested, and in technological improvements to cars and vehicles in general. another solution which i have long advocated would be to invest in the railway sector, which is undoubtedly a safer mode of transport than road transport and could represent a genuinely sustainable alternative to the road sector, which is becoming increasingly congested.

the fundamental question here is whether it is really possible for genetically modified crops to coexist with conventional and organic crops. without a concrete and precise answer to this question there is no basis for the so-called freedom of choice. there will be no choice for farmers of conventional and organic crops, there will be no choice for consumers if genetically modified crops affect conventional and organic crops. we must prevent the imposition of a powerful lobby, an increasingly small group of large multinationals marketing genetically modified crops, which wish to control agriculture and food to the detriment of the will of european farmers and consumers who, in numerous opinion polls, have already expressed their reservations and even their rejection of genetically modified organisms. i therefore welcome this own-initiative report, which is all the more important because the commission itself delayed this debate, while at the same time paving the way for the lifting of the moratorium which has in fact been in place since 1998. this is a demand which i myself made in a joint motion for a resolution with members of my group last march. no one is unaware of the inherent risks of contamination from the release of gmos into the environment. scientific studies on cross-polymiation and the spread of gmos are still too limited to enable us to make an accurate and complete assessment of all their consequences. but in all this debate, taking into account the opinions presented at the parliamentary hearing, the conclusion is that contamination cannot really be avoided in the presence of genetically modified crops on a large scale, with consequences ranging from loss of biodiversity to economic damage to conventional and organic agriculture. so while the degree of risk of spread varies according to the type of genetically modified crops, the truth is that its management cannot be contained in an efficient and viable way. a holding that opts for a genetically modified crop cannot revert to a conventional, organic crop. past experience with animal diseases, particularly bse and foot-and-mouth disease, points to the problem of the control systems to be set up, their reliability and their costs. the rapporteur, whom i welcome, has stated in his report that the most effective and cost-effective measure to ensure coexistence is the voluntary or regional abandonment of genetically modified crops. the community provisions which are introduced must not affect the right of each member state to prohibit genetically modified crops throughout its territory or in geographically limited areas. of course, the obvious thing in this whole process is that if coexistence is not possible, then the moratorium should be maintained to take account of the precautionary principle, and so at the very least point 9 of this report should be supported. i hope that this parliament will adopt the report in its entirety tomorrow.
