in writing. - (pt) the proposal aims to reduce the negative environmental impact of heavy goods vehicles passing through austria, due to the particular geographical and environmental situation of the region. the aim is to penalise vehicles that consume 6,7 or 8 points (heavy goods vehicles of euro 2 category). transit through austria will be prohibited for highly polluting trucks (euro 0 and 1 category), while the least polluting ones (euro 3 and 4 category) will be allowed to transit freely. the proposal is to extend an existing eco-points system as such, and i therefore voted in favour. i also support the agreement on the extension of the points system to acceding countries from may 2004.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate mr lisi on the excellent report he has drawn up on the joint text approved by the conciliation committee for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights and repealing regulation (eec) no 295/91. i support this report, in particular the guarantee protecting passengers' rights in the event of flight delays or cancellations. under these clearly defined rules, air carriers will always be obliged to provide immediate assistance to passengers for whatever reason a flight is delayed or cancelled, and it will therefore be easier for citizens to assert their rights.
in writing. - (pt) the benefits to users of the liberalisation of air transport, in particular the significant reduction in the price of air tickets, should not make us forget the issues of flight delays and cancellations. the solutions proposed in the financial compensation system in case of overbooking/cancellation of flights, reimbursement in case of delay, the system of liability of carriers and assistance to passengers in case of flight cancellation are satisfactory and protect the various interests involved, in particular those of passengers. in view of this positive assessment, i voted in favour of the proposal put forward by the committee on regional policy, transport and tourism and signed by mr lisi.
in writing. - (pt) i applaud the work done by the rapporteur, who has solved an increasingly common problem, in that he holds airlines operating within the european union responsible when anomalies such as those described above occur. in reality, the reduction in the cost of air tickets and the consequent increase in the number of passengers, which have resulted from the liberalisation of air transport and the development of the sector in recent years, have led to the emergence of an ever-increasing number of situations that flout the rights of citizens. in this context, the proposal suggests that in the event of overbooking, long delay and flight cancellation, users should be reimbursed or compensated, as appropriate, for the damage incurred. the agreement also provides for assistance to be provided at the airport or at the hotel, as the case may be. the rights of air passengers need to be strengthened, especially since the committee responsible unanimously approved the rapporteur's proposals. finally, i welcome the european commission's proposal to extend these provisions to other modes of transport, and i stress that the basis of this regulation will guarantee the rights of all types of passengers.
in writing. - (pt) the mere fact that this recommendation for second reading is aimed at enabling a real development of cogeneration, which is expected to increase energy efficiency and improve security of supply, has led me to support this report, even though i realise that binding targets for the community and the member states will probably be adopted, as well as a stricter timetable for the transposition of the relevant directive, which is likely to create difficulties for some member states.
in writing. - (pt) i welcome the persistence of the rapporteur (who was unanimously supported in committee) in inviting the council to a constructive and fruitful debate after the majority of the first reading amendments had been rejected. i believe that this debate should be encouraged, so that this energy solution and its positive effects on the environment can be evaluated in depth. in reality, the present recommendation for second reading is aimed at enabling a real development of cogeneration, which is hoped to increase energy efficiency - and the resulting savings - and improve security of supply. these advantages should therefore encourage the european union to carry out an evaluation and to provide special support for this activity. without prejudice to the strictest respect for the principle of subsidiarity which the situation requires, i believe that more ambitious objectives and a more appropriate timetable could be set by promoting, in a constructive way (as the report proposes), areas of common ground with the council.
in writing. - (pt) among the major conclusions of the brussels summit, i feel i cannot fail to highlight the adoption of the european security strategy and the declaration on transatlantic relations, which the european parliament shares and welcomes, but which we reject. while they were probably adopted with the conviction of concluding the igc, and at a time when the us is excluding some of its partners from the iraq "dossier", these two documents are very revealing of the ambitions of the forces that dominate the eu - the great powers and big business. they are a call to the united states to commit to a 'balanced' partnership of joint action and the use of all means, including military. they also show the eu's determination to consolidate its capabilities by sharing with the us the ambition to dominate the world. the so-called security strategy sets the tone by saying that the first line of defence will often be abroad, that we must be ready to act before a crisis occurs, that we must develop a strategic culture that encourages upstream, rapid and, if necessary, robust interventions, that we should be able to conduct several operations simultaneously, and that by acting together, the european union and the united states can be a formidable force for good in the world. this is pure militarism. we therefore voted against.
in writing. - (pt) the failure of the brussels summit to deliver on the igc's results is to be welcomed. but it is regrettable that the european parliament has not learned the lesson and continues to defend the 'european constitution' with this resolution sponsored by the right wing, the social democrats and the greens. in fact, this time the contradictions concerning the distribution of power between the 'big' countries became clear to the igc. we have also seen the failure of the attempt to impose an anti-democratic, neo-liberal and militarist project in a context that is not alien to inter-imperialist rivalries, particularly with the united states. in the meantime, since it is still too early to assess when and how this process will be relaunched, the blackmail on the forthcoming financial perspective is gaining strength, since six countries are demanding an annual ceiling of 1% of community gnp, which is unacceptable. for our part, we will continue to expose, as we must, the real aims and dangers of the unacceptable 'european constitution', which has serious consequences for the workers and for portugal. we will continue our fight for a europe of cooperation between sovereign and equal states, aimed at improving the living conditions of workers and the population, peace and solidarity with all the peoples of the world - a path that effectively serves the interests of portugal.
in writing. - (pt) all those concerned are aware of the positions i have publicly expressed on the process of revising the treaties, the work of the convention and the legal and political implications of the conclusions of the intergovernmental conference. these positions are duly set out in this draft resolution, as well as in the draft resolution that my group has tabled on the igc summit of heads of state or government. it is for these same reasons that i have opposed the compromise resolution tabled on the same subject by the main parties in this parliament. i continue to believe that the european union is a union of states and that it is the responsibility of the states to take the final decision in this area. it is not the role of parliament to try to exert political pressure in order to rush the approval of an unsatisfactory agreement, or to allow the hidden threats to the emergence of a multi-speed europe to be revealed, by introducing, once again, unnecessary tensions in a process which requires maturity, responsibility and common sense in the difficult policies to be adopted.
in writing. - (pt) it is regrettable that a majority of this house has not heard anything. by obstinately refusing to see the facts, it creates crises that are not really felt among the population, and by promoting an illusion, it fuels disappointments and sows frustration. it is not the igc method that has failed, nor the convention that has been a success. it's the opposite. the convention method has shown its limitations and its fundamental lie: the widely-vaunted 'consensus' has never existed. it is a grave mistake to insist that the irish presidency act with the rashness that caused the failure of brussels. we need time and a deep and calm reassessment so that we do not repeat the same mistakes and set ourselves up for failure again. throughout the year, i repeatedly quoted a sentence from the famous schuman declaration: 'europe will not be built all at once, or in a single building: it will be built by concrete achievements, first creating a de facto solidarity'. this is what happened: the constitution was not passed, because europe "will not be built all at once, nor in a joint construction". but the important growth initiative was launched because europe "will be made by concrete achievements by first creating de facto solidarity". it was the founding spirit of robert schuman that blew through the brussels summit. i voted against the report but i support the paragraph which seeks to clarify the points of agreement ((short explanation of vote under rule 137 (1) of the rules of procedure))
in writing. - (pt) we support the position that the creation of the european toll service should be postponed until 1 january 2007 and that the directive should aim at ensuring general interoperability between the different systems. the commission will also have to present a study on the generalisation and interoperability of the different technologies and a cost-benefit analysis by 31 december 2009. on the basis of this study, it will then be able to submit a proposal for a migration strategy. the commission's objective in presenting this proposal is to create a european toll service for the entire road network subject to tolls, since the existence of different national toll systems which are not compatible with each other creates problems for international traffic - especially for heavy goods vehicles, which are forced to have several contracts and several boxes - and hinders the proper functioning of the internal market. in short, the objective is: one contract per customer, one case per vehicle. the commission is trying to impose a system which has yet to be tested. other issues still need to be resolved, such as the process of transferring tolls collected in one member state to a contract established in another member state. the aim is to oblige operators to ensure interoperability on the basis of three technologies by 2005 and then to oblige them to adopt a single system. that is a position which we reject.
in writing. - (pt) on the whole, i support the european commission's proposal. if there is one chapter in which portugal has really made progress on european issues, it is the chapter on the rationalisation of toll collection, thanks to the introduction of the 'via verde' (green road), which has proved to be the most efficient, practical and convenient system in europe. the rationalization of toll collection throughout the european union will certainly help to make life easier for european citizens, especially for transport professionals, and on the other hand it represents an important step towards deepening the internal market. i fully support the ideas put forward by the rapporteur on the need - without prejudice to the recommended and supported interoperability - not to lose sight of the principle of subsidiarity in respect of the technical choices of each country, which would have various inevitable financial consequences. i also call for caution in the common adoption of new technologies - which must actually exist and have proved themselves to users - and for the need not to violate the rules of the market and their functioning when these technologies are introduced.
in writing. - (pt) i voted in favour of this proposal for the extension of the abovementioned regulation. i agree with the rapporteur's assessment of the european commission's proposal. in particular, i welcome the extension of the regulation to local organisations in developing countries, such as cultural organisations, political foundations, the media, consumer organisations, universities and municipal authorities. they are what we call the "living forces" of society and they must therefore be the main architects of the development process of their countries, regions, towns and villages. the union must therefore, in accordance with its past commitments, promote and support this form of decentralised cooperation. perhaps we should also consider a gradual increase in this form of cooperation which, if its implementation is subject to rigorous quality control, could constitute a preferential form of cooperation and development aid. i deplore the fanaticism shown by some representatives of the left in calling for the term 'churches' to be replaced by 'philosophical and religious organisations', which, in the current context of the debate on the treaty text, is by no means a neutral formulation. that is why i voted for amendment no 10, which corrects this point, and i am glad that it was approved by a large majority in the plenary.
in writing. - (pt) we welcome the content of this report, which aims to promote equality between women and men in development cooperation, and we therefore voted in favour. the general objective of the european union's development cooperation policy is to combat poverty and eradicate it once and for all. however, more concrete support for this objective is essential if poverty is to be effectively tackled, and other policies are needed in the areas of cooperation and fair trade. equal rights for men and women and greater political voice for women must also be fought for. at the fourth world conference on women (beijing, 1995), a clear agenda for the promotion of equal rights between men and women was set for the first time. in the european union, this has led, inter alia, to the adoption of council regulation (ec) no 2836/98 on the mainstreaming of gender issues in development cooperation. in 2001, an action programme for mainstreaming gender issues in community development cooperation was adopted, which will expire in 2006. this regulation is the legal basis for budget line b7-6220 (article 21 02 06) - 'integration of gender issues in development cooperation'. this regulation will expire on 31 december 2003 and will have to be replaced by this proposal, which the commission has been very slow to present.
in writing. - (pt) i congratulate mrs zrihen zaari on her excellent report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the promotion of gender equality in development cooperation, which i fully support with regard to the amendments tabled. in this context, i would like to express my particular support for the introduction of a regulatory text which does not contain an exhaustive list of projects to be supported and which genuinely encourages the launching of actions promoting equality between men and women in development cooperation. i would also like to stress the importance of supporting the collection and dissemination of statistics in this area. without proper collection of statistics, the whole process of analysing these statistics is undermined and without their adequate dissemination, society cannot become aware of the situation.
in writing. - (pt) the main aspects of development cooperation are financing measures to combat poverty and disease and developing solutions to education problems while establishing a culture of protection of fundamental human rights. i am fully in favour of adopting measures which can help to achieve these objectives of aid to the poorest and, since i believe that the rapporteur's suggestions can help to achieve these objectives, i supported this report. i cannot, however, fail to express some concerns which i fear have not been duly considered. on the one hand, it is essential to take account of the appalling differences between the realities of the developing countries and those of our own countries. in societies where the primary struggle is for survival, we can in no way delay these primary objectives. secondly, it is important to define clearly what we mean by 'sexual and reproductive health' so that the meaning underlying this reasonable concern is not hijacked and turned into a 'password' for the development of international programmes to promote abortion, which i categorically reject. it should be made clear at all times that 'sexual and reproductive health' means preventing sexually transmitted diseases, including hiv/aids, and ensuring women have decent conditions during pregnancy, childbirth and the postpartum period.
in writing. - (pt) the fifth fisheries protocol between the european community and côte d'ivoire expired on 30 june. the commission's proposal is to extend the current protocol by one year, and we support it. however, we believe, as does the rapporteur, that the commission should consult the european parliament instead of presenting us with a fait accompli. a delay of more than three months is completely unjustifiable. the extension of this protocol will guarantee fishing opportunities to 71 vessels of the community fleet, in particular tuna seiners, including five portuguese surface longliners. this extension will also provide a reasonable timeframe for negotiating the renewal of the agreement. this agreement has been beneficial to both parties and shows the importance of international fisheries agreements, not only for community fleets but also for local development. although tuna catches have been slightly below the reference tonnage for some years, the value of the catches exceeds the cost of the protocol, which translates into a financial advantage for the community. the agreement also contributes to local development. the port of abidjan is the largest tuna base in west africa, and the landed fish contribute to the development of the local processing industry.
in writing. - (pt) it is important that we maintain this essential fisheries agreement not only because it is important for the fishing fleets operating under it, but also as a sign of the confidence that the european union has in the process of political stabilisation in côte d'ivoire. the commission proposal includes a request for the extension for one year, for the period 1 july 2003 to 30 june 2004, of the fisheries agreement governing fisheries relations between the european union and the republic of côte d'ivoire, in accordance with the provisions of the protocol in force, both in terms of financial compensation and fishing opportunities. this extension would allow the shipowners to continue their activities without interruption and the commission would have additional time to negotiate and renew the agreement. i support the recommendations in the report that the commission should be consistent with the assessment of the state of stocks and with the real activity of the community fleets, in order to avoid the acquisition of concessions that shipowners do not really need. i also invite the commission to present in due time the proposals it asks parliament to approve.
in writing. - (pt) all those concerned are aware of my public positions on the process of revising the treaties, the work of the convention and the legal and political implications of the conclusions of the intergovernmental conference. these positions are duly set out in this draft resolution, as well as in the draft resolution that my group has tabled on the igc summit of heads of state or government. it is for these same reasons that i have opposed the compromise resolution tabled on the same subject by the main parties in this parliament. i continue to believe that the european union is a union of states and that it is the responsibility of the states to take the final decision in this area. i also believe that it is not the role of parliament to exert political pressure which could hasten the approval of an unsatisfactory agreement, or to allow the expression of hidden threats concerning the emergence of a multi-speed europe, by introducing, once again, unnecessary tensions in a process which requires maturity, responsibility and common sense in the difficult and sensitive political decisions to be taken.
in writing. - (pt) although i voted in favour of this resolution, i would like to stress that the recent european council in brussels was not a failure. it is a success, a double success, in fact: there was no agreement on the fanciful and hasty constitution, but the initiative for growth was established. by 2010, we will mobilise investment of several million euro in projects for real harmonisation, cohesion and growth: the trans-european networks (transport, telecommunications and energy), innovation, research and development. this is european integration! as i said in another explanation of vote on the igc, this double decision betrays the influence of the founding spirit of robert schuman: 'europe will not be made all at once, nor in an overall construction: it will be made by concrete achievements first creating a de facto solidarity'. it is for the same reason that it is regrettable - and something we must firmly reject - that after the brussels summit, germany and france - they are still the same! - unfortunately joined this time by the united kingdom, sweden, the netherlands and austria, have exerted intolerable pressure to limit the eu budget for 2004 to 1% of community gdp. this attitude ignores all current developments, it is harmful to europe and tears it apart, it betrays schuman and the european spirit. i also welcome the inclusion of paragraph 49 on cuba and oswaldo payá, which follows from my proposal on the original text of the une.
in writing. - (pt) following a complaint to the committee on petitions on the treatment in the member states of the european union of persons diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, the european parliament today invited the commission to include a debate on the issues raised in this report on the agenda of a forthcoming meeting of eu health ministers. this is to develop a code of best practice to be followed in all member states and which will also focus on international research cooperation to combat this disease. another very interesting point raised by the rapporteur is the psychological treatment of multiple sclerosis, a disease which, because it generally affects young people at a time in their lives when they should be most productive, places them in an uncertain future, both socially and professionally. for the reasons i have just mentioned, and because i believe that this disease deserves greater recognition from the public authorities who must be committed to finding effective solutions to the problems faced by people with this disease, i have approved this report by giving it my unreserved vote.
in writing. - (pt) i too received a disappointing reply from the european commission on the sensitive subject of health when i asked it about the possibility of introducing a european charter for the inpatient child. the question is a tricky one: the principle of subsidiarity can only be called into question by a revision of the treaties. any increase in social burdens and responsibilities that the eu wants to impose on member states must be accompanied by an increase in the community resources allocated, which raises very serious questions and problems that are not easy to solve. the european union must find the right instruments to promote better protection for the poorest and most needy. and there are ways of doing this without infringing subsidiarity. it is difficult to explain why lamps should be standardised and why we are producing initiatives and legislation in this area when, at the same time, we are too busy to look after our own citizens. worse still, this need is felt most cruelly in childhood, in sickness and in old age. commissioner byrne once again informed a fellow member that the commission is sensitive to 'greater interaction between health systems'. this is precisely the europe that the citizens want to see. a europe with or without a constitution, but a europe with a heart. a europe that promotes 'best practice', starting with the citizens' greatest needs. i supported this well-considered and appropriate proposal in the hope that it could bring about a change in the situation. the plenary has spoken. (explanation of vote abbreviated pursuant to rule 137 (1) of the rules of procedure)
mr president, i believe that when we saw the iron curtain fall and the soviet union disappear, we were all convinced that a great opportunity had been opened up for development, peace and progress throughout central and eastern europe. we convinced ourselves that we were facing the end of history, that we were facing a new dawn. and perhaps the most dramatic denial of that hope we have had to date is precisely in moldova. moldova is the clear example that history does not always run the way its protagonists begin to plot, moldova is one of the worst examples of contemporary europe. it is an example of a country torn by ethnic strife, with part of it occupied by foreign military forces, where the economy is in total collapse, where the mafia rules, where its inhabitants try to leave the country in any way they can. we must not forget that from 2007, according to the official timetable we have for enlargement, moldova will be on the border of the european union. and so moldova - and i am addressing myself directly to the commissioner - cannot be treated as a minor issue. it must be seen as a priority for our european diplomacy. this state of affairs cannot continue, and i believe that our resolution should be seen as a great warning to all the institutions to look at moldova with the greatest attention and to try to find a solution to the current conflict, which is threatening the stability of this country and of the whole of central and eastern europe.
